knowledge_statements.statement_title: QP, Convex QP, and Convex Programming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines quadratic programming and convex QP and identifies convex programming as the broader model class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quadratic program has the form \(\min_{x\in F}q(x)\), where \(q:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is quadratic and \(F\) is defined by linear constraints. It is a convex quadratic program when \(q\) is convex. More generally, \(\min_{x\in C}f(x)\) is a convex program when \(f\) is convex and \(C\) is convex; the objective need not be quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic program minimizes a quadratic objective subject to linear constraints. It is a convex QP when the quadratic objective is convex. Convex programming is the broader class in which the objective and feasible region are convex, without requiring a quadratic objective.
assumptions_latex: q:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is quadratic and }F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is defined by linear constraints}
f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is convex and }C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{x\in F}q(x)\text{ is a QP; if }q\text{ is convex, it is a convex QP. Moreover, }\min_{x\in C}f(x)\text{ is a convex program.}

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\) is strongly convex and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}q(x)\) consists of exactly one point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic programs with strictly positive curvature in every nonzero direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n_{++}\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(r\in\mathbb{R}\), and let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. A positive-definite quadratic program has the form \[\min_{x\in C}\;q(x):=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r.\] Since \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\) for every \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\), the objective is strongly convex and coercive. Consequently, the minimum over \(C\) is attained and its minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite QP minimizes a strongly convex, coercive quadratic over a nonempty closed convex feasible set, so it has a unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite QP Models

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative curvature bounds intrinsic to a positive-definite quadratic objective and its constrained minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\) with \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), and set \(m=\lambda_{\min}(Q)\) and \(L=\lambda_{\max}(Q)\). Then for every \(x,y\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\frac m2\|y-x\|_2^2\le q(y)-q(x)-\nabla q(x)^{\mathsf T}(y-x)\le\frac L2\|y-x\|_2^2.\] If \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex and \(x^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}q(x)\), then \[q(x)-q(x^*)\ge\frac m2\|x-x^*\|_2^2\qquad\text{for every }x\in C.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extreme Hessian eigenvalues give exact lower and upper quadratic curvature bounds, and the smallest eigenvalue gives quadratic growth around the unique constrained minimizer.
assumptions_latex: For constrained growth, \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\) has curvature between \(m=\lambda_{\min}(Q)>0\) and \(L=\lambda_{\max}(Q)\), and \(q(x)-q(x^*)\ge(m/2)\|x-x^*\|_2^2\) on \(C\).

notation.meaning: Smallest eigenvalue of the positive-definite Hessian.
Largest eigenvalue of the positive-definite Hessian.
Unique minimizer over the closed convex feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Curvature and Quadratic Growth

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\) is convex on \(C\), and its minimizer set is convex whenever nonempty.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic programs that may have flat curvature directions.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(r\in\mathbb{R}\), and let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. A positive-semidefinite quadratic program is \[\min_{x\in C}\;q(x):=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r.\] Because \(Q\succeq0\), the function \(q\) is convex but need not be strictly convex. Its minimizer set, when nonempty, is convex and may contain multiple points. Attainment follows, for example, if \(C\) is compact or if \(q\) is level-bounded on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite QP minimizes a convex quadratic over a closed convex feasible set; flat directions can cause nonunique minimizers, and attainment requires compactness or another suitable existence condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite QP Models

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundedness and minimizer characterization for an unconstrained positive-semidefinite quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). Then \(q\) is bounded below, attains its infimum, \(c\in\operatorname{range}(Q)\), and \(c\perp\ker(Q)\) are equivalent. When they hold, \[\operatorname*{argmin}q=-Q^\dagger c+\ker(Q),\qquad \min q=r-\tfrac12c^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger c.\] Otherwise some \(d\in\ker(Q)\) satisfies \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\), and \(q(x+td)\to-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unconstrained PSD quadratic has a minimum exactly when its linear coefficient lies in the Hessian range. Its minimizers then form an affine translate of the Hessian nullspace; otherwise it is unbounded along a flat direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf q>-infty\iff c\in\operatorname{range}(Q)\), and then \(\operatorname*{argmin}q=-Q^\dagger c+\ker(Q)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Positive-Semidefinite Quadratic Solvability

children.title: Structured Curvature Models
children.top_down_role: Diagonal, separable, block, banded, low-rank, and graph-structured quadratic models.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Storage and Matrix-Vector Costs of Principal Curvature Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic and storage consequences of retaining common structured curvature representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an \(n\times n\) matrix, diagonal storage and multiplication cost \(O(n)\). A scalar half-bandwidth \(b\) gives \(O(nb)\) storage and multiplication. For \(Q=D+UU^{\mathsf T}\) with \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), retaining the factors costs \(O(nk)\) storage and \(O(nk)\) per product when \(D\) is diagonal. For \(Q=B^{\mathsf T}WB\) with diagonal \(W\), a product can be evaluated as \(B^{\mathsf T}(W(Bx))\) in \(O(\operatorname{nnz}B)\) operations. Corresponding block and local-sum costs equal the total storage or multiplication work of their retained components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retaining diagonal, banded, low-rank, graph, block, or local factors avoids the quadratic storage and multiplication costs of an explicitly dense Hessian when the defining parameters remain sparse or low-dimensional.
assumptions_latex: The structured factors, rather than an explicitly assembled dense matrix, are stored
\(b\) is scalar half-bandwidth and \(k\) is factor rank
\(W\) is diagonal in the graph-form cost
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Structured storage and matrix-vector multiplication scale with bandwidth, rank, graph sparsity, or total component size rather than necessarily with \(n^2\).

notation.meaning: number of nonzero entries of B

knowledge_statements.title: Storage and Matrix-Vector Costs of Principal Curvature Structures

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operations that can destroy diagonal, banded, sparse, or low-rank-plus-diagonal structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Positive semidefiniteness is preserved by congruence, sums, and elimination through valid Schur complements, but a dense coordinate congruence \(T^{\mathsf T}QT\), summation of components with incompatible sparsity patterns, or variable elimination can make a diagonal, banded, graph-sparse, or block-sparse matrix dense. Likewise, adding unrelated structured factors can increase rank or destroy a fixed low-rank-plus-diagonal budget. Thus PSD preservation does not imply preservation of the advertised computational structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Algebraic transformations may preserve convexity while destroying sparsity, bandwidth, separability, or a prescribed low-rank representation.
assumptions_latex: The stated congruences, sums, or eliminations are dimensionally well defined
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Preservation of \(Q\succeq0\) does not imply preservation of diagonal, block, banded, sparse, or fixed-rank structure.
knowledge_statements.title: Structured-Curvature Preservation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical algebraic forms for diagonal, block, banded, low-rank, graph, and locally assembled PSD curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Computationally structured PSD curvature includes: \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(d)\) with \(d\ge0\); block-diagonal PSD matrices; PSD banded matrices; \(Q=D+UU^{\mathsf T}\) with \(D\succeq0\); graph forms \(Q=B^{\mathsf T}WB\) with \(W\succeq0\); and local assemblies \(Q=\sum_iE_i^{\mathsf T}Q_iE_i\) with \(Q_i\succeq0\). Each construction is PSD. Diagonal curvature is coordinate-separable, block-diagonal curvature is block-separable, while banded, factor, graph, and local forms expose limited interaction or compact factors without necessarily being separable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal, block, banded, low-rank-plus-diagonal, graph-Gram, and local-sum forms expose different kinds of PSD curvature structure.
assumptions_latex: All component matrices have compatible dimensions
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every displayed construction satisfies \(Q\succeq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Principal Structured Positive-Semidefinite Curvature Forms
Structured Curvature Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common algebraic and sparsity representations of positive-semidefinite quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structured convex quadratic model has objective \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\) with \(Q\succeq0\) represented in a computationally exploitable form. Standard forms include diagonal \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(d)\) with \(d\ge0\); block-diagonal or banded positive-semidefinite \(Q\); low-rank-plus-diagonal \(Q=D+UU^{\mathsf T}\) with \(D\succeq0\); and graph structure \(Q=B^{\mathsf T}WB\) with diagonal \(W\succeq0\). Sum-of-local-quadratics models satisfy \(Q=\sum_{k=1}^m E_k^{\mathsf T}Q_kE_k\), where each \(Q_k\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structured QPs encode curvature through diagonal, block, banded, low-rank, graph, or local positive-semidefinite components.
assumptions_latex: All displayed component matrices have compatible dimensions
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each displayed factorization defines a convex quadratic objective and exposes separability, sparsity, or low-rank structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(r\in\mathbb{R}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and assume \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\). An equality-constrained convex quadratic program is \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b.\] Its feasible set is affine and convex. The problem has a unique minimizer if and only if \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\) for every \(d\in\ker A\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality-constrained convex QP minimizes a quadratic over a nonempty affine set and has a unique minimizer exactly when the quadratic has positive curvature along every nonzero feasible direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained QP Models

children.title: Lower-Bound-Constrained QP Models
children.top_down_role: QP templates governed by finite lower bounds on selected variables.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:x\ge\ell\}=\ell+\mathbb{R}^n_+\) is a nonempty closed convex polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic programs with componentwise lower bounds.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\), \(c,\ell\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(r\in\mathbb{R}\). A lower-bound-constrained quadratic program is \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\ge\ell,\] where the inequality is componentwise. Its feasible region is \(\ell+\mathbb{R}^n_+\), a nonempty closed convex polyhedron. The model is a convex QP; attainment follows if, for example, the objective is level-bounded on the feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-bound QP minimizes a convex quadratic over the translated nonnegative orthant defined by componentwise lower limits.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Bound-Constrained QP Models

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality certificate for the translated nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g(x)=Qx+c\), a point \(x^\star\ge\ell\) minimizes the convex quadratic if and only if \[g(x^\star)\ge0,\qquad (x^\star-\ell)_ig_i(x^\star)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-bound-feasible point is optimal exactly when the gradient is nonnegative and complementary to its slack above the bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\ge\ell}q(x)\iff Qx^\star+c\ge0,\ (x^\star-\ell)\odot(Qx^\star+c)=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Bound KKT and Complementarity Conditions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recession boundary for the translated nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The lower-bound QP has value \(-\infty\) if and only if there exists \(d\ge0\) such that \(Qd=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\). If no such direction exists, its finite minimum is attained. In particular, when \(Q=0\), any \(c_i<0\) makes the problem unbounded below along \(e_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-bound QP is unbounded below exactly when a nonnegative zero-curvature direction has negative linear slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\ge\ell}q(x)=-\infty\iff\exists d\ge0:\ Qd=0,\ c^{\mathsf T}d<0.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Bound QP Unboundedness Test

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:x\le u\}=u-\mathbb{R}^n_+\) is a nonempty closed convex polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic programs with componentwise upper bounds.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\), \(c,u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(r\in\mathbb{R}\). An upper-bound-constrained quadratic program is \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\le u,\] where the inequality is componentwise. Its feasible region is \(u-\mathbb{R}^n_+\), a nonempty closed convex polyhedron. The model is a convex QP; attainment follows if, for example, the objective is level-bounded on the feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An upper-bound QP minimizes a convex quadratic over the translated nonpositive orthant defined by componentwise upper limits.
knowledge_statements.title: Upper-Bound-Constrained QP Models

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality certificate for the translated nonpositive orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g(x)=Qx+c\), a point \(x^\star\le u\) minimizes the convex quadratic if and only if \[g(x^\star)\le0,\qquad (u-x^\star)_ig_i(x^\star)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An upper-bound-feasible point is optimal exactly when the gradient is nonpositive and complementary to its slack below the bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\le u}q(x)\iff Qx^\star+c\le0,\ (u-x^\star)\odot(Qx^\star+c)=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Upper-Bound KKT and Complementarity Conditions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recession boundary for the translated nonpositive orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The upper-bound QP has value \(-\infty\) if and only if there exists \(d\le0\) such that \(Qd=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\). If no such direction exists, its finite minimum is attained. In particular, when \(Q=0\), any \(c_i>0\) makes the problem unbounded below along \(-e_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An upper-bound QP is unbounded below exactly when a nonpositive zero-curvature direction has negative linear slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\le u}q(x)=-\infty\iff\exists d\le0:\ Qd=0,\ c^{\mathsf T}d<0.
knowledge_statements.title: Upper-Bound QP Unboundedness Test

children.title: Box-Constrained QP Models
children.top_down_role: QP templates with two-sided variable intervals and mixed finite-bound patterns.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\ell\le x\le u}q(x)\ne\varnothing\), and this set is a singleton if \(Q\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic programs over a finite componentwise interval box.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\), \(c,\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(r\in\mathbb{R}\), with \(\ell\le u\) componentwise. A box-constrained quadratic program is \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;q(x):=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\quad\text{subject to}\quad \ell\le x\le u.\] The feasible set \([\ell,u]\) is a nonempty compact convex polytope, so the continuous objective \(q\) attains a minimum. If \(Q\succ0\), the minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box-constrained QP minimizes a convex quadratic between finite componentwise lower and upper bounds; a minimizer exists and is unique when the quadratic matrix is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.title: Box-Constrained QP Models

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 11. The alphaBB for Box Constrained Twice-Differentiable NLPs: Theory p. 315

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality test specialized to finite two-sided bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=Qx+c\). A feasible \(x^\star\in[\ell,u]\) minimizes the convex quadratic if and only if, for every \(i\), \[g_i(x^\star)=0\ \text{if }\ell_i<x_i^\star<u_i,\quad g_i(x^\star)\ge0\ \text{if }x_i^\star=\ell_i<u_i,\quad g_i(x^\star)\le0\ \text{if }x_i^\star=u_i>\ell_i.\] No sign restriction is imposed when \(\ell_i=u_i=x_i^\star\). Equivalently, for every \(\alpha>0\), \(x^\star=\Pi_{[\ell,u]}(x^\star-\alpha g(x^\star))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box-feasible point is optimal exactly when its gradient has the proper active-bound signs, equivalently when its projected-gradient residual is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\ell\le x\le u}q(x)\iff x^\star=\Pi_{[\ell,u]}(x^\star-\alpha(Qx^\star+c)).
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinatewise Box KKT Conditions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility and Nonuniqueness Boundaries for Box QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp endpoint-feasibility and nonuniqueness boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The box \([\ell,u]\) is nonempty if and only if \(\ell\le u\) componentwise. Positive definiteness of \(Q\) guarantees a unique minimizer, but positive semidefiniteness alone does not: if \(Q=0\), \(c=0\), and \([\ell,u]\) contains two distinct points, then every feasible point is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reversed endpoints cause infeasibility, while a constant objective shows that convexity alone does not imply a unique box minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: [\ell,u]\ne\varnothing\iff\ell\le u;\qquad Q=0,\ c=0,\ |[\ell,u]|>1\Rightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}q=[\ell,u].
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility and Nonuniqueness Boundaries for Box QPs

children.title: Simplex-Constrained QP Models
children.top_down_role: QP templates over normalized nonnegative decision vectors.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A minimizer exists on \(\Delta_\tau=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:x\ge0,\ \mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}x=\tau\}\), and it is unique if \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\) satisfying \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}d=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic programs over the standard or scaled simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(r\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(\tau>0\). A simplex-constrained quadratic program is \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\ge0,\quad \mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}x=\tau.\] Its feasible set \(\Delta_\tau\) is nonempty, compact, and convex, so a minimizer exists. It is unique if \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}d=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simplex QP minimizes a convex quadratic over nonnegative vectors with prescribed total mass; a minimizer exists and is unique under positive curvature along every nonzero zero-sum direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Simplex-Constrained QP Models

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality test expressed through a common simplex multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=Qx+c\). A point \(x^\star\in\Delta_\tau\) minimizes the convex quadratic if and only if there exists \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\) such that \[g_i(x^\star)+\lambda\ge0,1qquad x_i^\star(g_i(x^\star)+\lambda)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).\] Equivalently, all positive coordinates have the same gradient value \(-\lambda\), and every zero coordinate has gradient at least that value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a simplex optimum, gradient components are equal on the support and no smaller off the support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\Delta_\tau}q\iff\exists\lambda:\ Qx^\star+c+\lambda\mathbf1\ge0,\ x^\star\odot(Qx^\star+c+\lambda\mathbf1)=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Simplex-QP KKT and Support Characterization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical failure of uniqueness under positive-semidefinite curvature alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Q=0\) and \(c=0\), then \(q\) is constant on \(\Delta_\tau\). For \(n\ge2\) and \(\tau>0\), every point of \(\Delta_\tau\) is optimal, so positive-semidefinite curvature alone does not imply uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant objective makes the entire nontrivial simplex optimal, showing why tangential positive curvature is needed for a general uniqueness guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\Delta_\tau}q(x)=\Delta_\tau.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniqueness Without Tangential Positive Curvature

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaling Between Standard and Mass Simplexes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical equivalence of positive-mass simplex QP models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The substitution \(x=\tau y\) is a bijection from \(\Delta_1\) to \(\Delta_\tau\). Under it, \[\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r=\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}(\tau^2Q)y+(\tau c)^{\mathsf T}y+r.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing variables by their prescribed mass converts a scaled-simplex QP into a standard-simplex QP with exact optimizer correspondence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x=\tau y:\Delta_1\to\Delta_\tau\text{ is bijective and preserves objective values under }(Q,c)\mapsto(\tau^2Q,\tau c).
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Between Standard and Mass Simplexes

children.title: Budget-Constrained QP Models
children.top_down_role: QP templates with aggregate resource or expenditure limits.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:x\ge0,\ a^{\mathsf T}x\le B\}\) is nonempty, compact, and convex, so a minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic allocation models with nonnegativity and an aggregate upper budget.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(r\in\mathbb{R}\), \(a\in\mathbb{R}^n_{++}\), and \(B\ge0\). A budget-constrained quadratic program is \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\ge0,\quad a^{\mathsf T}x\le B.\] Its feasible set is a nonempty compact convex polytope, so the objective attains a minimum. Replacing the inequality by \(a^{\mathsf T}x=B\) gives the full-allocation variant, whose feasible set is nonempty when \(B\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A budget QP minimizes a convex quadratic over nonnegative allocations whose positively weighted aggregate use does not exceed a nonnegative budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Budget-Constrained QP Models

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality conditions for nonnegative allocations under one aggregate upper budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=Qx+c\). A feasible \(x^\star\ge0\), \(a^{\mathsf T}x^\star\le B\), minimizes the convex budget QP if and only if there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \[g(x^\star)+\lambda a\ge0,\qquad x_i^\star(g_i(x^\star)+\lambda a_i)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,n),\qquad \lambda(a^{\mathsf T}x^\star-B)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative budget price, complementary reduced gradients, and complementary slackness exactly certify optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{q(x):x\ge0,\ a^{\mathsf T}x\le B\}\iff\exists\lambda\ge0\text{ satisfying the displayed system}.
knowledge_statements.title: Budget-QP KKT Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp role of the seed's strictly positive resource-price assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(B\ge0\) and \(a\in\mathbb R_+^n\), the set \(C_B=\{x\ge0:a^{\mathsf T}x\le B\}\) is bounded if and only if every \(a_i>0\). If some \(a_i=0\), then \(te_i\in C_B\) for every \(t\ge0\), and with \(Q=0\) and \(c_i<0\) the corresponding budget QP is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly positive prices are exactly what makes the nonnegative upper-budget region bounded; a zero-priced coordinate creates an unbounded ray.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_B\text{ is bounded}\iff a\in\mathbb R_{++}^n.
knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Positive Prices and Compactness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact distinction between an upper-budget model and its full-allocation variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a nonnegative-orthant minimizer \(\bar x\) satisfies \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x\le B\), then it also solves the budget QP and the aggregate constraint need not be active. Conversely, every KKT point with \(\lambda>0\) satisfies \(a^{\mathsf T}x^\star=B\). Thus full allocation is not automatic; it is forced by a strictly positive budget multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The budget need not be exhausted, but a positive shadow price forces full expenditure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda>0\Rightarrow a^{\mathsf T}x^\star=B;\qquad \bar x\in\arg\min_{x\ge0}q,\ a^{\mathsf T}\bar x\le B\Rightarrow\bar x\in\arg\min_{x\ge0,\ a^{\mathsf T}x\le B}q.
knowledge_statements.title: Active and Slack Budget Regimes

children.title: Balance-Constrained QP Models
children.top_down_role: QP templates with conservation, clearing, or net-balance restrictions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set \(\{x\in X:Bx=d\}\) is nonempty and convex; it is polyhedral if \(X\) is polyhedral.

notation.meaning: image of X under the linear map B

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic flow or allocation models satisfying linear conservation equations.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2 The Method of Multipliers for Equality Constrained Problems
source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(r\in\mathbb{R}\), \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(d\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex. A balance-constrained quadratic program is \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\quad\text{subject to}\quad Bx=d,\quad x\in X.\] The equations represent linear conservation or accounting balance. The feasible set is convex and is nonempty exactly when \(d\in B(X)\); if \(X\) is polyhedral, the feasible set is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A balance QP minimizes a convex quadratic subject to linear conservation equations and a convex domain of admissible signs or capacities.
knowledge_statements.title: Balance-Constrained QP Models

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2 The Method of Multipliers for Equality Constrained Problems
source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality condition for a balance equation intersected with a convex admissible domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(X\) is closed and convex and \(\operatorname{ri}(X)\cap\{x:Bx=d\}\ne\varnothing\). A feasible \(x^\star\) minimizes \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\) over \(X\cap\{Bx=d\}\) if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \[0\in Qx^\star+c+B^{\mathsf T}y+N_X(x^\star).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the relative-interior qualification, optimality is equivalent to balance stationarity with a normal to the admissible domain.
assumptions_latex: X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is closed and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X,\ Bx=d}q(x)\iff\exists y:\ 0\in Qx^\star+c+B^{\mathsf T}y+N_X(x^\star).

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal cone of X at the feasible point

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone Optimality for Balance QPs

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closedness and Level-Boundedness Requirements for Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing that convexity and balance feasibility alone do not imply existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=X\cap\{x:Bx=d\}\ne\varnothing\). A minimizer exists if \(F\) is compact, or if \(F\) is closed and \(q\) is level-bounded on \(F\). Convexity of \(X\) alone is insufficient: with no effective balance equations, \(X=(0,\infty)\), and \(q(x)=x^2\), the infimum \(0\) is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balance feasibility plus convexity does not ensure attainment; compactness or closedness with level-boundedness does.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ compact, or }(F\text{ closed and }q\text{ level-bounded on }F)\Rightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}_{F}q\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Closedness and Level-Boundedness Requirements for Attainment

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\) is a closed convex polyhedron, and the optimization problem is convex.

notation.meaning: numbers of equality and inequality constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic programs over finite systems of affine equalities and inequalities.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_e,m_i\) be nonnegative integers, \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(r\in\mathbb{R}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m_e\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{m_e}\), \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i}\). A general polyhedrally constrained convex quadratic program is \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\;\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\quad Gx\le h.\] Its feasible region \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\) is a closed convex polyhedron. If \(P\ne\varnothing\), attainment follows when \(P\) is bounded or when the objective is level-bounded on \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general polyhedrally constrained convex QP minimizes a quadratic subject to finitely many explicitly dimensioned affine equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: General Polyhedrally Constrained QP Models

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT Certificate for a Polyhedrally Constrained Convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order optimality certificate for the mixed affine model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\), \(Q\succeq0\), and \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\), a feasible \(x^\star\) is globally optimal if and only if there exist \(y\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\) and \(z\in\mathbb R^{m_i}_+\) such that \[Qx^\star+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\qquad z_i(G_ix^\star-h_i)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m_i).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility, stationarity, nonnegative inequality multipliers, and complementary slackness exactly characterize global optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}q(x)\iff\exists(y,z)\text{ satisfying the displayed KKT system}.
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Certificate for a Polyhedrally Constrained Convex QP

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-value boundary for a convex quadratic over a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=\{d:Ad=0,\ Gd\le0\}\) be the recession cone of nonempty \(P\). Then \[\inf_{x\in P}q(x)=-\infty\iff\exists d\in R:\ Qd=0,\ c^{\mathsf T}d<0.\] If no such direction exists, the optimal value is finite and is attained on \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The problem is unbounded below exactly along a feasible recession direction with zero quadratic curvature and negative linear slope; otherwise it attains a minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\in P}q(x)=-\infty\iff\exists d\in R:\ Qd=0,\ c^{\mathsf T}d<0;\quad\text{otherwise }\operatorname*{argmin}_{P}q\ne\varnothing.

notation.meaning: recession cone of the feasible polyhedron

knowledge_statements.title: Attainment and Unboundedness Recession Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Symmetric representation and derivatives of a quadratic objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained real quadratic objectives, including reduction to the symmetric part of the quadratic matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=-x^Tb+\tfrac12x^THx\) and set \(S=(H+H^T)/2\). Since \(x^THx=x^TSx\), the same function has the symmetric representation \(f(x)=-x^Tb+\tfrac12x^TSx\), with \(\nabla f(x)=-b+Sx\) and \(\nabla^2f(x)=S\) for every \(x\). Thus the quadratic matrix may be assumed symmetric without loss of generality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only the symmetric part of a matrix contributes to a real quadratic form. Using that symmetric part, the gradient is -b + Sx and the Hessian is the constant matrix S.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^THx=x^TSx,\qquad \nabla f(x)=-b+Sx,\qquad \nabla^2f(x)=S.

source_evidence.locator: Basic Concepts / 1.5. Quadratic Objective Functions / Definition 1.5-extra-1

source_refs.locator: Basic Concepts / 1.5. Quadratic Objective Functions / Definition 1.5-extra-1

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric representation and derivatives of a quadratic objective

source_witnesses.locator: Basic Concepts / 1.5. Quadratic Objective Functions / Definition 1.5-extra-1

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Form Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical matrix representation of real scalar quadratic objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every real scalar quadratic function on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) can be written as \[q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r,\] with \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(r\in\mathbb{R}\). If an initial representation uses a nonsymmetric matrix \(M\), then \(x^{\mathsf T}Mx=x^{\mathsf T}((M+M^{\mathsf T})/2)x\), so only its symmetric part matters. In this convention, \(\nabla q(x)=Qx+c\) and \(\nabla^2q(x)=Q\); hence \(q\) is convex exactly when \(Q\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar quadratic equals a symmetric quadratic form plus a linear and constant term; its Hessian is the symmetric matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla q(x)=Qx+c\), \(\nabla^2q(x)=Q\), and \(q\) is convex if and only if \(Q\succeq0\).

children.title: Ordinary Least-Squares Quadratic Models
children.top_down_role: Quadratic objectives expressed through unweighted residual fitting.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordinary Least-Squares Quadratic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional unconstrained ordinary least squares in convex-QP form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the residual map \(r(x)=Ax-b\) satisfies
\[
\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2
=\frac12x^{\mathsf T}A^{\mathsf T}Ax-(A^{\mathsf T}b)^{\mathsf T}x+\frac12b^{\mathsf T}b.
\]
Thus the objective is a convex quadratic model with Hessian \(H=A^{\mathsf T}A\succeq0\) and linear coefficient \(g=-A^{\mathsf T}b\). Dropping the constant \(b^{\mathsf T}b/2\) preserves the complete set of minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordinary least squares is a convex quadratic with Hessian A-transpose-A and linear coefficient minus A-transpose-b; omitting its constant term preserves all minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H=A^{\mathsf T}A\succeq0,\quad g=-A^{\mathsf T}b

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact unconstrained solution characterization for finite-dimensional ordinary least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\tfrac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2=\{x:A^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)=0\}=A^\dagger b+\ker(A).\] The fitted vector is uniquely \(AA^\dagger b\), the orthogonal projection of \(b\) onto \(\operatorname{range}(A)\). The parameter minimizer is unique exactly when \(A\) has full column rank; among all minimizers, \(A^\dagger b\) is the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: OLS minimizers solve the normal equations and equal the pseudoinverse solution plus the design nullspace. Fits are unique, while parameters are unique exactly under full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}\tfrac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2=A^\dagger b+\ker(A)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Ordinary Least-Squares Solution Set

children.title: Weighted Least-Squares Quadratic Models
children.top_down_role: Residual-fitting objectives carrying observation or residual weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Least-Squares Quadratic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal nonnegative observation weights; zero weights yield a seminorm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_1,\ldots,w_m)\) with \(w_i\ge0\),
\[
\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_W^2
=\frac12x^{\mathsf T}A^{\mathsf T}WAx-(A^{\mathsf T}Wb)^{\mathsf T}x+\frac12b^{\mathsf T}Wb.
\]
Consequently, its QP Hessian is \(H=A^{\mathsf T}WA\succeq0\), and its linear coefficient is \(g=-A^{\mathsf T}Wb\). The model is strictly convex exactly when \(A^{\mathsf T}WA\succ0\), equivalently when \(W^{1/2}A\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative diagonal residual weights produce a convex quadratic. Strict convexity holds exactly when the weighted design matrix has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H=A^{\mathsf T}WA\succeq0,\quad g=-A^{\mathsf T}Wb

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-scaling equivalence, normal equations, and minimizer family for nonnegative diagonal observation weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_1,\ldots,w_m)\succeq0\), \(D=W^{1/2}\), and consider \(\tfrac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_W^2\). Its minimizers are \[\{x:A^{\mathsf T}W(Ax-b)=0\}=(DA)^\dagger Db+\ker(DA).\] Rows with \(w_i=0\) have no effect on the objective or solution set. The weighted fitted vector \(DAx\) is unique, while the parameter vector is unique exactly when \(DA\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal weighted least squares is OLS after row scaling. Zero-weight observations disappear, and minimizers differ by the scaled design's nullspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_x\tfrac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_W^2=(DA)^\dagger Db+\ker(DA)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Weighted Least-Squares Solution Set

children.title: General Weighted-Norm Quadratic Models
children.top_down_role: Quadratic objectives expressed through positive-semidefinite metric structure.

knowledge_statements.title: General Weighted-Norm Quadratic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite, possibly nondiagonal residual metric in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(W\in\mathbb{S}_+^m\), let \(L\) be any matrix satisfying \(L^{\mathsf T}L=W\). Then
\[
\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_W^2
=\frac12\lVert L(Ax-b)\rVert_2^2
=\frac12x^{\mathsf T}A^{\mathsf T}WAx-(A^{\mathsf T}Wb)^{\mathsf T}x+\frac12b^{\mathsf T}Wb.
\]
Hence the convex-QP data are \(H=A^{\mathsf T}WA\succeq0\) and \(g=-A^{\mathsf T}Wb\). A nondiagonal \(W\) permits coupling between distinct residual components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite residual metric, including a nondiagonal one, gives a convex quadratic equivalent to ordinary least squares after a matrix-factor transformation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H=A^{\mathsf T}WA\succeq0,\quad g=-A^{\mathsf T}Wb

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal equations, solution set, and uniqueness for unconstrained least squares with a PSD residual metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W=L^{\mathsf T}L\succeq0\). The minimizers of \(\tfrac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_W^2\) are exactly the solutions of \[A^{\mathsf T}W(Ax-b)=0,\] and form \[(LA)^\dagger Lb+\ker(LA).\] The transformed fitted value \(LAx\) is the same at every minimizer. The parameter minimizer is unique exactly when \(\ker(LA)=\{0\}\), equivalently \(A^{\mathsf T}WA\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PSD-metric least squares always has minimizers; they solve the weighted normal equations and differ precisely by null directions of the transformed design.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_x\tfrac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_W^2=(LA)^\dagger Lb+\ker(LA)\).

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the transformed design matrix

knowledge_statements.title: General Weighted-Norm Minimizer Characterization
Sum-of-Local-Quadratics Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation of finitely many convex quadratic terms defined on selected or transformed coordinates of a global decision vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). For \(i=1,\ldots,p\), let \(E_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i\times n}\) and define
\[
q_i(y)=\frac12y^{\mathsf T}H_i y+g_i^{\mathsf T}y+c_i,
\qquad H_i\in\mathbb{S}_+^{n_i},\quad g_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i},\quad c_i\in\mathbb{R}.
\]
Then
\[
\sum_{i=1}^p q_i(E_i x)
=\frac12x^{\mathsf T}\left(\sum_{i=1}^pE_i^{\mathsf T}H_iE_i\right)x
+\left(\sum_{i=1}^pE_i^{\mathsf T}g_i\right)^{\mathsf T}x
+\sum_{i=1}^pc_i.
\]
Thus the aggregate Hessian is \(H=\sum_{i=1}^pE_i^{\mathsf T}H_iE_i\succeq0\). Coordinate-local terms are obtained by taking each \(E_i\) to be a coordinate-selection matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finitely many local convex quadratic contributions combine into a convex quadratic whose Hessian, linear coefficient, and constant are assembled through the local coordinate maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H=\sum_{i=1}^pE_i^{\mathsf T}H_iE_i\succeq0,\quad g=\sum_{i=1}^pE_i^{\mathsf T}g_i,\quad c=\sum_{i=1}^pc_i

notation.meaning: map from the global decision vector to local coordinates

source_refs.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Convexity of an Assembled Local Quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp nullspace criterion for positive definiteness of a sum of embedded PSD local Hessians.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\sum_{i=1}^pE_i^{\mathsf T}H_iE_i\) with \(H_i\succeq0\). Then \[\ker(H)=\bigcap_{i=1}^p\ker(H_i^{1/2}E_i).\] Consequently, the assembled quadratic is strictly convex exactly when \[\bigcap_{i=1}^p\ker(H_i^{1/2}E_i)=\{0\}.\] Individual local terms may therefore be singular while their aggregate is positive definite, provided every nonzero global direction is curved by at least one term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nullspace of an assembled PSD Hessian is the intersection of its embedded local nullspaces; strict convexity holds exactly when that intersection is trivial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\succ0\iff\bigcap_i\ker(H_i^{1/2}E_i)=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: positive-semidefinite square root of the local Hessian

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Convexity of an Assembled Local Quadratic

children.title: Equivalent QP Formulations
children.top_down_role: Representation changes that preserve the model while altering dimension, sparsity, or conditioning.

children.title: Affine Variable Elimination
children.top_down_role: Reduced QP forms obtained by resolving affine equalities for selected variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Variable Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct elimination using a nonsingular equality-constraint column block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1\le r\le n\), partition \(x=(x_B,x_F)\in\mathbb{R}^r\times\mathbb{R}^{n-r}\), and write \(A=[A_B\ A_F]\), where \(A_B\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\) is nonsingular, \(A_F\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times(n-r)}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^r\). Then \(Ax=b\) is equivalent to
\[
x_B=A_B^{-1}(b-A_Fx_F).
\]
For \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Hx/2+g^{\mathsf T}x\), substitution produces an unconstrained quadratic in \(x_F\). The resulting affine map from \(x_F\) to \(x\) is a bijection onto \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b\}\), so feasible points, objective values, and global minimizers correspond exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible equality block determines its variables affinely from the remaining variables, yielding a reduced quadratic with exactly corresponding feasible points and minimizers.
assumptions_latex: A_B\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\text{ is nonsingular},\quad A_F\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times(n-r)},\quad b\in\mathbb{R}^r
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_B=A_B^{-1}(b-A_Fx_F)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of an Eliminable Square Block
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic boundary for direct block elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), an \(r\times r\) nonsingular column block \(A_B\) exists if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=r\). If \(A\) lacks full row rank, direct elimination of one variable per displayed equation is unavailable until redundant equations are removed or a rank-revealing reduction is performed. Even at full row rank, an ill-conditioned selected block can make explicit inversion numerically unstable; implementations should use stable linear solves with pivoting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct elimination of one variable per equation is possible exactly at full row rank, while numerical stability also depends on the selected block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists B,\ |B|=r,\ \det(A_B)\ne0\iff\operatorname{rank}(A)=r.

notation.meaning: index set of eliminated or basic columns

knowledge_statements.title: Existence of an Eliminable Square Block

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit Reduced Quadratic Under Block Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-level form of the seed's direct affine substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(p=(A_B^{-1}b,0)\) and \(Z=\begin{bmatrix}-A_B^{-1}A_F\\ I\end{bmatrix}\), so every equality-feasible point is \(x=p+Zx_F\). Then \[q(p+Zx_F)=\tfrac12x_F^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)x_F+\bigl(Z^{\mathsf T}(Hp+g)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}x_F+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Hp+g^{\mathsf T}p.\] If \(H\succeq0\), then \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succeq0\); if \(H\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\setminus\{0\}\), then \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block elimination gives explicit reduced coefficients, preserves convexity, and converts positive curvature on feasible directions into a positive-definite reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_{\mathrm{red}}=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ,\qquad g_{\mathrm{red}}=Z^{\mathsf T}(Hp+g).

notation.meaning: particular feasible point obtained by setting free variables to zero
elimination matrix whose columns span the equality null space

children.title: Null-Space Reduced Forms
children.top_down_role: Reduced QP forms parameterized within the null space of equality constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Reduced Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space parameterization of a consistent finite-dimensional linear equality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have rank \(r\), let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and suppose \(x_p\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(Ax_p=b\). If \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-r)}\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\), every solution of \(Ax=b\) has a unique representation \(x=x_p+Zz\) with \(z\in\mathbb{R}^{n-r}\). Under this substitution,
\[
\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x
=\frac12z^{\mathsf T}Z^{\mathsf T}HZz+\bigl(Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_p+g)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}z+c,
\]
where \(c=x_p^{\mathsf T}Hx_p/2+g^{\mathsf T}x_p\). Thus \(H_r=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succeq0\), \(g_r=Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_p+g)\), and minimizers correspond through \(x=x_p+Zz\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point plus a null-space basis uniquely parameterizes all equality-feasible points and converts the objective into a lower-dimensional convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_r=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succeq0,\quad g_r=Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_p+g)

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of changing the null-space basis and feasible affine origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde Z=ZT\), where \(Z\) and \(\widetilde Z\) are bases of \(\ker A\) and \(T\) is nonsingular, and let \(\widetilde x_p=x_p+Za\). The coordinate relation is \(z=a+T\widetilde z\). Consequently,\[\widetilde H_r=T^{\mathsf T}H_rT,\qquad \widetilde g_r=T^{\mathsf T}(H_ra+g_r),\]and the constant becomes \(\widetilde c=c+g_r^{\mathsf T}a+\tfrac12a^{\mathsf T}H_ra\). Thus the reduced problems are identical under an invertible affine coordinate change; in particular, rank, inertia, semidefiniteness, and definiteness of the reduced Hessian are basis invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing the null-space basis and feasible origin applies an invertible affine change to reduced coordinates and preserves all intrinsic curvature and optimization properties.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z=a+T\widetilde z,\quad \widetilde H_r=T^{\mathsf T}H_rT,\quad \widetilde g_r=T^{\mathsf T}(H_ra+g_r)

notation.meaning: displacement between feasible origins in the original null-space coordinates

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Invariance of Null-Space Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality classification of the convex quadratic obtained in null-space coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\phi(z)=\tfrac12z^{\mathsf T}H_rz+g_r^{\mathsf T}z+c\) with \(H_r\succeq0\), the following are equivalent: \(\inf_z\phi(z)>-\infty\), \(\phi\) attains its minimum, \(g_r\in\operatorname{range}(H_r)\), and \(g_r\perp\ker H_r\). In this case\[\operatorname*{argmin}\phi=\{-H_r^\dagger g_r+v:v\in\ker H_r\},\]and the minimizer is unique exactly when \(H_r\succ0\). If \(g_r\notin\operatorname{range}(H_r)\), then \(\inf_z\phi(z)=-\infty\). These conclusions transfer through \(x=x_p+Zz\) to the equality-constrained QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite reduced QP is solvable exactly when its linear term lies in the reduced-Hessian range; positive definiteness gives uniqueness, while a linear component along its kernel gives unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g_r\in\operatorname{range}(H_r)\iff\operatorname*{argmin}\phi\ne\varnothing,\qquad H_r\succ0\iff |\operatorname*{argmin}\phi|=1

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the reduced Hessian

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-QP Solvability and Uniqueness

children.title: Rank-Deficient Equality Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural treatment of redundant or rank-deficient affine equality systems.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ax=b\text{ is feasible}\iff b\in\operatorname{range}(A)

notation.meaning: basis matrix for the kernel of A

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistent and inconsistent regimes without a full-row-rank assumption.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A rank-deficient equality system \(Ax=b\) is feasible if and only if \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\), equivalently \(y^{\mathsf T}b=0\) for every \(y\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\). If it is feasible, choose any \(x_p\) satisfying \(Ax_p=b\) and any full-column-rank \(Z\) with \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\). Then
\[
\{x:Ax=b\}=\{x_p+Zz:z\in\mathbb{R}^{n-r}\}.
\]
If the consistency condition fails, the associated equality-constrained QP is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank deficiency is harmless when the right-hand side lies in the matrix range; otherwise the equality-constrained QP is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Equality Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Removal of redundant equality rows without changing the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(r\), and let \(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\operatorname{range}(A)\). Define \(\bar A=U^{\mathsf T}A\) and \(\bar b=U^{\mathsf T}b\). Then \(\bar A\) has full row rank and, whenever \((I-UU^{\mathsf T})b=0\),\[Ax=b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bar Ax=\bar b.\]If the consistency condition fails, \(Ax=b\) is infeasible. Thus a consistent rank-deficient equality block can be replaced exactly by \(r\) independent equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting a consistent equality system onto coordinates for its column space removes redundant rows and produces an equivalent full-row-rank system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (I-UU^{\mathsf T})b=0\Longrightarrow\bigl(Ax=b\iff U^{\mathsf T}Ax=U^{\mathsf T}b\bigr),\quad \operatorname{rank}(U^{\mathsf T}A)=r

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis matrix for the column space of A

knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Row Compression of Consistent Equalities

children.title: Slack-Variable Lifts
children.top_down_role: QP lifts that expose inequality residuals through auxiliary slack variables.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Gx\le h\iff \exists s\in\mathbb{R}_+^p:\ Gx+s=h
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equality lift of componentwise affine inequalities.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The affine inequality system \(Gx\le h\) has the exact lifted representation
\[
Gx+s=h,\qquad s\in\mathbb{R}_+^p.
\]
For every feasible \(x\), the slack is uniquely determined by \(s=h-Gx\); conversely, every lifted feasible pair projects to an \(x\) satisfying \(Gx\le h\). If the original objective is \(q(x)\), assigning the lifted objective \(q(x)\) preserves all objective values and the projected minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each affine inequality is equivalent to an equality with a uniquely determined nonnegative slack, preserving projected feasible points and minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Variable Lifts

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

children.title: Split-Variable Lifts
children.top_down_role: QP lifts that replace signed quantities with structured auxiliary components.

knowledge_statements.title: Split-Variable Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative-variable lift of an unrestricted finite-dimensional vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Hx/2+g^{\mathsf T}x+c\). Every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) can be represented as \(x=x^+-x^-\) with \(x^+,x^-\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\). With \(u=(x^+,x^-)\in\mathbb{R}_+^{2n}\) and \(T=[I\ -I]\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times2n}\), substitution gives
\[
q(Tu)=\frac12u^{\mathsf T}T^{\mathsf T}HTu+(T^{\mathsf T}g)^{\mathsf T}u+c.
\]
Constraints are transformed by replacing \(x\) with \(Tu\). Projection by \(x=Tu\) preserves feasibility and objective values, although the lifted representation of a fixed \(x\) is generally nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unrestricted variable is the difference of two nonnegative variables; substituting this split gives an equivalent, generally nonunique, lifted QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x=x^+-x^-=Tu,\quad T=[I\ -I],\quad u=(x^+,x^-)\in\mathbb{R}_+^{2n}

notation.meaning: projection from lifted variables to the original variable

children.title: Epigraph Lifts
children.top_down_role: QP lifts that represent compatible objective or penalty pieces through epigraph variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective epigraph lift; the direct lifted model is generally a convex QCQP rather than a linearly constrained QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and let \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Hx/2+g^{\mathsf T}x+c\), where \(H\in\mathbb{S}_+^n\), \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}\). Then
\[
\inf_{x\in C}q(x)=\inf_{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}}\{t:x\in C,\ q(x)\le t\}.
\]
Whenever an optimum is attained in the lifted problem, every optimal pair satisfies \(t=q(x)\); hence optimal values and optimal \(x\)-coordinates agree with the original problem. Because \(H\succeq0\), the epigraph inequality is convex. Unless it has an additional linear or conic representation, the direct lift is a convex quadratically constrained quadratic program rather than a linearly constrained QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a convex quadratic equals minimizing an upper-bound variable over its epigraph, though the direct lift is generally a convex QCQP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\in C}q(x)=\inf_{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}}\{t:x\in C,\ q(x)\le t\}

notation.meaning: epigraph variable bounding the objective value

source_refs.locator: 9.2 Problems with General Convex Constraints p. 188

source_witnesses.locator: 9.2 Problems with General Convex Constraints p. 188

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Epigraph Lift of a Piecewise-Affine Term
knowledge_statements.scope_note: QP-preserving epigraph lift for a finite maximum of affine functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x+c\) with \(H\succeq0\), let \(C\) be polyhedral, and let \(p(x)=\max_{1\le i\le k}(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+b_i)\). Then\[\inf_{x\in C}\{q(x)+p(x)\}=\inf_{x,t}\left\{q(x)+t:x\in C,\ a_i^{\mathsf T}x+b_i\le t\ (i=1,\ldots,k)\right\}.\]At every lifted optimum, \(t=p(x)\). The lifted problem remains a linearly constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite maximum of affine objective terms is replaced exactly by one epigraph variable and affine upper-bound constraints, preserving the convex-QP class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(x)\le t\iff a_i^{\mathsf T}x+b_i\le t\quad(i=1,\ldots,k)
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Epigraph Lift of a Piecewise-Affine Term

children.title: Variable Scaling Forms
children.top_down_role: Equivalent QP forms produced by rescaling primal decision coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Scaling Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertible diagonal change of decision coordinates in a finite-dimensional QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular and diagonal, and substitute \(x=Dz\) into \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Hx/2+g^{\mathsf T}x+c\). Then
\[
q(Dz)=\frac12z^{\mathsf T}D^{\mathsf T}HDz+(D^{\mathsf T}g)^{\mathsf T}z+c.
\]
Thus \(H_D=D^{\mathsf T}HD\) and \(g_D=D^{\mathsf T}g\). For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb{R}^p\), equalities \(Ax=b\) become \(ADz=b\), and inequalities \(Gx\le h\) become \(GDz\le h\). The bijection \(z\mapsto Dz\) preserves feasibility, objective values, convexity, and corresponding minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular diagonal variable substitution congruently scales the Hessian and right-scales constraint matrices while preserving the optimization problem exactly.
assumptions_latex: D\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\text{ is nonsingular and diagonal}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_D=D^{\mathsf T}HD,\quad g_D=D^{\mathsf T}g

children.title: Constraint Equilibration Forms
children.top_down_role: Equivalent forms that balance constraint rows or constraint blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Equilibration Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving row transformations for linear constraints in a finite-dimensional QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). If \(R\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular, then
\[
Ax=b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad RAx=Rb.
\]
If \(S=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_p)\) with \(s_i>0\), then
\[
Gx\le h\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad SGx\le Sh.
\]
Therefore these row transformations leave the feasible set and any unchanged objective exactly the same. A general nonsingular, nondiagonal premultiplier is not valid for componentwise inequalities because it need not preserve the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible row transformations preserve equalities, while positive diagonal row scaling preserves componentwise inequalities and hence the QP feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ax=b\iff RAx=Rb,\qquad Gx\le h\iff SGx\le Sh

source_refs.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation of KKT multipliers under feasibility-preserving row transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider constraints \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), using the Lagrangian convention \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)+\mu^{\mathsf T}(Gx-h)\) with \(\mu\ge0\). For the transformed constraints \(R(Ax-b)=0\) and \(S(Gx-h)\le0\), where \(R\) is nonsingular and \(S\) is positive diagonal, define\[\widehat\lambda=R^{-\mathsf T}\lambda,\qquad \widehat\mu=S^{-1}\mu.\]Then stationarity terms, multiplier signs, and componentwise complementarity agree under this bijection. Thus complete KKT tuples correspond between the original and transformed formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint row transformations preserve KKT tuples when equality and inequality multipliers are transformed by the inverse transpose and inverse positive diagonal scalings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\lambda=R^{-\mathsf T}\lambda,\qquad \widehat\mu=S^{-1}\mu

notation.meaning: multipliers for the transformed equality and inequality rows

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Correspondence Under Constraint Scaling

children.title: Scaling Quality Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem structures where scaling materially changes numerical balance or has limited benefit.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Quality Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies diagonal congruence scalings by their relative spectral conditioning of a nonsingular QP system matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular and let \(D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be diagonal with strictly positive diagonal entries. Define \(K_D=DKD\), \(q(D)=\kappa_2(K_D)\), and \(\rho(D)=q(D)/q(I)\). For prescribed thresholds \(0<\alpha<1<\beta\), the scaling is improving when \(\rho(D)\leq\alpha\), neutral when \(\alpha<\rho(D)<\beta\), and degrading when \(\rho(D)\geq\beta\). These regimes compare conditioning only; they do not change the solution represented by the consistently scaled linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive diagonal scaling is improving, neutral, or degrading according to how much it decreases or increases the system’s spectral condition number relative to no scaling.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is diagonal with strictly positive entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(D)\leq\alpha\), \(\alpha<\rho(D)<\beta\), and \(\rho(D)\geq\beta\) define the improving, neutral, and degrading regimes, respectively.

notation.meaning: Condition-number ratio relative to the unscaled matrix.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive diagonal congruence scaling and spectral condition-number comparison are standard numerical linear algebra conventions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but the particular threshold-based regime terminology and the solution-equivalence qualification lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Sparsity-Preserving QP Forms
children.top_down_role: Equivalent formulations retaining local variables, constraints, or block sparsity.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity-Preserving QP Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted convex QP form retaining auxiliary variables and the sparse affine relations that define them.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(z\in\mathbb R^p\), a sparsity-preserving lifted QP has the form
\[\min_{x,z}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+h^{\mathsf T}x+\tfrac12z^{\mathsf T}Rz+r^{\mathsf T}z\]
subject to \(z=Fx+f\), \(Ax+Bz=b\), and \(Cx+Dz\leq d\), where \(H\succeq0\) and \(R\succeq0\). Retaining \(z\) exposes the nonzero patterns of \(H,R,F,A,B,C,D\). Its feasible points project exactly onto the feasible \(x\)-points obtained by substituting \(z=Fx+f\), and corresponding points have the same objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted QP keeps auxiliary variables and sparse affine linking equations; eliminating those variables yields an equivalent projected problem but may create dense coefficients.
assumptions_latex: All displayed matrices and vectors have compatible finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted and substituted formulations have identical feasible \(x\)-projections and identical objective values under \(z=Fx+f\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: retaining affine-linked auxiliary variables is the standard lifted formulation of a structured convex QP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lifted representation and projection claim are mathematically coherent, but no inspectable citation supports this exact sparsity-preserving formulation.

children.title: Fully Condensed QP Forms
children.top_down_role: Reduced formulations eliminating intermediate variables at the cost of denser coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Fully Condensed QP Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact elimination of all affine-defined auxiliary variables from a lifted convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the lifted QP with objective \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+h^{\mathsf T}x+\tfrac12z^{\mathsf T}Rz+r^{\mathsf T}z\), constraints \(z=Fx+f\), \(Ax+Bz=b\), and \(Cx+Dz\leq d\). Substitution gives the fully condensed QP
\[\min_x\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}(H+F^{\mathsf T}RF)x+\bigl(h+F^{\mathsf T}(Rf+r)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}x\]
subject to \((A+BF)x=b-Bf\) and \((C+DF)x\leq d-Df\), up to an objective constant. The two formulations have corresponding feasible points \(z=Fx+f\) and the same minimizers in \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full condensation substitutes every affine-defined auxiliary variable, reducing dimension while potentially making the Hessian and constraint matrices denser.
assumptions_latex: All displayed matrices and vectors have compatible finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The condensed Hessian is \(H+F^{\mathsf T}RF\succeq0\), and the condensed problem has the same minimizing \(x\)-vectors as the lifted problem.

notation.meaning: Hessian contribution created by eliminating the auxiliary vector.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: affine substitution and the displayed quadratic expansion are direct standard QP reformulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condensation formulas and representation kind fit the leaf, but the record supplies no source with a specific locator.

children.title: Partial Condensation Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Intermediate reduction regimes balancing dimension against retained sparsity.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Condensation Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intermediate elimination regime between fully lifted and fully condensed structured QP formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(z=(z_E,z_R)\), suppose \(z_E=F_Ex+f_E\), and retain \(z_R\) in a convex lifted QP. Eliminating only \(z_E\) produces a QP in \((x,z_R)\) with the same feasible projection and objective values under the substitution. If the eliminated objective block is \(\tfrac12z_E^{\mathsf T}R_Ez_E+r_E^{\mathsf T}z_E\), its contribution to the reduced Hessian is \(F_E^{\mathsf T}R_EF_E\). Thus partial condensation removes \(\dim z_E\) variables and their defining equalities, but it may introduce fill in the reduced Hessian and in every constraint containing \(z_E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial condensation eliminates selected auxiliary variables. It reduces the number of variables and defining equalities but may introduce fill in the reduced Hessian and affected constraints.
assumptions_latex: The eliminated variables satisfy the exact affine identity \(z_E=F_Ex+f_E\).
All data have compatible finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Partial elimination preserves optimization equivalence while trading fewer variables and equalities against possible coefficient fill from \(F_E^{\mathsf T}R_EF_E\).

notation.meaning: Auxiliary variables retained in the reduced QP.
Reduced-Hessian contribution from the eliminated objective block.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: blockwise affine elimination gives the stated dimension and possible-fill tradeoff

children.title: Equality-Constrained Least Squares
children.top_down_role: Least-squares QPs subject solely to affine equality restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained Least Squares
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical convex QP representation of linear least squares with affine equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), equality-constrained least squares is
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12\lVert Mx-y\rVert_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b.\]
After discarding the constant \(\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}y\), this is the convex QP with Hessian \(M^{\mathsf T}M\succeq0\), linear coefficient \(-M^{\mathsf T}y\), and equality constraint \(Ax=b\). If the affine constraint set is nonempty, both formulations have exactly the same minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality-constrained least squares minimizes a squared residual over an affine set and is a convex QP with Hessian equal to the Gram matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(M,A,y,b\) have the displayed compatible finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax=b}\tfrac12\lVert Mx-y\rVert_2^2=\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax=b}\bigl(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}M^{\mathsf T}Mx-y^{\mathsf T}Mx\bigr)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient optimality certificate without rank assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible \(x^*\) solves \(\min\{\tfrac12\|Mx-y\|_2^2:Ax=b\}\) if and only if some \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\) satisfies \[M^{\mathsf T}(Mx^*-y)+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0,\qquad Ax^*=b.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility and an equality multiplier making the residual gradient orthogonal to all feasible directions exactly certify optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is optimal if and only if the displayed system has a multiplier \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained Normal-Equation Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution-set geometry for feasible equality-constrained least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x:Ax=b\}\neq\varnothing\). The affine set \(MF\) is closed, so \(z^*=\operatorname{proj}_{MF}(y)\) exists uniquely, and \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}\|Mx-y\|_2^2=F\cap M^{-1}(z^*)\neq\varnothing.\] The coefficient minimizer is unique if and only if \(\ker M\cap\ker A=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum is attained and the fitted value is unique; the coefficient is unique exactly when no nonzero feasible direction lies in the design null space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}\|Mx-y\|^2=F\cap M^{-1}(z^*)\), uniquely iff \(\ker M\cap\ker A=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Projection of the target onto the attainable fitted-value affine set.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection, Existence, and Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the model, feasibility, and global optimality. The extract's large-penalty discussion is informal and does not establish a convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), and \(d\in\mathbb{R}^p\), the equality-constrained least-squares problem is
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\ \|Ax-b\|_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad Cx=d.
\]
A vector \(x\) is feasible if \(Cx=d\). A vector \(\widehat x\) is optimal if it is feasible and \(\|A\widehat x-b\|_2^2\leq\|Ax-b\|_2^2\) for every feasible \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality-constrained least squares minimizes a squared linear residual subject to linear equations. A point is feasible when it satisfies those equations and optimal when no feasible point has a smaller objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat x\text{ is optimal}\iff C\widehat x=d\ \text{and}\ \forall x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ Cx=d\Rightarrow\|A\widehat x-b\|_2^2\leq\|Ax-b\|_2^2.
