children.title: Polyhedrally Constrained Least Squares
children.top_down_role: Least-squares QPs over general polyhedral feasible regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedrally Constrained Least Squares
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex least-squares QP over a polyhedron described by finitely many linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), and \(d\in\mathbb R^q\), polyhedrally constrained least squares is
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12\lVert Mx-y\rVert_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad Cx\leq d.\]
It is the convex QP with Hessian \(M^{\mathsf T}M\succeq0\), linear coefficient \(-M^{\mathsf T}y\), and polyhedral feasible set \(P=\{x:Cx\leq d\}\). The least-squares and QP objectives differ only by the constant \(\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}y\), so their minimizer sets over \(P\) coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyhedrally constrained least squares is a convex quadratic program obtained by minimizing a squared linear residual subject to finitely many linear inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(M,C,y,d\) have the displayed compatible finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}\tfrac12\lVert Mx-y\rVert_2^2=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}\bigl(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}M^{\mathsf T}Mx-y^{\mathsf T}Mx\bigr)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact multiplier certificate for affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible \(x^*\) minimizes \(\tfrac12\|Mx-y\|_2^2\) over \(Cx\leq d\) if and only if some \(\mu\geq0\) satisfies \[M^{\mathsf T}(Mx^*-y)+C^{\mathsf T}\mu=0,\qquad \mu_i(C_ix^*-d_i)=0\quad\forall i.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility, stationarity, nonnegative multipliers, and complementary slackness exactly certify optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is optimal if and only if such a multiplier \(\mu\) exists.

notation.meaning: Row i of the inequality matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Least-Squares KKT Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection characterization over a nonempty inequality-described polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x:Cx\leq d\}\neq\varnothing\), the image \(MP\) is a closed convex polyhedron. Hence \(z^*=\operatorname{proj}_{MP}(y)\) exists uniquely and \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}\|Mx-y\|_2^2=P\cap M^{-1}(z^*)\neq\varnothing.\] The coefficient minimizer is unique exactly when this fiber is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least squares over a nonempty polyhedron attains its minimum and has a unique fitted value; coefficient uniqueness is singletonness of the optimal fiber.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}\|Mx-y\|^2=P\cap M^{-1}(z^*)\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Projection onto the attainable fitted-value polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Attainment and Solution Fiber

children.title: Mixed Affine-Constraint Least Squares
children.top_down_role: Least-squares templates combining equality restrictions with polyhedral inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Affine-Constraint Least Squares
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-squares QP combining affine equalities and linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), and \(d\in\mathbb R^q\), mixed affine-constraint least squares is
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12\lVert Mx-y\rVert_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\quad Cx\leq d.\]
Equivalently, after removing the constant \(\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}y\), minimize \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}M^{\mathsf T}Mx-y^{\mathsf T}Mx\) over the same feasible set. This is a convex QP because \(M^{\mathsf T}M\succeq0\); the equality and inequality constraints define a polyhedron, and the two objectives have identical minimizers on it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed affine-constraint least squares combines linear equalities and inequalities with a squared residual objective, giving a standard convex QP.
assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), and \(d\in\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The least-squares model and its expanded convex QP have the same feasible set and the same minimizers.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Affine Sets p. 3; 1.2 Convex Sets p. 5

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 Affine Sets p. 3; 1.2 Convex Sets p. 5

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality conditions for equality-and-inequality constrained least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A point \(x^*\) is optimal if and only if there are \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^q\) such that \[Ax^*=b,\quad Cx^*\leq d,\quad M^{\mathsf T}(Mx^*-y)+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda+C^{\mathsf T}\mu=0,\quad \mu_i(C_ix^*-d_i)=0\ \forall i.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility, multiplier signs, stationarity, and complementary slackness exactly certify optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is optimal if and only if the displayed KKT system is feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Affine KKT Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution-set geometry over a nonempty mixed affine polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ Cx\leq d\}\neq\varnothing\), the image \(MP\) is a closed convex polyhedron. Thus \(z^*=\operatorname{proj}_{MP}(y)\) exists uniquely and \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}\|Mx-y\|_2^2=P\cap M^{-1}(z^*)\neq\varnothing.\] The coefficient minimizer is unique exactly when this fiber is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible mixed affine least-squares problem attains its minimum and has a unique fitted value; coefficient uniqueness is singletonness of the optimal fiber.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}\|Mx-y\|^2=P\cap M^{-1}(z^*)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Attainment and Fitted-Value Geometry

children.title: Bounded Least Squares
children.top_down_role: Least-squares QPs with finite lower or upper bounds on decision variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Least Squares
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-squares QP with componentwise lower and upper bounds on every decision variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and bounds \(\ell,u\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\ell\leq u\), bounded least squares is
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12\lVert Mx-y\rVert_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad \ell\leq x\leq u.\]
Its expanded QP objective is \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}M^{\mathsf T}Mx-y^{\mathsf T}Mx\), up to the constant \(\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}y\). The feasible set is the nonempty box \([\ell,u]\), so the two formulations have identical minimizers; the box is compact when all bounds are finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded least squares minimizes a squared residual over a componentwise box and is a convex QP with simple bound constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bounded least-squares and expanded QP formulations have identical minimizers over \([\ell,u]\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical active-set specialization for finite box constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bounded-variable least-squares active-set method partitions variables into lower-active, upper-active, and free sets. It solves least squares on the free variables, truncates an infeasible trial at the first encountered bound, and releases an active variable whose bound-gradient sign violates optimality. It stops when the bound KKT conditions hold. Under exact arithmetic and deterministic anti-cycling and degeneracy handling, it terminates after finitely many active-set changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BVLS alternates free-variable least-squares solves with bound activation or release until the exact bound optimality signs hold.
assumptions_latex: Ties and degeneracy are handled by a deterministic anti-cycling rule.
The finite-termination claim uses exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination at the bound KKT conditions returns a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Variable Least-Squares Active-Set Method

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lower-and-upper-bound optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g=M^{\mathsf T}(Mx-y)\). A feasible \(x^*\) is optimal if and only if there are \(\alpha,\beta\geq0\) such that \[g(x^*)-\alpha+\beta=0,\quad \alpha_i(x_i^*-\ell_i)=0,\quad \beta_i(u_i-x_i^*)=0.\] For \(\ell_i<u_i\), equivalently \(g_i=0\) in the interior, \(g_i\geq0\) at a lower bound, and \(g_i\leq0\) at an upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gradient vanishes on free coordinates and points inward at active lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is optimal iff \(0\in M^{\mathsf T}(Mx^*-y)+N_{[\ell,u]}(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Least-Squares Complementarity Conditions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and Fitted-Value Uniqueness on a Box
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution geometry for finite componentwise bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite \(\ell\leq u\), \(B=[\ell,u]\) is compact. Thus a minimizer exists, \(z^*=\operatorname{proj}_{MB}(y)\) is unique, and \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in B}\|Mx-y\|_2^2=B\cap M^{-1}(z^*).\] The coefficient minimizer is unique exactly when this fiber is a singleton; full column rank of \(M\) is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite bounds ensure existence and a unique fitted value; coefficient uniqueness is determined by the optimal box fiber.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in B}\|Mx-y\|^2=B\cap M^{-1}(z^*)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Existence and Fitted-Value Uniqueness on a Box

children.title: Nonnegative Least Squares
children.top_down_role: Least-squares QPs restricted to nonnegative decision vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative Least Squares
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical least-squares QP over the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), nonnegative least squares is
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12\lVert Mx-y\rVert_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\geq0.\]
Expanding the square gives the equivalent convex QP \(\min_{x\geq0}\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}M^{\mathsf T}Mx-y^{\mathsf T}Mx\), since the omitted term \(\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}y\) is constant. The Hessian \(M^{\mathsf T}M\) is positive semidefinite, and both formulations have exactly the same minimizer set in the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative least squares minimizes a squared linear residual with every decision variable constrained to be nonnegative; its expansion is a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\geq0}\tfrac12\lVert Mx-y\rVert_2^2=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\geq0}\bigl(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}M^{\mathsf T}Mx-y^{\mathsf T}Mx\bigr)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical active-set algorithm for NNLS.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Lawson–Hanson method maintains a passive set \(P\) of variables allowed to be positive and an active set fixed at zero. It moves an index with a violated reduced-gradient condition into \(P\), solves least squares on \(M_P\), and, when the trial is not positive, steps toward it until a coefficient reaches zero and returns such indices to the active set. It stops when all inactive reduced gradients satisfy the NNLS KKT sign. With exact arithmetic and anti-cycling tie and degeneracy handling, it terminates after finitely many active-set changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lawson–Hanson alternates passive-set least-squares solves and feasibility-restoring steps until NNLS complementarity holds.
assumptions_latex: Tie and degeneracy handling prevent cycling.
The finite-termination claim uses exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination the iterate satisfies the NNLS KKT certificate and is globally optimal.

notation.meaning: Passive set of variables currently allowed to be positive.

knowledge_statements.title: Lawson–Hanson Active-Set Method

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent coordinate and residual certificates for global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r=y-Mx\), a vector \(x^*\geq0\) solves NNLS if and only if \[M^{\mathsf T}(Mx^*-y)\geq0,\qquad x_i^*[M^{\mathsf T}(Mx^*-y)]_i=0\quad\forall i.\] Equivalently, \(M^{\mathsf T}r^*\leq0\) and \(\langle Mx^*,r^*\rangle=0\): the residual lies in the polar cone of \(M\mathbb R_+^n\) and is orthogonal to the fitted value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative reduced gradients and complementarity, equivalently polar-cone residual membership and orthogonality, certify NNLS optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is optimal iff \(x^*\geq0\), \(M^{\mathsf T}(Mx^*-y)\geq0\), and \(x^*\odot M^{\mathsf T}(Mx^*-y)=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: NNLS KKT and Polar-Cone Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric characterization of fitted values and coefficient solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=M\mathbb R_+^n=\operatorname{cone}(M_1,\ldots,M_n)\). This finitely generated cone is closed and convex. Therefore \(z^*=\operatorname{proj}_K(y)\) exists uniquely and \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\geq0}\|Mx-y\|_2^2=\{x\geq0:Mx=z^*\}\neq\varnothing.\] The coefficient minimizer is unique exactly when this nonnegative fiber is a singleton; full column rank is sufficient but not necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: NNLS is projection onto the cone generated by the design columns; the fitted value is unique although its nonnegative coefficients may not be.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^*=\operatorname{proj}_{M\mathbb R_+^n}(y)\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}=\mathbb R_+^n\cap M^{-1}(z^*)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Projection and NNLS Existence

children.title: Mixed Sign-Restricted Least Squares
children.top_down_role: Least-squares QPs combining free, bounded, and sign-restricted variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Sign-Restricted Least Squares
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-squares QP with disjoint nonnegative, nonpositive, and unrestricted variable groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I_+,I_-,I_0\) partition \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Mixed sign-restricted least squares is
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12\lVert Mx-y\rVert_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i\geq0\ (i\in I_+),\quad x_i\leq0\ (i\in I_-),\]
with \(x_i\) unrestricted for \(i\in I_0\). Expanding the objective yields the equivalent convex QP with Hessian \(M^{\mathsf T}M\succeq0\) and linear coefficient \(-M^{\mathsf T}y\). The sign restrictions define a closed convex polyhedral cone, and the expanded and residual formulations have identical minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed sign-restricted least squares assigns variables to nonnegative, nonpositive, or free groups and expands directly into a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual and expanded quadratic objectives have the same minimizers over the mixed-sign polyhedral cone.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise necessary and sufficient optimality conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g=M^{\mathsf T}(Mx-y)\). A mixed-sign feasible \(x^*\) is optimal if and only if \[g_i=0\ (i\in I_0),\qquad g_i\geq0,\ x_i^*g_i=0\ (i\in I_+),\qquad g_i\leq0,\ x_i^*g_i=0\ (i\in I_-).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual gradient vanishes on free variables and has complementary one-sided signs on constrained variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\) is optimal iff \(0\in M^{\mathsf T}(Mx^*-y)+N_K(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Sign Gradient Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction to nonnegative coordinates and its redundancy boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i\in I_-\), set \(z_i=-x_i\geq0\). For \(i\in I_0\), set \(x_i=z_i^+-z_i^-\) with \(z_i^+,z_i^-\geq0\). This converts the model to NNLS with an expanded design matrix. Sign flips are injective, but the free-variable split is not: \((z_i^+,z_i^-)\) and \((z_i^++t,z_i^-+t)\) represent the same \(x_i\) for every \(t\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sign flips normalize nonpositive variables, while splitting free variables gives an equivalent but coefficient-redundant NNLS formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{I_-}=-z_{I_-}\) and \(x_{I_0}=z_{I_0}^+-z_{I_0}^-\) reduce the model to nonnegative coordinates.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative parts representing a free variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Sign Normalization and Free-Variable Splitting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection geometry and coefficient-uniqueness boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the mixed-sign polyhedral cone \(K\), the image \(MK\) is a closed convex polyhedral cone. Hence \(z^*=\operatorname{proj}_{MK}(y)\) exists uniquely and \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}\|Mx-y\|_2^2=K\cap M^{-1}(z^*)\neq\varnothing.\] The coefficient minimizer is unique exactly when this fiber is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-sign least squares always attains its minimum and has one fitted value; coefficient uniqueness depends on its cone fiber.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is defined by the seed's mixed sign restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}\|Mx-y\|^2=K\cap M^{-1}(z^*)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Attainment over the Mixed-Sign Cone

children.title: Diagonally Weighted Least Squares
children.top_down_role: Least-squares templates with independent residual weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonally Weighted Least Squares
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-squares QP using nonnegative scalar weights on individual residual components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_1,\ldots,w_m)\) with \(w_i\geq0\), diagonally weighted least squares is
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12(Mx-y)^{\mathsf T}W(Mx-y)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^m w_i(m_i^{\mathsf T}x-y_i)^2.\]
Up to the constant \(\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}Wy\), its QP Hessian is \(M^{\mathsf T}WM\succeq0\) and its linear coefficient is \(-M^{\mathsf T}Wy\). Positive weights penalize residual components, while zero weights omit them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal weighted least squares assigns a nonnegative scalar weight to each residual component and produces a convex QP with a weighted Gram Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The QP representation has Hessian \(M^{\mathsf T}WM\succeq0\) and linear coefficient \(-M^{\mathsf T}Wy\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality and uniqueness for unconstrained diagonally weighted least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_i)\succeq0\), \(x^\star\) minimizes \(\tfrac12\|W^{1/2}(Mx-y)\|_2^2\) if and only if \(M^{\mathsf T}W(Mx^\star-y)=0\). The minimizer is unique if and only if \(\ker(W^{1/2}M)=\{0\}\), equivalently \(M^{\mathsf T}WM\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted normal equations are necessary and sufficient, and uniqueness holds exactly when the positively weighted rows have full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\tfrac12\|W^{1/2}(Mx-y)\|_2^2\iff M^{\mathsf T}W(Mx^\star-y)=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal-Weight Normal Equations and Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary of the convex diagonal-weight template.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A zero weight deletes its residual component and may cause nonuniqueness. Negative weights do not generally preserve convexity: with \(M=[1]\), \(y=0\), and \(W=[-1]\), the objective is \(-x^2/2\), which is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero weights omit observations; negative weights can make the quadratic nonconvex and unbounded.
assumptions_latex: Diagonal weights are allowed to equal or cross zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w_i=0\text{ omits residual }i,\qquad w_i<0\text{ does not generally yield a convex QP}.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero and Negative Weight Boundaries

children.title: Full-Metric Weighted Least Squares
children.top_down_role: Least-squares templates with coupled residual weighting.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Metric Weighted Least Squares
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-squares QP measured by a general positive-semidefinite residual metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and a symmetric matrix \(W\in\mathbb S_+^m\), full-metric weighted least squares is
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12(Mx-y)^{\mathsf T}W(Mx-y).\]
Equivalently, for any factor \(L\) satisfying \(W=L^{\mathsf T}L\), it minimizes \(\tfrac12\lVert L(Mx-y)\rVert_2^2\). Its QP Hessian is \(M^{\mathsf T}WM\succeq0\), its linear coefficient is \(-M^{\mathsf T}Wy\), and the omitted constant is \(\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}Wy\). Off-diagonal entries of \(W\) couple distinct residual components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-metric weighted least squares measures residuals with a positive-semidefinite matrix, allowing coupling between components while retaining a convex QP representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tfrac12(Mx-y)^{\mathsf T}W(Mx-y)=\tfrac12\lVert L(Mx-y)\rVert_2^2\), and the QP Hessian is \(M^{\mathsf T}WM\succeq0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality and uniqueness under a positive-semidefinite residual metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(W\in\mathbb S_+^m\), \(x^\star\) minimizes \(\tfrac12(Mx-y)^{\mathsf T}W(Mx-y)\) if and only if \(M^{\mathsf T}W(Mx^\star-y)=0\). The minimizer is unique if and only if \(\ker(W^{1/2}M)=\{0\}\), equivalently \(M^{\mathsf T}WM\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full-metric normal equations characterize all minimizers; uniqueness is equivalent to injectivity after metric factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\text{ is optimal}\iff M^{\mathsf T}W(Mx^\star-y)=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Metric Normal Equations and Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information loss caused by a singular residual metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(W\succeq0\) is singular, the objective is only a seminorm on residual space and ignores \(\ker W\). For \(M=I_2\), \(y=0\), and \(W=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\), every \((0,t)\) is optimal although \(M\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular metric ignores its nullspace and can destroy uniqueness even for a full-rank design.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ker W\ne\{0\}\text{ creates unpenalized residual directions and may cause nonuniqueness}.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Residual-Metric Boundary

children.title: Generalized Least Squares
children.top_down_role: Least-squares templates using structured covariance or precision information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the ordinary inverse-covariance formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conventional GLS formula requires \(\Sigma\succ0\). If \(\Sigma\succeq0\) is singular, \(\Sigma^{-1}\) is undefined. In a degenerate covariance model, replacing it only by \(\Sigma^\dagger\) omits the deterministic consistency condition \(P_{\ker\Sigma}(Ax-b)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singular covariance requires both pseudoinverse weighting and consistency in zero-variance directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Sigma\not\succ0\implies\text{the ordinary inverse-covariance GLS formula is incomplete}.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the covariance nullspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Covariance GLS Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical unconstrained generalized least-squares model with positive-definite covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\). Generalized least squares minimizes \(\tfrac12(Ax-b)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}(Ax-b)\). If \(L^{\mathsf T}L=\Sigma^{-1}\), this is ordinary least squares for the whitened system \(LAx\approx Lb\), with normal equation \(A^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}(Ax-b)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: GLS weights residuals by inverse covariance and is ordinary least squares after whitening.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_x\tfrac12(Ax-b)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}(Ax-b)=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\tfrac12\|L(Ax-b)\|_2^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Covariance and Whitened GLS Forms

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best linear unbiased estimation under known correlated-error covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(b=Ax_0+\varepsilon\), \(\mathbb E\varepsilon=0\), \(\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon)=\Sigma\succ0\), and \(A\) has full column rank. Then \(\widehat x=(A^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}A)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}b\) is linear and unbiased, has covariance \((A^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}A)^{-1}\), and has no larger covariance than any other linear unbiased estimator in the Loewner order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the correlated linear model, GLS is the best linear unbiased estimator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat x\text{ is BLUE},\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(\widehat x)=(A^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}A)^{-1}.
knowledge_statements.title: Gauss–Markov–Aitken Property
Generalized Least Squares
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional generalized least squares with a positive-definite covariance metric and optional polyhedral constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), let \(\Sigma\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^m\), and let \(X=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Fx\le g\}\) be nonempty. The generalized least-squares estimator is
\[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\frac12(Ax-b)^\top\Sigma^{-1}(Ax-b).\]
It is equivalently the convex quadratic program
\[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\frac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\right\},\qquad Q=A^\top\Sigma^{-1}A\succeq0,\quad c=-A^\top\Sigma^{-1}b,\]
where the omitted constant is \(\frac12b^\top\Sigma^{-1}b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized least squares is a convex QP obtained by measuring residuals in the inverse-covariance metric; expanding the weighted square gives its Hessian and linear term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=A^\top\Sigma^{-1}A\succeq0\), so the generalized least-squares model is a convex QP.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically correct and fits the Generalized Least Squares leaf, but the cited linear least-squares section does not specifically establish inverse-covariance weighting or the constrained GLS specialization. A directly supporting GLS locator is required.

children.title: Ridge QPs
children.top_down_role: Quadratically regularized fitting templates with isotropic coefficient shrinkage.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unconstrained Ridge Solution and Spectral Shrinkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form unconstrained ridge solution and singular-value filter factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=\mathbb R^n\) and \(\lambda>0\), \(x_\lambda=(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}b\). If \(A=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\) is a full singular value decomposition, then \[x_\lambda=V\operatorname{Diag}\!\left(\frac{\sigma_i}{\sigma_i^2+\lambda}\right)U^{\mathsf T}b,\] with zero entries for null directions. Moreover, \(\kappa_2(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda I)=(\sigma_{\max}^2+\lambda)/(\sigma_{\min}^2+\lambda)\), allowing \(\sigma_{\min}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unconstrained ridge solves shifted normal equations and attenuates small-singular-value directions while improving normal-matrix conditioning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solution and spectral filter have the displayed forms.

notation.meaning: singular values of A, including zeros as needed

knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Ridge Solution and Spectral Shrinkage

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and Uniqueness of Constrained Ridge Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment specific to positive isotropic ridge regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron and \(\lambda>0\). Then \(x\mapsto\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|x\|_2^2\) is coercive and strongly convex. Consequently, it has exactly one minimizer on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive ridge regularization makes every nonempty polyhedrally constrained ridge problem attain a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}(\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|x\|_2^2)\) is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence and Uniqueness of Constrained Ridge Solutions
Ridge QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ridge-regularized linear least squares with scalar isotropic quadratic regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(\lambda>0\), and let \(X=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Fx\le g\}\) be nonempty. The ridge problem
\[\min_{x\in X}\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2+\frac\lambda2\lVert x\rVert_2^2\]
is the convex QP
\[\min_{x\in X}\left\{\frac12x^\top(A^\top A+\lambda I)x-(A^\top b)^\top x\right\}.\]
Its Hessian satisfies \(A^\top A+\lambda I\succ0\); hence the objective is strongly convex and has at most one minimizer on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ridge regression adds an isotropic squared-norm penalty to least squares, producing a positive-definite QP Hessian and therefore a unique feasible minimizer when one exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^\top A+\lambda I\succ0\), and the ridge objective is strongly convex.

notation.meaning: identity matrix in the parameter space

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ridge QP expansion, positive-definite Hessian, and uniqueness statement are correct, and representation is the appropriate content kind. The cited ordinary least-squares section does not specifically support ridge regularization; an authoritative ridge or Tikhonov locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal-Equation and SVD Representations of Ridge Regression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Isotropically quadratically regularized linear regression, including the ordinary-least-squares boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f_\lambda(\beta)=\|y-X\beta\|_2^2+\lambda\|\beta\|_2^2\), assume \(\lambda\ge0\) and \(X^TX+\lambda I\) is invertible. Then the unique minimizer satisfies \((X^TX+\lambda I)\widehat\beta=X^Ty\) and \(\widehat\beta=(X^TX+\lambda I)^{-1}X^Ty\). If \(X=U_r\Sigma_rV_r^T\) is a compact SVD, then \(\widehat\beta=\sum_{j=1}^r\frac{\sigma_j}{\sigma_j^2+\lambda}(u_j^Ty)v_j\) and \(\widehat y=\sum_{j=1}^r\frac{\sigma_j^2}{\sigma_j^2+\lambda}(u_j^Ty)u_j\). Relative to the unregularized coefficient in a positive-singular-value direction, the shrinkage factor is \(\sigma_j^2/(\sigma_j^2+\lambda)\), so smaller singular values receive stronger relative shrinkage. Under the invertibility assumption, \(\lambda=0\) gives ordinary least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ridge regression adds an isotropic squared-norm penalty to linear least squares. Its SVD representation shows direction-dependent shrinkage, with stronger relative shrinkage in directions having smaller positive singular values. Zero regularization recovers ordinary least squares when the normal matrix is invertible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\beta=(X^TX+\lambda I)^{-1}X^Ty=\sum_{j=1}^r\frac{\sigma_j}{\sigma_j^2+\lambda}(u_j^Ty)v_j.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Equation and SVD Representations of Ridge Regression

children.title: Tikhonov QPs
children.top_down_role: Quadratically regularized fitting templates using a general regularization operator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent unconstrained formulations for one-operator Tikhonov regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda\ge0\), define \(\widehat A=\begin{bmatrix}A\\ \sqrt\lambda L\end{bmatrix}\) and \(\widehat b=\begin{bmatrix}b\\ \sqrt\lambda Lx_0\end{bmatrix}\). Then \[\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|L(x-x_0)\|_2^2=\tfrac12\|\widehat Ax-\widehat b\|_2^2.\] In the unconstrained case, \(x\) is a minimizer if and only if \[(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda L^{\mathsf T}L)x=A^{\mathsf T}b+\lambda L^{\mathsf T}Lx_0.\] The minimizer set is nonempty and equals any one solution plus \(\ker A\cap\ker(\sqrt\lambda L)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tikhonov regularization is augmented least squares; unconstrained minimizers solve its normal equations and differ only along the common nullspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented identity, normal equations, and minimizer-set characterization hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Least-Squares and Normal-Equation Forms
Tikhonov QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General matrix-valued Tikhonov regularization around a prescribed reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(L\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be polyhedral. The Tikhonov problem
\[\min_{x\in X}\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2+\frac\lambda2\lVert L(x-x_0)\rVert_2^2\]
is a convex QP with
\[Q=A^\top A+\lambda L^\top L\succeq0,\qquad c=-A^\top b-\lambda L^\top Lx_0.\]
For \(\lambda>0\), the objective is strictly convex exactly when \(\ker(A)\cap\ker(L)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tikhonov regularization penalizes a linear transformation of displacement from a reference point. Its QP Hessian combines the data and regularization Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=A^\top A+\lambda L^\top L\succeq0\); for \(\lambda>0\), \(Q\succ0\iff\ker(A)\cap\ker(L)=\{0\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The QP coefficients and the strict-convexity criterion for positive lambda are correct and fit the Tikhonov QPs leaf. The cited linear least-squares section does not specifically support matrix-valued Tikhonov regularization, so a direct source locator is required.

children.title: Structured Tikhonov Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regularization regimes shaped by anisotropic, block, or problem-specific operators.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient structural conditions for exact decomposition into independent blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(x=(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(q)})\). If \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_q\) and every residual row of \(A\) and every active \(L_j\) involves variables from only one block, then the structured objective is \(\sum_{k=1}^q q_k(x^{(k)})\), and \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\sum_kq_k(x^{(k)})=\prod_k\operatorname*{argmin}_{x^{(k)}\in X_k}q_k(x^{(k)}).\] Cross-block residuals generally destroy this decomposition, although exceptional algebraic cancellations may preserve it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block-local residual operators and a product feasible set make the structured problem decompose into independent block QPs.
assumptions_latex: Every data and active regularization residual is block-local
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The global minimizer set is the Cartesian product of the block minimizer sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Separable Structured Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stacked-Operator Form of Structured Tikhonov Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between finitely many weighted penalties and one augmented least-squares operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s\ge1\), \(\lambda_j\ge0\), \(L_j\in\mathbb R^{p_j\times n}\), \(r_j\in\mathbb R^{p_j}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Define \[\widetilde A=\begin{bmatrix}A\\ \sqrt{\lambda_1}L_1\\ \vdots\\ \sqrt{\lambda_s}L_s\end{bmatrix},\qquad \widetilde b=\begin{bmatrix}b\\ \sqrt{\lambda_1}r_1\\ \vdots\\ \sqrt{\lambda_s}r_s\end{bmatrix}.\] Then \(\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\tfrac12\sum_{j=1}^s\lambda_j\|L_jx-r_j\|_2^2=\tfrac12\|\widetilde Ax-\widetilde b\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite collection of weighted structured penalties stacks into one augmented least-squares system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structured objective equals \(\tfrac12\|\widetilde Ax-\widetilde b\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Stacked-Operator Form of Structured Tikhonov Regularization
Structured Tikhonov Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple structured quadratic regularizers with an exact strict-convexity criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), operators \(L_j\in\mathbb{R}^{p_j\times n}\), references \(r_j\in\mathbb{R}^{p_j}\), weights \(\lambda_j\ge0\), and a polyhedron \(X\), consider
\[\min_{x\in X}\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2+\frac12\sum_{j=1}^s\lambda_j\lVert L_jx-r_j\rVert_2^2.\]
This is a convex QP with
\[Q=A^\top A+\sum_{j=1}^s\lambda_jL_j^\top L_j,\qquad c=-A^\top b-\sum_{j=1}^s\lambda_jL_j^\top r_j.\]
Moreover, \(Q\succ0\) exactly when \(\ker(A)\cap\bigcap_{j:\lambda_j>0}\ker(L_j)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Several structured Tikhonov penalties combine by adding their Gram matrices. Strict convexity holds precisely when no nonzero direction is invisible to every active operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\succeq0\), with \(Q\succ0\iff\ker(A)\cap\bigcap_{j:\lambda_j>0}\ker(L_j)=\{0\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite sums of squared affine residuals expand into a positive-semidefinite QP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-sum QP representation and common-kernel criterion are correct, and representation fits the leaf. However, no cited source is supplied, and the statement does not explicitly introduce b, require a positive integer s, or state that X is a polyhedron in R^n. A sourced, fully quantified version is required.

children.title: Roughness-Penalty QPs
children.top_down_role: Quadratic regularization templates controlling variation or curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sign Boundary for the Roughness Weight
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity boundary for the derivative-penalty coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H(\lambda)=A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda R\) with \(R\succeq0\), every \(\lambda\geq0\) gives \(H(\lambda)\succeq0\). If \(\lambda<0\) and some \(d\) satisfies \(Ad=0\) and \(d^{\mathsf T}Rd>0\), then \(d^{\mathsf T}H(\lambda)d<0\), so the objective is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative roughness weights preserve convexity; a negative weight creates negative curvature along any rough direction invisible to the data term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda\geq0\) guarantees convexity, while the displayed direction certifies nonconvexity for \(\lambda<0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sign Boundary for the Roughness Weight

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null directions and uniqueness in derivative-penalized least-squares QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a<b\), \(r\geq0\), \(f_x=\sum_{j=1}^n x_j\phi_j\), and \(R_{ij}=\int_a^b\phi_i^{(r)}(t)\phi_j^{(r)}(t)\,dt\). Then \(x\in\ker R\) if and only if \(f_x^{(r)}=0\) almost everywhere. For \(\lambda>0\), \[\ker(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda R)=\ker A\cap\ker R.\] Thus the unconstrained Hessian is positive definite exactly when the observations identify every roughness-null direction. On a convex feasible set \(X\), strict convexity holds exactly when \(\ker(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda R)\cap(X-X)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The penalty vanishes precisely on basis combinations having zero penalized derivative. Strict convexity requires the data term to identify every such feasible direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda R)=\ker A\cap\ker R\), with the stated strict-convexity test.
knowledge_statements.title: Roughness Nullspace and Strict Convexity
Roughness-Penalty QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic roughness penalties induced by squared derivatives of a basis expansion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_x(t)=\sum_{j=1}^n x_j\phi_j(t)\), where each basis function has a square-integrable derivative of order \(r\) on \([a,b]\). Define
\[R_{ij}=\int_a^b\phi_i^{(r)}(t)\phi_j^{(r)}(t)\,dt.\]
Then \(R\succeq0\) and
\[\int_a^b\lvert f_x^{(r)}(t)\rvert^2\,dt=x^\top Rx.\]
Consequently, for \(\lambda\ge0\) and a polyhedron \(X\), smoothing by
\[\min_{x\in X}\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2+\frac\lambda2x^\top Rx\]
is a convex QP with Hessian \(A^\top A+\lambda R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A squared-derivative roughness penalty becomes a positive-semidefinite quadratic form in basis coefficients, so penalized least-squares smoothing is a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\succeq0\) and the penalized model has Hessian \(A^\top A+\lambda R\succeq0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: integrated squared derivatives induce Gram-matrix quadratic forms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The derivative Gram-matrix representation is correct and appropriate for this leaf, but no source is cited. The statement should also specify a<b, the admissible derivative order r, and the dimensions of A and b before review can be completed against authoritative evidence.

children.title: Difference-Penalty QPs
children.top_down_role: Quadratic regularization templates built from discrete difference operators.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp identifiability condition for a positive difference penalty combined with least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), \(Q=A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda D_k^{\mathsf T}D_k\) is positive definite if and only if \(\ker A\cap\ker D_k=\{0\}\). Equivalently, the observation operator detects every nonzero sampled polynomial trend of degree below \(k\). Under this condition, minimizing the difference-regularized objective over any nonempty polyhedron has a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict convexity holds exactly when the data identify all low-degree polynomial trends left unpenalized by differencing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda D_k^{\mathsf T}D_k\succ0\iff\ker A\cap\ker D_k=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Convexity Criterion for Difference-Regularized Fitting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic structure of the free-boundary order-k forward-difference penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1\le k<n\), the forward-difference matrix \(D_k\in\mathbb R^{(n-k)\times n}\) has rank \(n-k\), and \[D_kx=0\iff \exists p\in\mathbb R[t],\ \deg p<k,\quad x_i=p(i)\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).\] Thus \(\dim\ker D_k=k\). Moreover, \(D_k^{\mathsf T}D_k\) is symmetric positive semidefinite and banded with half-bandwidth \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-k difference penalty ignores exactly sampled polynomial trends of degree below k and produces sparse banded curvature.
assumptions_latex: The standard free-boundary forward-difference operator is used
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}D_k=n-k\), \(\dim\ker D_k=k\), and \(D_k^{\mathsf T}D_k\) has half-bandwidth \(k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Nullspace and Banded Curvature
Difference-Penalty QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete order-k difference regularization for ordered coefficient vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and an integer \(1\le k<n\), define the forward-difference operator \(D_k\in\mathbb{R}^{(n-k)\times n}\) by
\[(D_kx)_i=\sum_{j=0}^k(-1)^{k-j}\binom{k}{j}x_{i+j},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n-k.\]
For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and a polyhedron \(X\),
\[\min_{x\in X}\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2+\frac\lambda2\lVert D_kx\rVert_2^2\]
is a convex QP with Hessian \(A^\top A+\lambda D_k^\top D_k\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalizing finite differences of an ordered vector yields a convex QP whose regularization Hessian is the Gram matrix of the selected difference operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^\top A+\lambda D_k^\top D_k\succeq0\), so the difference-penalized model is a convex QP.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: squared finite differences are positive-semidefinite quadratic forms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward-difference definition and resulting positive-semidefinite QP Hessian are mathematically correct, with representation fitting the leaf. No inspectable authoritative source is supplied for the difference-penalty model.

children.title: Boundary Treatment Regimes
children.top_down_role: Endpoint, periodic, and free-boundary structures affecting difference-based penalties.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral distinction between free-path and periodic-cycle first-difference Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_f\in\mathbb R^{(n-1)\times n}\) satisfy \((D_fx)_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\), and let \(D_p\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) append the row \((D_px)_n=x_1-x_n\). The eigenvalues of \(D_f^{\mathsf T}D_f\) are \(4\sin^2(\pi j/(2n))\), \(j=0,\ldots,n-1\), while those of \(D_p^{\mathsf T}D_p\) are \(4\sin^2(\pi j/n)\), \(j=0,\ldots,n-1\). Both have rank \(n-1\); the periodic matrix is circulant and has a different nonzero spectrum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Free and periodic boundaries retain the same constant null direction but produce different path and cycle spectra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two Gram matrices have the displayed spectra and rank \(n-1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Free and Periodic Boundary Spectra
Boundary Treatment Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nullspace effects of free, periodic, and endpoint-anchored first-difference penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(n\ge2\), define
\[J_{\mathrm{free}}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(x_{i+1}-x_i)^2,\qquad J_{\mathrm{per}}(x)=J_{\mathrm{free}}(x)+(x_1-x_n)^2,\]
and, for fixed endpoints \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}\),
\[J_{\mathrm{anc}}(x)=J_{\mathrm{free}}(x)+(x_1-a)^2+(x_n-b)^2.\]
All three are convex quadratic functions. The homogeneous Hessians of \(J_{\mathrm{free}}\) and \(J_{\mathrm{per}}\) have nullspace \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf{1}\}\), whereas the Hessian of \(J_{\mathrm{anc}}\) is positive definite. Thus endpoint anchoring removes the constant-shift ambiguity retained by free and periodic treatments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Free and periodic first-difference penalties ignore constant shifts. Adding endpoint anchors makes the penalty strictly convex and removes that boundary-induced ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\ker(
abla^2J_{\mathrm{free}})=\ker(
abla^2J_{\mathrm{per}})=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf{1}\}\), while \(
abla^2J_{\mathrm{anc}}\succ0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nullspaces follow directly from the displayed difference penalties

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated nullspaces and positive definiteness under endpoint anchoring are correct, and property is the appropriate content kind for this regime leaf. The record lacks an authoritative source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp positive-definiteness condition for graph-Laplacian regularized least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), \(Q=A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda L\) is positive definite if and only if \(\ker A\cap\ker L=\{0\}\). Equivalently, the data operator detects every nonzero vector constant on each positive-weight connected component. Under this condition, the graph-regularized QP has a unique minimizer over every nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict convexity holds exactly when the data term identifies all componentwise-constant directions left unpenalized by the graph.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is an undirected nonnegative-weight graph Laplacian
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda L\succ0\iff\ker A\cap\ker L=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Uniqueness Criterion for Graph-Regularized Fitting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-incidence representation and exact nullspace of an undirected graph Laplacian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Orient the positive-weight edges of a finite undirected graph arbitrarily, let \(B\) be its edge-vertex incidence matrix, and let \(W_E=\operatorname{Diag}(w_e)\succ0\). Then \(L=B^{\mathsf T}W_EB\), and \[\ker L=\{x:x_i=x_j\text{ whenever }i,j\text{ belong to the same positive-weight connected component}\}.\] Thus \(\dim\ker L\) is the number of such components; for a connected graph, \(\ker L=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph Laplacian is a weighted incidence Gram matrix, and its unpenalized vectors are exactly those constant on each connected component.
assumptions_latex: The graph is finite and undirected
Only positive-weight edges are retained in \(B\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=B^{\mathsf T}W_EB\succeq0\), with the displayed componentwise-constant nullspace.
knowledge_statements.title: Incidence Factorization and Component Nullspace

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\succeq0\) and \(A^\top A+\lambda L\succeq0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the Laplacian energy equals a sum of weighted squared edge differences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic smoothing over an undirected weighted graph via its combinatorial Laplacian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W=(w_{ij})\in\mathbb{S}^n\) satisfy \(w_{ij}\ge0\) and \(w_{ii}=0\), let \(D=\operatorname{Diag}(W\mathbf{1})\), and set \(L=D-W\). Then
\[x^\top Lx=\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}w_{ij}(x_i-x_j)^2\ge0.\]
Hence, for \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and a polyhedron \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[\min_{x\in X}\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2+\frac\lambda2x^\top Lx\]
is a convex QP with Hessian \(A^\top A+\lambda L\succeq0\). The regularizer penalizes variation only across pairs having positive weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph Laplacian formed from symmetric nonnegative edge weights measures weighted squared differences across edges. Adding this quadratic form to least squares gives a convex graph-smoothing QP.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Laplacian Regularization QPs

children.title: Piecewise-Linear Penalty QP Lifts
children.top_down_role: QP-representable lifts combining quadratic loss or regularization with polyhedral penalty models.

children.title: Lasso QP Lifts
children.top_down_role: QP representations of absolute-value sparsity penalties.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for unconstrained lasso.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_1\), \(x^\star\) is optimal if and only if \(0\in A^{\mathsf T}(Ax^\star-b)+\lambda\partial\|x^\star\|_1\). Equivalently, active coordinates attain the signed correlation threshold and zero coordinates satisfy \(|a_j^{\mathsf T}(Ax^\star-b)|\le\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lasso optimality is exactly a coordinatewise residual-correlation threshold condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\iff0\in A^{\mathsf T}(Ax^\star-b)+\lambda\partial\|x^\star\|_1.
knowledge_statements.title: Lasso Subgradient Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-rank uniqueness and duplicate-column nonuniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\) has full column rank, the lasso objective is strongly convex and has a unique minimizer. Rank deficiency removes this guarantee: for \(A=[1\ 1]\), \(b=1\), and \(0<\lambda<1\), every nonnegative pair with \(x_1+x_2=1-\lambda\) is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full column rank guarantees uniqueness, while duplicate columns can produce a continuum of lasso solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}(A)=n\implies|\operatorname*{argmin}F|=1;\quad\operatorname{rank}(A)<n\text{ may permit nonuniqueness}.
knowledge_statements.title: Lasso Uniqueness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact auxiliary-variable QP representation of L1-penalized least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(X=\{x:Fx\le g\}\). The lasso problem \(\min_{x\in X}\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_1\) is exactly equivalent to minimizing \(\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}t\) subject to \(Fx\le g\) and \(-t\le x\le t\). Every optimum satisfies \(t_i=|x_i|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Magnitude variables replace the L1 penalty by a linear objective term and affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x\operatorname*{argmin}(\text{lifted QP})=\operatorname*{argmin}(\text{lasso problem}).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Lasso Magnitude Lift
Lasso QP Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact auxiliary-variable QP representation of an L1-penalized least-squares problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(X=\{x:Fx\le g\}\). The lasso problem
\[\min_{x\in X}\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert x\rVert_1\]
has the exact QP lift
\[\min_{x,t}\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2+\lambda\mathbf{1}^\top t\quad\text{subject to}\quad Fx\le g,\;-t\le x\le t.\]
At every optimum, \(t_i=\lvert x_i\rvert\). Therefore projection of the lifted optimal set onto the \(x\)-coordinates equals the optimal set of the original lasso problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introducing componentwise magnitude variables converts the lasso absolute-value penalty into linear constraints and a linear objective term, yielding an exact convex QP lift.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x\operatorname*{argmin}_{x,t}\{\text{lifted QP}\}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert x\rVert_1\}\).

children.title: Elastic-Net QP Lifts
children.top_down_role: QP representations combining sparsity penalties with quadratic shrinkage.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained optimality certificate and positive-ridge uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_1+\tfrac\gamma2\|x\|_2^2\), \(x^\star\) is optimal if and only if \(0\in A^{\mathsf T}(Ax^\star-b)+\gamma x^\star+\lambda\partial\|x^\star\|_1\). If \(\gamma>0\), \(F\) is \(\gamma\)-strongly convex and coercive, hence has exactly one minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subgradient stationarity completely certifies unconstrained elastic-net optimality, and positive ridge weight guarantees a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\text{ is optimal}\iff0\in A^{\mathsf T}(Ax^\star-b)+\gamma x^\star+\lambda\partial\|x^\star\|_1.
knowledge_statements.title: Elastic-Net Optimality and Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact QP lift for combined L1 and squared-L2 regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(\lambda>0\), \(\gamma\ge0\), and \(X=\{x:Fx\le g\}\). The elastic-net problem \(\min_{x\in X}\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_1+\tfrac\gamma2\|x\|_2^2\) is exactly equivalent to the QP minimizing \(\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\tfrac\gamma2\|x\|_2^2+\lambda\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}t\) subject to \(Fx\le g\) and \(-t\le x\le t\). Every optimum satisfies \(t_i=|x_i|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Magnitude variables convert the L1 term to affine constraints while the squared-L2 term remains quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x\operatorname*{argmin}(\text{lifted QP})=\operatorname*{argmin}(\text{elastic-net problem}).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Elastic-Net Magnitude Lift
Elastic-Net QP Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact QP lift for combined L1 and squared L2 regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(\lambda>0\), \(\gamma\ge0\), and \(X=\{x:Fx\le g\}\). The elastic-net problem
\[\min_{x\in X}\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert x\rVert_1+\frac\gamma2\lVert x\rVert_2^2\]
has the exact QP lift
\[\min_{x,t}\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2+\frac\gamma2\lVert x\rVert_2^2+\lambda\mathbf{1}^\top t\quad\text{subject to}\quad Fx\le g,\;-t\le x\le t.\]
At an optimum, \(t_i=\lvert x_i\rvert\); if \(\gamma>0\), the objective is strongly convex in \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elastic net uses the lasso magnitude-variable lift while retaining its squared-norm term. A positive squared-norm weight makes the objective strongly convex in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted QP is exact, and \(\gamma>0\) makes its objective strongly convex in \(x\).

children.title: Penalty Mixing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes determined by the relative roles of sparse and quadratic regularization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between pure L1 and positive quadratic mixing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A=[1\ 1]\), \(b=1\), \(0<\lambda<1\), and \(\gamma=0\), every nonnegative pair satisfying \(x_1+x_2=1-\lambda\) minimizes \(F_{\lambda,0}\). For every \(\gamma>0\), the added squared-L2 term makes the objective strongly convex and selects a unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate predictors can make pure lasso nonunique, while any positive quadratic weight restores uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \gamma=0\text{ permits a continuum of minimizers, whereas }\gamma>0\text{ yields one}.
knowledge_statements.title: Pure-Lasso Nonuniqueness Regime

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness consequences of the mixing weights on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R^n\), if \(\lambda>0\) or \(\gamma>0\), then \(F_{\lambda,\gamma}\) is coercive and attains its minimum. It is strongly convex and has a unique minimizer whenever \(\gamma>0\) or \(A\) has full column rank. With \(\gamma=0\) and rank-deficient \(A\), uniqueness is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Either regularizer gives coercivity; positive ridge weight or a full-rank design gives uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda+\gamma>0\implies F_{\lambda,\gamma}\text{ is coercive};\qquad(\gamma>0\lor\operatorname{rank}A=n)\implies|\operatorname*{argmin}F_{\lambda,\gamma}|=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Coercivity and Uniqueness Transitions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter partition linking least squares, lasso, ridge, and elastic net.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(F_{\lambda,\gamma}(x)=\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_1+\tfrac\gamma2\|x\|_2^2\) with \(\lambda,\gamma\ge0\): \((0,0)\) is ordinary least squares; \(\lambda>0,\gamma=0\) is lasso; \(\lambda=0,\gamma>0\) is ridge; and \(\lambda>0,\gamma>0\) is elastic net.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two regularization weights partition the model into least-squares, lasso, ridge, and elastic-net regimes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\lambda,\gamma)\text{ determines exactly one of the four displayed regimes}.

notation.meaning: Mixed L1 and squared-L2 penalized least-squares objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Four Penalty-Mixing Regimes
Penalty Mixing Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter regimes linking least squares, lasso, ridge, and elastic-net QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and define
\[F_{\lambda,\gamma}(x)=\frac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert x\rVert_1+\frac\gamma2\lVert x\rVert_2^2,\qquad \lambda,\gamma\ge0.\]
The regime \((\lambda,\gamma)=(0,0)\) is ordinary least squares; \(\lambda>0,\gamma=0\) is lasso; \(\lambda=0,\gamma>0\) is ridge; and \(\lambda>0,\gamma>0\) is elastic net. Whenever \(\gamma>0\), \(F_{\lambda,\gamma}\) is coercive and \(\gamma\)-strongly convex, so it has a unique minimizer on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two penalty weights recover least squares, lasso, ridge, or elastic net. Any positive squared-norm weight guarantees existence and uniqueness over a nonempty closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\gamma>0\), then \(F_{\lambda,\gamma}\) has exactly one minimizer on \(X\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the parameter cases follow from substitution and the positive quadratic term supplies strong convexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four parameter regimes and the existence-and-uniqueness conclusion for positive gamma are correct, and property fits this regime leaf. No source is cited, and A and b are not explicitly introduced with their domains in the statement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of continuous polyhedral epigraph lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An arbitrary nonconvex piecewise-linear loss does not have a convex epigraph and therefore cannot be represented exactly by continuous auxiliary variables and affine inequalities. For example, \(-|x|\) has a nonconvex epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous affine epigraph lifts represent convex piecewise-linear losses, not arbitrary nonconvex piecewise-linear functions.
assumptions_latex: Only continuous auxiliary variables and affine constraints are permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell\text{ nonconvex piecewise-linear}\implies\operatorname{epi}\ell\text{ is not a convex polyhedron}.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Piecewise-Linear Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical special cases of the finite-max QP lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The hinge loss \(\max\{0,1-y_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+\beta_i)\}\) is represented by \(t_i\ge0\) and \(t_i\ge1-y_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+\beta_i)\). For \(\tau\in(0,1)\), the check loss \(\rho_\tau(r)=\tau r_++(1-\tau)r_-\) is represented by \(r=u-v\), \(u,v\ge0\), with objective contribution \(\tau u+(1-\tau)v\). Adding either loss to a convex quadratic over a polyhedron gives a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hinge loss uses an epigraph variable; quantile check loss uses positive and negative residual parts.
assumptions_latex: The remaining quadratic Hessian is positive semidefinite and the domain is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Both canonical losses admit exact linearly constrained convex-QP lifts}.

notation.meaning: Positive and negative parts of a scalar residual.

knowledge_statements.title: Hinge and Quantile-Loss Specializations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fully quantified exact epigraph QP lift for finite convex piecewise-linear losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(X=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Fx\le g\}\), and \(\ell_i(x)=\max_{1\le k\le K_i}(a_{ik}^{\mathsf T}x+\beta_{ik})\), where \(a_{ik}\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\beta_{ik}\in\mathbb R\), and \(K_i<\infty\). Then minimizing \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_{i=1}^m\ell_i(x)\) over \(X\) is exactly equivalent to minimizing \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_i t_i\) subject to \(Fx\le g\) and \(t_i\ge a_{ik}^{\mathsf T}x+\beta_{ik}\) for all \(i,k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One epigraph variable and finitely many affine inequalities exactly represent each finite convex piecewise-linear loss.
assumptions_latex: \(K_i<\infty\) and all affine-piece data have the displayed finite-dimensional domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x\operatorname*{argmin}(\text{lifted QP})=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_i\ell_i(x)\right).

notation.meaning: Number of affine pieces in loss \(i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Max Piecewise-Linear Loss Lift
Piecewise-Linear Loss QP Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph QP lift for finite maxima of affine loss pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Fx\le g\}\), let \(H\in\mathbb{S}_+^n\), and for each observation \(i\) define the convex piecewise-linear loss
\[\ell_i(x)=\max_{1\le k\le K_i}\{a_{ik}^\top x+\beta_{ik}\}.\]
Then
\[\min_{x\in X}\frac12x^\top Hx+c^\top x+\sum_{i=1}^m\ell_i(x)\]
has the exact QP lift
\[\min_{x,t}\frac12x^\top Hx+c^\top x+\sum_{i=1}^m t_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad Fx\le g,\;t_i\ge a_{ik}^\top x+\beta_{ik}\ \text{for all }i,k.\]
Every optimal lift satisfies \(t_i=\ell_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite maximum of affine loss pieces is represented by one epigraph variable and linear inequalities. Adding a convex quadratic term produces an exact QP lift.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted problem is a convex QP and its projection onto \(x\) has the same minimizers as the original problem.

notation.meaning: epigraph variable for the ith loss

The cited chapter-level locator is not sufficiently specific, and the statement does not explicitly introduce the domains of a_ik, beta_ik, c, m, and K_i. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary-and-sufficient primal-dual certificate for projection onto an inequality-and-equality polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility, stationarity, multiplier signs, and complementary slackness exactly certify a polyhedral projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed conditions hold if and only if \(p=\Pi_P(y)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Projection KKT Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global regularity specific to the polyhedral projector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty polyhedron \(P\), \(\|\Pi_P(u)-\Pi_P(v)\|_2^2\le\langle\Pi_P(u)-\Pi_P(v),u-v\rangle\) for all \(u,v\in\mathbb R^n\). Hence \(\Pi_P\) is 1-Lipschitz. Moreover, \(\mathbb R^n\) has a finite polyhedral subdivision on each cell of which \(\Pi_P\) is affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polyhedral projector is firmly nonexpansive and piecewise affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi_P\) is firmly nonexpansive, 1-Lipschitz, and piecewise affine.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric and Piecewise-Affine Structure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-cone and Pythagorean characterizations of Euclidean projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron, \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(p\in P\). Then \(p=\Pi_P(y)\) if and only if \(\langle y-p,x-p\rangle\le0\) for every \(x\in P\), equivalently \(y-p\in N_P(p)\). Consequently, \(\|y-x\|_2^2\ge\|y-p\|_2^2+\|x-p\|_2^2\) for all \(x\in P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is the projection exactly when the target displacement belongs to its normal cone; this yields the projection Pythagorean inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=\Pi_P(y)\iff y-p\in N_P(p)\).

notation.meaning: normal cone of P at p

knowledge_statements.title: Variational Characterization of Polyhedral Projection
Projection onto Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection represented as a convex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\}\) be a nonempty polyhedron and let \(y\in\mathbb R^n\). Its Euclidean projection is represented by the convex quadratic program \[\Pi_P(y)=\mathop{\operatorname{argmin}}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\tfrac12\|x-y\|_2^2:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\right\}.\] The objective has Hessian \(I\), so the optimizer exists and is unique. The squared distance satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(y,P)^2=\|y-\Pi_P(y)\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a nonempty polyhedron is the unique minimizer of squared Euclidean distance, hence a strictly convex quadratic program with linear constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi_P(y)\) is the unique solution of the displayed convex QP.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection of y onto P

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and uniqueness claim are mathematically standard, but the cited polyhedral-sets section does not specifically support Euclidean projection, attainment, or uniqueness. An inspectable projection theorem or convex-QP reference is required; dimensions of b and f should also be stated.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient geometric optimality test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty closed convex sets \(P,Q\), \((x^\star,y^\star)\in P\times Q\) minimizes \(\tfrac12\|x-y\|_2^2\) if and only if \(y^\star-x^\star\in N_P(x^\star)\) and \(x^\star-y^\star\in N_Q(y^\star)\), where \(N_C(z)=\{v:v^{\mathsf T}(w-z)\le0\ \forall w\in C\}\). For polyhedra, these inclusions are equivalent to active-constraint multipliers and QP stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closest pair is certified when its connecting vector is normal to both sets in opposite directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^\star,y^\star)\text{ is closest}\iff y^\star-x^\star\in N_P(x^\star),\ x^\star-y^\star\in N_Q(y^\star).
knowledge_statements.title: Closest-Pair Normal-Cone Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry of possibly nonunique closest pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: All closest pairs of two nonempty closed convex sets with attained distance have the same displacement \(d=y^\star-x^\star\). If \(d\ne0\), then \(d^{\mathsf T}x\le d^{\mathsf T}x^\star<d^{\mathsf T}y^\star\le d^{\mathsf T}y\) for all \(x\in P\), \(y\in Q\), and the separation gap equals \(\|d\|_2^2\). Closest pairs themselves need not be unique, as parallel faces demonstrate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closest displacement is unique and strictly separates disjoint sets, even when closest point pairs are nonunique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d=y^\star-x^\star\text{ is unique; if }d\ne0\text{ it gives strict separation with gap }\|d\|_2^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Unique Closest Displacement and Separation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Squared Euclidean distance between two nonempty polyhedra as a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\}\) and \(Q=\{y:Cy\le d,\ Fy=g\}\) be nonempty polyhedra in \(\mathbb R^n\). Then \(\operatorname{dist}(P,Q)^2=\min\{\|x-y\|_2^2:x\in P,\ y\in Q\}\). This convex QP attains its minimum. Its value is zero if and only if \(P\cap Q\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared distance between two nonempty polyhedra is an attained convex QP over their product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(P,Q)^2=\min_{(x,y)\in P\times Q}\|x-y\|_2^2,\qquad\operatorname{dist}(P,Q)=0\iff P\cap Q\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Set-Distance QP
Distance Between Polyhedral Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Squared Euclidean set distance as a linearly constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\}\) and \(Q=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:Cy\le d,\ Fy=g\}\) be nonempty polyhedra. Their squared Euclidean distance is the optimal value of \[\operatorname{dist}(P,Q)^2=\min_{x,y}\left\{\|x-y\|_2^2:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f,\ Cy\le d,\ Fy=g\right\}.\] This is a convex QP in \((x,y)\). An optimal pair exists, although it need not be unique; the optimal value is zero exactly when \(P\cap Q\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared distance between two nonempty polyhedra is obtained by jointly minimizing squared separation subject to both polyhedral constraint systems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(P,Q)^2\) equals the displayed QP value.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The QP representation is standard, but the cited section does not specifically support attainment of distance between possibly unbounded polyhedra or the zero-distance equivalence. A source with an exact projection/set-distance result is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate for linear shape inequalities and equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility and the linear-constraint KKT conditions exactly characterize optimal reconstructions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed primal-dual conditions are necessary and sufficient for global optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Shape-Constrained Reconstruction KKT Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Encodings of Common Shape Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral encodings of monotonicity and discrete convexity for ordered reconstructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), monotone nondecreasing shape is represented by \(x_i-x_{i+1}\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n-1\). For \(n\ge3\), discrete convexity is represented by \(2x_i-x_{i-1}-x_{i+1}\le0\) for \(i=2,\ldots,n-1\). Intersecting these systems with affine equalities and componentwise bounds gives a polyhedron, so imposing them on a convex quadratic reconstruction objective preserves the convex-QP class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotonicity, discrete convexity, bounds, and affine normalization are linear shape restrictions that can be combined in a reconstruction QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed shape-restricted sets are polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Encodings of Common Shape Restrictions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and exact nonuniqueness characterization for feasible shape-constrained quadratic reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron and \(q(x)=\tfrac12\|Hx-y\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|Lx\|_2^2\), where \(\lambda\ge0\). The minimum of \(q\) over \(S\) is attained. If \(x^*\) is a minimizer, then \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S}q(x)=\{z\in S:H(z-x^*)=0,\ \sqrt\lambda L(z-x^*)=0\}.\] Hence the minimizer is unique exactly when this set is \(\{x^*\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible reconstruction exists, and all ambiguity consists of feasible alternatives invisible to both the data and active regularization operators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimum is attained and the minimizer set has the displayed fiber representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Attainment and Exact Reconstruction Ambiguity
Shape-Constrained Reconstruction QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-squares reconstruction under linear shape restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given observations \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), a linear observation operator \(H\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and a nonempty polyhedral shape set \(S=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\}\), a shape-constrained reconstruction is any solution of \[\min_{x\in S}\ \tfrac12\|Hx-y\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|Lx\|_2^2,\qquad \lambda\ge0.\] Its Hessian is \(H^{\mathsf T}H+\lambda L^{\mathsf T}L\succeq0\), so the model is a convex QP. The reconstruction is unique when this Hessian is positive definite on every nonzero feasible direction of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear shape constraints combined with least-squares data fitting and quadratic regularization produce a convex reconstruction QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed reconstruction model is a convex QP.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited sections separately concern linear least squares and polyhedra but do not support the complete regularized shape-constrained model or its uniqueness condition. The dimensions of L should be introduced, and “feasible direction” should be defined precisely for the uniqueness claim.

children.title: Linear SVM Primal QPs
children.top_down_role: Hard- and soft-margin linear classification templates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separability, Geometric Margin, and Primal Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility, margin, and uniqueness properties of hard- and soft-margin linear SVM primals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The hard-margin constraints are feasible if and only if some \((\bar w,\bar b)\) satisfies \(y_i(\bar w^{\mathsf T}x_i+\bar b)>0\) for every \(i\); positive rescaling then enforces unit functional margins. When both label classes occur, the distance between the normalized supporting hyperplanes is \(2/\|w\|_2\), so minimizing \(\tfrac12\|w\|_2^2\) maximizes geometric margin. Whenever either primal has an optimum, its optimal \(w\) is unique, although \(b\) need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard-margin feasibility is strict linear separability; norm minimization maximizes normalized margin, and the optimal normal vector is unique even if the intercept is not.
assumptions_latex: Both classes occur for the two-supporting-hyperplane interpretation
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Hard-margin feasibility is equivalent to strict separation, the normalized margin is \(2/\|w\|_2\), and optimal \(w\) is unique.
knowledge_statements.title: Separability, Geometric Margin, and Primal Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hinge-Loss Form of the Soft-Margin Primal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slack-eliminated form of the linear soft-margin SVM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \((w,b)\), the smallest feasible slack is \[\xi_i=\max\{0,1-y_i(w^{\mathsf T}x_i+b)\}.\] Hence the explicit-slack QP is equivalent to \[\min_{w,b}\ \tfrac12\|w\|_2^2+C\sum_{i=1}^m\max\{0,1-y_i(w^{\mathsf T}x_i+b)\}.\] The first form is a linearly constrained QP; the eliminated form is an unconstrained convex piecewise-quadratic optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the slacks converts the soft-margin QP into weight regularization plus summed hinge loss.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The explicit-slack QP and hinge-loss form have identical optimal \((w,b)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Hinge-Loss Form of the Soft-Margin Primal
Linear SVM Primal QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard- and soft-margin primal linear SVM formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For labeled data \((x_i,y_i)\in\mathbb R^d\times\{-1,1\}\), the hard-margin linear SVM is \[\min_{w,b}\ \tfrac12\|w\|_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad y_i(w^{\mathsf T}x_i+b)\ge1\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] It requires feasibility. For \(C>0\), the soft-margin formulation is \[\min_{w,b,\xi}\ \tfrac12\|w\|_2^2+C\sum_{i=1}^m\xi_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad y_i(w^{\mathsf T}x_i+b)\ge1-\xi_i,\quad \xi_i\ge0.\] Both are convex QPs; the soft-margin problem is always feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear SVM training minimizes weight norm subject to hard margins, or adds nonnegative slacks penalized by a positive soft-margin parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both displayed primal SVM models are convex QPs.
