children.title: Support-Vector Machine Dual QPs
children.top_down_role: Linear and kernelized dual templates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Application-specific primal-dual certificate for the soft-margin SVM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((w,b,\xi,\alpha)\) be primal-dual feasible and satisfy \[w=\sum_i\alpha_i y_i\phi(x_i),\quad y^{\mathsf T}\alpha=0,\quad0\leq\alpha_i\leq C,\] \[\alpha_i(y_if_i-1+\xi_i)=0,\qquad(C-\alpha_i)\xi_i=0,\] where \(f_i=\langle w,\phi(x_i)\rangle+b\). These conditions certify optimality and imply \[\alpha_i=0\Rightarrow \xi_i=0,":"y_if_i\geq1,\] \[0<\alpha_i<C\Rightarrow \xi_i=0,":"y_if_i=1,\] \[\alpha_i=C\Rightarrow y_if_i=1-\xi_i\leq1.\] If some \(0<\alpha_i<C\), then \(b=y_i-\langle w,\phi(x_i)\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SVM KKT conditions certify optimality and distinguish non-support, free-support, and bounded-support samples.
assumptions_latex: The displayed primal-dual feasibility and complementarity conditions hold
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The KKT system certifies optimality and yields support-vector classification and bias recovery.

notation.meaning: classifier score on training sample i

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Vector KKT Classification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel-matrix condition guaranteeing uniqueness of the SVM dual multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=YKY\succeq0\). If \[d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\quad\text{for every }0\neq d\in y^\perp,\] then the dual objective is strictly concave on \(y^{\mathsf T}\alpha=0\), so the box-constrained dual has a unique optimizer. If this condition fails, distinct optimal multipliers can occur even when the represented primal normal vector is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive curvature of the labeled kernel matrix on the equality-feasible subspace guarantees a unique dual multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive definiteness of \(Q\) on \(y^\perp\) implies uniqueness of \(\alpha^*\).

notation.meaning: directions satisfying the homogeneous dual equality

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Curvature and Multiplier Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasible-direction curvature boundary for the kernelized SVM dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Positive semidefiniteness of \(K\) implies \(YKY\succeq0\) and therefore makes the SVM dual concave. More generally, concavity on the equality-feasible affine hull requires \[d^{\mathsf T}YKYd\geq0\quad\text{for every }d\in y^\perp.\] Thus global \(K\succeq0\) is sufficient but not necessary for this particular finite dual. If some \(d\in y^\perp\) satisfies \(d^{\mathsf T}YKYd<0\), the maximization objective has positive curvature along that equality-feasible direction and is not concave on the affine hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PSD kernel guarantees a convex SVM dual, while the exact finite-problem requirement is nonnegative labeled-kernel curvature on equality-feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\succeq0\) is sufficient; negative labeled-kernel curvature on \(y^\perp\) certifies loss of concavity.
knowledge_statements.title: Kernel Curvature Boundary
Support-Vector Machine Dual QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soft-margin SVM dual for linear or positive-semidefinite kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be positive semidefinite, with \(K_{ij}=x_i^{\mathsf T}x_j\) in the linear case, and let \(Y=\operatorname{diag}(y)\). The soft-margin SVM dual is \[\max_{\alpha\in\mathbb R^m}\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\alpha-\tfrac12\alpha^{\mathsf T}YKY\alpha\quad\text{subject to}\quad y^{\mathsf T}\alpha=0,\quad 0\le\alpha_i\le C.\] For a feature map \(\phi\) realizing \(K\), the associated primal vector satisfies \(w=\sum_i\alpha_i y_i\phi(x_i)\). For the feasible hard-margin primal, deleting the upper bounds gives its dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SVM dual maximizes a concave quadratic over a box and one equality; kernels replace inner products through a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed concave QP is dual to the soft-margin SVM primal.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction between least-squares label fitting and SVM training.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y_i\in\{-1,1\}\), squared label loss \((w^{\mathsf T}x_i+b-y_i)^2\) penalizes numerical deviation from the coded label. Hinge loss \(\max\{0,1-y_i(w^{\mathsf T}x_i+b)\}\) instead vanishes for every score having margin at least one. Thus a correctly classified point with margin strictly greater than one has zero hinge loss but generally positive squared label loss. The two training objectives are not equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared-loss classification fits coded label values, whereas SVM hinge loss enforces margins; they are distinct models.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Squared label loss and hinge loss define non-equivalent classification objectives.
knowledge_statements.title: Squared-Loss versus Margin-Loss Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality system for ridge-regularized least-squares classification with an unpenalized intercept.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z=[X\ \mathbf1]\), \(\theta=(w,b)\), and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(I_d,0)\). Then every minimizer of \[\tfrac12\|Z\theta-y\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\theta^{\mathsf T}D\theta\] satisfies \[(Z^{\mathsf T}Z+\lambda D)\theta=Z^{\mathsf T}y.\] The minimizer is unique exactly when \(\ker Z\cap\ker D=\{0\}\). In particular, if \(m\geq1\) and \(\lambda>0\), the Hessian is positive definite despite the unpenalized intercept.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least-squares classification obeys ridge normal equations, with uniqueness characterized by the augmented design and penalty nullspaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normal equations characterize minimizers, and uniqueness is equivalent to \(\ker Z\cap\ker D=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: design matrix augmented by an intercept column
penalty matrix leaving the intercept unpenalized

knowledge_statements.title: Normal Equations and Uniqueness
Least-Squares Classification QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized linear classification fitted by squared loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a design matrix \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\), labels \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\lambda\ge0\), regularized least-squares classification fits \((w,b)\) by \[\min_{w\in\mathbb R^d,\ b\in\mathbb R}\ \tfrac12\|Xw+b\mathbf1-y\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|w\|_2^2.\] This is an unconstrained convex QP. Additional linear restrictions on \((w,b)\) preserve the QP form. A binary prediction may be defined by \(\widehat y(x)=\operatorname{sign}(w^{\mathsf T}x+b)\), with a separately specified convention at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least-squares classification fits a linear score by squared label error, optionally with quadratic regularization and linear parameter constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fitting problem is a convex quadratic program.

children.title: Minimum-Variance QPs
children.top_down_role: Single-period portfolio QPs centered on direct variance minimization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular-covariance behavior on a convex portfolio set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty closed convex portfolio set on which the minimum is attained, and let \(\Sigma\succeq0\). The minimum variance is zero if and only if \(X\cap\ker\Sigma\ne\varnothing\). If \(\ker\Sigma\cap(X-X)=\{0\}\), the quadratic is strictly convex on \(X\), so the minimizer is unique. If two feasible points lie in \(\ker\Sigma\), both have zero variance and are optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible covariance-null portfolio has zero risk, while covariance-null feasible differences delimit strict convexity and uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: The variance minimum over \(X\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Kernel intersections characterize zero variance and the strict-convexity boundary on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Variance and Uniqueness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-only minimum-variance model permitting short positions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\Sigma\succ0\), then \[\min_x\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x\quad\text{subject to}\quad\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1\] has the unique solution \[x^{\mathrm{gmv}}=\frac{\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1}{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1},\qquad (x^{\mathrm{gmv}})^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x^{\mathrm{gmv}}=\frac1{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive-definite covariance and only full investment, the global minimum-variance portfolio has the inverse-covariance closed form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed \(x^{\mathrm{gmv}}\) is the unique fully invested minimum-variance portfolio.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Form Fully Invested Minimum-Variance Portfolio
Minimum-Variance QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Long-only fully invested minimum-variance portfolio template.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S_+^n\) be an asset-return covariance matrix. The long-only fully invested minimum-variance portfolio is any solution of \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x\quad\text{subject to}\quad \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1,\quad x\ge0.\] More generally, additional linear portfolio restrictions may be appended without changing convexity. The feasible set is nonempty and compact, so an optimizer exists. It is unique if \(d^{\mathsf T}\Sigma d>0\) for every nonzero feasible direction \(d\) satisfying \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}d=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimum-variance portfolio minimizes covariance-weighted quadratic risk over fully invested, long-only weights and any additional linear restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed portfolio model is a convex QP with an attained optimum.

children.title: Target-Return QPs
children.top_down_role: Single-period portfolio QPs subject to a prescribed expected-return target.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed form for a fully invested portfolio with an exact return target and unrestricted signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\Sigma\succ0\), and set \[A=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1,\quad B=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}\mu,\quad C=\mu^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{-1}\mu,\quad D=AC-B^2.\] If \(D>0\), the problem \[\min_x\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x\quad\text{subject to}\quad\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1,\ \mu^{\mathsf T}x=\rho\] has the unique solution \[x(\rho)=\Sigma^{-1}\left(\frac{C-B\rho}{D}\mathbf1+\frac{A\rho-B}{D}\mu\right),\] with variance \((A\rho^2-2B\rho+C)/D\). If \(D=0\), \(\mu\) is proportional to \(\mathbf1\), so expected return is constant on the full-investment affine space and only that target is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive-definite covariance and unrestricted signs, the exact-return efficient portfolio and its frontier variance have closed forms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed portfolio is unique and has variance \((A\rho^2-2B\rho+C)/D\).
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Equality Efficient-Frontier Formula
Target-Return QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance minimization subject to a required expected return.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S_+^n\) be a covariance matrix, \(\mu\in\mathbb R^n\) an expected-return vector, and \(\rho\in\mathbb R\) a target return. A long-only target-return portfolio solves \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x\quad\text{subject to}\quad \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1,\quad x\ge0,\quad \mu^{\mathsf T}x\ge\rho.\] This is a convex QP. It is feasible exactly when \(\rho\le\max_i\mu_i\); under a general nonempty polyhedral portfolio set \(X\), feasibility is equivalent to \(\rho\le\sup_{x\in X}\mu^{\mathsf T}x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A target-return QP minimizes portfolio variance while enforcing full investment, long-only holdings, and an expected return threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed target-return model is a convex QP with the stated feasibility threshold.

children.title: Return-Constraint Activity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Portfolio regimes distinguished by inactive, binding, or infeasible return targets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible and infeasible thresholds over a compact portfolio set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty compact portfolio set and define \(\rho_{\max}=\max_{x\in X}\mu^{\mathsf T}x\). Then \[X\cap\{x:\mu^{\mathsf T}x\ge\rho\}\ne\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\rho\le\rho_{\max}.\] For the long-only simplex, \(\rho_{\max}=\max_i\mu_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A return target is feasible exactly up to the maximum expected return attainable over the underlying portfolio set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho\le\rho_{\max}\) is necessary and sufficient for target feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Target-Return Feasibility Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Activity at the Minimum-Variance Return
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier behavior at the transition from an inactive to a binding target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^0\) minimize variance over the base feasible set \(X\), and set \(r_0=\mu^{\mathsf T}x^0\). At target \(\rho=r_0\), the inequality \(\mu^{\mathsf T}x\ge\rho\) is active at \(x^0\), but a KKT certificate can use multiplier zero for that added constraint. Thus geometric activity does not imply a positive shadow price at the transition target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the minimum-variance return, the target constraint binds geometrically but may be weakly active with zero multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(x^0\) is a minimum-variance portfolio over the base convex feasible set.
A KKT certificate exists for the base problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(\rho=r_0\), the added return constraint is active and admits a zero multiplier.

notation.meaning: expected return of the minimum-variance portfolio

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Activity at the Minimum-Variance Return
Return-Constraint Activity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: When a target-return inequality is inactive or binding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty compact convex portfolio set, let \(\Sigma\succ0\), and let \(x^0\) uniquely minimize \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x\) over \(X\). For the feasible target-return problem minimizing \(q(x)\) over \(X\cap\{x:\mu^{\mathsf T}x\ge\rho\}\), if \(\rho<\mu^{\mathsf T}x^0\), the return constraint is inactive and \(x^0\) remains optimal. If \(\rho=\mu^{\mathsf T}x^0\), it is active at \(x^0\). If \(\rho>\mu^{\mathsf T}x^0\), the unique optimizer \(x^\rho\) satisfies \(\mu^{\mathsf T}x^\rho=\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative to the unconstrained minimum-variance return, a lower target is inactive, an equal target is active, and a higher feasible target binds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The activity regime is determined by comparing \(\rho\) with \(\mu^{\mathsf T}x^0\).

notation.meaning: minimum-variance portfolio without the return constraint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Behavior at zero and negative risk-aversion weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(\gamma=0\), the objective becomes the linear return-maximization problem \(\max_{x\in X}\mu^{\mathsf T}x\), rather than a genuine quadratic risk-return tradeoff. If \(\gamma<0\) and \(\Sigma\) has positive curvature along some feasible affine-hull direction, the quadratic objective is nonconvex on that affine hull. Thus \(\gamma>0\) is the standard convex mean-variance regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero risk aversion reduces the model to return maximization, while negative risk aversion generally destroys convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma>0\) gives the stated convex risk-return QP interpretation.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Aversion Parameter Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparative statics of mean-variance scalarization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_j\) solve \[\min_{x\in X}\ \frac{\gamma_j}{2}x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x-\mu^{\mathsf T}x,\qquad j=1,2,\] for \(0<\gamma_1<\gamma_2\). Then \[x_2^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x_2\le x_1^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x_1,\qquad \mu^{\mathsf T}x_2\le\mu^{\mathsf T}x_1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing risk aversion selects an optimizer with no greater variance and no greater expected return.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(X\) is common to both problems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Attained variance and expected return are weakly nonincreasing with \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Aversion Monotonicity
Risk-Return Tradeoff QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted mean-variance portfolio optimization over polyhedral constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedral portfolio set, \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(\mu\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\gamma>0\). A risk-return tradeoff portfolio solves \[\min_{x\in X}\ \tfrac\gamma2x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x-\mu^{\mathsf T}x.\] The quadratic term penalizes variance and the linear term rewards expected return. This is a convex QP. If \(X\) is compact, an optimizer exists; if \(\Sigma\) is positive definite on every nonzero feasible direction of \(X\), the optimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mean-variance tradeoff model minimizes risk aversion times variance minus expected return over a polyhedral portfolio set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed mean-variance tradeoff model is a convex QP.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variational characterization of a benchmark-tracking solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty closed convex set \(X\) and \(V\succeq0\), a feasible \(x^*\in X\) minimizes \(\tfrac12(x-x^b)^{\mathsf T}V(x-x^b)\) if and only if \[\langle V(x^*-x^b),x-x^*\rangle\ge0\quad\text{for every }x\in X,\] equivalently \(0\in V(x^*-x^b)+N_X(x^*)\). For polyhedral \(X\), this is equivalent to the associated primal-feasibility, stationarity, multiplier-sign, and complementary-slackness conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tracking portfolio is a covariance-seminorm projection of the benchmark and is certified by a variational inequality or polyhedral KKT system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed variational inequality is necessary and sufficient for optimal tracking.

notation.meaning: normal cone of the feasible set at the candidate

knowledge_statements.title: Tracking-Projection Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel effects for a singular tracking metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be nonempty and closed and suppose the tracking minimum is attained. For \(V\succeq0\), the minimum tracking error is zero if and only if \[X\cap(x^b+\ker V)\ne\varnothing.\] If \(X\) is convex and \(\ker V\cap(X-X)=\{0\}\), the objective is strictly convex on \(X\), so the minimizer is unique. Distinct feasible portfolios whose difference lies in \(\ker V\) have identical tracking objective values; in particular, distinct zero-error portfolios are all optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero tracking error means a feasible portfolio differs from the benchmark only in a null direction; such null directions also delimit uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The kernel of \(V\) characterizes zero-error portfolios and the principal nonuniqueness boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Error and Nonuniqueness Regimes
Benchmark-Tracking QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic tracking-error minimization against a benchmark portfolio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^b\in\mathbb R^n\) be benchmark weights, \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) a nonempty polyhedral portfolio set, and \(V\in\mathbb S_+^n\) a covariance or tracking metric. The benchmark-tracking portfolio solves \[\min_{x\in X}\ \tfrac12(x-x^b)^{\mathsf T}V(x-x^b).\] Equivalently, after discarding the constant term, it minimizes \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Vx-(Vx^b)^{\mathsf T}x\). Thus tracking is a convex QP; the minimizer is unique when \(V\) is positive definite on every nonzero feasible direction of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Benchmark tracking minimizes a covariance-weighted quadratic distance between portfolio and benchmark weights under polyhedral investment constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tracking-error model has the stated convex QP representation.

children.title: Long-Only Constraints
children.top_down_role: Portfolio feasible regions excluding short positions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry and existence consequence of long-only full investment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The fully invested long-only feasible set is \[\Delta_n=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x\ge0,\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1\}=\operatorname{conv}\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}.\] It is a nonempty compact polytope of affine dimension \(n-1\) for \(n\ge2\). Consequently, every continuous quadratic objective attains a minimum on \(\Delta_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Long-only fully invested portfolios form the compact unit simplex, so every continuous quadratic portfolio objective attains a minimum there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Delta_n=\operatorname{conv}\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}\text{ is compact and nonempty}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fully Invested Long-Only Simplex
Long-Only Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise nonnegativity restriction on portfolio holdings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a portfolio weight vector \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), the long-only condition is \[x_i\ge0\qquad(i=1,\ldots,n),\] equivalently \(x\in\mathbb R_+^n\). When combined with full investment, it gives the simplex constraint \(x\ge0\) and \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1\). The condition prohibits negative asset weights and is a system of linear inequalities, so adjoining it to a convex quadratic portfolio objective preserves the convex QP structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A portfolio is long-only exactly when every asset weight is nonnegative; with full investment, feasible weights lie in the unit simplex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Long-only feasibility is equivalent to \(x\in\mathbb R_+^n\).

children.title: Exposure Constraints
children.top_down_role: Portfolio feasible regions controlling asset, sector, factor, or aggregate exposures.

knowledge_statements.title: Exposure Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear bounds on portfolio exposures to specified factors or groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be portfolio weights and let \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}\) contain exposure vectors as columns. Given bounds \(\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}^k\) with \(\ell\leq u\), the portfolio satisfies the exposure constraints precisely when
\[\ell\leq B^{\mathsf T}x\leq u.\]
For benchmark-relative exposures, replace \(x\) by \(x-x^{\mathrm{b}}\), where \(x^{\mathrm{b}}\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is fixed. These inequalities are componentwise and define a closed convex polyhedron; hence they preserve the quadratic-program form of any convex portfolio objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Portfolio factor or group exposures are bounded componentwise by linear inequalities, optionally relative to a fixed benchmark; the resulting feasible set is polyhedral.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) and any benchmark \(x^{\mathrm{b}}\) are fixed data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:\ell\leq B^{\mathsf T}x\leq u\}\) is a closed convex polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificate specialized to two-sided exposure limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The system \(\ell\le B^{\mathsf T}x\le u\) is infeasible exactly when there exist \(p,q\in\mathbb R_+^k\) such that \[B(p-q)=0,\qquad u^{\mathsf T}p-\ell^{\mathsf T}q<0.\] For benchmark-relative bounds, the same alternative applies after translating the bounds by \(B^{\mathsf T}x^{\mathrm b}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative multipliers with zero combined exposure normal and a negative combined bound certify inconsistent exposure limits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:\ell\le B^{\mathsf T}x\le u\}=\varnothing\iff\exists p,q\ge0:\ B(p-q)=0,\ u^{\mathsf T}p-\ell^{\mathsf T}q<0.
knowledge_statements.title: Exposure-Bound Infeasibility Certificate

children.title: Neutrality Constraints
children.top_down_role: Portfolio feasible regions imposing zero net exposure to selected directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Neutrality Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact zero active exposure to selected factors, groups, or market directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x,x^{\mathrm{b}}\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(N\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) collect the exposure directions to be neutralized. Benchmark-relative neutrality is the affine equality
\[N^{\mathsf T}(x-x^{\mathrm{b}})=0.\]
Absolute neutrality is obtained by setting \(x^{\mathrm{b}}=0\). A dollar-neutral portfolio is the special case \(N=\mathbf{1}\), while factor neutrality uses the corresponding factor-loading columns. The neutrality set is affine, and its intersection with any polyhedral portfolio constraints remains QP-representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Neutrality requires selected absolute or benchmark-relative exposures to equal zero. It is an affine constraint and includes dollar and factor neutrality as special cases.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:N^{\mathsf T}(x-x^{\mathrm{b}})=0\}\) is an affine set.

notation.meaning: matrix of directions whose exposures must vanish

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incompatibility of absolute dollar neutrality and full investment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Absolute dollar neutrality requires \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=0\), whereas full investment of the same weight vector requires \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1\). Hence no portfolio satisfies both. More generally, equalities \(a^{\mathsf T}x=\beta_1\) and \(a^{\mathsf T}x=\beta_2\) are inconsistent when \(\beta_1\ne\beta_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute dollar neutrality cannot be combined with full investment on the same weight vector.
assumptions_latex: Both equalities constrain the same portfolio vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=0,\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1\}=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Dollar-Neutrality and Full-Investment Incompatibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dimension of the Neutrality Affine Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-based geometry of simultaneous neutrality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(N\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), \[\mathcal N=\{x:N^{\mathsf T}(x-x^{\mathrm b})=0\}=x^{\mathrm b}+\ker(N^{\mathsf T}).\] Thus \(\mathcal N\) is nonempty, has affine dimension \(n-\operatorname{rank}(N)\), and is unchanged by redundant neutrality directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Benchmark-relative neutrality is a translated nullspace whose dimension equals the number of unconstrained independent directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal N=x^{\mathrm b}+\ker(N^{\mathsf T}),\qquad\dim(\mathcal N)=n-\operatorname{rank}(N).
knowledge_statements.title: Dimension of the Neutrality Affine Space

children.title: Dense Covariance Models
children.top_down_role: Portfolio QPs using unrestricted dense covariance representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Covariance Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit full-matrix representation of portfolio variance in a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be a portfolio-weight vector. A dense covariance model stores \(\Sigma\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\) explicitly, without imposing a factor or sparsity decomposition, and represents portfolio variance by
\[\operatorname{Var}(x)=x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x.\]
For a risk-aversion coefficient \(\gamma\geq0\) and expected-return vector \(\mu\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the mean-variance objective is
\[\tfrac{\gamma}{2}x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x-\mu^{\mathsf T}x.\]
It is a convex quadratic objective because its Hessian is \(\gamma\Sigma\succeq0\). Explicit storage generally requires \(n(n+1)/2\) distinct covariance entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a portfolio-weight vector, a dense model stores the full positive-semidefinite covariance matrix and uses its quadratic form for variance, producing a convex mean-variance objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\mapsto \tfrac{\gamma}{2}x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x-\mu^{\mathsf T}x\) is convex.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense Covariance Storage and Product Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage and arithmetic consequences of unstructured covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dense symmetric \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^n\) has \(n(n+1)/2=\Theta(n^2)\) independent entries. Without additional structure, computing \(\Sigma x\) costs \(\Theta(n^2)\); evaluating \(x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x\) or its gradient after that product costs \(O(n)\) more.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unstructured dense covariance uses quadratic storage and quadratic work per matrix-vector product.
assumptions_latex: \(\Sigma\) is stored as an unstructured dense symmetric matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{storage}(\Sigma)=\Theta(n^2),\qquad \operatorname{cost}(\Sigma x)=\Theta(n^2).
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Covariance Storage and Product Cost

children.title: Factor Covariance Models
children.top_down_role: Portfolio QPs using low-dimensional factor structure plus residual risk.

knowledge_statements.title: Factor Covariance Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Low-rank factor risk plus asset-specific diagonal risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) be a portfolio-weight vector, \(F\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}\) an asset-by-factor loading matrix, \(C\in\mathbb{S}^k_+\) a factor covariance matrix, and \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n_+\). Define \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d)\). Then
\[\Sigma=FCF^{\mathsf T}+D\succeq0,\qquad x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x=(F^{\mathsf T}x)^{\mathsf T}C(F^{\mathsf T}x)+\sum_{i=1}^n d_i x_i^2.\]
Thus portfolio risk is represented by factor exposures and separable specific risk. Introducing \(y=F^{\mathsf T}x\) yields an equivalent convex QP with the linear equality \(y=F^{\mathsf T}x\) and quadratic term \(y^{\mathsf T}Cy+x^{\mathsf T}Dx\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a portfolio-weight vector, factor covariance decomposes risk into a low-dimensional factor quadratic and diagonal asset-specific risk, with an equivalent convex QP using factor-exposure variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(FCF^{\mathsf T}+D\succeq0\), and the displayed factor-risk representation equals \(x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma x\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage and products for low-dimensional factor covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Sigma=FCF^{\mathsf T}+D\), with \(F\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), dense \(C\in\mathbb S^k\), and diagonal \(D\), storage and computation of \(\Sigma x=F(C(F^{\mathsf T}x))+Dx\) cost \(O(nk+k^2+n)\). This is subquadratic in \(n\) when \(k=o(n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor covariance admits factor-scale storage and matrix-vector products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{storage},\operatorname{cost}(\Sigma x)=O(nk+k^2+n).

notation.meaning: loadings, factor covariance, and specific covariance

knowledge_statements.title: Factor-Risk Evaluation Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact nullspace condition for strict risk curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C\succeq0\) and diagonal \(D\succeq0\), \(\Sigma=FCF^{\mathsf T}+D\) is positive definite exactly when \[\ker(D)\cap\{x:F^{\mathsf T}x\in\ker(C)\}=\{0\}.\] In particular, \(D\succ0\) is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor covariance is positive definite exactly when no nonzero portfolio is unpenalized by both specific and factor risk.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: FCF^{\mathsf T}+D\succ0\iff\ker(D)\cap\{x:F^{\mathsf T}x\in\ker(C)\}=\{0\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definiteness of Factor Covariance

children.title: Regularized Covariance Models
children.top_down_role: Portfolio QPs using stabilized, shrunk, or otherwise regularized covariance estimates.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Covariance Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite shrinkage of a sample covariance toward a structured target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(S,T\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\) be a sample covariance and a structured target covariance, and let \(\alpha\in[0,1]\). The linear shrinkage estimator is
\[\Sigma_{\alpha}=(1-\alpha)S+\alpha T.\]
Because the positive-semidefinite cone is convex, \(\Sigma_{\alpha}\succeq0\), so \(x^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{\alpha}x\) is a convex quadratic risk model. A ridge-regularized instance uses \(T=\tau I_n\) with \(\tau>0\); when \(\alpha>0\), it satisfies \(\Sigma_{\alpha}\succeq\alpha\tau I_n\) and is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a portfolio vector, shrinkage combines a sample covariance with a positive-semidefinite target, preserving convexity; a positive ridge target makes the covariance positive definite when weighted positively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Sigma_{\alpha}\succeq0\); if \(T=\tau I_n\), \(\tau>0\), and \(\alpha>0\), then \(\Sigma_{\alpha}\succ0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: When positive shrinkage fails to create strict curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S,T\succeq0\) and \(0<\alpha<1\), \[\ker((1-\alpha)S+\alpha T)=\ker(S)\cap\ker(T).\] Hence shrinkage toward a merely semidefinite target remains singular exactly when sample and target covariances share a nonzero null direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semidefinite shrinkage remains singular precisely along null directions shared by the sample covariance and target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ker(\Sigma_\alpha)=\ker(S)\cap\ker(T).
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite-Target Singularity Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme-eigenvalue and conditioning bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Sigma_\alpha=(1-\alpha)S+\alpha T\), where \(S,T\succeq0\) and \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), \[\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_\alpha)\ge(1-\alpha)\lambda_{\min}(S)+\alpha\lambda_{\min}(T),\] \[\lambda_{\max}(\Sigma_\alpha)\le(1-\alpha)\lambda_{\max}(S)+\alpha\lambda_{\max}(T).\] When the lower bound is positive, their ratio bounds \(\kappa_2(\Sigma_\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrinkage has explicit extreme-eigenvalue and condition-number bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_\alpha)\ge(1-\alpha)\lambda_{\min}(S)+\alpha\lambda_{\min}(T).
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Bounds for Shrinkage Covariance

children.title: QP-Representable Turnover Models
children.top_down_role: QP-compatible representations of portfolio change magnitude or turnover limits.

knowledge_statements.title: QP-Representable Turnover Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary-variable QP formulation of weighted absolute trading turnover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x,x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define trades by \(d=x-x^0\), and let \(w\in\mathbb{R}^n_+\). Introduce \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying
\[u\geq d,\qquad u\geq-d.\]
Then
\[\sum_{i=1}^n w_i|d_i|=\min_{u}\{w^{\mathsf T}u:u\geq d,\ u\geq-d\}.\]
Consequently, either a turnover penalty \(\lambda w^{\mathsf T}u\), with \(\lambda\geq0\), or a turnover limit \(w^{\mathsf T}u\leq\tau\), with \(\tau\geq0\), can be added to a convex QP using only linear variables, objectives, and constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted absolute turnover has an exact linear auxiliary-variable formulation, so turnover penalties and limits can be included in a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i w_i|d_i|=\min\{w^{\mathsf T}u:u\geq d,\ u\geq-d\}\).

notation.meaning: auxiliary upper bound on absolute trades

source_refs.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

source_witnesses.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility test for a turnover-constrained portfolio set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty closed polyhedron, \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(w\ge0\). Define \[\tau_{\min}=\min_{x\in X}\sum_iw_i|x_i-x_i^0|.\] Then \(X\cap\{x:\sum_iw_i|x_i-x_i^0|\le\tau\}\ne\varnothing\) if and only if \(\tau\ge\tau_{\min}\). The value is obtained by the linear program with \(u\ge x-x^0\) and \(u\ge-(x-x^0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A turnover cap is feasible exactly when it is at least the weighted L1 distance from the current portfolio to the admissible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau\ge\tau_{\min}\) is necessary and sufficient for feasibility.

notation.meaning: minimum turnover required to reach the admissible set

knowledge_statements.title: Turnover-Cap Feasibility Threshold

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for the weighted-turnover epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\min\{w^{\mathsf T}u:u\ge d,\ u\ge-d\}\), if some \(w_i<0\), increasing \(u_i\) makes the problem unbounded below. If \(w_i=0\), coordinate \(i\) is unmeasured, so a turnover cap does not restrict that trade coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative turnover weights invalidate the epigraph minimization, while zero weights leave their trade coordinates uncontrolled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite exact weighted-turnover modeling requires \(w\ge0\), and \(w>0\) is needed to control every coordinate.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative-Weight Boundary

children.title: QP-Representable Transaction-Cost Models
children.top_down_role: QP-compatible linear, piecewise-linear, or quadratic trading-cost structures.

knowledge_statements.title: QP-Representable Transaction-Cost Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex linear-plus-quadratic trading costs represented by QP variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a trade vector \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\), consider the transaction cost
\[C(d)=c^{\mathsf T}|d|+\tfrac12 d^{\mathsf T}Hd,\]
where \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n_+\) and \(H\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\). Introducing \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(u\geq d\) and \(u\geq-d\) gives the exact QP representation
\[C(d)=\min_u\{c^{\mathsf T}u+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}Hd:u\geq d,\ u\geq-d\}.\]
Thus proportional bid-ask costs and convex quadratic market-impact costs can coexist in a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative proportional trading costs plus positive-semidefinite quadratic impact have an exact convex QP formulation using absolute-value auxiliaries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(d)\) equals the displayed auxiliary-variable QP value and is convex in \(d\).

source_refs.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

source_witnesses.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient and functional-form boundaries of the transaction-cost representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The formulation \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}u+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}Hd:u\ge d,\ u\ge-d\}\) is finite and exact for every fixed \(d\) when \(c\ge0\). If some \(c_i<0\), it is unbounded below in \(u_i\). If \(H\not\succeq0\), the resulting quadratic model is not a convex QP. Discontinuous fixed-trade charges are not representable by this continuous convex-QP construction without discrete activation variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative proportional-cost coefficients make the auxiliary problem unbounded, indefinite impact loses convexity, and fixed charges require activation modeling outside continuous convex QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c\ge0\) and \(H\succeq0\) delimit the stated continuous convex-QP construction.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-QP Boundary for Trading Costs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Different nonnegative purchase and sale rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(d=d^+-d^-\), where \(d^+,d^-\ge0\). For \(c^+,c^-\ge0\), \[\sum_i\bigl(c_i^+(d_i)_++c_i^-(-d_i)_+\bigr)+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}Hd=\min\left\{(c^+)^{\mathsf T}d^++(c^-)^{\mathsf T}d^-+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}Hd:d=d^+-d^-,\ d^+,d^-\ge0\right\}.\] If \(H\succeq0\), this is a convex QP. Every optimum satisfies \(d_i^+d_i^-=0\) when \(c_i^++c_i^->0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive and negative trade variables exactly represent different nonnegative buy and sell rates; positive-semidefinite impact preserves convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The split-variable model exactly represents asymmetric proportional-plus-quadratic trading cost as a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymmetric Proportional Trading Costs

children.title: Joint Turnover-Cost QP Representations
children.top_down_role: Portfolio formulations combining turnover controls with transaction-cost terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Turnover-Cost QP Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One auxiliary system simultaneously models turnover limits and convex trading costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x,x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define \(d=x-x^0\), choose \(w,c\in\mathbb{R}^n_+\), \(H\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\), and \(\tau\geq0\), and introduce \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(u\geq d\) and \(u\geq-d\). The joint model imposes
\[w^{\mathsf T}u\leq\tau\]
and adds
\[c^{\mathsf T}u+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}Hd\]
to the objective. Whenever the remaining portfolio objective is convex quadratic and the remaining constraints are linear, the augmented problem is a convex QP. Any componentwise excess of \(u\) above \(|d|\) can be reduced to obtain \(u=|d|\) without violating the turnover constraint or increasing the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same absolute-trade auxiliaries can enforce a turnover cap and price proportional-plus-quadratic transaction costs while preserving a convex QP.
assumptions_latex: The remaining objective is convex quadratic and the remaining constraints are linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The joint turnover-cost formulation is a convex quadratic program.

notation.meaning: trade vector relative to current holdings

source_refs.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

source_witnesses.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

knowledge_statements.title: Horizon-Coupled Portfolio QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-period portfolio QP coupled by holdings dynamics and intertemporal constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\geq1\) be finite. For each \(t=1,\ldots,T\), let \(x_t,d_t\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(x_t=x_{t-1}+d_t\), where \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is fixed. Let \(Q_t,H_t\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\) and \(\mu_t,c_t\in\mathbb{R}^n\). A horizon-coupled portfolio QP has the form
\[\min_{(x_t,d_t)_{t=1}^T}\sum_{t=1}^T\left(\tfrac12x_t^{\mathsf T}Q_tx_t-\mu_t^{\mathsf T}x_t+\tfrac12d_t^{\mathsf T}H_td_t+c_t^{\mathsf T}d_t\right)\]
subject to the holdings dynamics and additional linear constraints coupling one or more periods. The stacked Hessian is positive semidefinite and all temporal coupling is linear; therefore the finite-horizon model is a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite sequences of n-dimensional holdings and trades form a convex multi-period QP when stage risk and impact matrices are positive semidefinite and all temporal coupling is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stacked finite-horizon portfolio problem is a convex quadratic program.

notation.meaning: holdings after trading in period t

source_refs.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

source_witnesses.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Convexity of the Condensed Trade Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact curvature condition for unique trades.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H_D=\bar H+L^{\mathsf T}\bar QL\) with \(\bar H,\bar Q\succeq0\), \[\ker H_D=\ker\bar H\cap\{D:LD\in\ker\bar Q\}.\] On a convex feasible trade set \(\mathcal D\), strict convexity holds exactly when \[\ker H_D\cap(\mathcal D-\mathcal D)=\{0\}.\] In particular, \(H_t\succ0\) for every period is sufficient for a unique optimal trade sequence whenever an optimum exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible trade direction must be curved by transaction impact or induced holdings risk; positive-definite impact in each period is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed kernel intersection characterizes strict convexity and unique trades.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Convexity of the Condensed Trade Model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of constant-budget holdings and self-financing trade equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x_0=B\) and \(x_t=x_{t-1}+d_t\). Then \[\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}d_t=0\quad(t=1,\ldots,T)\] if and only if \[\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x_t=B\quad(t=1,\ldots,T).\] Thus, once the initial budget and holdings dynamics are enforced, zero-net-trade equalities and per-period constant-budget holdings equalities are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Holdings dynamics make constant-budget holdings constraints equivalent to zero-net-trade constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}d_t=0\) for all \(t\) if and only if \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x_t=B\) for all \(t\).
knowledge_statements.title: Budget Propagation Through Holdings Dynamics

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination of holdings from the accepted horizon-coupled portfolio QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Stack \(D=(d_1,\ldots,d_T)\), \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_T)\), and let \(L\) be the block cumulative-sum operator, so \[X=\mathbf1_T\otimes x_0+LD.\] With \(\bar Q=\operatorname{blkdiag}(Q_1,\ldots,Q_T)\) and \(\bar H=\operatorname{blkdiag}(H_1,\ldots,H_T)\), eliminating \(X\) gives the trade Hessian \[H_D=\bar H+L^{\mathsf T}\bar QL\succeq0.\] Linear holdings-and-trades constraints remain linear. The stacked form exposes temporal sparsity, whereas the equivalent trade-only form generally has dense cross-period curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating cumulative holdings yields an equivalent trade-only QP with a PSD but generally dense cross-period Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The condensed Hessian is \(H_D=\bar H+L^{\mathsf T}\bar QL\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Trade-Only Condensed Horizon QP
Quadratic Transaction-Cost QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-period QPs with positive-semidefinite quadratic trading-impact costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\geq1\) be finite. For each \(t=1,\ldots,T\), let \(x_t,x_{t-1}\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define \(d_t=x_t-x_{t-1}\), and let \(H_t\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\) and \(h_t\in\mathbb{R}^n\). A quadratic transaction-cost term is
\[C_t(d_t)=\tfrac12d_t^{\mathsf T}H_td_t+h_t^{\mathsf T}d_t.\]
Adding \(\sum_{t=1}^T C_t(d_t)\) to a convex quadratic holdings objective, while imposing linear holdings dynamics and linear portfolio constraints, produces a convex QP in the stacked variables. If \(H_t\succ0\), the period cost is strictly convex in \(d_t\); positive definiteness of every \(H_t\) makes the aggregate cost strictly convex in the stacked trade vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over a finite horizon, positive-semidefinite quadratic trading costs preserve the convex QP structure; positive-definite impact matrices make the aggregate cost strictly convex in trades.
assumptions_latex: Holdings dynamics and other constraints are linear.
The remaining objective is convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting stacked trading model is a convex quadratic program.

source_refs.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

source_witnesses.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convexity boundary for quadratic transaction impact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C(d)=\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}Hd+h^{\mathsf T}d\), with \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), \(C\) is convex exactly when \(H\succeq0\). If \(H\) has negative curvature, the combined trading objective is convex only if its total Hessian remains positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic impact is convex exactly for a positive-semidefinite impact matrix; negative impact curvature must be offset by other objective curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\text{ is convex}\iff H\succeq0.
knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite Impact-Matrix Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate transaction impact expressed in stacked holdings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Stack \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_T)\), fix \(x_0\), and let \(D\) denote the linear part of the block first-difference map. For \(H=\operatorname{blkdiag}(H_1,\ldots,H_T)\succeq0\), the aggregate quadratic-impact Hessian in \(X\) is \(D^{\mathsf T}HD\succeq0\) and is block tridiagonal. Since \(D\) is nonsingular, \(H_t\succ0\) for every \(t\) implies \(D^{\mathsf T}HD\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic trading costs induce a positive-semidefinite block-tridiagonal holdings Hessian, positive definite when every period impact matrix is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D^{\mathsf T}HD\succeq0;\quad (\forall t,\ H_t\succ0)\Rightarrow D^{\mathsf T}HD\succ0.
knowledge_statements.title: Holdings-Space Difference-Operator Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient terminal-continuation condition for successive horizon QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a feasible date-\(k\) horizon plan is followed by its first trade. If the remaining planned tail is feasible for the shifted date-\(k+1\) constraints and a terminal continuation trade maps the old terminal state into the new terminal set while satisfying all terminal-stage constraints, then the date-\(k+1\) QP is feasible. Induction gives recursive feasibility while these shift-consistency and terminal-continuation conditions persist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shifted feasible tail plus an admissible terminal continuation is a sufficient certificate of recursive feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The state update used by the QP matches the implemented update.
Shifted forecasts and constraints preserve feasibility of the retained tail.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\in\mathcal X_k^{\mathrm{feas}}\Rightarrow x_{k+1}\in\mathcal X_{k+1}^{\mathrm{feas}}.

notation.meaning: states admitting a feasible date-k horizon plan

knowledge_statements.title: Shifted-Tail Recursive-Feasibility Condition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Generic Recursive-Feasibility or Full-Horizon Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on conclusions available from first-action execution alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Feasibility of the current horizon QP does not by itself imply feasibility after its first trade when forecasts, constraints, or terminal requirements change. Likewise, repeated first-action solutions need not equal the optimizer of a longer fixed-horizon problem and have no generic stability or performance guarantee without additional model, terminal-set, and terminal-cost assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solving each current QP is not alone enough to guarantee future feasibility, fixed-horizon optimality, stability, or a performance bound.
assumptions_latex: No shift-consistency, invariant terminal mechanism, or closed-loop performance assumptions are imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Current feasibility alone}\not\Rightarrow\text{recursive feasibility or a closed-loop performance guarantee}.
knowledge_statements.title: No Generic Recursive-Feasibility or Full-Horizon Guarantee

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy induced by repeatedly applying the first optimizer component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At date \(k\), let \(S_k(x_k)\) be the optimizer set of the current feasible horizon trading QP. The receding-horizon action is any \(d_k\in\pi_1(S_k(x_k))\), where \(\pi_1\) selects the first planned trade. After applying \(d_k\), the observed holdings and forecasts define the next QP. Thus the implemented policy can be set-valued when the horizon QP has multiple minimizers; it is single-valued when its first trade is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Receding-horizon trading repeatedly applies the first trade from the current horizon-QP solution; the induced policy may be set-valued without first-trade uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: The current horizon QP is feasible and attains a minimizer.
The implemented state is observed before the next solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_k\in\pi_1(S_k(x_k)).

knowledge_statements.title: First-Trade Receding-Horizon Policy
Receding-Horizon Trading QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-predictive trading by repeatedly solving and truncating finite-horizon QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given current holdings \(x_k\), forecasts over \(H\) periods, and a terminal convention, form at decision time \(k\) a convex horizon QP in predicted trades \((d_{k|k},\ldots,d_{k+H-1|k})\) and holdings satisfying \(x_{t+1|k}=x_{t|k}+d_{t|k}\) with \(x_{k|k}=x_k\). Solve the QP, execute only \(d_{k|k}^{\star}\), observe or estimate the new state, set
\[x_{k+1}=x_k+d_{k|k}^{\star},\]
shift the horizon, refresh forecasts, and repeat. Stop at the prescribed final trading time or when an external termination criterion is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each date, solve a forecast-horizon convex QP, execute only its first trade, update holdings and forecasts, shift the horizon, and repeat.
assumptions_latex: Each finite-horizon subproblem is a feasible convex QP.
The executed-trade holdings update is exact or replaced by an observed state.
A horizon length \(H\geq1\) and stopping convention are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs the implemented sequence \((d_{k|k}^{\star})_k\) generated by repeated first-action execution.

A source with a specific MPC or multi-period receding-horizon locator is required before the algorithmic statement can be relied upon.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Quadratic Resource Allocation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box-constrained allocation with separable convex quadratic costs and one balance equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(a_i>0\), \(b_i\in\mathbb{R}\), bounds \(\ell_i\leq u_i\), and required resource \(R\in\mathbb{R}\), the separable quadratic allocation model is
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\sum_{i=1}^n\left(\tfrac12a_ix_i^2+b_ix_i\right)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^n x_i=R,\quad \ell_i\leq x_i\leq u_i.\]
It is feasible exactly when \(\sum_i\ell_i\leq R\leq\sum_i u_i\). Under feasibility, the positive diagonal Hessian \(\operatorname{diag}(a)\) makes the objective strictly convex, so the optimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resources are allocated under box bounds and one balance equation using separable strictly convex quadratic costs; feasibility has a simple aggregate-bound test and the optimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility is equivalent to \(\sum_i\ell_i\leq R\leq\sum_i u_i\), and every feasible instance has a unique minimizer.

source_refs.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

source_witnesses.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case exact-arithmetic solution without fully sorting all breakpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A median-selection breakpoint search can maintain the aggregate affine contribution of discarded regimes, repeatedly select a median remaining breakpoint, evaluate the balance residual there, and discard the half that cannot contain a root. With linear-time median selection and bookkeeping proportional to the discarded coordinates, the optimizer is obtained in \(O(n)\) arithmetic-comparison time and \(O(n)\) storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Median breakpoint selection improves exact water filling from sorting time to worst-case linear time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The clipped balance root and }x^*\text{ can be found in }O(n)\text{ time and }O(n)\text{ storage}.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Time Breakpoint Selection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic strictly convex separable quadratic allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The clipped coordinates change regime only at \(\lambda=-b_i-a_i\ell_i\) and \(\lambda=-b_i-a_i u_i\). Sorting the \(2n\) breakpoints and scanning identifies the balance root and optimizer in \(O(n\log n)\) arithmetic-comparison time and \(O(n)\) storage. Bisection is an approximate alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sorting the bound-entry breakpoints gives an exact water-filling solution in order n log n time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Breakpoint sorting computes }x^*\text{ in }O(n\log n)\text{ time and }O(n)\text{ storage}.
knowledge_statements.title: Breakpoint Allocation Algorithm

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictly convex separable quadratic allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The unique optimizer is \(x_i^*(\lambda)=\operatorname{clip}_{[\ell_i,u_i]}(-(b_i+\lambda)/a_i)\), where \(\sum_i x_i^*(\lambda)=R\). Free coordinates satisfy \(a_ix_i^*+b_i=-\lambda\), with the corresponding one-sided inequalities at bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip each coordinate at a common balance price.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i^*=\operatorname{clip}_{[\ell_i,u_i]}(-(b_i+\lambda)/a_i),\qquad\sum_i x_i^*=R.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Allocation KKT Formula

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension from strictly convex to merely convex separable costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If some \(a_i=0\), the problem remains convex but the division-based clipping formula does not apply to those coordinates. Allocations can be nonunique when resource can move between zero-curvature coordinates with equal linear marginal cost without reaching a bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero quadratic coefficients preserve convexity but can invalidate the standard formula and uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_i=0\text{ preserves convexity but not guaranteed uniqueness or the division-based formula}.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Curvature Allocation Boundary

children.title: Quadratic-Cost Flow QPs
children.top_down_role: Network-flow templates with convex quadratic arc or node costs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-commodity flow with balances and finite lower and upper capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Shift \(f=\ell+y\), assign residual capacities \(u-\ell\), and encode \(b-B\ell\) using a super-source and super-sink. The original system is feasible iff the auxiliary maximum flow saturates every required artificial arc.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower-bounded flow feasibility reduces in polynomial time to feasible circulation or maximum flow.
assumptions_latex: Capacities and balances are finite and dimensionally compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bf=b,\ \ell\le f\le u\text{ is feasible}\iff\text{the auxiliary flow saturates all required artificial arcs}.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility by Circulation Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacitated convex quadratic flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible \(f^*\) is optimal iff there exist \(\pi\) and \(\alpha,\beta\ge0\) such that \(Qf^*+c+B^{\mathsf T}\pi-\alpha+\beta=0\), \(\alpha_i(f_i^*-\ell_i)=0\), and \(\beta_i(u_i-f_i^*)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Node potentials, capacity prices, stationarity, and complementarity form an exact optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^*\text{ is optimal}\iff\text{the displayed primal-dual conditions hold}.
knowledge_statements.title: Arc KKT Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-cost flow restricted to the affine hull of its feasible flow polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be the direction space of the affine hull of \(\{f:Bf=b,\ell\le f\le u\}\); equivalently, \(Bd=0\) and \(d_i=0\) on coordinates fixed throughout the feasible set. Every finite linear-cost perturbation has a unique optimum iff \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Universal uniqueness requires positive curvature only along capacity-compatible circulation directions.
assumptions_latex: The feasible flow polyhedron is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q|_T\succ0\iff\text{every finite linear-cost perturbation has a unique optimum}.
knowledge_statements.title: Cycle-Space Uniqueness Criterion

assumptions_latex: The directed network has node-arc incidence matrix \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\).
The balance and capacity data admit at least one \(f\) satisfying \(Bf=b\) and \(\ell\le f\le u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting optimization problem is a convex quadratic program in the arc flows.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-commodity capacitated flow with separable convex quadratic arc costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quadratic-cost flow model has the form
\[
\min_{f\in\mathbb{R}^{m}}\;\frac12 f^{\mathsf T}Qf+c^{\mathsf T}f
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
Bf=b,\qquad \ell\le f\le u.
\]
Here \(Bf=b\) enforces conservation with prescribed node injections \(b\), while the componentwise bounds impose arc capacities. Since \(Q\succeq0\), the objective is convex; the equality and bound constraints define a polyhedron. Thus every feasible instance is a convex QP, including the linear-cost case \(Q=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize convex quadratic arc costs subject to node-flow conservation and arc capacities; a positive-semidefinite cost matrix makes the model a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Cost Flow QPs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the application-specific flow template.

children.title: Network-Energy QPs
children.top_down_role: Network templates whose quadratic objective represents energy, dissipation, or potential.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic energy over a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{z:Az=d,\ Gz\le h\}\) and assume an optimum exists. The optimizer is unique iff no two distinct optimal points have a difference in \(\ker H\). A data-only sufficient condition is \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv>0\) for every nonzero \(v\in\operatorname{span}(F-F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniqueness depends on curvature along actual feasible differences, not an unspecified set of active homogeneous constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ker H\cap\{z_1-z_2:z_1,z_2\in\operatorname{argmin}_F q\}=\{0\}\iff\text{the optimizer is unique}.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Feasible-Difference Uniqueness Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic convexity versus domain-specific energy interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conditions \(H\succeq0\) and affine network constraints establish a convex QP, but do not establish that the quadratic is a physically valid energy or dissipation law. That interpretation requires domain-specific constitutive assumptions; an indefinite \(H\) additionally removes the general convexity guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-semidefinite algebra gives a convex QP, but physical energy meaning requires separate constitutive justification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\succeq0\Rightarrow\text{convex quadratic},\qquad H\succeq0\centernot\Rightarrow\text{physical validity}.
knowledge_statements.title: Physical-Energy Interpretation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Undirected weighted network energy in node-potential variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For incidence matrix \(B\) and positive diagonal edge weights \(W\), \(L=BWB^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) and \(v^{\mathsf T}Lv=\|W^{1/2}B^{\mathsf T}v\|^2\). Its nullspace consists of vectors constant on each connected component, so potentials are unique only modulo these constants unless affine reference constraints remove the gauge freedom.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted Laplacian energy has one additive-potential freedom per connected component unless the network is grounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ker(BWB^{\mathsf T})=\ker(B^{\mathsf T})=\{v:v\text{ is constant on each connected component}\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Laplacian Energy and Gauge Freedom

assumptions_latex: The network quantity is represented by \(z\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), and \(H\succeq0\) models its energy.
Network laws and operating restrictions are affine: \(Az=d\) and \(Gz\le h\).
The affine constraints are jointly feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The network-energy minimization is a convex QP, and any positive-definite restriction of \(H\) to feasible directions yields a unique optimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic affine network model with a convex quadratic energy functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A network-energy QP is represented by
\[
\min_{z\in\mathbb{R}^{m}}\;\frac12 z^{\mathsf T}Hz+r^{\mathsf T}z
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
Az=d,\qquad Gz\le h.
\]
The equalities encode linear network laws, and the inequalities encode operating limits. The matrix condition \(H\succeq0\) makes the energy functional convex. If \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv>0\) for every nonzero feasible direction \(v\) satisfying \(Av=0\) and all active homogeneous constraints, then the objective is strictly convex on the feasible set and the minimizer, when it exists, is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A network-energy QP minimizes a positive-semidefinite quadratic energy over affine network laws and operating limits; strict curvature along feasible directions ensures uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.title: Network-Energy QPs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the network-energy interpretation, and the reference to active homogeneous constraints does not precisely define the feasible directions on which strict curvature must hold.

children.title: Coupled Flow-Energy QPs
children.top_down_role: Network templates combining flow-allocation costs with energy-based quadratic structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint flow-energy quadratic with symmetric block Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H=\begin{psmallmatrix}Q&C\\C^{\mathsf T}&R\end{psmallmatrix}\), joint convexity is equivalent to \(H\succeq0\). If \(R\succ0\), this is equivalent to \(Q-CR^{-1}C^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross terms preserve convexity exactly when the full block Hessian is positive semidefinite; a Schur-complement test applies when a diagonal block is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R\succ0\Rightarrow[H\succeq0\iff Q-CR^{-1}C^{\mathsf T}\succeq0].
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Hessian Convexity Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-class boundary for physical flow-energy coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing \(Ey+Ff=g\) by a genuinely nonlinear conservation, conversion, or loss equation generally leaves the linearly constrained QP class. Affine linearization gives a QP approximation, not an equivalent model unless the original relation was affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinear flow-energy laws are not QP constraints; linearization normally yields only an approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{nonaffine coupling}\Rightarrow\text{not a linearly constrained QP in general}.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Coupling Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling equations uniquely determine energy variables from flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(E\) is nonsingular, then \(y=E^{-1}(g-Ff)\). Substitution produces an equivalent flow-only QP with Hessian \(T^{\mathsf T}HT\succeq0\), where \(T=\begin{psmallmatrix}I\\-E^{-1}F\end{psmallmatrix}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When affine coupling uniquely determines the energy state, eliminating it yields an equivalent convex flow-only QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y=E^{-1}(g-Ff),\qquad H_{\mathrm{red}}=T^{\mathsf T}HT\succeq0.

notation.meaning: affine-elimination linear map from flow to stacked variables

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Energy-State Elimination
Coupled Flow-Energy QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint flow and energy decisions connected by affine conversion or network equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\) and \(y\in\mathbb{R}^{p}\) denote the flow and energy variables, and set \(z=(f,y)\). A coupled flow-energy QP has the form
\[
\min_{f,y}\;\frac12
\begin{pmatrix}f\\y\end{pmatrix}^{\mathsf T}
H
\begin{pmatrix}f\\y\end{pmatrix}
+c_f^{\mathsf T}f+c_y^{\mathsf T}y
\]
subject to
\[
Bf=b,\qquad Ey+Ff=g,\qquad \ell\le f\le u,\qquad Gy\le h.
\]
The equations impose flow conservation and affine flow-energy coupling. Because \(H\succeq0\) and every constraint is affine, every feasible instance is a convex quadratic program. Off-diagonal blocks of \(H\) may represent quadratic interaction between \(f\) and \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stack flow and energy decisions, impose conservation, affine coupling, flow bounds, and energy limits, and minimize a jointly positive-semidefinite quadratic cost to obtain a convex QP.
assumptions_latex: The flow vector is \(f\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), the energy-variable vector is \(y\in\mathbb{R}^{p}\), and the displayed matrices and vectors have compatible dimensions.
Flow variables satisfy \(Bf=b\) and \(\ell\le f\le u\).
Energy variables and flows satisfy the affine coupling \(Ey+Ff=g\) and the affine limits \(Gy\le h\).
The joint Hessian satisfies \(H\succeq0\), and the complete constraint system is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled flow-energy model is a convex QP in the stacked variable \(z=(f,y)\).

children.title: Quadratic Dispatch QPs
children.top_down_role: Allocation templates for convex quadratic production or operating costs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiable separable convex quadratic economic dispatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C_i(p_i)=\tfrac12a_ip_i^2+c_ip_i\), a feasible \(p^*\) is optimal iff some \(\lambda\) satisfies \(a_ip_i^*+c_i=\lambda\) at interior units, \(a_i\underline p_i+c_i\ge\lambda\) at lower bounds, and \(a_i\overline p_i+c_i\le\lambda\) at upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interior units have equal marginal cost, with the corresponding one-sided inequalities at output limits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*\text{ is optimal}\iff p^*\text{ is feasible and satisfies the displayed conditions for some }\lambda.

notation.meaning: system marginal cost and balance multiplier

knowledge_statements.title: Equal-Incremental-Cost Conditions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous, lossless, single-period quadratic dispatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Binary commitment or start-up decisions generally produce an MIQP. Genuinely nonaffine loss equations or nonquadratic production costs leave the linearly constrained QP class. Affine network and ramp constraints preserve convex-QP structure when the objective Hessian remains positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete commitment and nonlinear losses leave the continuous dispatch QP, whereas affine operational constraints preserve it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{binary decisions}\Rightarrow\text{MIQP in general};\quad\text{nonaffine losses}\Rightarrow\text{not a linearly constrained QP in general}.
knowledge_statements.title: Dispatch Model-Class Boundaries

assumptions_latex: There are \(n\) dispatchable units with outputs \(p\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\).
The demand balance and unit bounds are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dispatch problem is a convex QP; it is strictly convex when every \(a_i>0\).

notation.meaning: quadratic cost coefficient of unit i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-period economic dispatch without discrete commitment or nonlinear network losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The quadratic dispatch template is
\[
\min_{p\in\mathbb{R}^{n}}\;\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(\frac12 a_i p_i^2+c_i p_i\right)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}p=D,
\qquad \underline p_i\le p_i\le\overline p_i
\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).
\]
The equality requires aggregate production to meet demand, and the bounds describe unit operating ranges. The conditions \(a_i\ge0\) make the separable objective convex. If \(a_i>0\) for every unit, the objective is strictly convex, so a feasible instance has a unique optimal dispatch vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose bounded unit outputs meeting total demand while minimizing separable convex quadratic production costs; positive quadratic coefficients give a unique dispatch.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Dispatch QPs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The single-period convex dispatch representation and uniqueness claim are coherent and appropriately scoped, but no inspectable economic-dispatch source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-period lossless dispatch with unit bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}p=D,\ \underline p\le p\le\overline p\) is feasible iff \(\sum_i\underline p_i\le D\le\sum_i\overline p_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Demand is dispatchable exactly when it lies between total minimum and maximum output.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists p\iff\sum_i\underline p_i\le D\le\sum_i\overline p_i.
knowledge_statements.title: Dispatch Capacity Feasibility

children.title: Load-Balancing QPs
children.top_down_role: Allocation templates distributing demand across resources or locations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity and uniqueness boundary for the deviation penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(W\succeq0\) and a nonzero feasible-segment direction \(d\) satisfies \(Wd=0\), the objective is constant along that segment and the optimum need not be unique. If \(W\not\succeq0\), convexity is not guaranteed; the restriction can remain convex only when all feasible directions avoid negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Null feasible curvature can cause nonuniqueness, while an indefinite weight matrix does not generally define a convex load-balancing QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Wd=0\text{ on a nontrivial feasible segment}\Rightarrow\text{nonuniqueness is possible}.
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Strict Load-Sharing Curvature

assumptions_latex: Allocation variables satisfy \(x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\), and the target aggregate load is \(D\).
The balance equation and componentwise bounds define a nonempty feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is a convex QP that balances the aggregate load while penalizing deviation from the preferred allocation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static load sharing around a prescribed allocation with affine balance and bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A load-balancing QP can be written as
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}}\;\frac12(x-r)^{\mathsf T}W(x-r)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}x=D,
\qquad \ell\le x\le u.
\]
The equality allocates the total load \(D\), while \(r\) specifies the preferred sharing pattern. With \(W\succeq0\), the deviation penalty is convex and the feasible set is polyhedral. More general affine balancing equations \(Ax=d\) may replace the scalar aggregate equation without changing the QP structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate a fixed total load within bounds while minimizing a weighted quadratic deviation from preferred sharing; the resulting model is a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.title: Load-Balancing QPs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the load-balancing leaf and is mathematically coherent, but it has no supporting source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal positive load-sharing weights and feasible aggregate demand.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_i)\) with \(w_i>0\), then \(x_i^*=\operatorname{clip}_{[\ell_i,u_i]}(r_i-\lambda^*/w_i)\), where \(\sum_i x_i^*=D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal weighted load balancing has the standard clipped multiplier solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i^*=\operatorname{clip}_{[\ell_i,u_i]}(r_i-\lambda^*/w_i).
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Projection and Clipping Formula

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=D,\ \ell\le x\le u\) is feasible iff \(\sum_i\ell_i\le D\le\sum_i u_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Demand must lie between aggregate lower and upper capacity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x\iff\sum_i\ell_i\le D\le\sum_i u_i.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Feasibility Test
