children.title: Reserve-Constrained Dispatch QPs
children.top_down_role: Dispatch templates incorporating capacity margins or reserve requirements.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-period upward reserve with shared upper capacity and no additional reserve restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R\ge0\), the displayed energy-reserve constraints are feasible iff \(\sum_i\underline p_i\le D\le\sum_i\overline p_i\) and \(R\le\sum_i\overline p_i-D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Demand must be dispatchable and aggregate unused capacity must cover reserve.
assumptions_latex: No unit-specific, zonal, ramping, or deliverability constraints are imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{feasible}\iff \sum_i\underline p_i\le D\le\sum_i\overline p_i\ \land\ R\le\sum_i\overline p_i-D.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Energy-Reserve Feasibility Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic affine reserve requirements versus richer security models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Unit reserve caps, zonal sums, and finitely many deterministic contingency inequalities preserve the convex-QP class when affine. Binary eligibility or outage logic generally produces a mixed-integer model, while unresolved probabilistic or robust requirements do not define the displayed fixed QP without an additional interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine reserve refinements remain QPs; discrete logic and unresolved uncertainty require another formulation or interpretation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{affine reserve restrictions preserve QP structure; discrete or unresolved uncertain restrictions do not in general}.
knowledge_statements.title: Reserve Requirement Modeling Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictly convex energy cost with affine or absent reserve cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strict convexity in \(p\) can make scheduled dispatch unique without making \((p,s)\) unique. If distinct feasible reserve vectors have the same optimal affine reserve cost at \(p^*\), both pairs are optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unique scheduled output does not imply unique reserve allocation when reserve variables lack strict curvature.
assumptions_latex: The energy cost is strictly convex in \(p\).
The reserve cost is affine or independent of \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*\text{ unique}\centernot\Rightarrow(p^*,s^*)\text{ unique}.
knowledge_statements.title: Reserve-Allocation Nonuniqueness

assumptions_latex: Scheduled outputs obey \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}p=D\) and \(\underline p\le p\le\overline p\).
Upward reserve variables satisfy \(s\ge0\), \(p+s\le\overline p\), and \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}s\ge R\).
The quadratic dispatch-cost matrix satisfies \(Q\succeq0\), and the constraints are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding reserve variables and linear reserve requirements preserves convex quadratic-program structure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-period dispatch with explicit upward reserve and shared unit capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A reserve-constrained dispatch QP is
\[
\min_{p,s}\;\frac12p^{\mathsf T}Qp+c^{\mathsf T}p+d^{\mathsf T}s
\]
subject to
\[
\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}p=D,
\qquad \mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}s\ge R,
\qquad \underline p\le p\le\overline p,
\qquad s\ge0,
\qquad p+s\le\overline p.
\]
The last inequality prevents scheduled output and offered upward reserve from exceeding unit capacity. Since \(Q\succeq0\), the objective is convex in \((p,s)\); all displayed constraints are affine. Hence every feasible instance is a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Co-optimize scheduled output and upward reserve under demand balance, reserve adequacy, and shared capacity limits using a convex quadratic dispatch cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Reserve-Constrained Dispatch QPs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reserve constraints preserve convex-QP structure as stated, but the application-specific formulation has no inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate for bounded exact minimum-effort allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(W\succeq0\), a feasible command \(u^*\) solves \[\min\tfrac12u^{\mathsf T}Wu\quad\text{subject to}\quad Gu=v,\ \ell\le u\le h\] if and only if there exist \(\lambda\), \(\alpha\ge0\), and \(\beta\ge0\) such that \[Wu^*+G^{\mathsf T}\lambda-\alpha+\beta=0,\quad \alpha_i(u_i^*-\ell_i)=0,\quad \beta_i(h_i-u_i^*)=0.\] Together with primal feasibility, these conditions are necessary and sufficient. If \(W\succ0\), the command is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity, bound signs, complementarity, and exact-effect feasibility certify an optimal bounded actuator command.
assumptions_latex: The exact-allocation feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed KKT system is an exact optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Allocation KKT Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient feasibility test for bounded exact allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=[\ell,h]\) and \(Z=GU=\{Gu:u\in U\}\). The constraints \(Gu=v\), \(u\in U\), are feasible if and only if \(v\in Z\). Equivalently, they are infeasible if and only if some \(y\in\mathbb R^r\) satisfies \[y^{\mathsf T}v>\max_{u\in U}y^{\mathsf T}Gu=\sum_{j=1}^m\max\{(G^{\mathsf T}y)_j\ell_j,(G^{\mathsf T}y)_jh_j\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A desired effect is achievable exactly when it lies in the bounded-actuator reachable zonotope; a separating vector certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership in \(G[\ell,h]\) is necessary and sufficient for exact allocation, and the displayed inequality certifies nonmembership.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Allocation Feasibility and Separation Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed form for the unbounded exact-allocation variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(W\succ0\) and \(v\in\operatorname{range}(G)\). Then \[\min_u\ \tfrac12u^{\mathsf T}Wu\quad\text{subject to}\quad Gu=v\] has the unique solution \[u^*=W^{-1}G^{\mathsf T}(GW^{-1}G^{\mathsf T})^{\dagger}v.\] If \(G\) has full row rank, the pseudoinverse is an ordinary inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without actuator bounds, exact minimum-effort allocation is the weighted pseudoinverse of the effectiveness map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The weighted-pseudoinverse formula gives the unique minimum-effort command.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Minimum-Effort Exact Allocation
Actuator-Allocation QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static allocation among redundant bounded actuators with soft or exact effect matching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A soft-tracking actuator-allocation QP is
\[
\min_{u\in\mathbb{R}^{m}}\;\frac12u^{\mathsf T}Wu+\frac12(Gu-v)^{\mathsf T}S(Gu-v)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\ell\le u\le h.
\]
Its Hessian is \(W+G^{\mathsf T}SG\succ0\), so the objective is strictly convex. Exact allocation is obtained by replacing the tracking penalty with the affine constraint \(Gu=v\). In either form, the actuator bounds are affine; therefore a nonempty feasible set yields a convex QP with a unique optimizer under the stated positive-definiteness assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate a desired control effect among bounded actuators by minimizing effort and tracking error; positive-definite effort weighting ensures a unique command whenever the applicable constraints are feasible.
assumptions_latex: The command is \(u\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), the desired generalized control effect is \(v\in\mathbb{R}^{r}\), and \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times m}\).
The effort matrix satisfies \(W\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^{m}\), and the tracking matrix satisfies \(S\in\mathbb{S}_{+}^{r}\).
The componentwise actuator bounds are \(\ell\le u\le h\).
For the exact-allocation variant, the constraints \(Gu=v\) and \(\ell\le u\le h\) are jointly feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The actuator-allocation model is a convex QP, and its optimizer is unique whenever the applicable feasible set is nonempty.

children.title: Linear-Quadratic Optimal-Control QPs
children.top_down_role: Finite-horizon optimal-control QPs that supply the structural prerequisite for MPC formulations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dynamic-programming solution of unconstrained finite-horizon regulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(S_N=P\). For \(k=N-1,\ldots,0\), define \[G_k=R_k+B^{\mathsf T}S_{k+1}B,\qquad K_k=G_k^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}S_{k+1}A,\] \[S_k=Q_k+A^{\mathsf T}S_{k+1}A-A^{\mathsf T}S_{k+1}BG_k^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}S_{k+1}A.\] If \(Q_k,P\succeq0\) and \(R_k\succ0\), then \(G_k\succ0\), \(S_k\succeq0\), \(u_k^*=-K_kx_k^*\), and the value from stage \(k\) is \(\tfrac12x_k^{\mathsf T}S_kx_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backward Riccati recursion computes the unique optimal inputs and quadratic value functions for unconstrained finite-horizon regulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unique optimal policy is \(u_k^*=-K_kx_k^*\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Riccati Backward Recursion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense arithmetic and storage scaling for fixed-dimensional finite-horizon regulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For dense state dimension \(n_x\) and input dimension \(n_u\), a Riccati sweep uses \[O\!\left(N(n_x^3+n_x^2n_u+n_xn_u^2+n_u^3)\right)\] arithmetic. Retaining all value matrices and gains uses \(O(N(n_x^2+n_xn_u))\) storage. For fixed \(n_x,n_u\), both bounds are linear in \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense Riccati solution scales linearly with the horizon when state and input dimensions are fixed.
assumptions_latex: All stage value matrices and gains are retained
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Arithmetic and retained-factor storage grow linearly with \(N\) for fixed dimensions.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Horizon Riccati Complexity
Finite-Horizon Regulation QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time finite-horizon regulation of a linear system to the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Finite-horizon regulation is represented by
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_N,\,u_0,\ldots,u_{N-1}}
\frac12x_N^{\mathsf T}Px_N+\frac12\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}
\left(x_k^{\mathsf T}Q_kx_k+u_k^{\mathsf T}R_ku_k\right)
\]
subject to
\[
x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k,
\qquad k=0,\ldots,N-1,
\]
with \(x_0\) fixed. The dynamics are affine equalities and the objective is convex. Because every \(R_k\succ0\), the reduced objective is strictly convex in the input sequence, so the problem has a unique optimal input sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over a finite horizon, choose inputs satisfying linear dynamics to minimize quadratic state deviation and control effort; positive-definite input weights ensure a unique optimal input sequence.
assumptions_latex: The states satisfy \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n_x}\), the inputs satisfy \(u_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n_u}\), and the dynamics are \(x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k\) for \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\), with fixed \(x_0\).
The horizon \(N\ge1\) is finite, and all matrices are dimensionally compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite-horizon linear-quadratic regulation is an equality-constrained convex QP with a unique optimal input sequence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dynamic-programming solution of unconstrained finite-horizon tracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(V_k(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}S_kx+q_k^{\mathsf T}x+c_k\), with \(S_N=P\) and \(q_N=-Pr_N\). For \(k=N-1,\ldots,0\), let \[G_k=R_k+B^{\mathsf T}S_{k+1}B,\quad K_k=G_k^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}S_{k+1}A,\] \[\ell_k=G_k^{-1}(R_ks_k-B^{\mathsf T}q_{k+1}),\] \[S_k=Q_k+A^{\mathsf T}S_{k+1}A-A^{\mathsf T}S_{k+1}BG_k^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}S_{k+1}A,\] \[q_k=-Q_kr_k+A^{\mathsf T}q_{k+1}+A^{\mathsf T}S_{k+1}B\ell_k.\] Then \(u_k^*=-K_kx_k^*+\ell_k\). The constants \(c_k\) affect values but not the optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tracking uses an affine Riccati recursion: feedback comes from quadratic curvature and feedforward from the references.
assumptions_latex: The horizon is finite and \(x_0\) is fixed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unique optimal tracking input has affine-feedback form \(u_k^*=-K_kx_k^*+\ell_k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Riccati Recursion for Tracking

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact condition for reducing tracking to homogeneous origin regulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(e_k=x_k-r_k\) and \(v_k=u_k-s_k\). Then \[e_{k+1}=Ae_k+Bv_k+\delta_k,\qquad \delta_k=Ar_k+Bs_k-r_{k+1}.\] Tracking has homogeneous error dynamics exactly when \(r_{k+1}=Ar_k+Bs_k\) at every stage. Otherwise the nonzero forcing \(\delta_k\) produces essential affine terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tracking is literally regulation in error coordinates only when the state and input references form a dynamically feasible trajectory.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Homogeneous error dynamics hold if and only if \(r_{k+1}=Ar_k+Bs_k\) for all stages.
knowledge_statements.title: Error-Coordinate Reduction Boundary

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite-horizon tracking is an equality-constrained convex QP, with affine terms determined by the references.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time linear tracking with prescribed state and input reference sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Finite-horizon tracking is represented by
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_N,\,u_0,\ldots,u_{N-1}}
\frac12(x_N-r_N)^{\mathsf T}P(x_N-r_N)
+\frac12\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}
\left((x_k-r_k)^{\mathsf T}Q_k(x_k-r_k)
+(u_k-s_k)^{\mathsf T}R_k(u_k-s_k)\right)
\]
subject to \(x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k\) for \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\), with \(x_0\) fixed. Expanding the shifted quadratic penalties produces a positive-semidefinite quadratic objective plus affine terms, while the dynamics remain affine equalities; hence the model is a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a dynamically feasible state-input trajectory minimizing weighted quadratic deviations from prescribed state and input references over a finite horizon.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Tracking QPs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-horizon tracking representation is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no inspectable optimal-control source is provided.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility and uniqueness tests for the condensed constrained-control template.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U=\{U:G_cU\leq g_c,\ E_cU=e_c\}\). Trajectory feasibility is equivalent to \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\). The objective is strictly convex on \(\mathcal U\) exactly when \[\ker H_c\cap(\mathcal U-\mathcal U)=\{0\},\] in which case any attained optimum has a unique input sequence. In particular, \(\bar R\succ0\) implies \(H_c\succ0\) and is sufficient for uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The condensed affine system exactly tests trajectory feasibility, and curvature along every feasible input difference guarantees a unique optimal control sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U\neq\varnothing\) characterizes feasibility, and the kernel test characterizes strict convexity on \(\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility and Unique-Control Conditions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Input-only elimination of states in a finite-horizon constrained-control QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_{k+1}=A_kx_k+B_ku_k+c_k\) with fixed \(x_0\), stacking gives \[X=\mathcal A x_0+\mathcal B U+\mathcal c.\] Substitution into a convex quadratic stage-terminal cost and affine trajectory constraints gives \[\min_U\ \tfrac12U^{\mathsf T}H_cU+h_c^{\mathsf T}U\quad\text{s.t.}\quad G_cU\leq g_c,\ E_cU=e_c,\] where \(H_c=\mathcal B^{\mathsf T}\bar Q\mathcal B+\bar R\succeq0\) when \(\bar Q,\bar R\succeq0\). Each feasible \(U\) determines exactly one state trajectory, so the stacked and condensed formulations have identical feasible inputs and objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the states produces an equivalent input-only convex QP, generally at the cost of denser matrices.
assumptions_latex: The horizon is finite and \(x_0\) is fixed
Dynamics and trajectory restrictions are affine
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stacked and condensed formulations are equivalent convex QPs with \(H_c\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Condensed Constrained-Control QP

assumptions_latex: The discrete-time dynamics are linear and the initial state is fixed.
Stage and terminal costs have positive-semidefinite Hessians, with positive-definite input penalties.
State, input, mixed, and terminal restrictions are affine and jointly feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constrained finite-horizon control problem is a convex QP over the stacked trajectory.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon linear-quadratic control with polyhedral trajectory constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Stack the finite-horizon states and inputs as \(z=(X,U)\). Linear dynamics, the fixed initial condition, and affine trajectory restrictions can be assembled as
\[
Ez=e,
\qquad Fz\le g.
\]
After expanding the quadratic stage and terminal costs, the constrained optimal-control problem has the form
\[
\min_z\;\frac12z^{\mathsf T}Hz+h^{\mathsf T}z
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
Ez=e,
\qquad Fz\le g,
\]
where \(H\succeq0\). Consequently the problem is a convex QP. Positive-definite input penalties provide strict curvature in the input sequence, although uniqueness of the entire stacked trajectory also depends on the dynamics and fixed initial state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stack states and inputs, encode linear dynamics and polyhedral trajectory limits, and minimize a convex quadratic finite-horizon cost to obtain a constrained-control QP.
knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Optimal-Control QPs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stacked constrained-control representation is correct in scope and appropriately avoids overstating uniqueness, but it lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: State-Space Prediction Models
children.top_down_role: MPC prediction structures retaining explicit state evolution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncondensed finite-horizon state-space representation retained in an MPC QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_{i+1}=Ax_i+Bu_i\), the decision vector \(z=(x_1,\ldots,x_N,u_0,\ldots,u_{N-1})\) satisfies a sparse block-banded system \(\mathcal Ez=d(x_0)\): its stage-\(i\) equation is \(x_{i+1}-Ax_i-Bu_i=0\), with the known \(x_0\) term moved to the right-hand side at \(i=0\). The state-state block is block bidiagonal and the input block is stage diagonal. Retaining these equations produces a sparse trajectory-space QP; eliminating the uniquely determined predicted states produces the lifted state prediction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping every predicted state and dynamics equation yields a sparse trajectory model equivalent to the lifted prediction obtained by eliminating states.
assumptions_latex: Any path constraints are imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal Ez=d(x_0)\text{ is equivalent to the horizon state recursion and has sparse block-banded structure.}
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse State-Trajectory Prediction Equations

assumptions_latex: The prediction dynamics are \(x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k\), with measured initial state \(x_0\).
The horizon is \(N\ge1\), and the matrices are dimensionally compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stacked predicted state is an affine function \(X=\mathcal A x_0+\mathcal B U\) of the initial state and stacked inputs.

notation.meaning: lifted state and input prediction matrices

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted finite-horizon prediction for a discrete-time linear time-invariant system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(X=(x_1^{\mathsf T},\ldots,x_N^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\) and \(U=(u_0^{\mathsf T},\ldots,u_{N-1}^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\). Repeated substitution in the state equation gives
\[
X=\mathcal A x_0+\mathcal B U,
\]
where
\[
\mathcal A=\begin{pmatrix}A\\A^2\\\vdots\\A^N\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\mathcal B=\begin{pmatrix}
B&0&\cdots&0\\
AB&B&\cdots&0\\
\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\
A^{N-1}B&A^{N-2}B&\cdots&B
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus the entire state prediction is affine in the measured initial state and linear in the future input sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly substitute the linear dynamics to express all predicted states as an affine function of the measured initial state and future inputs.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Space Prediction Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lifted state-space prediction matrices and indexing are coherent, but no MPC or control source with a specific locator is cited.

children.title: Input-Output Prediction Models
children.top_down_role: MPC prediction structures expressed directly through manipulated inputs and predicted outputs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition for lifted output and future-input stacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y_k=Cx_k+Du_k\) and \(U=(u_0^{\mathsf T},\ldots,u_{N-1}^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\), the output stack \(Y=(y_0^{\mathsf T},\ldots,y_{N-1}^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\) is determined by \((x_0,U)\). The alternative stack \((y_1,\ldots,y_N)\) is determined by the same \(U\) only when \(D=0\), \(u_N\) is separately supplied, or an explicit terminal-input convention is imposed; otherwise its final block contains the unspecified term \(Du_N\). For example, with scalar \(A=B=C=0\) and \(D=1\), fixed \((x_0,u_0,\ldots,u_{N-1})\) does not determine \(y_N=u_N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With direct feedthrough, outputs through index N require an input through index N; inputs only through N−1 suffice only under an additional convention or when D is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (y_1,\ldots,y_N)\text{ is not generally determined by }(x_0,u_0,\ldots,u_{N-1})\text{ when }D\ne0.
knowledge_statements.title: Direct-Feedthrough Indexing Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon lifted output model with matching output and input indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k\) and \(y_k=Cx_k+Du_k\), define \(U=(u_0^{\mathsf T},\ldots,u_{N-1}^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\) and \(Y=(y_0^{\mathsf T},\ldots,y_{N-1}^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\). Then \[Y=\mathcal O_0x_0+\mathcal T_0U,\] where, for zero-based block indices \(0\le i,j<N\), \[(\mathcal O_0)_i=CA^i,\qquad (\mathcal T_0)_{ij}=\begin{cases}D,&i=j,\\CA^{i-1-j}B,&j<i,\\0,&j>i.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching output and input indices gives an affine lifted prediction with direct feedthrough on the diagonal and Markov parameters below it.
assumptions_latex: All matrices have compatible finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y=\mathcal O_0x_0+\mathcal T_0U\text{ with the displayed causal block coefficients.}

notation.meaning: Input stack from index zero through N minus one
Output stack over the same indices

knowledge_statements.title: Consistently Indexed Lifted Input-Output Prediction

assumptions_latex: The initial state \(x_0\) is known, and the prediction horizon is \(N\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stacked predicted output satisfies \(Y=\mathcal O x_0+\mathcal T U\), with \(\mathcal T\) block lower triangular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted output prediction using outputs indexed from one through the horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For predicted outputs \(y_k=Cx_k+Du_k\), stack \(Y=(y_1^{\mathsf T},\ldots,y_N^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\) and \(U=(u_0^{\mathsf T},\ldots,u_{N-1}^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\), using the convention that \(u_N=0\) when a terminal direct-feedthrough term would otherwise occur. Then
\[
Y=\mathcal O x_0+\mathcal T U,
\]
where the block rows of \(\mathcal O\) are \(CA,CA^2,\ldots,CA^N\), and \(\mathcal T\) is block lower triangular with blocks generated by the Markov parameters \(CB,CAB,\ldots\), together with the appropriately indexed direct term \(D\). This gives an affine input-output prediction over the horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stack future outputs to obtain an affine function of the initial state and input sequence, with coefficients formed from observability and Markov parameters.
knowledge_statements.title: Input-Output Prediction Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: With outputs stacked as y_1 through y_N but inputs stacked only as u_0 through u_{N-1}, the model y_k=Cx_k+Du_k requires an unavailable u_N for y_N. Setting u_N=0 is an extra terminal convention rather than the standard lifted input-output formula, so a source and a consistent indexing convention are required.

children.title: Prediction-Representation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondences and data requirements linking the two prediction representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Data required to transfer state constraints through prediction-state elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a deterministic linear horizon model with fixed \(x_0\), eliminating predicted states transfers every polyhedral state constraint \(E_ix_i\le e_i\) exactly by substituting \(x_i=F_ix_0+G_iU\), giving \(E_i(F_ix_0+G_iU)\le e_i\). An input-output prediction model that does not retain this state map, an equivalent realization, or sufficient state information does not by itself encode arbitrary state constraints; output equality alone is insufficient whenever output-equivalent states can have different values of \(E_ix_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State constraints transfer exactly by substituting the affine state prediction; an output-only description lacking equivalent state information need not represent arbitrary state constraints.
assumptions_latex: The horizon model is deterministic, linear, and finite-dimensional.
The compared formulations must represent the same feasible trajectories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_ix_i\le e_i\iff E_i(F_ix_0+G_iU)\le e_i\text{ under exact state elimination.}
knowledge_statements.title: State-Constraint Transfer Condition
Prediction-Representation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface between lifted state-space and input-output predictions for finite-horizon MPC.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the discrete-time LTI model be \(x_{i+1}=Ax_i+Bu_i\) and \(y_i=Cx_i+Du_i\). For a finite horizon \(N\), stack \(U=(u_0,\ldots,u_{N-1})\) and \(Y=(y_0,\ldots,y_{N-1})\). Recursive substitution defines matrices \(F_N\) and \(G_N\) such that \(Y=F_Nx_0+G_NU\). Thus the lifted state-space formulation and its condensed input-output formulation produce identical predicted outputs whenever they use the same \(x_0\), \(U\), and model matrices; eliminating the uniquely determined state variables does not change the feasible input-output trajectories.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State-space recursion can be condensed into an affine map from the initial state and horizon input sequence to the correspondingly indexed predicted outputs, preserving feasible input-output trajectories.
assumptions_latex: The lifted and condensed formulations impose equivalent constraints after substitution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y=F_Nx_0+G_NU\), and the lifted and condensed formulations have the same feasible input-output trajectories.

notation.meaning: stacked inputs from indices 0 through N-1
stacked outputs from indices 0 through N-1

children.title: Incremental-Input Models
children.top_down_role: MPC formulations parameterized by changes in manipulated inputs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity and strict-convexity boundary after cumulative input reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=c+S\Delta U\), with \(S=L_N\otimes I\), and let the input-dependent objective contain \(\tfrac12U^{\mathsf T}HU+h^{\mathsf T}U+\tfrac12\Delta U^{\mathsf T}R_\Delta\Delta U\), where \(H\succeq0\) and \(R_\Delta\succeq0\). Its Hessian in incremental coordinates is \[S^{\mathsf T}HS+R_\Delta\succeq0.\] It is positive definite exactly when \(\ker(H^{1/2}S)\cap\ker(R_\Delta)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative input reconstruction preserves convexity; strict convexity fails exactly when the absolute-input and move penalties share a flat incremental direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla^2_{\Delta U}J=S^{\mathsf T}HS+R_\Delta\succeq0.
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature Under Incremental-Input Coordinates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent recursive and horizon-wide representations using input changes as MPC decision variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k\), \(y_k=Cx_k+Du_k\), define \(\Delta u_k=u_k-u_{k-1}\) and \(z_k=(x_k,u_{k-1})\). Then \[z_{k+1}=\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\0&I\end{bmatrix}z_k+\begin{bmatrix}B\\I\end{bmatrix}\Delta u_k,\qquad y_k=\begin{bmatrix}C&D\end{bmatrix}z_k+D\Delta u_k.\] Equivalently, for stacked horizon vectors, \[U=(\mathbf1_N\otimes I)u_{-1}+(L_N\otimes I)\Delta U,\] where \(L_N\) is unit lower triangular. Thus move bounds are direct bounds on \(\Delta U\), while absolute-input bounds remain affine inequalities after cumulative lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Augmenting the state with the previous input or cumulatively summing input moves gives equivalent linear incremental-input models, with both move and absolute-input bounds remaining affine.
assumptions_latex: u_{-1}\text{ is known at the start of the horizon}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U=(\mathbf1_N\otimes I)u_{-1}+(L_N\otimes I)\Delta U\text{ and the recursive realization is linear in }\Delta u_k.

notation.meaning: Plant state augmented with the preceding input

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental-Input Realization and Cumulative Lifting
Incremental-Input Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LTI prediction model using input increments as MPC decision variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k\), define \(\Delta u_k=u_k-u_{k-1}\) and \(z_k=(x_k,u_{k-1})\). children.title: Integral-Action Augmentations
children.top_down_role: Augmented prediction structures supporting accumulated error or disturbance states.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: PBH rank test for the stabilizability of the output-error integral augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A_a=\begin{bmatrix}A&0\\C&I_p\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B_a=\begin{bmatrix}B\\0\end{bmatrix}\), the pair \((A_a,B_a)\) is stabilizable exactly when \((A,B)\) has no uncontrollable eigenvalue \(\lambda\ne1\) with \(|\lambda|\ge1\) and \[\operatorname{rank}\begin{bmatrix}I-A&B\\C&0\end{bmatrix}=n+p.\] Rank loss is the unit-mode obstruction introduced by the integrators, equivalently a blocking invariant zero at \(z=1\) for the integrated outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integral augmentation is stabilizable exactly when the plant's unstable modes are stabilizable and no blocking zero at one obstructs the integrated outputs.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n},\ B\in\mathbb R^{n\times m},\ C\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (A_a,B_a)\text{ is stabilizable}\iff\operatorname{rank}\begin{bmatrix}I-A&B\\C&0\end{bmatrix}=n+p\text{ and all other unstable plant modes are stabilizable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Stabilizability Boundary for Output Integrators

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear prediction augmentation exposing accumulated output tracking error to the MPC objective and constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k\), \(y_k=Cx_k\), introduce \(\eta_{k+1}=\eta_k+y_k-r_k\) and \(z_k=(x_k,\eta_k)\). Then \[z_{k+1}=\begin{bmatrix}A&0\\C&I\end{bmatrix}z_k+\begin{bmatrix}B\\0\end{bmatrix}u_k+\begin{bmatrix}0\\-I\end{bmatrix}r_k.\] For a fixed reference sequence this remains a linear-affine prediction model and preserves the convex-QP class under positive-semidefinite quadratic penalties and affine constraints. The augmentation alone does not guarantee offset-free tracking or closed-loop stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Appending an output-error integrator makes accumulated tracking error available to MPC while retaining a linear QP model, but does not alone guarantee stability or zero offset.
assumptions_latex: r_k\text{ has the same dimension as }y_k\text{ and is fixed prediction data}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_{k+1}=A_az_k+B_au_k+E_ar_k.

children.title: Regulation Models
children.top_down_role: MPC QPs centered on stabilization near a fixed operating condition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: MPC QP centered on the origin or a fixed feasible state-input equilibrium.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x_s,u_s)\) satisfy \(x_s=Ax_s+Bu_s\), and define \(e_i=x_i-x_s\), \(v_i=u_i-u_s\). Then \(e_{i+1}=Ae_i+Bv_i\). A regulation model minimizes \[\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}(e_i^{\mathsf T}Qe_i+v_i^{\mathsf T}Rv_i)+e_N^{\mathsf T}Pe_N\] subject to the initial deviation and state-input constraints translated by \((x_s,u_s)\). If \(Q,R,P\succeq0\) and the constraints are affine, this is a convex QP. Positive definiteness or suitable reduced-space curvature is additionally required for uniqueness; the finite-horizon objective alone does not establish closed-loop convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regulation MPC penalizes deviations from a feasible equilibrium and forms a convex QP under positive-semidefinite weights and affine constraints, without by itself guaranteeing uniqueness or stability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_{i+1}=Ae_i+Bv_i\text{ and the finite-horizon regulation model is a convex QP}.

children.title: Reference-Tracking Models
children.top_down_role: MPC QPs centered on following prescribed state, output, or input references.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex MPC QP for feasible or arbitrary fixed state-input reference sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed sequences \((x_i^r,u_i^r)\), define \(e_i=x_i-x_i^r\), \(v_i=u_i-u_i^r\), and \(w_i=Ax_i^r+Bu_i^r-x_{i+1}^r\). Then \[e_{i+1}=Ae_i+Bv_i+w_i.\] A tracking objective \[\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}(e_i^{\mathsf T}Qe_i+v_i^{\mathsf T}Rv_i)+e_N^{\mathsf T}Pe_N\] with \(Q,R,P\succeq0\), together with translated affine constraints, defines a convex QP. The reference is dynamically feasible exactly when \(w_i=0\) at every stage; dynamic infeasibility otherwise creates a known affine forcing term but does not by itself destroy the QP form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tracking MPC optimizes deviations from a fixed reference; reference defects appear as known affine forcing terms, while convex quadratic weights and affine constraints preserve the QP structure.
assumptions_latex: The original prediction constraints are affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_{i+1}=Ae_i+Bv_i+w_i,\quad w_i=0\ \forall i\iff (x_i^r,u_i^r)\text{ is dynamically feasible}.

children.title: Offset-Free Models
children.top_down_role: MPC QPs incorporating disturbance or target structures intended to remove steady-state offset.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear-algebraic feasibility and uniqueness test for the corrected steady target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(\hat d\) and \(r\), the corrected target equations are solvable exactly when \[\begin{bmatrix}B_d\hat d\\r-C_d\hat d\end{bmatrix}\in\operatorname{range}\begin{bmatrix}I-A&-B\\C&0\end{bmatrix}.\] If this range condition fails, no exact disturbance-consistent equilibrium target exists. If the block matrix has full column rank, a feasible target is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A corrected steady target exists exactly when its right-hand side lies in the range of the steady-state plant matrix; full column rank additionally gives uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: (x_s,u_s)\text{ must satisfy the stated equilibrium and output equations}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists(x_s,u_s)\iff\begin{bmatrix}B_d\hat d\\r-C_d\hat d\end{bmatrix}\in\operatorname{range}\begin{bmatrix}I-A&-B\\C&0\end{bmatrix}.
knowledge_statements.title: Disturbance-Aware Steady-Target Solvability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disturbance-state augmentation, corrected steady-target calculation, and conditional zero-offset conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use the augmented model \[x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k+B_dd_k,\qquad y_k=Cx_k+C_dd_k,\qquad d_{k+1}=d_k.\] Given an estimate \(\hat d_k\) and constant reference \(r\), choose a steady target satisfying \[x_s=Ax_s+Bu_s+B_d\hat d_k,\qquad r=Cx_s+C_d\hat d_k,\] and regulate \((x,u)\) toward \((x_s,u_s)\). If the persistent plant-model mismatch is representable by a constant \(d\), \(\hat d_k\) converges to the corresponding value, the target remains feasible, and the regulated closed loop converges to that target, then \(y_k-r\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant-disturbance estimate and disturbance-corrected steady target yield zero asymptotic tracking error when the mismatch is representable and estimation, feasibility, and regulation converge.
assumptions_latex: The persistent mismatch is representable by the stated constant disturbance model.
\hat d_k\text{ converges to the disturbance value consistent with the plant output}.
The corrected steady-target equations remain feasible.
The regulated closed loop converges to the corrected target.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lim_{k\to\infty}(y_k-r)=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Data Reuse Boundary for LTI MPC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reusable numerical structure specific to a fixed LTI horizon model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(A,B,N\), quadratic weights, and affine-constraint geometry, the condensed LTI MPC matrices \(H\) and \(M\), together with their sparsity patterns, are independent of the measured initial state. Matrix assembly and symbolic factorizations may therefore be reused across samples. A numerical factorization is reusable only while the solver coefficient matrix itself remains unchanged; changes in an active set, barrier diagonal, regularization, horizon, model, weights, or constraint geometry generally invalidate it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed LTI MPC data permit offline matrix assembly and structural reuse, but numerical factors can be cached only while the actual solver matrix remains unchanged.
assumptions_latex: A fixed finite horizon and fixed LTI model are used.
Weights and affine-constraint geometry remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\text{ and }M\text{ are sample-invariant; numerical-factor reuse additionally requires an unchanged coefficient matrix.}
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Data Reuse Boundary for LTI MPC
LTI MPC QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condensed convex QP generated by an LTI prediction model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_{i+1}=Ax_i+Bu_i\), stack the horizon inputs into \(U\) and write the predicted states as \(X=F_Nx_0+G_NU\). Substitution into a convex quadratic stage-terminal objective and affine state-input constraints gives \[\min_U\ \tfrac12U^{\mathsf T}HU+(h+Sx_0)^{\mathsf T}U\quad\text{subject to}\quad MU\le b+Ex_0.\] The matrices \(H,M,S,E\) are fixed across sampling instants for fixed horizon, model, weights, and constraint geometry, and \(H\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Condensing an LTI prediction model yields a parametric convex QP whose matrices remain fixed while the initial-state-dependent vectors change.
assumptions_latex: The horizon and LTI model are fixed.
State and input constraints are affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_U \tfrac12U^{\mathsf T}HU+(h+Sx_0)^{\mathsf T}U\) subject to \(MU\le b+Ex_0\), with \(H\succeq0\).

children.title: Stage Quadratic Penalties
children.top_down_role: Quadratic MPC penalties accumulated across intermediate horizon stages.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of changing state and input references in a fixed stage quadratic penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_i=(x_i,u_i)\), \(r_i=(x_i^r,u_i^r)\), and \(W_i=W_i^{\mathsf T}\). Then \[\ell_i(y_i)=(y_i-r_i)^{\mathsf T}W_i(y_i-r_i)=y_i^{\mathsf T}W_i y_i-2r_i^{\mathsf T}W_i y_i+r_i^{\mathsf T}W_i r_i.\] Hence \(\nabla^2\ell_i=2W_i\): changing references changes only linear and constant coefficients and leaves all curvature properties unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing stage references alters affine objective data but not the stage Hessian or curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla^2_{y_i}\ell_i=2W_i\quad\text{independently of }r_i.
knowledge_statements.title: Reference Translation Preserves Stage Curvature

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Schur-Complement Criterion for Convex Stage Cross Terms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional equivalent test for convexity of a joint state-input stage weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W_i=\begin{bmatrix}Q_i&S_i\\S_i^{\mathsf T}&R_i\end{bmatrix}\), where \(Q_i=Q_i^{\mathsf T}\) and \(R_i=R_i^{\mathsf T}\succ0\). Then \[W_i\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Q_i-S_iR_i^{-1}S_i^{\mathsf T}\succeq0.\] Thus, with positive-definite input weight, admissible state-input cross weighting is characterized exactly by the state-side Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive-definite input weight, a stage quadratic containing state-input cross terms is convex exactly when its state-side Schur complement is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\begin{bmatrix}Q_i&S_i\\S_i^{\mathsf T}&R_i\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\iff Q_i-S_iR_i^{-1}S_i^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: State-side Schur complement of the input-weight block

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Criterion for Convex Stage Cross Terms

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Completed-Square Form of a Stage Cross Term
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent stage-cost representation when the input weight is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e_x=x_i-x_i^r\), \(e_u=u_i-u_i^r\), and \(R_i\succ0\). Then \[e_x^{\mathsf T}Q_ie_x+2e_x^{\mathsf T}S_ie_u+e_u^{\mathsf T}R_ie_u=(e_u+R_i^{-1}S_i^{\mathsf T}e_x)^{\mathsf T}R_i(e_u+R_i^{-1}S_i^{\mathsf T}e_x)+e_x^{\mathsf T}(Q_i-S_iR_i^{-1}S_i^{\mathsf T})e_x.\] This exposes the Schur-complement convexity condition and interprets the cross term as a state-dependent shift of the input-tracking error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive-definite input weight, a stage cross term becomes a shifted input square plus a Schur-complement state penalty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell_i=(e_u+R_i^{-1}S_i^{\mathsf T}e_x)^{\mathsf T}R_i(e_u+R_i^{-1}S_i^{\mathsf T}e_x)+e_x^{\mathsf T}(Q_i-S_iR_i^{-1}S_i^{\mathsf T})e_x.
knowledge_statements.title: Completed-Square Form of a Stage Cross Term

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized Schur-Complement Criterion for Singular Input Weights
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact positive-semidefiniteness test for a joint stage weight when the input block may be singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W_i=\begin{bmatrix}Q_i&S_i\\S_i^{\mathsf T}&R_i\end{bmatrix}\), with \(Q_i=Q_i^{\mathsf T}\) and \(R_i=R_i^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). Then
\[
W_i\succeq0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(I-R_iR_i^{\dagger})S_i^{\mathsf T}=0
\quad\text{and}\quad
Q_i-S_iR_i^{\dagger}S_i^{\mathsf T}\succeq0.
\]
Thus a cross term may couple only through directions in \(\operatorname{range}(R_i)\); otherwise the stage quadratic is nonconvex even when both diagonal blocks are positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a singular positive-semidefinite input weight, convexity requires the cross term to lie in its range and the generalized Schur complement to be positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_i\succeq0\iff (I-R_iR_i^{\dagger})S_i^{\mathsf T}=0\ \text{and}\ Q_i-S_iR_i^{\dagger}S_i^{\mathsf T}\succeq0.\)

notation.meaning: Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of the input-weight block
Range-compatibility condition for the stage cross term

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Schur-Complement Criterion for Singular Input Weights
Stage Quadratic Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex per-stage penalty used in finite-horizon MPC QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For predicted state \(x_i\), input \(u_i\), and references \(x_i^r,u_i^r\), a stage quadratic penalty is \[\ell_i(x_i,u_i)=(x_i-x_i^r)^{\mathsf T}Q_i(x_i-x_i^r)+(u_i-u_i^r)^{\mathsf T}R_i(u_i-u_i^r)+2(x_i-x_i^r)^{\mathsf T}S_i(u_i-u_i^r).\] It is convex exactly when the symmetric block matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}Q_i&S_i\\S_i^{\mathsf T}&R_i\end{bmatrix}\) is positive semidefinite. The common separable case has \(S_i=0\), \(Q_i\succeq0\), and \(R_i\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stage penalty is a quadratic form in state and input tracking errors; it is convex precisely when its joint block Hessian is positive semidefinite.
assumptions_latex: All weighting matrices have compatible finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_i\) is convex if and only if \(\begin{bmatrix}Q_i&S_i\\S_i^{\mathsf T}&R_i\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: stage penalty at prediction index i

children.title: Terminal Quadratic Penalties
children.top_down_role: Quadratic MPC penalties applied at the horizon endpoint.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expansion of a fixed terminal quadratic about an arbitrary terminal reference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\) and reference \(r\), \[V_f(x)=(x-r)^{\mathsf T}P(x-r)=x^{\mathsf T}Px-2r^{\mathsf T}Px+r^{\mathsf T}Pr.\] Consequently \(\nabla^2V_f=2P\): changing the terminal reference alters only linear and constant coefficients and cannot change convexity, strict convexity, or null-curvature directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing the terminal reference translates the quadratic but leaves its Hessian and curvature classification unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla^2V_f=2P\quad\text{independently of }r.
knowledge_statements.title: Reference Translation Preserves Terminal Curvature

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nullspace Characterization of Unpenalized Terminal Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies terminal-state errors invisible to a positive-semidefinite terminal weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) and \(V_f(x)=(x-r)^{\mathsf T}P(x-r)\). Then \[V_f(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad P(x-r)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x-r\in\ker P.\] Hence a singular terminal weight permits nonzero terminal errors with zero terminal cost, whereas \(P\succ0\) makes \(r\) the unique zero-cost terminal state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite terminal penalty ignores exactly the terminal-error directions in the weight matrix's nullspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_f(x)=0\iff x-r\in\ker P\); if \(P\succ0\), then \(V_f(x)=0\iff x=r\).

notation.meaning: Nullspace of the terminal weight matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Nullspace Characterization of Unpenalized Terminal Errors

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminal quadratic expressed in condensed MPC decision variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the terminal prediction is affine in a condensed decision vector \(U\): \(x_N=\Phi x_0+\Gamma U+d\). For terminal reference \(r_N\) and \(P\succeq0\), \[V_f(U)=(\Phi x_0+\Gamma U+d-r_N)^{\mathsf T}P(\Phi x_0+\Gamma U+d-r_N).\] Its condensed Hessian contribution is \(2\Gamma^{\mathsf T}P\Gamma\succeq0\), and its null-curvature directions are exactly the vectors \(v\) satisfying \(P^{1/2}\Gamma v=0\). Hence \(P\succ0\) need not make the condensed input objective strictly convex when \(\Gamma\) has a nontrivial nullspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After state elimination, the terminal penalty contributes the positive-semidefinite matrix \(2\Gamma^TP\Gamma\); even a positive-definite terminal weight may leave condensed decision directions unpenalized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla_U^2V_f=2\Gamma^{\mathsf T}P\Gamma\succeq0,\qquad v^{\mathsf T}\nabla_U^2V_fv=0\iff P^{1/2}\Gamma v=0.

notation.meaning: Terminal-state sensitivity to the condensed decision vector

knowledge_statements.title: Condensed Terminal-Penalty Contribution
Terminal Quadratic Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic endpoint penalty in a finite-horizon MPC objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For terminal predicted state \(x_N\) and terminal reference \(x_N^r\), a terminal quadratic penalty is \[V_f(x_N)=(x_N-x_N^r)^{\mathsf T}P(x_N-x_N^r),\] where \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). It is a convex function of \(x_N\), and it is strictly convex exactly when \(P\succ0\). When \(P\) is chosen as a control-Lyapunov or Riccati matrix and paired with compatible terminal ingredients, additional stability claims may hold; those claims are not implied by positive semidefiniteness alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A terminal penalty is a positive-semidefinite quadratic form in terminal state error; convexity alone does not establish closed-loop stability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_f\) is convex, and it is strictly convex if and only if \(P\succ0\).

children.title: Stage-Terminal Weighting Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cost structures distinguished by the relative emphasis placed on intermediate and terminal behavior.

assumptions_latex: The stage and terminal weights satisfy \(Q_k\succeq0\), \(R_k\succeq0\), and \(P\succeq0\).
The predicted states are affine functions of the QP decision variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting finite-horizon objective is a convex quadratic function; it is strictly convex in the input sequence when its reduced input Hessian is positive definite.

notation.meaning: Predicted state and input at stage k
Stage state, stage input, and terminal weights

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex stage-terminal quadratic weighting for finite-horizon linear MPC.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For predicted pairs \((x_k,u_k)\), references \((\bar x_k,\bar u_k)\), and terminal reference \(\bar x_N\), define \[J_N=\frac12\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\!\left(\lVert x_k-\bar x_k\rVert_{Q_k}^{2}+\lVert u_k-\bar u_k\rVert_{R_k}^{2}\right)+\frac12\lVert x_N-\bar x_N\rVert_P^{2}.\] Here \(\lVert v\rVert_M^2=v^{\mathsf T}Mv\). The semidefinite regime permits zero or singular weights. A strictly convex input-weighting regime requires the Hessian obtained after substituting the affine prediction dynamics to be positive definite; the sufficient condition \(R_k\succ0\) for every \(k\) guarantees this property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive semidefinite stage and terminal weights produce a convex MPC objective; positive definite reduced input curvature yields a unique minimizing input sequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Stage-Terminal Weighting Regimes

children.title: Polyhedral Path Constraints
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral restrictions applied across intermediate prediction stages.

assumptions_latex: For each stage, \(G_k^x\), \(G_k^u\), and \(g_k\) have compatible finite dimensions.
The dynamics and any variable substitutions are affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The path-feasible set is polyhedral, and its intersection with affine dynamics remains a polyhedron.

notation.meaning: Predicted state and input at stage k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stage-separable linear inequalities in a sparse MPC trajectory formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Polyhedral path constraints over a horizon \(N\) have the stagewise form \[G_k^x x_k+G_k^u u_k\le g_k,\qquad k=0,\ldots,N-1.\] With the trajectory variables stacked into \(z\), these inequalities are equivalently \(G_{\mathrm{path}}z\le g_{\mathrm{path}}\), where each row block of \(G_{\mathrm{path}}\) acts only on the variables of its stage. Consequently the path-feasible set is a polyhedron. Adding affine dynamics equalities preserves polyhedrality, although eliminating the state variables may convert the stage-sparse inequality matrix into a dense matrix in the input variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagewise linear state-input inequalities stack into a polyhedral path-feasible set; eliminating states can destroy the visible stage sparsity.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Path Constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric separability of stage-local path restrictions before horizon dynamics are imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each stage define \(\mathcal P_k:=\{(x_k,u_k):G_k^xx_k+G_k^uu_k\le g_k\}\). Before dynamics equalities are imposed, the path-feasible set is exactly \(\prod_{k=0}^{N-1}\mathcal P_k\). Intersecting this product with consecutive-stage affine dynamics preserves polyhedrality but generally destroys Cartesian-product separability because each dynamics equality couples adjacent stage blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stage-local path restrictions form a Cartesian product before dynamics are imposed; affine dynamics preserve polyhedrality but couple adjacent factors.
assumptions_latex: Every path inequality uses variables from one stage only.
All path restrictions and dynamics are affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal P_{\mathrm{path}}=\prod_{k=0}^{N-1}\mathcal P_k\text{ before dynamics, while the dynamics-constrained set is polyhedral but generally nonproduct.}
knowledge_statements.title: Product Structure Before Dynamics Coupling

children.title: Polyhedral Terminal Constraints
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral restrictions applied to the final predicted state or output.

assumptions_latex: The terminal-set data satisfy \(F_f\in\mathbb{R}^{q_f\times n}\) and \(f_f\in\mathbb{R}^{q_f}\).
The terminal prediction \(x_N\) depends affinely on the QP variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The terminal restriction is a finite system of affine inequalities and therefore preserves the convex-QP model class.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite polyhedral restrictions imposed on the last predicted state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polyhedral terminal constraint is specified by \[x_N\in\mathcal X_f:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:F_f x\le f_f\}.\] If the terminal prediction has the affine representation \(x_N=Tz+t\), then the same restriction is \(F_fTz\le f_f-F_ft\). Thus it contributes finitely many affine inequalities to the horizon problem and preserves convex quadratic-program structure. Unlike a path constraint, its rows act only on \(x_N\) in the sparse trajectory formulation, but they generally involve every earlier input after state elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral terminal set becomes finitely many affine inequalities in either sparse trajectory variables or condensed input variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Terminal Constraints

children.title: Coupled Path-Terminal Constraint Regimes
children.top_down_role: MPC feasible regions shaped jointly by horizon-wide and endpoint restrictions.

assumptions_latex: All coupling matrices have compatible finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coupled path-terminal regimes remain polyhedral but need not retain stagewise block separability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear inequalities that jointly involve multiple stages and the terminal state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coupled path-terminal constraint regime is represented by \[Cz\le h,\] or, row block by row block, by inequalities of the form \[\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}(E_kx_k+F_ku_k)+E_Nx_N\le h.\] This representation includes separate path and terminal constraints when each row has support in only one stage block. If some row has support in multiple stage blocks, the feasible set is still polyhedral, but the corresponding constraint is not stage separable and may introduce long-range coupling into the KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear inequalities may couple several stages and the terminal state; feasibility stays polyhedral while stagewise sparsity can be lost.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Path-Terminal Constraint Regimes

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pure Quadratic Slack Penalties Need Not Be Exact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite exactness when violation is penalized only quadratically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the hard problem \(\min\{(x-1)^2:x\le0\}\), whose unique solution is \(x^*=0\). Its quadratic-slack softening \[\min_{x,s}\ (x-1)^2+\rho s^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\le s,\quad s\ge0\] has, for every finite \(\rho>0\), the unique solution \(x=s=(1+\rho)^{-1}>0\). Hence no finite pure quadratic penalty parameter enforces the hard inequality exactly in this example.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unlike a sufficiently large linear slack penalty, a finite purely quadratic penalty can retain a positive optimal violation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_\rho=s_\rho=(1+\rho)^{-1}>0\quad\text{for every finite }\rho>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Pure Quadratic Slack Penalties Need Not Be Exact

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness of the one-sided linear slack penalty for a feasible convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(z)=\tfrac12z^{\mathsf T}Hz+c^{\mathsf T}z\) with \(H\succeq0\), and suppose \(z^*\) solves \(\min\{f(z):Az\le b\}\) with a KKT multiplier \(\lambda^*\ge0\). Consider \[\min_{z,s}\ f(z)+\rho\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s\quad\text{subject to}\quad Az-b\le s,\quad s\ge0.\] If \(\rho\ge\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\), then \((z^*,0)\) is optimal for the softened problem. If \(\rho>\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\), every softened optimum has \(s=0\) and its \(z\)-component solves the hard QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear slack penalty is exact once its coefficient dominates an optimal hard-constraint multiplier; strict domination forces every softened optimum to have zero violation.
assumptions_latex: The hard QP has an optimizer \(z^*\) and a KKT multiplier \(\lambda^*\ge0\).
The softened inequalities are \(Az-b\le s\) with \(s\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho\ge\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\Rightarrow(z^*,0)\text{ is soft-problem optimal};\quad \rho>\|\lambda^*\|_\infty\Rightarrow s=0\text{ at every soft optimum}.

notation.meaning: Optimal multiplier vector for the hard inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Linear-Slack Penalty Threshold

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Slack Elimination as Linear-Plus-Squared Hinge Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent reduced objective for separably penalized one-sided violation slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w_i>0\) and \(\rho_i\ge0\), consider \[\min_{z,s}\ f(z)+\sum_{i=1}^m\left(\rho_i s_i+\tfrac12w_i s_i^2\right)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Az-b\le s,\quad s\ge0.\] For fixed \(z\), the unique minimizing slack is \(s_i(z)=[(Az-b)_i]_+\). Eliminating \(s\) gives the equivalent objective \[f(z)+\sum_{i=1}^m\left(\rho_i[(Az-b)_i]_++\tfrac12w_i[(Az-b)_i]_+^2\right).\] Constraints not assigned slacks remain imposed explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating positive, separably penalized slacks yields linear-plus-squared hinge penalties on the softened violations.
assumptions_latex: Only the listed inequalities receive slack variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s_i(z)=[(Az-b)_i]_+,\quad\text{and the lifted and reduced problems have the same optimal }z\text{-components}.
knowledge_statements.title: Slack Elimination as Linear-Plus-Squared Hinge Penalties

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Softening Selected Inequalities Does Not Guarantee Overall Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes relaxability of softened rows from feasibility of the complete lifted MPC QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the constraints into softened inequalities \(A_sz\le b_s\) and hard constraints \(A_hz\le b_h\), \(Ez=e\). The lift \[A_sz\le b_s+s,\qquad s\ge0,\qquad A_hz\le b_h,\qquad Ez=e\] is feasible if and only if there exists \(z\) satisfying \(A_hz\le b_h\) and \(Ez=e\). For any such \(z\), \(s=[A_sz-b_s]_+\) satisfies every softened row. Thus slackening selected inequalities cannot repair inconsistency among constraints left hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Violation slacks make their assigned inequalities relaxable, but the lifted QP is feasible exactly when its hard subsystem is feasible.
assumptions_latex: Only the rows \(A_sz\le b_s\) receive unrestricted nonnegative violation slacks.
All variables and constraint data are finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists(z,s)\text{ feasible for the lift}\iff\exists z:\ A_hz\le b_h,\ Ez=e\).
knowledge_statements.title: Softening Selected Inequalities Does Not Guarantee Overall Feasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex slack lifting of finite affine interval constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A two-sided affine constraint \(\ell\le Az\le u\) may be softened with separate slacks \(s^-,s^+\ge0\) as \[\ell-s^-\le Az\le u+s^+.\] Adding \[\rho_-^{\mathsf T}s^-+\rho_+^{\mathsf T}s^++\tfrac12(s^-)^{\mathsf T}W_-s^-+\tfrac12(s^+)^{\mathsf T}W_+s^+\] with \(\rho_\pm\ge0\) and \(W_\pm\succeq0\) preserves convex-QP structure whenever the original objective Hessian is positive semidefinite. For fixed \(z\), the componentwise least feasible slacks are \[s^-=[\ell-Az]_+,
\qquad s^+=[Az-u]_+.\] They are the unique penalty-minimizing slacks when each separable slack penalty is strictly increasing on \([0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate lower- and upper-violation slacks yield a convex QP lift of two-sided affine constraints; their least feasible values are the corresponding positive-part violations.
assumptions_latex: The original objective is convex quadratic.
Uniqueness of the penalty-minimizing slack requires each separable slack penalty to be strictly increasing on \([0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s^-_{\min}=[\ell-Az]_+,\qquad s^+_{\min}=[Az-u]_+,
review_flags: Zero or merely nondecreasing slack penalties need not select the least feasible slack uniquely.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Soft-Constraint QP Lift

assumptions_latex: The original objective is \(\frac12z^{\mathsf T}Hz+c^{\mathsf T}z\) with \(H\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted model is a convex QP and is feasible with respect to the softened inequalities for every finite \(z\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided slack lifting of affine MPC inequalities with convex penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The one-sided soft-constraint lift of \(Az\le b\) introduces \(s\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and solves \[\min_{z,s}\;\frac12z^{\mathsf T}Hz+c^{\mathsf T}z+\rho\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}s+\frac12s^{\mathsf T}Ws\quad\text{subject to}\quad Az\le b+s,\quad s\ge0.\] Its Hessian is \(\operatorname{diag}(H,W)\succeq0\), and all added constraints are affine, so the lift is a convex QP. For any finite \(z\), choosing \(s_i\ge\max\{0,(Az-b)_i\}\) satisfies every softened inequality. Constraints not assigned slacks remain hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative violation slacks and convex linear-quadratic penalties convert selected hard affine inequalities into an always-relaxable convex QP lift.
knowledge_statements.title: Soft-Constraint QP Lifts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lift is mathematically coherent, convex under the stated assumptions, and always relaxes the selected inequalities. However, the cited generic convex-inequalities section does not specifically substantiate the soft-constraint construction, penalty model, or QP-lift interpretation; an inspectable soft-constrained QP or MPC source is required.

children.title: Terminal-Set Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Modeling interfaces connecting MPC QPs to prescribed terminal feasible sets.

assumptions_latex: The terminal set is the polyhedron \(\mathcal X_f=\{x:F_fx\le f_f\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The terminal-set interface contributes the affine QP constraint \(F_fTz\le f_f-F_ft\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic interface between a terminal set and the horizon QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the horizon model expose its last predicted state through \(x_N=Tz+t\), and let \(\mathcal X_f=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:F_fx\le f_f\}\). The terminal-set interface is the substitution \[x_N\in\mathcal X_f\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F_fTz\le f_f-F_ft.\] In a sparse formulation where \(x_N\) is itself a decision block, this reduces to \(F_fx_N\le f_f\). Hence a finitely represented polyhedral terminal set enters the MPC model solely through affine inequalities and preserves the convex-QP class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substituting the affine terminal prediction into a polyhedral terminal set gives the terminal inequality block of the MPC QP.
knowledge_statements.title: Terminal-Set Interfaces

children.title: Invariant-Set Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Modeling interfaces connecting MPC QPs to controlled or positively invariant sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite linear implication test for an affine terminal controller on polyhedral sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X_f=\{x:H_fx\le h_f\}\), \(\mathcal Z=\{(x,u):G_xx+G_uu\le g\}\), and \(\kappa(x)=Kx+k\). The terminal interface conditions are exactly the two polyhedral inclusions \[\mathcal X_f\subseteq\{x:(G_x+G_uK)x\le g-G_uk\},\qquad (A+BK)\mathcal X_f+Bk\subseteq\mathcal X_f.\] Each inclusion can be checked row by row by linear programming; equivalently, every target inequality must have a finite maximum over \(\mathcal X_f\) no larger than its right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With polyhedral terminal and admissible sets and affine feedback, admissibility and invariance reduce to finitely many linear programs.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X_f\) and \(\mathcal Z\) have finite polyhedral inequality representations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Terminal admissibility and invariance hold iff the displayed polyhedral inclusions hold, and these are decidable by finitely many LPs.}
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Affine-Feedback Invariance Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Terminal Invariance Gives the Shifted Feasibility Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step recursive-feasibility mechanism supplied by a valid terminal controller and invariant terminal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k\) with admissible set \(\mathcal Z\). Suppose a feasible horizon-\(N\) prediction \((x_0,u_0,\ldots,u_{N-1},x_N)\) satisfies \(x_N\in\mathcal X_f\). If a terminal law \(\kappa\) satisfies \((x,\kappa(x))\in\mathcal Z\) and \(Ax+B\kappa(x)\in\mathcal X_f\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X_f\), then after applying \(u_0\) and assuming exact nominal dynamics, the shifted sequence \((u_1,\ldots,u_{N-1},\kappa(x_N))\) is feasible for the next horizon and its terminal state again lies in \(\mathcal X_f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible MPC sequence can be shifted and completed with the terminal controller; invariance makes the new endpoint feasible again.
assumptions_latex: The prediction model equals the applied nominal dynamics.
The original horizon prediction satisfies all path constraints and ends in \(\mathcal X_f\).
For every \(x\in\mathcal X_f\), \((x,\kappa(x))\in\mathcal Z\) and \(Ax+B\kappa(x)\in\mathcal X_f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (u_1,\ldots,u_{N-1},\kappa(x_N))\text{ is a feasible successor-horizon input sequence ending in }\mathcal X_f.
knowledge_statements.title: Terminal Invariance Gives the Shifted Feasibility Step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Farkas Certificates for Polyhedral Terminal Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual certificates for the rowwise admissibility and invariance inclusions of a polyhedral terminal interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X_f=\{x:H_fx\le h_f\}\ne\varnothing\). For any affine target inequality \(c^Tx\le d\), the inclusion \(\mathcal X_f\subseteq\{x:c^Tx\le d\}\) holds if and only if there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \[H_f^T\lambda=c,\qquad h_f^T\lambda\le d.\] Applying this condition separately to every row of \((G_x+G_uK)x\le g-G_uk\) and \(H_f(A+BK)x\le h_f-H_fBk\) gives finite nonnegative-multiplier certificates for the complete polyhedral affine-feedback interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each row of a polyhedral terminal admissibility or invariance inclusion has an equivalent nonnegative Farkas-multiplier certificate.
assumptions_latex: The admissibility and terminal sets have finite polyhedral representations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{All terminal-interface inclusions hold exactly when their rowwise Farkas multiplier systems are feasible.}

notation.meaning: Nonnegative certificate multiplier for one target inequality

knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Certificates for Polyhedral Terminal Inclusions

assumptions_latex: The terminal controller \(\kappa\) is defined on \(\mathcal X_f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface is valid precisely when terminal admissibility and positive invariance hold on \(\mathcal X_f\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard controlled-positive-invariance predicate for linear MPC
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled positive invariance as the semantic contract behind a terminal constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A terminal-set and invariant-set interface for \(x^+=Ax+Bu\) consists of a pair \((\mathcal X_f,\kappa)\) satisfying \[x\in\mathcal X_f\quad\Longrightarrow\quad (x,\kappa(x))\in\mathcal Z\ \text{ and }\ Ax+B\kappa(x)\in\mathcal X_f.\] The first predicate enforces terminal state-input admissibility; the second makes \(\mathcal X_f\) positively invariant under the terminal feedback. When \(\mathcal X_f\) is polyhedral and \(\kappa(x)=Kx+k\) is affine, membership and admissibility can be expressed by affine inequalities compatible with a convex-QP horizon model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A terminal controller must respect state-input constraints and map every terminal-set state back into the terminal set.
knowledge_statements.title: Invariant-Set Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The controlled-invariance predicates are standard, but no source is supplied. Moreover, the final affine-representability claim also requires the admissible set \(\mathcal Z\) to have a suitable finite polyhedral representation; that hypothesis is absent.

children.title: Set-Compatibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limits arising when terminal, invariant, and horizon constraint sets are incompatible.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-horizon compatibility condition between admissible endpoints and a prescribed terminal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R_N(x)\) be the set of endpoints of all length-\(N\) trajectories from \(x\) satisfying the dynamics and every nonterminal horizon constraint. Imposing \(x_N\in\mathcal X_f\) yields a feasible horizon problem exactly when \[\mathcal R_N(x)\cap\mathcal X_f\ne\varnothing.\] Thus an empty intersection is the sharp set-compatibility failure boundary. This condition is independent of whether \(\mathcal X_f\) is invariant and does not require a terminal feedback law to be encoded in the online QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The terminally constrained horizon is feasible exactly when its admissible endpoint set intersects the terminal set; invariance is a separate issue.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal R_N(x)\text{ contains exactly the endpoints satisfying all nonterminal horizon requirements}.
x_N\in\mathcal X_f\text{ is imposed as a terminal constraint}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is terminal-horizon feasible}\iff\mathcal R_N(x)\cap\mathcal X_f\ne\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Admissible endpoint set after N prediction steps from x

assumptions_latex: The MPC model permits only finitely many affine equalities and inequalities.

children.title: Stagewise Dynamics Structure
children.top_down_role: Sparse optimal-control QPs retaining per-stage states, inputs, and dynamics constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Row Rank and Unique State Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank and propagation properties of stacked consecutive-stage dynamics equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x_0\) and stack \(x_{k+1}-A_kx_k-B_ku_k=d_k\) for \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\). The coefficient matrix of these equations with respect to \((x_1,\ldots,x_N)\) is block lower triangular with identity diagonal blocks. Consequently, the complete stacked dynamics Jacobian has full row rank, and every input sequence \((u_0,\ldots,u_{N-1})\) determines a unique state sequence \((x_1,\ldots,x_N)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identity coefficients on successive states make the stacked dynamics full row rank and uniquely propagate the state trajectory from the initial state and inputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}E=Nn_x\text{ in the constant-state-dimension case, and each input sequence determines one state trajectory.}
knowledge_statements.title: Full Row Rank and Unique State Propagation

assumptions_latex: The horizon dynamics are linear and stagewise: \(x_{k+1}=A_kx_k+B_ku_k+d_k\).
The trajectory variables are ordered by consecutive stages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stacked dynamics matrix is block lower bidiagonal with block bandwidth independent of the horizon length.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse equality representation of consecutive-stage linear prediction dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\), write the dynamics as \[x_{k+1}-A_kx_k-B_ku_k=d_k.\] After stacking the trajectory blocks in temporal order, these equations have the form \(Ez=e\). Each block row of \(E\) has nonzero blocks only in the columns for \(x_k\), \(u_k\), and \(x_{k+1}\). Therefore \(E\) is block lower bidiagonal under a state-input stage partition, and its block bandwidth does not grow with \(N\) when the state and input dimensions are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each dynamics row touches only the current state, current input, and next state, producing a horizon-independent block bandwidth.

children.title: Block-Banded KKT Structure
children.top_down_role: Linear-algebra structure induced by local coupling between neighboring horizon stages.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct-factorization scaling for uniformly block-banded horizon KKT matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a stagewise KKT matrix have \(m=\Theta(N)\) block rows, maximum block dimension \(b\), and block half-bandwidth \(w\), with \(b,w\) independent of \(N\). If a block \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization completes with pivots and fill confined to a constant-width band, its arithmetic cost is \(O(mw^2b^3)\) and factor storage is \(O(mwb^2)\). Both are therefore \(O(N)\) for fixed \(b,w\). Pivoting or fill that enlarges the effective bandwidth invalidates the linear-horizon conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A band-preserving factorization of a fixed-width block-banded KKT matrix has linear horizon work and storage, whereas bandwidth-growing fill or pivoting can invalidate that bound.
assumptions_latex: The block factorization completes with fill and pivots confined to a constant-width band.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{work}=O(mw^2b^3)=O(N),\qquad \operatorname{storage}=O(mwb^2)=O(N)
knowledge_statements.title: Complexity of Band-Preserving KKT Factorization

assumptions_latex: The objective Hessian and active-constraint Jacobian couple only variables within a fixed number of neighboring stages.
The primal-dual variables are ordered stagewise.
State and input block dimensions do not depend on \(N\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block bandwidth of sparse optimal-control QP linear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an equality-constrained QP, or for a fixed active set, the linear system has the saddle-point form \[\mathcal K\begin{bmatrix}\Delta z\\ \Delta\lambda\end{bmatrix}=r,\qquad \mathcal K=\begin{bmatrix}H&E^{\mathsf T}\\ E&0\end{bmatrix}.\] If \(H\) contains only stage-local blocks and every row block of \(E\) couples only a bounded number of consecutive stages, then a stagewise permutation makes \(\mathcal K\) block banded. Its block bandwidth is bounded independently of the horizon \(N\); only the number of repeated stage blocks grows with \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local costs and consecutive-stage constraints yield a block-banded KKT matrix whose block bandwidth does not grow with the horizon.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Banded KKT Structure

children.title: Long-Range Horizon Coupling Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Model features that weaken or destroy the native block-banded structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bordered Structure from Finitely Many Global Couplings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual exploitable structure when a fixed number of horizon-wide linear constraints is added to a local KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_N\) be an invertible block-banded local KKT matrix and let \(G_N\) contain \(q\) global linear constraint rows, where \(q\) is independent of \(N\). The augmented matrix is \[\begin{bmatrix}K_N&G_N^{\mathsf T}\\G_N&0\end{bmatrix}.\] It is generally not fixed-band in temporal order. Eliminating the local variables gives the \(q\times q\) Schur complement \(-G_NK_N^{-1}G_N^{\mathsf T}\). Thus loss of temporal bandedness need not eliminate all exploitable structure when the number of global rows is fixed and applications of \(K_N^{-1}\) are efficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed number of global horizon constraints destroys strict temporal bandedness but leaves a bordered system with a small global Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{bmatrix}K_N&G_N^{\mathsf T}\\G_N&0\end{bmatrix}\text{ is bordered, and its global Schur complement has dimension }q.
knowledge_statements.title: Bordered Structure from Finitely Many Global Couplings
