children.title: Horizon-Shift Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Warm-start information transferred through receding-horizon shifts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers stage-indexed multipliers alongside the shifted primal MPC trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stage-indexed multipliers \((\lambda_{0|k}^*,\ldots,\lambda_{N-1|k}^*)\), set \(\widehat\lambda_{j|k+1}=\lambda_{j+1|k}^*\) for \(j=0,\ldots,N-2\), and initialize multipliers for newly appended terminal constraints by a prescribed estimate. The result is an initialization and must be repaired when dimensions, signs, or complementarity conditions are not preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift stage multipliers with the horizon, initialize new terminal multipliers, and repair them for the new QP.
assumptions_latex: Successive QPs have a known stagewise multiplier-index map.
The dimensions of newly introduced terminal multipliers are known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\lambda_{0:N-2|k+1}=\lambda_{1:N-1|k}^*.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility of the Shifted MPC Sequence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive-feasibility condition for the standard horizon-shift construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the plant follows the prediction model exactly, the new state equals the first predicted successor, stage constraints are time invariant, and the terminal set \(X_f\) is invariant under the append controller \(\kappa\). If the preceding horizon trajectory is feasible and terminates in \(X_f\), then deleting its first input, shifting the remaining inputs, and appending \(\kappa\) produces a feasible candidate for the next MPC problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under exact model matching and terminal invariance, the standard shifted sequence is recursively feasible.
assumptions_latex: Stage constraints and horizon length are unchanged.
The previous predicted trajectory is feasible and ends in \(X_f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (u_{1|k}^*,\ldots,u_{N-1|k}^*,\kappa(x_{N|k}^*))\text{ is feasible at time }k+1.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility of the Shifted MPC Sequence
Horizon-Shift Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal warm start obtained from the preceding MPC input sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the preceding horizon-\(N\) solution be \((u_{0|k}^*,\ldots,u_{N-1|k}^*)\). At time \(k+1\), initialize the input decision sequence by \(\hat u_{j|k+1}=u_{j+1|k}^*\) for \(j=0,\ldots,N-2\), and choose \(\hat u_{N-1|k+1}=\kappa(\hat x_{N-1|k+1})\) using a prescribed terminal controller or append rule. Roll the prediction dynamics forward from the new measured state, map the resulting trajectory into the solver's decision coordinates, and use it as the initial primal iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discard the applied input, shift the previous optimal sequence left, append a terminal input, and rebuild the trajectory from the new state.
assumptions_latex: The MPC horizon length and decision ordering are unchanged between samples.
A terminal append rule \(\kappa\) is available.

children.title: Active-Set Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of previously identified constraint activity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Worst-Case Guarantee from Working-Set Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits the benefit attributable solely to an active-set warm start.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Without a condition keeping successive QP parameters in an active-set stability neighborhood, consecutive optimal active sets may be disjoint. Consequently, initialization with the preceding working set alone supplies no solver-independent improvement in worst-case active-set iteration complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently large parameter change can make the previous working set irrelevant, so warm starting alone has no worst-case speedup guarantee.
assumptions_latex: No local parameter-change or active-set stability assumption is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal A_k^*\cap\mathcal A_{k+1}^*=\varnothing\text{ is possible}.
knowledge_statements.title: No Worst-Case Guarantee from Working-Set Reuse

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set-specific warm start for consecutive receding-horizon QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the working set \(\mathcal W_k\), map surviving stage-indexed constraints through the receding-horizon index map \(S\), discard constraints belonging to the departed stage or absent from the new model, and append only constraints prescribed by the new terminal-stage initialization rule. Initialize the active-set solver with \(\widehat{\mathcal W}_{k+1}=S(\mathcal W_k)\) and a compatible primal estimate. The solver then solves the active equality subproblem, adds violated inactive constraints, and drops active inequalities with multipliers of the wrong sign until its KKT acceptance test succeeds or its ordinary failure policy is invoked.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift surviving working-set indices, remove obsolete constraints, initialize new-stage constraints by rule, and repair the guess.
assumptions_latex: A mapping between stage-indexed constraints is available.
The solver supports adding violated constraints and dropping constraints with invalid multiplier signs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat{\mathcal W}_{k+1}=S(\mathcal W_k)\text{ is an initialization requiring repair and certification}.
knowledge_statements.title: Stage-Indexed Working-Set Transfer and Repair

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact test of whether a transferred working set already identifies an optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate set \(W\), solve the equality-constrained KKT equations for \((x,y,\lambda_W)\) and set \(\lambda_i=0\) for \(i\notin W\). Accept only if the active KKT equations are solvable, the primal equalities and \(G_Wx=h_W\) hold, every inactive constraint satisfies \(G_ix-h_i\le0\), every \(\lambda_i\) for \(i\in W\) is nonnegative, and full stationarity holds. For \(Q\succeq0\), these conditions certify global optimality; otherwise the transferred set requires repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a transferred set only after solvability, feasibility, inactive-slack, multiplier-sign, and stationarity checks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{all tests pass}\Rightarrow(x,y,\lambda)\text{ is a global KKT solution}.
knowledge_statements.title: Transferred Working-Set Acceptance Test
Active-Set Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Working-set initialization for successive closely related MPC QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A_k\) be the inequality working set returned at sample \(k\). Map its constraint indices through the horizon shift, delete indices for stages that leave the horizon, append no new active constraint unless prescribed by a terminal rule, and obtain \(\hat{\mathcal A}_{k+1}\). Initialize the active-set QP solver at sample \(k+1\) with this set and a compatible primal estimate. The solver must still perform feasibility and multiplier-sign tests, adding or dropping constraints until the QP optimality conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift the previous working set into the new horizon, then let the active-set solver repair feasibility and optimality.
assumptions_latex: Successive QPs use a known mapping between their constraint indices.
The QP solver can repair an incorrect initial working set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat{\mathcal A}_{k+1}=S(\mathcal A_k)\) is an initialization, not an optimality certificate.

The reduced Hessian is positive definite.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Terminal-Invariance Sufficient Condition for Shift Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nominal recursive-feasibility condition for a horizon-shifted MPC candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x_0,u_0,\ldots,u_{N-1},x_N)\) be feasible for \(x_{j+1}=f(x_j,u_j)\), \((x_j,u_j)\in\mathcal Z\), and \(x_N\in\mathcal X_f\). Shifted-Guess Feasibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility test for a horizon-shifted primal MPC guess.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For dynamics \(x_{j+1}=Ax_j+Bu_j\), state-input constraints \((x_j,u_j)\in\mathcal Z\), and terminal set \(\mathcal X_f\), a shifted input guess is feasible from the new state \(x_{k+1}\) exactly when its regenerated trajectory satisfies \((\hat x_j,\hat u_j)\in\mathcal Z\) for \(j=0,\ldots,N-1\) and \(\hat x_N\in\mathcal X_f\). Feasibility of the preceding optimum alone does not imply these conditions after measurement error, disturbance, model mismatch, constraint changes, or a terminal append rule that is not invariant on \(\mathcal X_f\).

assumptions_latex: The shifted trajectory is regenerated from the current measured state.
Feasibility is evaluated against the current dynamics and constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Numeric Factorization Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of an unchanged numerical KKT or normal-equation matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose repeated QP linear solves have the form \(Kz=r_k\), where the numerical matrix \(K\) and its permutation remain unchanged while only \(r_k\) varies. A previously computed factorization, such as \(PKP^\top=LDL^\top\), may then be reused: each new solve requires only permutation and triangular or diagonal substitutions. If any entry of \(K\) changes, the old numeric factors do not in general represent the new system, even when the sparsity pattern is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the numerical linear-system matrix is unchanged, reuse its factors and solve each new right-hand side by substitutions.
assumptions_latex: The numerical coefficient matrix and factorization permutation are unchanged.
The stored factorization remains numerically valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) fixed implies factorization reuse; changed numerical entries generally require refactorization or a valid update.

knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic-Structure Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of sparse analysis when matrix values change but structure does not.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_k\) be the sparse linear-system matrix formed at sample \(k\). If \(\operatorname{supp}(K_{k+1})=\operatorname{supp}(K_k)\) and the matrix dimensions and pivoting policy are compatible, the previously computed ordering, elimination tree, and symbolic nonzero allocation may be reused. The numerical factors must nevertheless be recomputed when matrix values change. Thus symbolic reuse avoids repeated graph analysis and memory planning, but it is distinct from numeric factorization reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unchanged sparsity pattern permits reuse of ordering and symbolic analysis, although changed values still require numerical refactorization.
assumptions_latex: Successive matrices have equal dimensions and sparsity patterns.
The factorization method does not introduce incompatible data-dependent symbolic pivoting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{supp}(K_{k+1})=\operatorname{supp}(K_k)\) permits symbolic reuse, not automatic numeric-factor reuse.

children.title: Reuse Invalidation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Data changes that invalidate symbolic or numeric reuse.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative pre-use decision procedure for numeric and symbolic reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reuse policy may certify an attempt admissible only after verifying compatible dimensions and ordering; containment of the current pattern in the analyzed envelope; compatibility of the pivot policy; either exact identity of the current factorized operator with the recorded operator or completion of a supported update; and matching factorization options and regularization. If any required item cannot be verified, the policy requires reanalysis, refactorization, or a separately validated update. A small post-solve residual is diagnostic and does not replace these provenance checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse requires verified operator or update provenance, structural and pivot compatibility, and matching factorization options.
assumptions_latex: Identity fingerprints are collision-free or followed by certified comparison.
The update mechanism declares its supported change class.
The symbolic envelope explicitly supports structural containment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{all required checks pass}\Rightarrow\text{reuse is admissible under the documented policy}.
review_flags: The checks are a conservative admissibility policy, not a universal necessary-and-sufficient characterization of every possible factorization implementation.
knowledge_statements.title: Reuse-Validity Provenance Check

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maps online MPC changes to the operator and structural metadata actually reused.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((K_k,P_k)=\mathcal F(N_k,A_k,B_k,Q_k,R_k,G_k,\rho_k,\mathcal W_k,\Delta_k)\) denote the factorized operator and required structural metadata assembled from horizon, model, weights, constraints, regularization, an implementation-dependent working set, and discretization. Numeric factors are invalid when \(K_{k+1}\ne K_k\), unless a supported factor update has been completed. Symbolic metadata cease to be guaranteed applicable when dimensions or ordering change, the required pattern leaves the analyzed envelope, or the pivot policy is no longer supported. An online data change matters only through its effect on \((K,P)\); a pure right-hand-side change affects neither.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classify MPC updates by whether they change matrix values or leave the analyzed structural envelope.
assumptions_latex: Reuse concerns a direct factorization of the assembled operator.
\(\mathcal F\) is the implementation's documented assembly map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_{k+1}\ne K_k\Rightarrow\text{numeric invalidation unless updated};\quad P_{k+1}\not\preceq P_{\mathrm{env}}\Rightarrow\text{symbolic invalidation}.

knowledge_statements.title: Assembly-Based MPC Reuse Invalidation Map
Reuse Invalidation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions invalidating numerical or symbolic linear-algebra reuse.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One prepared SQP step per sampling instant in real-time MPC.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precision-dependent false-zero residual caused by rounding before subtraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In binary round-to-nearest-ties-to-even arithmetic, \(1+u\) is the midpoint between the adjacent floating-point numbers \(1\) and \(1+2u\), and it rounds to \(1\). Hence \(\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(1+u)-1)=0\), although the corresponding exact real expression is \((1+u)-1=u>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding followed by cancellation can turn a nonzero residual into an apparent zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat r=0\quad\text{while}\quad r=u>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Cancellation after Input Rounding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic model for floating-point execution of embedded QP kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a radix-2 format of precision \(p\) using round-to-nearest, the unit roundoff is \(u=2^{-p}\). If the exact result of a basic operation is finite and normal, \(\operatorname{fl}(a\circ b)=(a\circ b)(1+\delta)\) with \(|\delta|\le u\). With gradual underflow, rounding a finite result in the subnormal range instead admits an absolute-error bound of one-half the smallest subnormal spacing. Overflow, division by zero, invalid operations, NaNs, infinities, and flush-to-zero modes require separate handling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal finite operations have bounded relative error; subnormal and exceptional results require different models.
assumptions_latex: The relative-error statement is restricted to finite normal results.
The stated subnormal bound assumes gradual underflow.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\delta|\le u\text{ for finite normal results; exceptional and underflow regimes are outside this relative model.}

notation.meaning: Binary significand precision, including the implicit leading bit.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise error bound tied to an explicitly specified residual computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(s=a^{\mathsf T}b\) is evaluated by \(k\) unfused floating-point multiplications followed by sequential floating-point additions, without exceptional results. If \(2ku<1\), then \(\widehat s=s+e\) with \(|e|\le\gamma_{2k}|a|^{\mathsf T}|b|\), where \(\gamma_{2k}=2ku/(1-2ku)\). A residual such as \(Hx+q+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda\) is bounded componentwise by applying the corresponding bound to every implemented product-and-sum chain, including the additions of \(q\) and the partial sums. A normwise bound follows by taking a monotone vector norm. Fused operations, reordered reductions, compensated summation, or another computational graph require a revised operation count or bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual error is bounded from the actual product-and-sum graph, not from the symbolic residual formula alone.
assumptions_latex: No intermediate operation overflows or produces an exceptional value.
The stated unfused sequential implementation is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\widehat s-a^{\mathsf T}b|\le\gamma_{2k}|a|^{\mathsf T}|b|.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-error model for floating-point evaluation of generated QP solver operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a floating-point regime with unit roundoff \(u\), each basic operation is modeled by \(\operatorname{fl}(a\circ b)=(a\circ b)(1+\delta)\), where \(|\delta|\le u\), provided no overflow or underflow occurs. For a computed QP residual \(\hat r\) formed by a fixed operation sequence, standard accumulation bounds give a perturbation proportional to \(\gamma_k=ku/(1-ku)\) when \(ku<1\). Consequently, solver tolerances must dominate both data quantization and the accumulated rounding-error scale; changing precision can change whether a computed iterate passes a residual test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Floating-point operations incur bounded relative errors that accumulate with operation count, so QP stopping tolerances must exceed the resulting numerical noise floor.
assumptions_latex: No intermediate operation overflows or underflows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Residual tests below the rounding scale governed by \(\gamma_k\) are not numerically reliable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Difference between saturation and modular wraparound in signed fixed-point arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a signed \(B\)-bit integer accumulator with representable integers \([-2^{B-1},2^{B-1}-1]\), the exact value \(2^{B-1}\) saturates to \(2^{B-1}-1\) but wraps modulo \(2^B\) to \(-2^{B-1}\). With fixed-point scale \(\Delta\), the respective absolute errors are \(\Delta\) and \(2^B\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-unit positive overflow has a small saturation error but becomes a large negative error under wraparound.
assumptions_latex: Two's-complement modular wraparound is used in the wraparound case.
Saturation clips to the nearest representable endpoint.
knowledge_statements.title: Wraparound Overflow Can Reverse Sign

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute error accumulation for a fixed-point dot product with separately bounded product and addition errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\). If each computed product is \(\widehat p_i=a_ix_i+e_i\), with \(|e_i|\le\varepsilon_m\), each of the \(n-1\) additions contributes an error of magnitude at most \(\varepsilon_a\), and no operation overflows, then \(|\widehat s-s|\le n\varepsilon_m+(n-1)\varepsilon_a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without overflow, bounded product and accumulator errors yield an explicit absolute dot-product error bound.
assumptions_latex: Every accumulator error has magnitude at most \(\varepsilon_a\).
No product or accumulator operation overflows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\widehat s-s|\le n\varepsilon_m+(n-1)\varepsilon_a.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arithmetic-Error Margin Certificate for QP Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of certified fixed-point evaluation errors into conservative feasibility and stationarity tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let exact QP residual vectors at a represented tuple be \(r_p\) and \(r_d\), and let fixed-point evaluation return \(\widehat r_p\) and \(\widehat r_d\). If range analysis proves that no operation overflows and error analysis proves \[\|\widehat r_p-r_p\|\le\delta_p,\qquad \|\widehat r_d-r_d\|\le\delta_d,\] then \[\|r_p\|\le\|\widehat r_p\|+\delta_p,\qquad \|r_d\|\le\|\widehat r_d\|+\delta_d.\] Consequently, exact residual tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d\) are certified whenever \(\|\widehat r_p\|\le\varepsilon_p-\delta_p\) and \(\|\widehat r_d\|\le\varepsilon_d-\delta_d\), with nonnegative right-hand sides. The same margin rule applies to scalar inequality violations and complementarity residuals when corresponding error bounds are available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified arithmetic-error bounds are subtracted from residual tolerances; passing the tightened fixed-point tests certifies the exact residual tests.
assumptions_latex: The residual norm is fixed, and all displayed error bounds use that norm.
Certified range analysis excludes overflow on every evaluated path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\widehat r_p\|\le\varepsilon_p-\delta_p\ \land\ \|\widehat r_d\|\le\varepsilon_d-\delta_d\ \Longrightarrow\ \|r_p\|\le\varepsilon_p\ \land\ \|r_d\|\le\varepsilon_d.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete arithmetic semantics needed to interpret range and error claims for an embedded QP computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A specified fixed-point arithmetic model assigns to every stored quantity a signed or unsigned word length, scale, and representable set; to every multiplication an exact-product format and subsequent rounding or truncation rule; to every accumulation an accumulator word length, scale, and update rule; and to every narrowing conversion a rounding mode and either saturation or modular-wraparound semantics. Together with a fixed evaluation order, these data define a deterministic map from representable inputs to representable outputs. Storage format alone does not determine the errors or overflow behavior of products and dot products.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operation-by-operation range certificate for one finite, bounded execution of a generated fixed-point QP computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite fixed-point computation with a completely specified arithmetic model and evaluation order. Associate each input and intermediate node \(v\) with an interval \(I_v=[\ell_v,u_v]\). For an addition, form the exact real-result enclosure \(I_a+I_b\); for a multiplication, form the exact real-result enclosure \(I_aI_b\) from the extrema of the four endpoint products. At each operation, first require its exact-result enclosure to lie in the declared product or accumulator range used before rounding, and then enlarge it by the certified rounding-error interval \([ -\rho_w,\rho_w]\). Require the enlarged enclosure to lie in the destination range before every storage or narrowing conversion. If all such checks pass, no product, accumulation, storage, or narrowing operation overflows or saturates for any covered input, and every computed value lies in its propagated enclosure.

assumptions_latex: The fixed-point formats, product and accumulator ranges, narrowing rules, overflow semantics, and evaluation order are specified.
Every input lies in its certified interval.
Each rounding or truncation step has a valid absolute error bound \(\rho_w\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Range and quantization conditions for fixed-point generated QP computations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a signed fixed-point format have quantization step \(\Delta>0\) and representable interval \([-M,M]\). A generated QP computation is admissible only if every stored input and intermediate exact value \(v\) satisfies \(|v|\le M-\Delta/2\). With rounding to nearest, its quantized value \(Q(v)\) then obeys \(|Q(v)-v|\le\Delta/2\). All arithmetic operations have explicitly bounded intermediate ranges.

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Complementarity Cancellation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validation procedure across selected deployment inputs, builds, and targets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each selected nominal, boundary, and adversarial QP instance, execute the generated solver on the deployment target; record its output, status, iteration trace, build identity, and arithmetic configuration; independently reconstruct the instance and recompute objective, constraint, and noncancelling KKT residuals in specified reference arithmetic; apply guard-banded thresholds; and repeat identical runs to test deterministic reproducibility. A pass establishes only the recorded properties of the tested instances, build, target, and arithmetic configuration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independently recompute guarded residuals on representative and adversarial cases and check repeatability; passing does not prove untested behavior.
assumptions_latex: The reference reconstruction is independent of the generated residual implementation.
Build, target, solver options, and arithmetic configuration are recorded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{campaign pass}\Rightarrow\text{specified checks hold for the tested executions only}.
knowledge_statements.title: Generated-Code Numeric Validation Campaign

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent residual certificate for one generated-code output of a convex inequality-form QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_z \tfrac12z^{\mathsf T}Hz+q^{\mathsf T}z\) subject to \(g(z)=Az-b\le0\), define \(r_p=\|(g(\widehat z))_+\|_\infty\), \(r_\lambda=\|(-\widehat\lambda)_+\|_\infty\), \(r_s=\|H\widehat z+q+A^{\mathsf T}\widehat\lambda\|_\infty\), and \(r_c=\|\widehat\lambda\odot g(\widehat z)\|_\infty\). After guard-banding for reference-evaluator error, bounds on all four residuals form a noncancelling approximate-KKT certificate for the tested output. At zero tolerances they are exactly the KKT conditions and, when \(H\succeq0\), certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check primal feasibility, multiplier sign, stationarity, and componentwise complementarity independently so errors cannot cancel.
assumptions_latex: Reference-evaluator error is incorporated into the acceptance thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (r_p,r_\lambda,r_s,r_c)\le(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_\lambda,\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_c).

notation.meaning: Primal, multiplier-sign, stationarity, and complementarity residuals.

review_flags: Positive residual tolerances alone do not imply an objective-error bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Noncancelling Approximate-KKT Validation Certificate
Generated-Code Numeric Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based validation certificate for a generated convex QP solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_z \tfrac12z^THz+q^Tz\) subject to \(Az\le b\), a generated-code output \((\hat z,\hat\lambda)\) has an \(\varepsilon\)-KKT certificate when \(\hat\lambda\ge0\), \(\|(A\hat z-b)_+\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\|H\hat z+q+A^T\hat\lambda\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_d\), and \(|\hat\lambda^T(A\hat z-b)|\le\varepsilon_c\). Validation must evaluate these quantities using an independently specified reference precision and test representative, boundary, and adversarial parameter values. The certificate verifies approximate primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity for each tested instance, but not untested inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independently recompute primal, dual, stationarity, and complementarity residuals; passing bounded residuals certifies only the tested generated-code outputs.
assumptions_latex: Reference residual evaluation has error below the prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities constitute an approximate KKT certificate for the tested QP instance.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports generated-code validation or approximate KKT tolerances.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the validation leaf, but the displayed scalar absolute complementarity residual can hide cancellation when small primal violations are permitted: components of lambda_hat^T(A z_hat-b) may have different signs. A noncancelling componentwise or norm-based complementarity residual and an authoritative approximate-KKT locator are required before the certificate is reliable.

children.title: MPC QP Applicability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Boundaries that require feasibility theory, uncertainty models, hybrid formulations, or nonlinear optimization beyond a nominal convex QP template.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-loop feasibility property of a receding-horizon MPC optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X_N\) be the set of states for which the horizon-\(N\) MPC problem is feasible, and let \(\kappa_N\) denote the applied receding-horizon policy. Recursive feasibility means \[x_0\in\mathcal X_N\Longrightarrow x_t\in\mathcal X_N\quad\text{for every }t\ge0\] under all transitions quantified by the stated closed-loop model. It is lost when an initially feasible closed-loop trajectory has a successor outside \(\mathcal X_N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursive feasibility means that every state reached from an initially feasible closed loop has another feasible horizon problem.
assumptions_latex: The horizon, constraints, prediction model, policy selection rule, and disturbance quantifiers defining \(\mathcal X_N\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{loss occurs}\iff\exists t:\ x_0\in\mathcal X_N,\ x_t\in\mathcal X_N,\ x_{t+1}\notin\mathcal X_N\) along a quantified closed-loop trajectory.
knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Feasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitations of the nominal shift-and-append guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The shift-and-append guarantee is unavailable if the realized successor differs from its prediction, if the dynamics or constraints change outside the assumptions used for the shifted plan, or if no admissible terminal input keeps the terminal state in \(X_f\). Failure of these assumptions invalidates this certificate but does not by itself prove that the successor MPC problem is infeasible, because another feasible sequence may exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mismatch, changing constraints, or loss of terminal invariance can invalidate the shifted-plan certificate without necessarily causing actual infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Recursive feasibility is being justified by the nominal shift-and-append construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\neg(\text{shift assumptions})\Longrightarrow\text{no shift-based guarantee}\), but not necessarily \(x^+\notin\mathcal X_N\).
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of the Shift Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard sufficient condition for nominal linear MPC with a control-invariant terminal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x^+=Ax+Bu\), time-invariant stage constraints \((x_k,u_k)\in\mathcal Z\), and terminal constraint \(x_N\in X_f\). Suppose every \(x\in X_f\) admits \(u=\kappa_f(x)\) with \((x,u)\in\mathcal Z\) and \(Ax+Bu\in X_f\). For any currently feasible input sequence, after its first input is applied under the exact prediction model, shifting the remaining inputs and appending \(\kappa_f(x_N)\) yields a feasible successor sequence. Hence current feasibility implies all subsequent feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact nominal dynamics and an admissibly control-invariant terminal set make the shifted previous plan a next-step feasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: The current horizon problem is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_t\in\mathcal X_N\Longrightarrow x_{t+1}\in\mathcal X_N\), and therefore \(x_t\in\mathcal X_N\) for all \(t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Shift-and-Append Recursive-Feasibility Condition
Loss of Recursive Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the implication from current MPC feasibility to next-step feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x^+=x+u+w\), constraints \(|x|\le1\), \(|u|\le0.1\), horizon one, and terminal constraint \(x^+=0\). At \(x=0\), the nominal MPC QP with \(w=0\) is feasible using \(u=0\). If the applied transition has \(w=0.2\), the successor is \(x^+=0.2\). At that state the next nominal QP requires \(u=-0.2\), which violates \(|u|\le0.1\). Thus current feasibility alone does not imply next-step feasibility when an unmodeled disturbance can move the successor outside the set of states steerable to the terminal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible nominal MPC step can be followed by an infeasible QP when an unmodeled disturbance moves the state beyond the terminally controllable region.
assumptions_latex: The realized first transition has disturbance \(w=0.2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility at \(x=0\) does not imply feasibility of the next QP at \(x=0.2\).
review_flags: Concrete construction is self-checking, but no supplied source addresses recursive MPC feasibility.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind exactly fits the leaf, and the scalar counterexample is internally consistent. Nevertheless, no source with a specific recursive-feasibility locator is supplied, so the record cannot satisfy the evidence requirements.

children.title: Nominal-Model Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Prediction errors caused by divergence from the nominal model.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rowwise condition separating harmless prediction error from realized constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nominal inequality \(C_i\hat x_k+D_i u_k\le d_i\), define \(s_{i,k}=d_i-C_i\hat x_k-D_i u_k\). If \(x_k=\hat x_k+e_k\), then the realized inequality holds exactly when \(C_ie_k\le s_{i,k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A realized constraint remains satisfied exactly when its signed prediction error fits within the available nominal slack.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_ix_k+D_iu_k\le d_i\iff C_ie_k\le s_{i,k}\).

notation.meaning: Nominal slack of row \(i\) at stage \(k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nominal Feasibility Margin Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact horizon propagation of additive prediction mismatch under fixed nominal linear dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\hat x_{k+1}=A\hat x_k+Bu_k\), \(x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k+r_k\), and \(x_0=\hat x_0\). Then \[e_{k+1}=Ae_k+r_k,\qquad e_k=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}A^{k-1-j}r_j.\] Thus horizon mismatch is governed by the powers of \(A\), including any transient or asymptotic attenuation or amplification they produce.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Horizon prediction error is the convolution of one-step residuals with powers of the nominal state matrix; stability alone does not exclude transient amplification.
assumptions_latex: The nominal and realized trajectories use the same input sequence.
All one-step mismatch is collected in \(r_k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Step Prediction-Error Propagation
Nominal-Model Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-prediction error caused by using nominal rather than actual linear dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the controller predict \(\hat x^+=Ax+Bu\), while the plant obeys \(x^+=(A+\Delta A)x+(B+\Delta B)u+w\). The one-step prediction error is \(e^+=x^+-\hat x^+=\Delta A x+\Delta B u+w\). Hence nominal satisfaction \(C\hat x^+\le d\) ensures actual satisfaction only when every row satisfies \(C_i\hat x^++\sup C_i e^+\le d_i\) over the admissible mismatch. Without such a margin, a nominally feasible QP solution may violate the plant constraint even if the QP is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plant-model mismatch adds a predictable error term; without constraint margins covering it, exact nominal QP feasibility does not ensure actual feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The predictor and plant use the displayed linear dynamics.
The same state \(x\) and input \(u\) initialize both transitions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nominal feasibility alone does not imply \(Cx^+\le d\) unless the mismatch error is covered by a robust margin.

notation.meaning: Errors in the nominal state and input matrices.

review_flags: The supplied uncertainty locator does not specifically support MPC model mismatch.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the nominal-mismatch leaf, and the one-step error identity is correct. The supremum is not fully defined because the admissible mismatch set and its quantifiers are omitted, and no MPC model-mismatch source or locator supports the robust-margin conclusion.

children.title: Bounded-Uncertainty Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structured disturbance or parameter-variation regimes near the nominal QP.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary for existence of a finite worst-case affine margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty closed convex uncertainty set \(\mathcal W\), its support value in direction \(y\) is finite exactly when \(y^{\mathsf T}d\le0\) for every \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(\mathcal W)\). If some recession direction satisfies \(y^{\mathsf T}d>0\), then \(\sigma_{\mathcal W}(y)=+\infty\), so no finite right-hand-side margin can enforce that uncertain affine inequality uniformly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worst-case affine margin is infinite exactly when uncertainty has a recession direction that increases the uncertain expression.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal W\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{\mathcal W}(y)<\infty\iff y^{\mathsf T}d\le0\ \forall d\in\operatorname{rec}(\mathcal W)\).

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the uncertainty set.
Support function of the uncertainty set.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Support-Margin Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form support function for an ellipsoidal bounded-uncertainty regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathcal W=\{\bar\omega+Q^{1/2}v:\|v\|_2\le1\}\) with \(Q\succeq0\), then \[\sigma_{\mathcal W}(y)=y^{\mathsf T}\bar\omega+\|Q^{1/2}y\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ellipsoidal uncertainty set contributes its center value plus a weighted Euclidean-norm worst-case margin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{\mathcal W}(y)=y^{\mathsf T}\bar\omega+\|Q^{1/2}y\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoidal-Uncertainty Margin

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-program representation of the support function of a bounded polyhedral uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal W=\{\omega:F\omega\le g\}\) be nonempty and bounded. For every \(y\), \[\sigma_{\mathcal W}(y)=\max_{\omega}\{y^{\mathsf T}\omega:F\omega\le g\}=\min_{\lambda\ge0}\{g^{\mathsf T}\lambda:F^{\mathsf T}\lambda=y\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For bounded polyhedral uncertainty, the worst-case affine margin equals a finite linear-program dual value.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal W=\{\omega:F\omega\le g\}\) is nonempty and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{\mathcal W}(y)=\min\{g^{\mathsf T}\lambda:F^{\mathsf T}\lambda=y,\ \lambda\ge0\}\).

notation.meaning: Dual multiplier for the polyhedral uncertainty description.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral-Uncertainty Support Function
Bounded-Uncertainty Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function condition for robust satisfaction of affine MPC constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the uncertain predicted state is \(x_k=\bar x_k+E_k\omega\), where \(\omega\in\mathcal W\) and \(\mathcal W\) is nonempty and bounded. The constraint \(C_i x_k+D_i u_k\le d_i\) holds for every \(\omega\in\mathcal W\) exactly when \(C_i\bar x_k+D_i u_k+\sigma_{\mathcal W}(E_k^TC_i^T)\le d_i\), where \(\sigma_{\mathcal W}(y)=\sup_{\omega\in\mathcal W}y^T\omega\). This bounded-uncertainty regime admits a finite deterministic tightening whenever the support function is finite and computationally representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine constraint is robustly satisfied exactly when its nominal value plus the uncertainty set’s support-function margin stays below the bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust affine constraint is equivalent to the displayed support-function inequality.

notation.meaning: Linear map from uncertainty to predicted-state error.
Support function of the uncertainty set.

review_flags: Available locator concerns stochastic uncertainty generally, not this robust support-function reformulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the bounded-uncertainty leaf, and the support-function equivalence is mathematically coherent for dimensionally compatible finite-dimensional data. The inventory's general stochastic-uncertainty locator does not support this robust counterpart, and the candidate cites no source.

children.title: Uncertainty-Aware Reformulation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundary where uncertainty treatment changes the nominal QP template.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary where decision-dependent ellipsoidal uncertainty introduces a second-order-cone constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal W=\{\bar\omega+Q^{1/2}v:\|v\|_2\le1\}\), the robust constraint \[a^{\mathsf T}z+(Pz+q)^{\mathsf T}\omega\le b\quad\forall\omega\in\mathcal W\] is equivalent to \[a^{\mathsf T}z+(Pz+q)^{\mathsf T}\bar\omega+\|Q^{1/2}(Pz+q)\|_2\le b.\] Unless the norm reduces to an affine or finite polyhedral expression on the feasible domain, this constraint is nonpolyhedral. With a positive-semidefinite quadratic objective, an epigraph formulation is an SOCP rather than a linearly constrained QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decision-dependent ellipsoidal uncertainty generally creates a norm constraint and crosses from linearly constrained QP form to conic form.
assumptions_latex: The uncertainty coefficient \(Pz+q\) is affine in the decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|Q^{1/2}(Pz+q)\|_2\) generally places the exact counterpart outside the linearly constrained QP class.
knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoidal Robust Counterpart Becomes Conic

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Robust Counterpart Remains a QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact model-class preservation for affine constraints with fixed bounded polyhedral uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider robust constraints \[a_i^{\mathsf T}z+(P_i z+q_i)^{\mathsf T}\omega\le b_i\quad\forall\omega\in\{\omega:F_i\omega\le g_i\}.\] If each uncertainty set is nonempty and bounded, the constraint is equivalent to the existence of \(\lambda_i\ge0\) such that \[F_i^{\mathsf T}\lambda_i=P_i z+q_i,\qquad a_i^{\mathsf T}z+g_i^{\mathsf T}\lambda_i\le b_i.\] With a convex quadratic objective, these affine lifted constraints yield a continuous convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed bounded polyhedral uncertainty can be dualized into affine lifted constraints, preserving convex-QP form.
assumptions_latex: Each set \(\{\omega:F_i\omega\le g_i\}\) is nonempty and bounded.
The reformulated objective remains convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{The exact robust counterpart is a convex QP in }(z,\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Robust Counterpart Remains a QP
Uncertainty-Aware Reformulation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between convex-QP tightenings and non-QP uncertainty-aware formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A robust or chance-constrained MPC model remains a convex QP only when every uncertainty-aware constraint can be represented by affine equalities or inequalities in the decision variables and the objective remains convex quadratic. Polyhedral robust counterparts with fixed uncertainty sets may satisfy this condition after dualization. If reformulation introduces a nonpolyhedral norm cone, semidefinite constraint, decision-dependent uncertainty set, integer variable, or nonlinear probability quantile, the resulting problem is generally an SOCP, SDP, mixed-integer problem, or nonlinear program rather than a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uncertainty handling stays within convex QP form only when all counterparts reduce to affine constraints and a convex quadratic objective.
assumptions_latex: The nominal decision vector is finite-dimensional.
Exact, rather than sampled or approximate, uncertainty reformulation is intended.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any essential nonpolyhedral, semidefinite, integer, or nonlinear constraint crosses the convex-QP model-class boundary.
review_flags: No supplied locator distinguishes QP, conic, semidefinite, and mixed-integer robust counterparts.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits this model-class boundary. The broad classification of robust and chance-constrained reformulations across QP, SOCP, SDP, mixed-integer, and nonlinear classes needs a specific authoritative source; none is cited. The exact representability qualifications also require source-backed formulation assumptions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed deterministic equivalent for finitely many fixed affine scenarios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\omega^1,\ldots,\omega^S\) be fixed scenarios. Stacking affine scenario constraints and summing nonnegatively weighted convex quadratic scenario costs yields a continuous convex QP in the shared decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite fixed scenarios preserve QP form under affine constraints and convex quadratic costs.
assumptions_latex: The scenario set is finite and fixed.
Scenario constraints are affine in one shared continuous decision.
Scenario weights are nonnegative and weighted Hessians are positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{The finite-scenario deterministic equivalent is a convex QP.}\)
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Scenario QP Preservation

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory covers the QP-preserving polyhedral robust counterpart and the conic ellipsoidal boundary, together with the seed's general model-class criterion. The proposed finite-scenario record was deferred as duplication of the dedicated scenario sibling. Detailed uncertainty geometry and nominal mismatch were excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Hybrid-Dynamics Boundary
children.top_down_role: Mode-dependent prediction structures outside a single convex QP.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid-Dynamics Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a single convex QP to encode endogenous mode-dependent dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For hybrid dynamics \(x_{k+1}=A_jx_k+B_ju_k+c_j\) when \((x_k,u_k)\in R_j\), a fixed, externally supplied mode sequence yields affine dynamics and may produce a convex QP. If the optimizer must choose among two or more regions \(R_j\), the feasible trajectory set is generally a union of polyhedra and need not be convex. Except when the mode alternatives admit an exact common affine representation or redundant convex description, a single continuous convex QP cannot encode this disjunction exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Known mode sequences can yield QPs, but endogenous switching creates a generally nonconvex union of trajectory sets that a continuous convex QP cannot exactly encode.
assumptions_latex: Each mode has affine dynamics on a polyhedral region \(R_j\).
Mode selection is endogenous unless stated otherwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Endogenous nonredundant mode selection generally lies outside the continuous convex-QP model class.
review_flags: No supplied locator addresses hybrid MPC or disjunctive dynamics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the hybrid-dynamics leaf. The known-mode versus endogenous-mode distinction is plausible, but the exact nonrepresentability claim and its exceptions require a hybrid or disjunctive optimization source with a specific locator. No citation is supplied.

children.title: Discrete-Control Boundary
children.top_down_role: Control choices requiring discrete decision variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Control Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-class boundary created by finite-valued MPC control decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If any control component must satisfy \(u_k\in\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}\) with at least two distinct values, its feasible set is nonconvex. A convex QP can enforce only a convex feasible set described by affine constraints, so replacing the finite set by its convex hull generally admits fractional or interpolated controls not permitted by the plant. Exact enforcement therefore requires enumeration, integer variables, or another nonconvex mechanism, unless the remaining constraints and objective independently force every optimizer to an allowed discrete value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A genuinely finite control alphabet is nonconvex; its exact enforcement normally requires integer or enumerative optimization rather than a continuous convex QP.
assumptions_latex: The alphabet contains at least two distinct control values.
Exact enforcement of the discrete alphabet is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint \(u_k\in\{v_1,\ldots,v_m\}\) is generally not exactly representable by a continuous convex QP.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports the discrete-control model-class boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the discrete-control leaf. A finite alphabet with at least two distinct values is nonconvex, but an objective forcing allowed optimizers does not itself make a convex-hull relaxation an exact feasible-set enforcement; the intended notion of exactness must be clarified. No supporting mixed-integer or discrete-control locator is supplied.

children.title: Mixed-Integer Reformulation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Transition from convex QP templates to mixed-integer formulations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal extended formulation for a bounded finite union of polyhedra used as a hybrid-MPC mode disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_j=\{z:A_jz\le b_j\}\) be nonempty bounded polyhedra for \(j=1,\ldots,m\). Introduce \(z^j\) and \(\delta_j\) satisfying \[z=\sum_{j=1}^m z^j,\qquad A_jz^j\le b_j\delta_j,\qquad \sum_{j=1}^m\delta_j=1,\qquad \delta_j\in\{0,1\}.\] The projection onto \(z\) is \(\bigcup_jP_j\). Replacing integrality by \(\delta_j\ge0\) projects onto \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_jP_j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregated mode copies exactly represent a bounded polyhedral disjunction, and their continuous relaxation projects to its convex hull.
assumptions_latex: \(P_j\) is nonempty and bounded for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_z(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{integer}})=\bigcup_jP_j\) and \(\operatorname{proj}_z(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{relaxed}})=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_jP_j)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Disaggregated Convex-Hull Formulation
Mixed-Integer Reformulation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact mixed-integer encoding of bounded affine disjunctions in hybrid MPC.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a bounded affine disjunction in which exactly one mode \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is active, introduce \(\delta_j\in\{0,1\}\) with \(\sum_j\delta_j=1\). A guarded inequality \(a_j^Tz\le b_j\) for the active mode is represented by \(a_j^Tz\le b_j+M_j(1-\delta_j)\), where \(M_j\) is a valid finite upper bound on \(a_j^Tz-b_j\) over the global variable bounds. With a convex quadratic objective, this produces an MIQP, not a continuous convex QP; invalid or excessively large \(M_j\) values respectively destroy equivalence or weaken the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary mode indicators and valid big-M bounds encode bounded affine disjunctions exactly, but the reformulated MPC problem is an MIQP rather than a convex QP.
assumptions_latex: Exactly one mode must be active.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The big-M system is an exact guarded-disjunction representation and changes the model class to MIQP.

notation.meaning: Binary indicator for activation of mode \(j\).
Valid deactivation bound for guarded inequality \(j\).

review_flags: No supplied locator supports big-M hybrid MPC reformulations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the reformulation leaf. The guarded-inequality formula is standard when M_j is valid, but exact encoding of a complete affine disjunction requires all constraints defining each mode and suitable global bounds, not merely the displayed isolated inequality. No authoritative big-M or hybrid-MPC locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonlinear Dynamics Can Reduce Exactly to a QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp exception to inferring the reduced model class solely from a nonlinear lifted prediction equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x_1=u^2\), \(-1\le u\le1\), and objective \(x_1\). The lifted equality is nonlinear and its graph is nonconvex, but exact elimination gives \[\min_{-1\le u\le1}u^2,\] a convex QP. Thus the QP classification must be applied after the intended exact substitutions or eliminations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear prediction equality can disappear under exact state elimination and leave a convex QP; nonaffinity of the transition map alone is therefore not a sufficient reduced-model test.
assumptions_latex: The predicted state appears only through \(x_1=u^2\) and the linear objective \(x_1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Dynamics Can Reduce Exactly to a QP
Nonlinear-Prediction Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary where exact nonlinear state prediction ceases to yield a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An MPC problem is a convex QP only if, after eliminating predicted states or retaining them explicitly, its objective is convex quadratic and every constraint is affine in the decision variables. For nonlinear prediction \(x_{k+1}=f(x_k,u_k)\), the equality \(x_{k+1}-f(x_k,u_k)=0\) is generally nonlinear and defines a nonconvex feasible set. A local affine approximation can produce a QP subproblem, but it is not an exact reformulation unless \(f\) is affine on the entire relevant domain and all resulting costs and constraints retain QP form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact nonlinear prediction generally leaves the convex-QP class; linearization creates only a local QP approximation unless the dynamics are affine on the relevant domain.
assumptions_latex: Exact enforcement of the prediction dynamics is required.
Decision variables include controls and, optionally, predicted states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonaffine \(f\) generally makes the MPC problem nonlinear or nonconvex rather than a convex QP.

notation.meaning: Predicted state and control at stage \(k\).

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses nonlinear MPC or exact QP representability.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the nonlinear-prediction leaf. The distinction between an exact nonlinear model and a local QP approximation is plausible, but the general convexity and exact-representability claims need a nonlinear MPC or convex-analysis source with a specific locator. None is supplied.

children.title: Ill-Conditioning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerically difficult QP instances caused by poor conditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioning Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical boundary for an active-set KKT system arising in an MPC QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an active constraint set \(I\), let \[K_I=\begin{bmatrix}H&G_I^{\mathsf T}\\G_I&0\end{bmatrix}.\] Given a relative data or arithmetic perturbation level \(\eta>0\), the associated MPC QP lies in an ill-conditioning regime when \(K_I\) is singular or \(\kappa_2(K_I)\eta\geq 1\), where \(\kappa_2(K_I)=\lVert K_I\rVert_2\lVert K_I^{-1}\rVert_2\) for nonsingular \(K_I\). In this regime, first-order perturbation bounds cannot guarantee a relative solution error smaller than one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active-set regime is ill-conditioned when its KKT matrix is singular or its condition number times the perturbation level reaches one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_I\text{ singular}\ \lor\ \kappa_2(K_I)\eta\geq1\) marks loss of a nontrivial first-order relative-error guarantee.

notation.meaning: KKT matrix for active set I

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition-number threshold and its interpretation as loss of a first-order relative-error guarantee require an inspectable perturbation-analysis source. The phrase “data or arithmetic perturbation” also needs a precise perturbation model.

children.title: Deadline-Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Execution regimes where solver completion exceeds control deadlines.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient per-update certificate excluding solver deadline failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_k\) be the hard update deadline and suppose a validated worst-case execution-time bound \(W_k\) satisfies \(T_k\le W_k\) for every admissible QP instance and execution condition at update \(k\). Then \(W_k\le D_k\) certifies absence of solver deadline failure at that update. An average time, median time, or finite-test maximum below \(D_k\) is not such a certificate unless it is also a valid worst-case upper bound over the declared operating set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A validated worst-case execution-time bound no larger than the deadline certifies schedulability; favorable average or sampled runtimes alone do not.
assumptions_latex: \(T_k\) is the first time to an accepted solver output.
\(W_k\) is valid over the declared instance and execution set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_k\le D_k\Longrightarrow T_k\le D_k.
knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Deadline Schedulability Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between mathematical QP status and real-time availability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: QP feasibility, boundedness, uniqueness, and exact optimality are properties of the mathematical instance and do not imply \(T_k\le D_k\). Conversely, a deadline miss \(T_k>D_k\) does not certify infeasibility or unboundedness. Solver-status certificates and timing certificates are therefore logically independent unless a particular implementation supplies an explicit worst-case execution-time guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A QP can be feasible and uniquely solvable yet arrive too late, while a deadline miss says nothing by itself about infeasibility or unboundedness.
assumptions_latex: A hard deadline \(D_k\) and accepted-output time \(T_k\) are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Mathematical QP status}\not\Rightarrow T_k\le D_k,\qquad T_k>D_k\not\Rightarrow\text{infeasibility or unboundedness}.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility–Timeliness Separation
Deadline-Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard real-time applicability boundary for receding-horizon QP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_k>0\) be the computation time available between sampling instant \(k\) and the required control update. Define \(T_k\in[0,+\infty]\) as the first elapsed time at which the QP solver returns an iterate satisfying the prescribed feasibility and optimality tolerances, with \(T_k=+\infty\) if no such iterate is returned. A deadline failure occurs exactly when \(T_k>D_k\). If no certified admissible fallback control is available at time \(D_k\), no admissible optimization-derived control update is available for that sampling instant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deadline failure occurs when the solver does not return a tolerance-certified QP solution by the update deadline, including when it never returns one; without a certified fallback, no admissible optimization-derived update is available.
assumptions_latex: Solver acceptance tolerances are fixed before execution
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_k>D_k\) is exactly the deadline-failure event; without a certified fallback, no admissible optimization-derived update is available at \(D_k\).

notation.meaning: available computation time at update k
first time to an accepted solver output, or positive infinity if none is returned

children.title: Conditioning-Driven Runtime Risk
children.top_down_role: Runtime variability attributable to numerical conditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning-Driven Runtime Risk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual accuracy required from a linear-system solve inside a QP method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular linear system \(Kz=b\) and an approximate solution \(\widehat z\) with residual \(r=b-K\widehat z\), \[\frac{\lVert z-\widehat z\rVert_2}{\lVert z\rVert_2}\leq\kappa_2(K)\frac{\lVert r\rVert_2}{\lVert b\rVert_2}.\] Consequently, guaranteeing relative solution error at most \(\varepsilon\) requires the sufficient residual tolerance \(\lVert r\rVert_2/\lVert b\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon/\kappa_2(K)\). Increasing conditioning therefore tightens the required residual tolerance and creates runtime risk for any solver whose work grows as its stopping tolerance decreases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A larger KKT condition number demands a proportionally smaller residual for the same solution accuracy, increasing the risk of exceeding a fixed runtime budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert r\rVert_2/\lVert b\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon/\kappa_2(K)\) is sufficient for relative solution error at most \(\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-to-forward-error inequality is mathematically consistent, but the runtime-risk interpretation depends on a solver work-versus-tolerance model. Both claims need specific inspectable locators.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed conjugate-gradient result is not canonically owned by this MPC runtime-coupling leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\succ0\), let \(z_\star\) solve \(Kz=b\), and let \(z_m\) be the \(m\)-th conjugate-gradient iterate. In exact arithmetic, \(\|z_m-z_\star\|_K/\|z_0-z_\star\|_K\le 2((\sqrt{\kappa_2(K)}-1)/(\sqrt{\kappa_2(K)}+1))^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed CG estimate is mathematically standard but belongs under Krylov linear-system algorithms, not this MPC-specific conditioning-to-runtime relation.
assumptions_latex: Conjugate gradients is performed in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m=O\!\left(\sqrt{\kappa_2(K)}\log(1/\varepsilon)\right)\text{ iterations suffice for the stated energy-norm reduction.}
knowledge_statements.title: Condition-Dependent Krylov Work Bound

intermediate_metadata.reason: The locally owned inventory is the conditional link from conditioning, through residual accuracy, to runtime risk. The proposed CG theorem is deferred because it belongs to Krylov solver theory. Numerical origins of ill-conditioning and the operational deadline-miss definition are excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Parametric-Repeated QP Family
children.top_down_role: QP families whose data change across scenarios, time samples, tuning paths, or outer computational loops.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Parametric problems, factorization caching, and warm starting

children.title: Objective-Vector Parameters
children.top_down_role: Parameter variation entering linear objective coefficients.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Vector Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine parameterization of only the QP linear objective term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An objective-vector-parametric QP has the form \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \frac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+q(\theta)^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad \ell\leq Ax\leq u,\qquad q(\theta)=q_0+Q\theta,\] for \(\theta\in\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p\). The Hessian and feasible set are independent of \(\theta\); only the objective vector varies. Convexity holds for every parameter whenever \(H\succeq0\), and strict convexity holds whenever \(H\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The parameter enters affinely through the linear objective vector, while the Hessian and all constraints remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\theta)=q_0+Q\theta\) with fixed \(H,A,\ell,u\) defines an objective-vector-parametric convex QP.

notation.meaning: linear map from parameters to objective coefficients

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and convexity statements are standard and internally consistent, but the record supplies no citation or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Constraint-Bound Parameters
children.top_down_role: Parameter variation entering equality or inequality bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Bound Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine parameterization of QP lower and upper constraint bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint-bound-parametric QP has the form \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \frac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+q^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad \ell_0+L\theta\leq Ax\leq u_0+U\theta,\qquad \theta\in\Theta.\] The matrices \(H\) and \(A\) and the objective vector \(q\) remain fixed. For each parameter, the problem is a convex QP when \(H\succeq0\), provided its parameter-dependent feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The parameter shifts constraint bounds affinely while the objective and constraint matrix remain fixed; feasibility may depend on the parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell(\theta)=\ell_0+L\theta\) and \(u(\theta)=u_0+U\theta\) define affine bound variation with a fixed convex quadratic objective.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine bound-parameter representation is mathematically consistent and fits the container, but it lacks a supporting citation or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Coupled Parameter-Variation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Joint variation across objective vectors plus constraint bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Parameter-Variation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared parameter components simultaneously varying objective coefficients and constraint bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A coupled linear-term-and-bound family is \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\  rac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+(q_0+Q	heta)^{\mathsf T}x\quad	ext{subject to}\quad \ell_0+L	heta\leq Ax\leq u_0+U	heta,\qquad 	heta\in\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p.\] It is coupled when there exists an index \(j\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\) such that \(Qe_j
eq0\) and either \(Le_j
eq0\) or \(Ue_j
eq0\), so the same scalar parameter component affects both the linear objective term and at least one constraint bound. If \(H\succeq0\), every feasible member is a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The family is coupled when at least one shared parameter component changes both the linear objective vector and one or more constraint bounds, while the Hessian and constraint matrix remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\theta\in\Theta\) having a nonempty feasible set defines a convex QP, and the stated shared-component condition defines coupled objective-and-bound variation.

notation.meaning: j-th coordinate vector in the parameter space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry of the parameter set on which an affine Hessian remains positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric matrices \(H_0,\ldots,H_p\), the set \[\Theta_{\mathrm{cvx}}=\left\{\theta\in\mathbb R^p:H_0+\sum_{j=1}^p\theta_jH_j\succeq0\right\}\] is a closed convex spectrahedron, possibly empty or lower-dimensional. For an externally prescribed domain \(\Theta\), the convexity-preserving parameters are \(\Theta\cap\Theta_{\mathrm{cvx}}\); this intersection is convex whenever \(\Theta\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameters preserving positive-semidefinite quadratic curvature form a closed convex spectrahedron; intersecting it with a convex prescribed domain preserves convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Theta_{\mathrm{cvx}}\) is a closed convex set described by one linear matrix inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectrahedral Convexity-Preserving Domain
Quadratic-Weight Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity-preserving parameter domain for an affine Hessian family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[H(\theta)=H_0+\sum_{j=1}^{p}\theta_jH_j,\qquad H_j=H_j^{\mathsf T}.\] The quadratic-weight parameter domain preserving convexity is \[\Theta_{\mathrm{cvx}}=\left\{\theta\in\mathbb R^p:H(\theta)\succeq0\right\}.\] For each \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{cvx}}\), the function \(x\mapsto\frac12x^{\mathsf T}H(\theta)x+q(\theta)^{\mathsf T}x\) is convex. If \(H(\theta)\succ0\), it is strictly convex and has at most one minimizer over any convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine quadratic-weight family remains convex exactly on the parameter set where its symmetric Hessian is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{cvx}}\) if and only if the parameterized quadratic objective is convex in \(x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-semidefinite parameter domain correctly characterizes convexity of the affine Hessian family and the condition role fits the container, but no supporting locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint-Matrix Parameters Destroy the Finite Piecewise-Affine Law
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contrast with parameterization confined to linear objective terms and constraint bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\theta>0\), consider \[\min_x\ \tfrac12(x-1)^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad \theta x\le1.\] Every fixed-parameter problem is a strictly convex QP with a polyhedral feasible set, but \[x^*(\theta)=\begin{cases}1,&0<\theta\le1,\\1/\theta,&\theta>1,\end{cases}\qquad v(\theta)=\begin{cases}0,&0<\theta\le1,\\\tfrac12(1/\theta-1)^2,&\theta>1.\end{cases}\] Hence affine constraint-matrix parameterization does not generally yield a finite piecewise-affine optimizer map or a finite piecewise-quadratic value map in \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parameter multiplying the decision variable can make the optimizer rational even though every fixed-parameter problem is a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*(\theta)=1/\theta\text{ on }(1,\infty),\text{ so }x^*\text{ is not finite piecewise affine there}.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Matrix Parameters Destroy the Finite Piecewise-Affine Law

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural failures specific to parameters appearing in constraint normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Although \(A(\theta)x\le b(\theta)\) is affine in \(x\) for fixed \(\theta\), it is generally bilinear in \((x,\theta)\). Parameter values at which a relevant row vanishes, reverses orientation, or becomes linearly dependent with other active rows can change feasibility, active-row rank, and multiplier uniqueness. Fixed-parameter convexity therefore does not imply joint convexity, a polyhedral parameter-decision feasible set, or regular active-set sensitivity across such values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing, reorienting, or dependent parameterized constraint rows can change feasibility and KKT regularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}A_I(\theta)\text{ and the geometry of }\{x:A(\theta)x\le b(\theta)\}\text{ may change with }\theta.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Row Rank and Orientation Changes
Constraint-Matrix Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine parameterization of coefficients multiplying the decision vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint-matrix-parametric QP may be written as \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \frac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+q(\theta)^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad A(\theta)x\leq b(\theta),\] where \(A(\theta)=A_0+\sum_{j=1}^{p}\theta_jA_j\). For every fixed \(\theta\), these constraints are affine in \(x\), so the feasible set is polyhedral and the problem is convex when \(H\succeq0\). Joint dependence on \((x,\theta)\) is generally bilinear rather than affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constraint matrix varies affinely with the parameter; each fixed-parameter problem is convex, although the combined decision-parameter description is generally bilinear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed \(\theta\), \(A(\theta)x\leq b(\theta)\) defines a polyhedral feasible set in \(x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-parameter polyhedrality and convexity claims are mathematically consistent, including the warning about joint bilinearity, but the representation lacks a source or standard-field rationale.

children.title: Active-Set Stability
children.top_down_role: Parameter neighborhoods retaining a fixed active-set pattern.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity Conditions Are Sufficient but Not Necessary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to necessity of LICQ and strict complementarity for active-set constancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\theta\in\mathbb R\), consider \(\min_x \tfrac12x^2+\theta\) subject to \(x\le0\) and \(2x\le0\). The unique optimizer is \(x^*(\theta)=0\), and both constraints are active for every parameter. Their normals are linearly dependent, and the KKT system admits \(\lambda=(0,0)\), so LICQ and strict complementarity fail although the active set is globally constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicated constraints can remain active for every parameter even though LICQ and strict complementarity fail.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I(\theta)=\{1,2\}\ \forall\theta,\qquad \operatorname{rank}\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\end{bmatrix}=1<2,\qquad \lambda=(0,0)\text{ is optimal}.

notation.meaning: set of inequalities tight at the optimizer

knowledge_statements.title: Regularity Conditions Are Sufficient but Not Necessary
Active-Set Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local stability theorem for a strictly convex affine multiparametric QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_x\ \frac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+(F\theta+f)^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Gx\leq W\theta+w,\] with \(H\succ0\). Suppose that at \(\theta_0\) the active rows \(G_I\) are linearly independent and the corresponding multipliers are strictly positive. Then there exists a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\theta_0\) on which the active set remains \(I\). On \(U\), the unique primal solution and active multipliers are affine functions of \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ and strict complementarity make an active set locally constant; within that neighborhood, the optimizer and active multipliers vary affinely.
assumptions_latex: Active multipliers at \(\theta_0\) are strictly positive
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a neighborhood \(U\) with \(I(\theta)=I\) and affine maps \(x^*(\theta)\), \(\lambda_I^*(\theta)\) for all \(\theta\in U\).

notation.meaning: parameter neighborhood with stable active set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local active-set stability theorem is plausible under strict convexity, LICQ, strict complementarity, and the implicit strict slackness of inactive constraints, but a theorem-level source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Critical-Region Geometry
children.top_down_role: Parameter-space regions associated with stable solution structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Critical-Region Cover of the Regular Feasible Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage and overlap properties of regular active-set regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible strictly convex affine multiparametric QP, every parameter at which some optimal active set has a nonsingular KKT system belongs to the critical region generated by that set. Hence the nonempty critical regions cover the regular feasible parameter domain. Relative interiors of distinct maximal regions carrying different affine optimizer laws are disjoint; overlaps can occur on shared boundaries or when redundant active-set descriptions generate the same law.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active-set regions cover all regular feasible parameters; different maximal affine pieces meet only at boundaries unless redundant labels describe the same law.
assumptions_latex: At every parameter under consideration, at least one optimal active set has a nonsingular KKT system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Theta_{\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq\bigcup_I\mathcal R_I.

notation.meaning: feasible parameters admitting a regular optimal active set
critical region generated by active set I

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Region Cover of the Regular Feasible Domain
Critical-Region Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral parameter region associated with one nondegenerate active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the strictly convex affine multiparametric QP and a candidate active set \(I\), solve the equality-constrained KKT system to obtain affine maps \(x_I(\theta)\) and \(\lambda_I(\theta)\). Its critical region is \[\mathcal R_I=\left\{\theta\in\Theta:G_{I^c}x_I(\theta)\leq W_{I^c}\theta+w_{I^c},\ \lambda_I(\theta)\geq0\right\}.\] Because every displayed inequality is affine in \(\theta\), \(\mathcal R_I\) is a polyhedron, possibly empty or lower-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A critical region consists of parameters satisfying inactive primal inequalities and active dual inequalities for one active set; it is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_I\) is the intersection of finitely many affine half-spaces and hence is polyhedral.

notation.meaning: critical region for active set I

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The critical-region formula and polyhedrality conclusion are internally consistent for the stated nondegenerate active set, but no inspectable multiparametric-QP source is cited.

children.title: Critical-Region Transition Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Interfaces where neighboring critical regions meet.
