knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of affine optimizer laws on a shared critical-region interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let closed critical regions \(\mathcal R_I\) and \(\mathcal R_J\) of a strictly convex multiparametric QP contain a common feasible parameter \(\bar\theta\), and let \(x_I\) and \(x_J\) be affine optimal-solution laws valid on those regions. Then \(x_I(\bar\theta)=x_J(\bar\theta)=x^*(\bar\theta)\). Thus the primal solution does not jump at a shared feasible interface, although active-set labels and multiplier representations may change or be nonunique there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Neighboring affine optimizer formulas agree on a shared feasible interface because strict convexity gives a unique optimizer.
assumptions_latex: The objective is strictly convex in the decision variable.
Both regional laws are optimal at \(\bar\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_I(\bar\theta)=x_J(\bar\theta).

notation.meaning: parameter on a shared critical-region interface

knowledge_statements.title: Agreement of Neighboring Primal Laws
Critical-Region Transition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary mechanisms through which a nondegenerate active set can change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a full-dimensional nondegenerate critical region \(\mathcal R_I\), an active-set transition can occur only on its boundary. This boundary is contained in the union of the affine sets \[G_jx_I(\theta)=W_j\theta+w_j\quad(j\notin I),\qquad \lambda_i^I(\theta)=0\quad(i\in I),\] together with the boundary of \(\Theta\). The first type of equality permits an inactive constraint to enter the active set, while the second permits an active constraint to leave. Simultaneous equalities identify degenerate or multiple-transition intersections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A critical-region transition can occur where an inactive constraint becomes tight, an active multiplier reaches zero, or the parameter domain ends; simultaneous events identify degenerate intersections.
assumptions_latex: The active-set KKT system is nonsingular in the region
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every nondegenerate transition point lies on an inactive-slack, active-multiplier, or parameter-domain boundary.

notation.meaning: affine optimizer candidate for active set I
candidate multiplier for active constraint i
critical region associated with active set I

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz Regularity of a Finite Continuous Piecewise-Affine Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity consequence of the finite critical-region representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a convex parameter domain \(\Theta\) be covered by finitely many closed polyhedra \(R_k\), and suppose \(x^*(\theta)=F_k\theta+g_k\) on \(R_k\), with the pieces agreeing on overlaps. Then \(x^*\) is globally Lipschitz on \(\Theta\); in the Euclidean norm, \[\|x^*(\theta_1)-x^*(\theta_2)\|_2\le \left(\max_k\|F_k\|_2\right)\|\theta_1-	heta_2\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite continuous piecewise-affine optimizer map on a convex domain is globally Lipschitz, with its largest regional slope as a valid bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Lip}(x^*;\Theta)\le\max_k\|F_k\|_2.

notation.meaning: linear part of the optimizer law on region k

knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Regularity of a Finite Continuous Piecewise-Affine Map
Piecewise-Affine Solution Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-region solution structure of a strictly convex affine multiparametric QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a feasible multiparametric QP \[\min_x\ \frac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+(F\theta+f)^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Gx\leq W\theta+w,\qquad \theta\in\Theta,\] where \(H\succ0\) and \(\Theta\) is polyhedral. If the relevant active-set KKT systems satisfy LICQ, then the unique optimizer map \(x^*: \Theta\to\mathbb R^n\) is affine on each nonempty critical region. Since only finitely many active sets exist, \(x^*\) is a finite piecewise-affine map; it is continuous wherever feasibility persists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly convex affine multiparametric QP has a unique optimizer that is affine on each of finitely many polyhedral critical regions.
assumptions_latex: Relevant active constraint matrices satisfy LICQ
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There are finitely many polyhedral regions \(\mathcal R_k\) and affine maps \(x_k(\theta)\) such that \(x^*(\theta)=x_k(\theta)\) on \(\mathcal R_k\).

notation.meaning: unique optimal solution at parameter theta

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the terminal container and its finite piecewise-affine conclusion is standard for the stated strictly convex affine multiparametric QP setting, but it requires a precise theorem or section locator, especially for the continuity claim.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Piecewise Quadratic Does Not Imply Parameter Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of parameter convexity when the parameter enters the linear objective coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The unconstrained strictly convex QP \(v(\theta)=\min_x\{\tfrac12x^2+\theta x\}\) has \(x^*(\theta)=-\theta\) and \(v(\theta)=-\tfrac12\theta^2\). Thus its value map has one quadratic piece but is concave, not convex, in \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a one-piece quadratic value function can be concave when the parameter enters the linear objective term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v(\theta)=-\tfrac12\theta^2\text{ is not convex in }\theta.
knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise Quadratic Does Not Imply Parameter Convexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order sensitivity of a quadratic value piece on a regular critical region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v(\theta)=\min_x\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+(c+C\theta)^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b+B\theta\}\), suppose a critical region has unique primal and multiplier laws \(x^*(\theta)\) and \(\lambda^*(\theta)\). In its relative interior, \[\nabla v(\theta)=C^{\mathsf T}x^*(\theta)-B^{\mathsf T}\lambda^*(\theta).\] Because both laws are affine there, the gradient is affine and the regional Hessian is constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a regular region, the value gradient is determined by the primal solution and inequality multipliers and is affine in the parameter.
assumptions_latex: The regional primal and multiplier solutions are unique.
The active-set KKT system is nonsingular.
\(\theta\) lies in the relative interior of the critical region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla v(\theta)=C^{\mathsf T}x^*(\theta)-B^{\mathsf T}\lambda^*(\theta).
knowledge_statements.title: Regional Value-Gradient Formula
Piecewise-Quadratic Value Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictly convex multiparametric QPs with affine parameter dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H\succ0\), define \(v(\theta)=\min_x\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+(c+C\theta)^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b+B\theta\}\). On any polyhedral parameter domain where the problem is feasible, the finitely many admissible active sets induce polyhedral critical regions \(R_j\). On each full-dimensional \(R_j\), the unique optimizer has the form \(x^*(\theta)=F_j\theta+g_j\), and substitution gives \(v(\theta)=\tfrac12\theta^{\mathsf T}Q_j\theta+q_j^{\mathsf T}\theta+r_j\). Hence \(v\) is continuous and piecewise quadratic on the feasible parameter domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible strictly convex parametric QP has an affine optimizer and quadratic optimal value on each polyhedral critical region; its value map is continuous and piecewise quadratic.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraint bounds depend affinely on \(\theta\).
The considered parameter domain is polyhedral and feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v|_{R_j}\) is quadratic for every critical region \(R_j\), and \(v\) is continuous and piecewise quadratic.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf and is mathematically plausible, but no citation supports the global continuity, finite polyhedral critical-region decomposition, and piecewise-quadratic conclusion under the stated hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to treating every degeneracy condition as a lower-dimensional parameter boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\theta>0\), consider \(\min_x\tfrac12(x-\theta)^2\) subject to \(x\le0\) and \(2x\le0\). The unique optimizer is \(x^*(\theta)=0\) throughout \((0,\infty)\). Both inequalities are active and their normals are dependent. The multiplier set is \(\{(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\ge0:\lambda_1+2\lambda_2=\theta\}\), so active-row and multiplier degeneracy persist on an open parameter region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicated constraints can produce active-row and multiplier degeneracy throughout an open parameter region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\end{bmatrix}=1<2\quad\text{for every }\theta\in(0,\infty).
knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy Need Not Be Boundary-Confined

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two distinct regularity failures relevant to parametric-QP strata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a parameter \(\theta\), let \(I(\theta)=\{i:G_i x^*(\theta)=w_i(\theta)\}\). Active-constraint degeneracy occurs when \(G_{I(\theta)}\) lacks full row rank. A particular KKT pair \((x^*(\theta),\lambda^*(\theta))\) is weakly complementary when \(\lambda_i^*(\theta)=0\) for some \(i\in I(\theta)\). These conditions are distinct: the first concerns active normals, whereas the second concerns a selected multiplier representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank-deficient active normals and zero multipliers on active constraints are distinct forms of degeneracy.
assumptions_latex: The parameterized QP has a KKT solution at \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}G_I<|I|\quad\text{and}\quad (\exists i\in I:\lambda_i^*=0)\quad\text{are distinct degeneracy conditions}.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Constraint and Complementarity Degeneracy
Degenerate Parametric Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundaries where regular active-set descriptions cease to be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a parametric QP and parameter \(\theta\), let \(I(\theta)\) be an active inequality set with multiplier vector \(z_I^*(\theta)\). A degenerate boundary consists of parameters satisfying at least one of \(\operatorname{rank}A_I<|I|\), \(z_i^*(\theta)=0\) for some \(i\in I\), or zero slack for an inactive constraint. At such parameters, multiple active-set labels or adjacent critical regions may describe the same optimizer, so the one-active-set/one-region correspondence and a locally unique affine sensitivity formula can fail, even when the primal optimizer remains unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank-deficient active constraints, zero active multipliers, or ambiguous zero slacks mark boundaries where active-set labels and affine sensitivity descriptions need not be unique.
assumptions_latex: The QP data depend continuously on \(\theta\).
KKT conditions hold at the parameter under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Degeneracy can destroy uniqueness of the active-set region description without destroying uniqueness of \(x^*(\theta)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this characterization. Moreover, rank deficiency or a zero active multiplier need not occur only on a parameter boundary, and an “inactive constraint” ordinarily cannot have zero slack. An authoritative treatment is needed to determine the correct degeneracy conditions and scope.

children.title: Primal-Dual Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of primal plus dual solution estimates across QP instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization contract for consecutive primal-dual QP solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the QP \(\min_x\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), a primal-dual warm start is an initialization tuple \((x^0,y^0,z^0)\) imported from a related solve, where \(x^0\) initializes the primal variable, \(y^0\) initializes equality multipliers, and \(z^0\ge0\) initializes inequality multipliers. An interior-point interface may additionally require strictly positive slacks \(s^0=h-Gx^0>0\) and \(z^0>0\), or apply a declared repair map before iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual warm start initializes a related QP with previously computed primal variables and equality and inequality multipliers, subject to the receiving solver’s domain requirements.
assumptions_latex: The new QP uses compatible primal and dual dimensions.
The solver declares whether infeasible or noninterior initial points are accepted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^0,y^0,z^0)\) is admissible only when it belongs to the receiving solver's initialization domain.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the warm-start interface leaf, but the solver-dependent admissibility and repair claims have no cited specification or textbook source.

children.title: Working-Set Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Reuse of working-set information across related QPs.

knowledge_statements.title: Working-Set Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set initialization for a related QP instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For inequalities indexed by \(\mathcal I\), a working-set warm start supplies a set \(W^0\subseteq\mathcal I\) inherited from a related QP. The receiving active-set method initially treats constraints in \(W^0\) as equalities, solves the corresponding equality-constrained QP, and then adds a violated inactive constraint or removes an active constraint with an inadmissible multiplier according to its pivot rule. The interface must reject or repair \(W^0\) when its indices are invalid or its active rows violate the solver's rank requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A working-set warm start reuses a candidate active-constraint set, which the active-set solver then corrects through its ordinary add-and-remove pivots.
assumptions_latex: The old and new inequality indices have a declared correspondence.
The receiving active-set method specifies rank and feasibility requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The warm start is the initial active set \(W^0\), not a certificate that \(W^0\) is optimal for the new QP.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The initial-working-set concept fits the leaf, but the stated equality-constrained solve and add/remove behavior describes a particular class of active-set methods rather than every receiving interface. A source is required to delimit the intended algorithm variant.

children.title: Warm-Start Compatibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Instance changes that reduce warm-start relevance or validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Compatibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural conditions limiting safe reuse of prior solver state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stored warm start is incompatible with a new QP whenever no declared mapping preserves the meanings and dimensions of its components. Concretely, primal-dual vectors cannot be copied if variable or constraint dimensions change without an embedding, and a working set cannot be copied if an index is deleted, reordered without a permutation, or mapped to a constraint outside the new model. Moreover, an interior-point state with \(s_i^0\le0\) or \(z_i^0\le0\) violates a strict-interior initialization contract. Such states must be transformed, repaired, or discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Warm starts cross a compatibility boundary when dimensions, constraint identities, ordering, or solver-domain requirements change without an explicit valid mapping or repair.
assumptions_latex: A previous solver state and a new QP instance are given.
The receiving solver has a declared initialization domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absent a valid state mapping into the new initialization domain, direct warm-start reuse is undefined or inadmissible.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the container, but the cross-instance mapping, strict-interior admissibility, and mandatory transform/repair/discard rules are solver-contract claims without supporting citations.

children.title: Symbolic Factorization Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of ordering, elimination trees, plus symbolic factor structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic Factorization Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of sparse elimination structure across repeated KKT systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given repeated sparse systems \(K_k u_k=r_k\), first form the structural pattern \(\mathcal P=\operatorname{supp}(K_1)\), compute a fill-reducing permutation \(P\), and construct the elimination tree and factor-storage layout for \(PK_1P^{\mathsf T}\). For each later \(K_k\), compare \(\operatorname{supp}(K_k)\) with \(\mathcal P\). If they agree, reuse \(P\), the elimination tree, and the storage layout, perform only numerical factorization and triangular solves, and output \(u_k\). Otherwise repeat symbolic analysis before numerical factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When repeated KKT matrices share a sparsity pattern, their ordering, elimination tree, and factor-storage layout can be analyzed once and reused.
assumptions_latex: Each \(K_k\) is factorable by the selected sparse direct method.
Pattern equality includes all structurally relevant symmetric entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{supp}(K_k)=\mathcal P\) permits reuse of symbolic analysis, but not automatically of numerical factors.

notation.meaning: KKT or linear-system matrix for instance k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits symbolic reuse, but reuse of an elimination tree and storage layout can depend on the factorization and pivoting strategy. No sparse-factorization source establishes the stated pattern-equality rule under the given assumptions.

children.title: Numeric Factorization Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse or updating of numeric factors across repeated QPs.

knowledge_statements.title: Numeric Factorization Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reuse of numerical factors for unchanged repeated systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a previous solve stored a verified factorization \(PKP^{\mathsf T}=LDL^{\mathsf T}\). For a new system \(K_k u_k=r_k\), test whether \(K_k=K\) under the same permutation and scaling. If equality holds, compute \(u_k=P^{\mathsf T}L^{-\mathsf T}D^{-1}L^{-1}Pr_k\) using only triangular and diagonal solves. If any numerical entry of \(K_k\) differs, the stored factors are not an exact factorization of the new matrix and numerical refactorization or a validated update method is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stored numerical factors may be reused exactly for new right-hand sides only when the factored matrix, permutation, and scaling remain unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The stored factorization is nonsingular and numerically accepted.
Matrix equality is tested after applying the same ordering and scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact factor reuse is valid when \(K_k=K\); pattern equality alone is insufficient.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact factor-reuse rule is plausible and the algorithm kind fits, but no cited source supports the equality requirements, scaling convention, or solve formula.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Validation of a Reused Numerical Factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic linear-system residual validation rather than a factor-reuse-specific certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat u\) be obtained by applying cached factors to \(K_{\rm new}u=r\), and define \[\eta=\frac{\lVert r-K_{\rm new}\widehat u\rVert}{\lVert K_{\rm new}\rVert\lVert\widehat u\rVert+\lVert r\rVert}.\] Then \(\eta\le\tau\) verifies the declared scaled-residual tolerance, but does not establish that the cached factors factor \(K_{\rm new}\) or that the forward error is small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaled residual checks a computed linear-system solution but does not validate exact numerical-factor reuse.
assumptions_latex: The residual is evaluated with the actual new matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta\le\tau\Longrightarrow\lVert r-K_{\rm new}\widehat u\rVert\le\tau(\lVert K_{\rm new}\rVert\lVert\widehat u\rVert+\lVert r\rVert).
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Validation of a Reused Numerical Factorization

intermediate_metadata.reason: The locally owned inventory is exact cached-factor application and its unchanged-matrix boundary. Symbolic preprocessing and pattern-change rules are excluded as sibling scopes; generic residual validation is deferred to the linear-system solve interface.

children.title: Sparsity-Pattern Change Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural changes requiring renewed symbolic processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity-Pattern Change Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural changes that invalidate cached symbolic factorization data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P_{m old}=\operatorname{supp}(K_{m old})\) be the pattern used to compute a permutation, elimination tree, and factor-storage layout. If \(\operatorname{supp}(K_{m new})\ne\mathcal P_{m old}\), then the cached symbolic objects are not certified for \(K_{m new}\): a newly nonzero entry may introduce unallocated fill or new elimination dependencies, while removed entries may change pivoting and structural-rank behavior. The safe boundary rule is to repeat symbolic analysis unless the factorization implementation explicitly supports and validates the particular pattern update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding or removing structural nonzeros crosses the default symbolic-reuse boundary and requires fresh analysis unless a validated dynamic-pattern update is available.
assumptions_latex: Symbolic data were computed for \(K_{m old}\).
No validated dynamic-pattern update procedure is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{supp}(K_{m new})\ne\operatorname{supp}(K_{m old})\) invalidates unconditional symbolic reuse.

notation.meaning: matrix for the new QP instance
structural nonzero pattern of a matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but the effects of added and removed structural entries depend on the sparse factorization and pivoting implementation. A direct source is needed for the stated default invalidation rule.

children.title: Batched QP Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces grouping multiple QP instances into a shared submission.

knowledge_statements.title: Batched QP Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-call interface for a finite collection of QP instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A batched QP interface accepts indexed data \(\{H_i,c_i,A_i,b_i\}_{i=1}^N\) representing \(N\) problems \(\min_{x_i}\tfrac12x_i^{\mathsf T}H_ix_i+c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i\) subject to \(A_ix_i\le b_i\), together with per-instance options or broadcast options. It returns indexed statuses and outputs \(\{(\sigma_i,x_i^*,v_i^*)\}_{i=1}^N\). The interface preserves instance identity: output \(i\) describes only input problem \(i\), even when storage, preprocessing, or computational kernels are shared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A batched interface submits many indexed QPs in one call and returns a separate status, optimizer, and value for each corresponding instance.
assumptions_latex: Every instance has a well-defined data slice and output index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The batch operation represents the indexed product of \(N\) QP solves.

notation.meaning: reported optimizer and value for instance i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches a batched QP interface, but no authoritative API or interface specification supports the required indexed outputs, broadcast-option behavior, and identity-preservation contract.

children.title: Parallel QP Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Concurrent execution interfaces across processing resources.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel QP Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent execution contract for multiple QP solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parallel QP interface maps an indexed family \(\{Q_i\}_{i=1}^N\) to indexed results \(\{R_i\}_{i=1}^N\) while permitting two or more solve intervals to overlap in time. Each result \(R_i=(\sigma_i,x_i^*,v_i^*)\) must be observationally equivalent, within declared numerical tolerances and nondeterminism, to solving \(Q_i\) alone with the same options. The contract must specify synchronization, cancellation, error isolation, and whether solver objects or factorization workspaces may be shared safely among concurrent instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parallel interface allows QP solves to overlap while preserving per-instance result identity and declaring synchronization, cancellation, errors, and shared-state safety.
assumptions_latex: The family contains finitely many indexed QPs.
Concurrent execution uses resources allowed by the implementation contract.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Concurrency may change execution order but must not mix the mathematical inputs or outputs of distinct instances.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the parallel-interface leaf, but observational equivalence, synchronization, cancellation, error isolation, and workspace-sharing requirements are implementation-contract claims with no cited specification.

children.title: Batch-Independence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Instance-separability conditions relevant to batched execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Batch-Independence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separability condition for a collection of QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the joint batch problem have variables \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\), objective \(\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)\), and feasible set \(X_1\times\cdots\times X_N\). This is a batch-independence regime precisely when no constraint, objective term, state update, or stopping rule couples distinct indices. Then \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in X_i,\,1\le i\le N}\sum_i f_i(x_i)=\prod_{i=1}^N\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in X_i}f_i(x_i)\), and the joint optimal value equals the sum of the individual optimal values whenever all minima are attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A batch is mathematically independent when its objective and feasible set separate by instance; the joint solution set is then the product of individual solution sets.
assumptions_latex: No cross-instance stopping or state rule changes the mathematical problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}\sum_i f_i=\prod_i\operatorname*{argmin}f_i\) and \(v^*=\sum_i v_i^*\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits and the separability formula is standard under attainment, but the record supplies no source for the exact product-of-argmin and value-additivity statement.

children.title: Cross-Instance Resource Contention
children.top_down_role: Memory, bandwidth, plus scheduling pressure across concurrent solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Instance Resource Contention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Execution boundary where independent solves compete for finite resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(N\) mathematically independent QP solves executed concurrently on a resource of capacity \(C\). If their simultaneous demands \(d_1,\ldots,d_N\) satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^N d_i>C\), at least one solve must wait, spill, or receive less than its requested share. Consequently, mathematical batch independence does not imply independent runtimes or linear speedup. The same boundary applies separately to worker slots, memory, memory bandwidth, accelerator capacity, and shared factorization workspaces; unsafe mutable workspace sharing can additionally invalidate result isolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent QPs can still contend for finite workers, memory, bandwidth, accelerators, or mutable workspaces, preventing independent runtimes and linear speedup.
assumptions_latex: A shared execution resource has finite capacity \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i d_i>C\) forces serialization, reduced allocation, or overflow handling for at least one instance.

notation.meaning: simultaneous resource demand of instance i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the scalar capacity model does not by itself define whether demands are divisible, spillable, queueable, or simultaneously measured. No source supports its extension to all listed resources or the workspace-isolation claim.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-Set Kink in a Differentiable QP Layer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure example at an active-set transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[x^*(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\ge0}\tfrac12(x-\theta)^2,\] one has \(x^*(\theta)=\max\{\theta,0\}\). Hence \(Dx^*(\theta)=0\) for \(\theta<0\), \(Dx^*(\theta)=1\) for \(\theta>0\), and no classical derivative exists at \(\theta=0\). At that parameter the bound is active with zero multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strongly convex QP layer can be nondifferentiable when a constraint enters or leaves the active set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*(\theta)=\max\{\theta,0\}\text{ is not differentiable at }\theta=0.

notation.meaning: Optimal scalar decision as a function of the parameter.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Kink in a Differentiable QP Layer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal regularity for a strongly convex QP with fixed constraint matrices and affine parameter dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[x^*(\theta)=\arg\min_x\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q(\theta)^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{s.t.}\quad Ax=b(\theta),\quad Gx\le h(\theta),\] where \(Q\succ0\), the matrices \(A,G\) are fixed, and \(q,b,h\) are affine in \(\theta\). On the feasible parameter set, the unique optimizer is a continuous piecewise-affine function on a finite polyhedral subdivision. It is differentiable on the relative interior of every region and almost everywhere relative to the affine hull of the feasible parameter set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strongly convex multiparametric QP has a continuous piecewise-affine optimizer map, with derivatives constant inside its critical regions.
assumptions_latex: The parameter is restricted to the feasible parameter set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*(\theta)\text{ is continuous and piecewise affine on the feasible parameter set.}
knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Affine Parametric QP Solution Map
Differentiable QP-Layer Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local implicit-differentiation interface for a convex QP with a fixed active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta\mapsto(Q,c,A,b,G,h)\) be continuously differentiable near \(\bar\theta\), and let \(w=(x,y,z_{\mathcal A})\) collect a primal solution and the multipliers of the active inequalities. Write the corresponding equality-form KKT equations as \(F(w,\theta)=0\). If the active set \(\mathcal A\) is locally constant, inactive slacks are strict, active multipliers are positive, and \(D_wF(\bar w,\bar\theta)\) is nonsingular, then a locally unique differentiable solution map exists and its directional derivative satisfies \[D_wF(\bar w,\bar\theta)\,Dw(\bar\theta)[\dot\theta]=-D_\theta F(\bar w,\bar\theta)[\dot\theta].\] For a scalar loss \(\ell(x)\), reverse-mode derivatives are obtained by solving \(D_wF(\bar w,\bar\theta)^{\mathsf T}v=(\nabla_x\ell,0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under active-set stability and a nonsingular KKT Jacobian, the QP solution is locally differentiable; forward and reverse derivatives require linear solves with that Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(\theta)\succeq0\) and all problem data are continuously differentiable near \(\bar\theta\).\)
Strict complementarity and locally unchanged active constraints hold at \((\bar w,\bar\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Dw(\bar\theta)[\dot\theta]=-D_wF(\bar w,\bar\theta)^{-1}D_\theta F(\bar w,\bar\theta)[\dot\theta].\)
review_flags: Exact differentiable-QP-layer theorem requires an authoritative sensitivity or implicit-differentiation source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interface and implicit-differentiation formula fit the leaf, but the precise active-set, strict-complementarity, nonsingularity, and reverse-mode claims require an authoritative sensitivity or differentiable-QP source.

children.title: QP Certificate-Duality-Sensitivity System
children.top_down_role: Certificate and dual-representation navigation specialized to convex QPs; general theorem statements and proofs remain in convex-analysis chapters.

children.title: QP KKT Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Terminal at the family level because further subdivision would enumerate individual KKT conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: QP KKT Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary-and-sufficient certificate for a finite-dimensional convex QP with affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_x\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\quad Gx\le h,\] where \(Q\succeq0\). A triple \((x,y,z)\) is a KKT optimality certificate when \[Ax=b,\quad Gx\le h,\quad z\ge0,\quad Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\quad z_i(G_ix-h_i)=0\ \text{for every }i.\] Every such certificate proves that \(x\) is globally optimal. Conversely, whenever an optimal solution exists, the polyhedral normal-cone formula yields multipliers \((y,z)\) satisfying these conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementary slackness jointly form a verifiable and complete global-optimality certificate for a convex polyhedral QP.
assumptions_latex: The constraints \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\) are affine.
A finite optimal solution exists for the converse assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y,z)\) satisfies the displayed KKT system if and only if \(x\) is optimal and \((y,z)\) are compatible optimal multipliers.

notation.meaning: Row i of the inequality matrix.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods
source_refs.locator: 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods
source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit global lower-bound identity furnished by a convex-QP KKT certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x,y,z)\) satisfy the convex-QP KKT system for \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), with \(z\ge0\). For every feasible \(u\), \[f(u)-f(x)=\tfrac12(u-x)^{\mathsf T}Q(u-x)-z^{\mathsf T}(Gu-Gx)\ge0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KKT certificate decomposes every feasible competitor's objective excess into nonnegative curvature and inequality-multiplier terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(u)\ge f(x)\) for every feasible \(u\).
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Objective-Difference Certificate
Positive-Definite Curvature Dual QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit Lagrange dual obtained by eliminating the primal variable when \(Q\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal QP \[\min_x\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\quad Gx\le h,\] suppose \(Q\succ0\). For equality multipliers \(y\) and inequality multipliers \(z\ge0\), set \(r=c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z\). The Lagrangian has the unique minimizer \(x(y,z)=-Q^{-1}r\), so the dual QP is \[\max_{y,\,z\ge0}\ -\tfrac12r^{\mathsf T}Q^{-1}r-b^{\mathsf T}y-h^{\mathsf T}z.\] If the primal is feasible and attains its optimum, its value equals this dual value, and any dual maximizer together with \(x(y,z)\) satisfies the KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-definite curvature permits exact elimination of the primal variable, producing a concave quadratic dual over equality and nonnegative inequality multipliers.
assumptions_latex: The primal is feasible and attains its optimum for the strong-duality conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=\max_{y,\,z\ge0}\{-\tfrac12r^{\mathsf T}Q^{-1}r-b^{\mathsf T}y-h^{\mathsf T}z\}\), with \(x^*=-Q^{-1}r^*\).

notation.meaning: Lagrangian linear coefficient in the primal variable.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods
source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessity of the Dual Range Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure when a singular-curvature pseudoinverse formula omits range compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\) and \(r=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(r\notin\operatorname{range}(Q)\) and \(\inf_x\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+r^{\mathsf T}x\}=\inf_{x_1,x_2}\{\tfrac12x_1^2+x_2\}=-\infty\). The bare expression \(-\tfrac12r^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger r\), however, equals zero. It represents the dual function only when \((I-QQ^\dagger)r=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without range compatibility, the pseudoinverse expression can be finite while the Lagrangian infimum is minus infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r\notin\operatorname{range}(Q),\quad\inf_xL(x)=-\infty,\quad-\tfrac12r^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger r=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Necessity of the Dual Range Constraint
Singular-Curvature Dual Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudoinverse dual representation for positive-semidefinite, possibly singular QP curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex QP with objective \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\), constraints \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), and \(Q\succeq0\), define \(r=c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z\). The infimum of the Lagrangian over \(x\) is finite exactly when \(r\in\operatorname{range}(Q)\); in that case it equals \(-\tfrac12r^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger r-b^{\mathsf T}y-h^{\mathsf T}z\). Hence the dual is \[\max_{y,\,z}\ -\tfrac12r^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger r-b^{\mathsf T}y-h^{\mathsf T}z\quad\text{subject to}\quad z\ge0,\quad (I-QQ^\dagger)r=0.\] Primal minimizers associated with feasible multipliers have the form \(x=-Q^\dagger r+v\), where \(v\in\ker Q\) is selected to satisfy the primal constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singular curvature adds a range constraint to the dual; the pseudoinverse determines the curved component, while null-space components remain free.
assumptions_latex: The primal constraints are \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed pseudoinverse problem is the Lagrange dual, and dual finiteness is equivalent to \((I-QQ^\dagger)r=0\).
review_flags: A source explicitly supporting the pseudoinverse dual and range constraint is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The range-constrained pseudoinverse dual is plausible and locally appropriate, but its exact formula and the interpretation of null-space primal components lack cited support.

knowledge_statements.title: Least-Squares Dual Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-variable dual of a linearly constrained least-squares QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_x\ \tfrac12\lVert Bx-d\rVert_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\quad Gx\le h.\] Introducing \(u=Bx-d\) and a multiplier \(w\) for that equation gives the dual model \[\max_{w,y,z}\ -\tfrac12\lVert w\rVert_2^2-d^{\mathsf T}w-b^{\mathsf T}y-h^{\mathsf T}z\quad\text{subject to}\quad B^{\mathsf T}w+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\quad z\ge0.\] At a primal-dual optimum, \(w=Bx-d\), and the remaining equality is stationarity. If the primal is feasible and attains a finite optimum, the primal and dual optimal values coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained least-squares QP has a dual whose quadratic term is the residual norm and whose equality constraint enforces stationarity.
assumptions_latex: The primal is feasible and has a finite attained optimum for the value-equality assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=\max\{-\tfrac12\lVert w\rVert_2^2-d^{\mathsf T}w-b^{\mathsf T}y-h^{\mathsf T}z:B^{\mathsf T}w+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\ z\ge0\}.\)

notation.meaning: Least-squares residual multiplier, equal to the optimal residual.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for the residual-variable least-squares dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal and dual models in the seed, let \(r=Bx-d\). If \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), \(z\ge0\), and \(B^{\mathsf T}w+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0\), then \[\tfrac12\lVert r\rVert^2-\bigl(-\tfrac12\lVert w\rVert^2-d^{\mathsf T}w-b^{\mathsf T}y-h^{\mathsf T}z\bigr)=\tfrac12\lVert r-w\rVert^2+z^{\mathsf T}(h-Gx)\ge0.\] The gap is zero exactly when \(w=r\) and \(z_i(h_i-G_i x)=0\) for every inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The least-squares primal-dual gap is a residual-multiplier mismatch square plus inequality complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(x)-d(w,y,z)=\tfrac12\lVert Bx-d-w\rVert^2+z^{\mathsf T}(h-Gx)\ge0.

Regular Polyhedral QP Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LICQ-based local regularity condition for an active face of a polyhedral QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) solve a convex QP with constraints \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), and define the active set \(\mathcal A(x^*)=\{i:G_ix^*=h_i\}\). The solution lies in the regular polyhedral regime when \[\operatorname{rank}\begin{bmatrix}A\\G_{\mathcal A(x^*)}\end{bmatrix}=m+|\mathcal A(x^*)|,\] after redundant equality rows have been removed. This linear-independence constraint qualification implies uniqueness of the KKT multiplier pair associated with \(x^*\). If, additionally, every active inequality multiplier is positive and the reduced Hessian is positive definite on \(\{d:Ad=0,\ G_{\mathcal A(x^*)}d=0\}\), then the local primal-dual KKT system is nonsingular and the active solution branch is locally isolated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral QP is locally regular when active constraint normals are independent; strict complementarity and positive reduced curvature make its KKT system nonsingular.
assumptions_latex: Redundant equality rows have been removed.
The additional nonsingularity conclusion assumes strict complementarity and positive reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: LICQ gives unique multipliers at \(x^*\); with the two additional conditions, the active-set KKT Jacobian is nonsingular.

notation.meaning: Indices of inequalities active at the solution.

review_flags: The locator may not cover LICQ, strict complementarity, and KKT nonsingularity in full.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits, but the cited polyhedral-sets locator does not clearly support LICQ multiplier uniqueness, strict complementarity, reduced-Hessian curvature, and KKT-Jacobian nonsingularity together. A sensitivity or nonlinear-programming regularity source is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes rank, complementarity, and curvature failures at a convex polyhedral-QP KKT point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a KKT point with active-constraint matrix \(C\), distinct degeneracy mechanisms are: \(C\) lacks full row rank; an active inequality has zero multiplier for the selected KKT triple; or the reduced Hessian \(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\), where \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker C\), is singular. Rank failure makes the active bordered KKT matrix singular. With full row rank and \(Q\succeq0\), reduced-Hessian singularity also makes it singular. A zero active multiplier marks a boundary at which the active set may change under perturbation, but alone implies neither primal nonuniqueness nor singularity of the equality-active bordered matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent active normals, weak complementarity, and flat reduced curvature are distinct failures with different consequences.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) stacks equality rows and selected active inequality rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}C<\operatorname{rows}(C)\ \text{or}\ \det(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ)=0\Rightarrow\text{singular active bordered KKT matrix}.

notation.meaning: Basis for the active tangent null space.

review_flags: Degeneracy terminology varies; the record distinguishes rather than equates the mechanisms.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Polyhedral KKT Degeneracy Mechanisms

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Complementarity without Rank or Curvature Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates zero active multipliers from the other degeneracy mechanisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x\tfrac12x^2\) subject to \(-x\le0\). The unique solution is \(x^*=0\), the active normal is nonzero, and the multiplier is \(\lambda^*=0\), so strict complementarity fails. The active bordered matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\-1&0\end{bmatrix}\) is nevertheless nonsingular. Thus weak complementarity alone need not cause primal nonuniqueness or bordered-system singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero active multiplier can occur at a unique, rank-regular solution with a nonsingular bordered KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda^*=0,\quad x^*=0\text{ is unique},\quad\det\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\-1&0\end{bmatrix}=-1.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Complementarity without Rank or Curvature Failure
Degenerate Polyhedral QP Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete multiplier degeneracy caused by dependent active polyhedral constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R}\ \tfrac12x^2+x\quad\text{subject to}\quad -x\le0,\quad -x\le0.\] The unique primal solution is \(x^*=0\), but the two active constraint normals are identical, so LICQ fails. The KKT multiplier set is \[\{(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb R_+^2:z_1+z_2=1\}.\] Thus strict convexity and uniqueness of the primal solution do not ensure uniqueness of multipliers or nonsingularity of the primal-dual KKT linearization. This example marks the boundary between a unique primal optimizer and a regular primal-dual solution representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicated active constraints can leave a strictly convex QP with a unique primal solution but infinitely many KKT multipliers and a singular KKT representation.
assumptions_latex: The two displayed inequalities are retained as distinct constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*=0\) is unique, whereas its multiplier set is the nontrivial segment \(\{z\ge0:z_1+z_2=1\}\).\)
review_flags: The self-contained counterexample requires an external source or registered standard-field rationale.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Infeasibility Certificate Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-type certificate for infeasibility of the affine constraint system underlying a QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the QP constraint system \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), a primal-infeasibility certificate is a pair \((y,z)\) satisfying \[z\ge0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z<0.\] These relations are directly checkable and imply that no \(x\) can satisfy the constraints. The certificate depends only on the affine feasible set, not on the quadratic objective. Conversely, if the finite-dimensional polyhedral system is infeasible, a pair satisfying the displayed strict separation conditions exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative linear combination of inequalities plus an unrestricted combination of equalities certifies infeasibility when it cancels all variables and yields a negative constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}=\varnothing\) if and only if such \((y,z)\) exists.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent normalization of strict affine-infeasibility certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \((y,z)\) satisfies \(z\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z<0\), then \(\alpha=-1/(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z)>0\) gives \(b^{\mathsf T}(\alpha y)+h^{\mathsf T}(\alpha z)=-1\). Conversely, every pair satisfying the same cancellation and sign conditions with contradictory constant \(-1\) satisfies the strict form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every strict Farkas certificate can be positively scaled so that its contradictory constant is minus one.
assumptions_latex: The certificate value \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z\) is finite and negative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strict inequality form and the normalization \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z=-1\) are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Farkas Certificates

children.title: Dual-Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate structures associated with dual infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional alternative characterizing feasibility of the singular-Hessian convex-QP dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\succeq0\) and \(K=\{d:Qd=0,\ Ad=0,\ Gd\le0\}\). Exactly one of the following holds: (i) there exist \(y\) and \(z\ge0\) such that \(c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z\in\operatorname{range}(Q)\); (ii) there exists \(d\in K\) with \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\). Hence the finite-valued Lagrange dual is feasible exactly when \(c^{\mathsf T}d\ge0\) for every \(d\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual feasibility is equivalent to nonnegative linear cost on every null-curvature feasible recession direction.
assumptions_latex: Inequalities use the convention \(Gx\le h\), with multipliers \(z\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists(y,z),\ z\ge0:\ c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z\in\operatorname{range}(Q)\iff c^{\mathsf T}d\ge0\ \forall d\in K\).

notation.meaning: Cone of null-curvature feasible recession directions.

review_flags: The term dual-infeasibility certificate here refers specifically to the finite-valued Lagrange-dual feasibility system, not every homogeneous-embedding convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Alternative for Lagrange-Dual Feasibility
Dual-Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction certificate excluding every feasible Lagrange-dual multiplier of a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex QP \(\min\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\), a vector \(d\) satisfying \[Qd=0,\qquad Ad=0,\qquad Gd\le0,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}d<0\] certifies infeasibility of the Lagrange-dual stationarity system. Indeed, any dual-feasible multipliers would have some \(r=c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z\in\operatorname{range}(Q)\) with \(z\ge0\); taking its inner product with \(d\) would give \(c^{\mathsf T}d+z^{\mathsf T}Gd=0\), contradicting strict negativity. Thus no dual-feasible multiplier pair exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null-curvature feasible direction with strictly negative linear cost contradicts dual stationarity and therefore certifies infeasibility of the QP dual.
assumptions_latex: The dual uses multipliers \(y\) for \(Ax=b\) and \(z\ge0\) for \(Gx\le h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed conditions imply that the Lagrange dual has no feasible multiplier pair.
review_flags: An authoritative source for the exact dual-infeasibility ray convention is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direction conditions do contradict feasibility of the singular-curvature Lagrange-dual stationarity system, but the exact dual-infeasibility terminology and convention require an authoritative source.

children.title: Recession-Direction Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate structures based on feasible recession behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneity and canonical normalization of convex-QP recession certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(d\) satisfies \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), \(Qd=0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\), then every \(\alpha d\) with \(\alpha>0\) satisfies the same directional conditions. In particular, \(\widehat d=d/(-c^{\mathsf T}d)\) is an equivalent witness satisfying \(c^{\mathsf T}\widehat d=-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An improving recession witness is scale invariant and can be normalized to have linear slope minus one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat d=d/(-c^{\mathsf T}d)\) satisfies the same homogeneous conditions and \(c^{\mathsf T}\widehat d=-1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Scale Normalization of Improving Rays
Recession-Direction Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable unboundedness ray for a feasible convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_0\) satisfy \(Ax_0=b\) and \(Gx_0\le h\). A nonzero vector \(d\) is a recession-direction certificate of unboundedness when \[Ad=0,\qquad Gd\le0,\qquad Qd=0,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}d<0.\] Then \(x(t)=x_0+td\) is feasible for every \(t\ge0\), and its objective satisfies \[\tfrac12x(t)^{\mathsf T}Qx(t)+c^{\mathsf T}x(t)=\tfrac12x_0^{\mathsf T}Qx_0+c^{\mathsf T}x_0+t\,c^{\mathsf T}d.\] Consequently the objective tends to \(-\infty\), so the primal QP is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible base point plus a null-curvature feasible direction of negative linear cost provides an explicit ray along which the QP objective tends to minus infinity.
assumptions_latex: A feasible base point \(x_0\) is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_0+td\) is feasible for all \(t\ge0\), and the primal optimal value is \(-\infty\).
review_flags: The standard recession calculation requires an authoritative QP unboundedness source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recession-ray calculation is correct under Qd=0 and a supplied feasible base point, and the certificate kind fits. An authoritative QP recession or unboundedness source is still required.

children.title: Certificate Interpretation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Distinctions between dual infeasibility, primal unboundedness, plus ambiguous numerical status.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Flat Recession Is Not Unbounded Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between objective-flat recession and unbounded descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}0\), every nonzero \(d\) satisfies \(Qd=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d=0\), and every ray is feasible. Nevertheless the optimal value is \(0\), not \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible null-curvature ray with zero linear slope may be noncoercive without proving unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A flat recession ray is not an unbounded-descent certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Flat Recession Is Not Unbounded Descent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction satisfying the homogeneous recession tests when no feasible base point exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x -x\) subject to \(0x=1\). The direction \(d=1\) satisfies \(Ad=0\), \(Qd=0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d=-1<0\), but the feasible set is empty. Thus an improving homogeneous direction alone does not certify primal unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An improving homogeneous direction does not prove unboundedness when the original constraints are infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The direction tests hold, but the QP is infeasible rather than unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.title: Recession Without Primal Feasibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative Initial Slope with Positive Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing why negative linear slope is insufficient without null curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the unconstrained QP \(\min_x \tfrac12x^2-x\), the direction \(d=1\) has \(c^{\mathsf T}d=-1<0\) but \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd=1>0\). Along \(x(t)=td\), the objective is \(\tfrac12t^2-t\), which tends to \(+\infty\), while the QP has the finite minimum \(-\tfrac12\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative linear slope does not yield an unbounded ray when positive quadratic curvature eventually dominates it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\) without \(Qd=0\) does not certify unboundedness below.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative Initial Slope with Positive Curvature
Certificate Interpretation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits on interpreting a direction as an unboundedness or dual-infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q\succeq0\), conditions \(Ad=0\) and \(Gd\le0\) alone identify only a recession direction of the constraint set. They do not certify primal unboundedness without a feasible base point and objective decrease. If \(Qd=0\) but \(c^{\mathsf T}d=0\), the objective is constant along the ray rather than decreasing. If \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\), the positive quadratic term eventually dominates any negative linear term, so the ray cannot prove divergence to \(-\infty\). Accordingly, a direction-only certificate must not be interpreted as primal unboundedness unless primal feasibility, null curvature, and strict negative linear cost are all verified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint recession direction is not automatically an unboundedness certificate: it also needs a feasible base point, zero quadratic curvature, and strictly negative linear cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unboundedness-ray interpretation is invalid if feasibility is unknown, \(c^{\mathsf T}d=0\), or \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\).
review_flags: A source distinguishing recession, unboundedness, and dual-infeasibility interpretations is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated distinctions among constraint recession, constant-objective rays, positive-curvature rays, and unboundedness are mathematically sound, but no source supports the interpretation boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous-QP Embedding Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-invariant extraction rules for outcomes returned by a homogeneous convex-QP embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a homogeneous embedding associated with \(\min\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\), an output \((x,y,z,\tau)\) is interpreted only through scale-invariant residual predicates. If \(\tau>0\) and the normalized variables \((x,y,z)/\tau\) satisfy primal feasibility, stationarity, nonnegativity, and complementarity, they form a KKT optimality certificate. If \(\tau=0\) and \((y,z)\) satisfies \(z\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z<0\), it is a primal-infeasibility certificate. If instead \(x\) satisfies \(Qx=0\), \(Ax=0\), \(Gx\le0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}x<0\), it is a dual-infeasibility ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous QP embedding yields an optimal solution when its scale is positive and infeasibility rays when the scale vanishes and the corresponding strict certificate predicate holds.
assumptions_latex: The embedding residuals are zero, or are checked against a declared numerical tolerance.
Certificate interpretation uses the sign convention \(Gx\le h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The \(\tau>0\) branch yields normalized KKT variables; either displayed \(\tau=0\) predicate yields the corresponding infeasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: Candidate dual-infeasibility direction in the zero-scale branch.

review_flags: Embedding equations and normalization conventions vary by solver; an authoritative homogeneous-QP embedding source is required.
The record specifies certificate extraction rather than a unique embedding construction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The extraction predicates resemble standard homogeneous-embedding outcomes, but the embedding equations and auxiliary variables are not specified and conventions vary across QP embeddings. A source tied to one explicit embedding is necessary.

children.title: Optimal-Value Sensitivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-Order Value Sensitivity to Linear-Cost Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact value Hessian on a fixed active face when only the linear objective coefficient varies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\succ0\), let \(C\) have full row rank, and consider \[v(u)=\min_{Cx=d}\left\{\tfrac12x^TQx+(c+Eu)^Tx\right\}.\] If the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker C\), then \[Dx(u)=-Z(Z^TQZ)^{-1}Z^TE,\qquad \nabla^2v(u)=-E^TZ(Z^TQZ)^{-1}Z^TE\preceq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a fixed regular face, pure linear-cost perturbations give a constant optimizer Jacobian and a negative-semidefinite reduced-Hessian value curvature.
assumptions_latex: Only the linear cost depends on \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla^2v(u)=-E^TZ(Z^TQZ)^{-1}Z^TE\preceq0.

notation.meaning: stacked equality and fixed active-inequality matrix
basis matrix for the null space of C

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular Envelope Formula for QP Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order value sensitivity under affine linear-cost and right-hand-side perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[v(u)=\min_x\left\{\tfrac12x^TQx+(c+Eu)^Tx:Ax=b+Bu,\ Gx\le h+Du\right\},\] and define \(L=f+y^T(Ax-b-Bu)+z^T(Gx-h-Du)\). If near \(u_0\) the primal-dual KKT point is unique, the active set is constant, and its constraint rows satisfy LICQ, then \(v\) is differentiable and \[\nabla v(u)=E^Tx(u)-B^Ty(u)-D^Tz(u).\] With fixed \(Q,A,G\), the primal-dual map is affine and \(v\) is quadratic on the region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within a regular active-set region, the value gradient equals the direct cost effect minus the right-hand-side shadow-price effects.
assumptions_latex: The active constraint rows satisfy LICQ.
The active set is locally constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla v(u)=E^Tx(u)-B^Ty(u)-D^Tz(u).

notation.meaning: parametric QP Lagrangian with the stated sign convention

knowledge_statements.title: Regular Envelope Formula for QP Values
Optimal-Value Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Envelope sensitivity for a right-hand-side and linear-cost parametrized strictly convex QP within one regular active-set regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(u)\) be the optimal value of \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TQx+(c+Eu)^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b+Bu\) and \(Gx\le h+Du\). Suppose that near \(u_0\) the optimizer and KKT multipliers \((x(u),y(u),z(u))\) are unique, the active set is constant, and its constraint gradients satisfy LICQ. Then \(v\) is differentiable near \(u_0\), and the envelope formula is \[\nabla v(u)=E^Tx(u)-B^Ty(u)-D^Tz(u).\] If the data depend affinely on \(u\), then \((x,y,z)\) is affine and \(v\) is quadratic on that active-set region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within a regular fixed active set, the value is differentiable; its gradient combines direct cost perturbation with equality and inequality shadow prices.
assumptions_latex: The active constraint gradients have full row rank.
The active set remains constant locally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla v(u)=E^Tx(u)-B^Ty(u)-D^Tz(u)\).

children.title: Multiplier Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Variation of dual multipliers under QP data perturbations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corrected self-contained multiplier derivative for affine cost and right-hand-side perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\min_x\ \tfrac12x^TQx+(c+Eu)^Tx\quad\text{s.t.}\quad Ax=b+Bu,\quad Gx\le h+Du,\] let \(I\) be locally constant, \(C_I=[A^T\ G_I^T]^T\), \(R_I=[B^T\ D_I^T]^T\), and \(\lambda_I=(y,z_I)\). If \(Q\succ0\) and \(C_I\) has full row rank, then \[K_I=\begin{bmatrix}Q&C_I^T\\C_I&0\end{bmatrix}\] is nonsingular and, for every direction \(d\), \[K_I\begin{bmatrix}x'(d)\\\lambda_I'(d)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-Ed\\R_Id\end{bmatrix}.\] Thus \(\lambda_I(u)\) is locally affine and Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a regular fixed active set, active multipliers are affine and their directional derivative is obtained from one correctly signed KKT solve.
assumptions_latex: The active set \(I\) is locally constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_I[x'(d)^T\ \lambda_I'(d)^T]^T=[(-Ed)^T\ (R_Id)^T]^T.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Active-Set Multiplier Derivative

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-Set Preservation for Smooth Multiplier Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primitive sufficient conditions for a unique smooth local multiplier map with unchanged activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a KKT point of a smoothly parametrized convex QP, suppose the equality and active-inequality gradients satisfy LICQ, the Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on their common null space, and every active inequality multiplier is strictly positive. Then a sufficiently small parameter neighborhood has a unique nearby primal-dual KKT triple with the same active set, and its multiplier map is continuously differentiable. If \(Q,A,G\) are fixed and only the linear cost and constraint right-hand sides depend affinely on the parameter, the map is affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ, positive reduced curvature, and strict complementarity preserve the active set and yield a unique smooth multiplier map; fixed matrices with affine vectors make it affine.
assumptions_latex: The active constraint gradients satisfy LICQ.
The Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on the active-constraint null space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,U\ni u_0:\ (y(u),z_I(u))\text{ is unique and }C^1\text{ on }U\text{ with active set }I.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Preservation for Smooth Multiplier Sensitivity
Multiplier Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local multiplier response obtained by differentiating the fixed-active-set KKT system of a strictly convex parametric QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the parametrized QP of the preceding record, let \(I\) be a locally constant active set and define \(C_I=[A^T\;G_I^T]^T\). If \(C_I\) has full row rank and \(Q\succ0\), then the active KKT matrix \(K_I=\begin{bmatrix}Q&C_I^T\\C_I&0\end{bmatrix}\) is nonsingular. Consequently, for every parameter direction \(d\), the directional derivatives of the primal variable and active multipliers are the unique solution of \[K_I\begin{bmatrix}x'(d)\\\lambda_I'(d)\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}E d\\-R_I d\end{bmatrix},\] where \(R_I=[B^T\;D_I^T]^T\). Thus the multiplier map is affine, hence locally Lipschitz, inside the regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed regular active set, multiplier derivatives are obtained from one KKT solve, and the multiplier map is locally affine and Lipschitz.
assumptions_latex: The active set \(I\) is locally constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_I[x'(d)^T\;\lambda_I'(d)^T]^T=-[Ed^T\;-R_Id^T]^T\), uniquely.

children.title: Coupled Value–Multiplier Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes linking value variation to multiplier behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface law coupling limiting value gradients to adjacent regular primal-dual selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a locally Lipschitz value function \(v\) be continuously differentiable on each of finitely many full-dimensional critical regions \(R_j\) incident to \(u_0\). If the regular primal-dual selection on \(R_j\) gives the envelope gradient \(g_j(u)=\nabla_uL(x_j(u),y_j(u),z_j(u);u)\), then \[\partial_Cv(u_0)=\operatorname{conv}\left\{\lim_{u\to u_0,\ u\in R_j}g_j(u):u_0\in\overline{R_j}\right\}.\] Coincident limiting gradients give classical differentiability at the interface; differing limits give a set-valued marginal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjacent primal-dual regimes determine the generalized value gradient, and their limiting envelope gradients must agree for classical interface sensitivity.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many incident full-dimensional critical regions.
Each regional envelope gradient extends continuously to \(u_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial_Cv(u_0)=\operatorname{conv}\{\lim g_j(u)\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Gradient Matching across Primal–Dual Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Self-contained critical-region representation coupling affine primal-dual selections to a quadratic value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_x\ \tfrac12x^TQx+(c+Eu)^Tx\quad\text{s.t.}\quad Ax=b+Bu,\quad Gx\le h+Du,\] with \(Q\succ0\), and use the Lagrangian \(L=f+y^T(Ax-b-Bu)+z^T(Gx-h-Du)\). Fix an active set \(I\) for which \([A^T\ G_I^T]^T\) has full row rank. Solving its nonsingular KKT system makes \((x(u),y(u),z_I(u))\) affine. Its validity region is the polyhedron \[\mathcal R_I=\{u:G_{I^c}x(u)\le h_{I^c}+D_{I^c}u,\ z_I(u)\ge0\}.\] On \(\mathcal R_I\), \(v(u)\) is quadratic and \[\nabla v(u)=E^Tx(u)-B^Ty(u)-D_I^Tz_I(u).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular active set determines one polyhedral critical region, affine primal-dual variables, and a quadratic value with an affine envelope gradient.
assumptions_latex: The equality and active-inequality rows are linearly independent.
The Hessian and constraint matrices are parameter independent; linear costs and right-hand sides depend affinely on \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal R_I\text{ is polyhedral, }(x,y,z_I)\text{ is affine, and }v\text{ is quadratic on }\mathcal R_I.
knowledge_statements.title: Regular Coupled Critical Region
Coupled Value–Multiplier Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-region representation coupling affine primal-dual solutions to a piecewise-quadratic value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an active set \(I\) for an affinely parametrized strictly convex QP. If its KKT matrix is nonsingular, solving the active equalities gives \((x(u),y(u),z_I(u))=(x_0,y_0,z_0)+Mu\). The associated critical region is the polyhedron \[\mathcal R_I=\{u:G_{I^c}x(u)\le h_{I^c}+D_{I^c}u,\ z_I(u)\ge0\}.\] On \(\mathcal R_I\), the value \(v(u)\) is quadratic and satisfies \(\nabla v(u)=E^Tx(u)-B^Ty(u)-D_I^Tz_I(u)\). Hence the same affine primal-dual representation determines both regime validity and the affine value gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each regular active set defines a polyhedral parameter region, affine primal-dual variables, and a quadratic value whose gradient is determined by the multipliers.
assumptions_latex: The active KKT matrix for \(I\) is nonsingular.
All problem data depend affinely on \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_I\) is polyhedral, \((x,y,z_I)\) is affine, and \(v\) is quadratic on \(\mathcal R_I\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Loss of Primal Stability without Strict Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact scalar QP showing that semidefinite curvature does not ensure a continuous optimizer selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(u\in\mathbb R\), let \[S(u)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{-1\le x\le1}ux.\] Then \[S(u)=\{-1\}\ (u>0),\qquad S(0)=[-1,1],\qquad S(u)=\{1\}\ (u<0).\] Consequently no single-valued selection \(x(u)\in S(u)\) is continuous at \(u=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With zero curvature, an arbitrarily small linear-cost perturbation can make every optimizer selection jump, even on a compact feasible interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No selection }x(u)\in S(u)\text{ is continuous at }u=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Primal Stability without Strict Curvature

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local affine and Lipschitz response of a strictly convex parametric QP within a regular fixed active set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_x\ \tfrac12x^TQx+(c+Eu)^Tx\quad\text{s.t.}\quad Ax=b+Bu,\quad Gx\le h+Du,\] with \(Q\succ0\). Let \(I\) be locally constant, set \(C_I=[A^T\ G_I^T]^T\), \(q_I=(b,h_I)\), and \(R_I=[B^T\ D_I^T]^T\). If \(C_I\) has full row rank, then \(K_I=\begin{bmatrix}Q&C_I^T\\C_I&0\end{bmatrix}\) is nonsingular and \((x(u),y(u),z_I(u))\) is affine locally. For every direction \(d\), \[K_I\begin{bmatrix}x'(d)\\y'(d)\\z_I'(d)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-Ed\\R_Id\end{bmatrix}.\] Hence \(x(u)\) is locally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inside a regular fixed active set, the primal solution is affine and its directional derivative is the primal block of one KKT solve.
assumptions_latex: The active set \(I\) is locally constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x(u)\text{ is locally affine and locally Lipschitz, with }x'(d)\text{ given by the displayed KKT system}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Active-Set Primal Sensitivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Metric-Projection Representation and Global Cost Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global primal sensitivity when the polyhedral feasible set is fixed and only the linear cost is perturbed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\succ0\), let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty closed polyhedron, and define \[x(u)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\tfrac12x^TQx+(c+Eu)^Tx\right\}.\] Then \[x(u)=\Pi_X^Q\bigl(-Q^{-1}(c+Eu)\bigr),\qquad \|x(u)-x(v)\|_Q\le\|Q^{-1/2}E(u-v)\|_2.\] The map is continuous and piecewise affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed polyhedral constraints, affine cost perturbations make the optimizer a globally Lipschitz, piecewise-affine metric projection.
assumptions_latex: Only the linear objective coefficient depends on \(u\).

notation.meaning: projection onto X in the Q-induced norm

Primal-Solution Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Lipschitz and affine sensitivity of the unique primal solution inside a regular active-set region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x(u)=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{\tfrac12x^TQx+(c+Eu)^Tx:Ax=b+Bu,\ Gx\le h+Du\}\). If \(Q\succ0\), the active set \(I\) is constant near \(u_0\), and \([A^T\;G_I^T]^T\) has full row rank, then \(x(u)\) is affine near \(u_0\). For a direction \(d\), its derivative is the primal block of the unique solution of the differentiated active KKT system. In particular, there exist \(L>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(u_0\) such that \(\|x(u)-x(w)\|\le L\|u-w\|\) for all \(u,w\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unique strictly convex QP solution varies affinely and Lipschitz-continuously while its regular active set remains unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The active constraint matrix has full row rank.
The active set is locally constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x(u)\) is locally affine and locally Lipschitz at \(u_0\).

notation.meaning: unique primal optimizer at parameter u

children.title: Active-Set Transition Geometry
children.top_down_role: Parameter-space interfaces where active-set patterns change.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which a zero-slack or zero-multiplier set is genuinely a critical-region facet.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonidentical boundary equality arising from one inactive slack or active multiplier defines a facet of a full-dimensional critical region only when its intersection with the region has codimension one and the equality is not implied by the remaining region inequalities. A redundant or identically zero equality, or one attained only together with another independent equality, need not define a facet.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate transition hyperplane is a facet only when it is nonredundant and cuts a full-dimensional region in codimension one.
assumptions_latex: The critical region is full dimensional for the facet assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zero slack or zero active multiplier is necessary for a regular transition but is not by itself sufficient for facet status.
knowledge_statements.title: Facet Qualification Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter-space representation associated with a regular active set in a fixed-matrix multiparametric QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a strictly convex QP whose Hessian and constraint matrices are fixed while its linear objective and constraint right sides depend affinely on \(u\). If the KKT matrix for active set \(I\) is nonsingular, its fixed-active-set primal and multiplier solution \((x_I(u),z_I(u))\) is affine in \(u\). Its critical region is \[\mathcal R_I=\{u:G_jx_I(u)\le h_j(u)\ (j\notin I),\ z_i(u)\ge0\ (i\in I)\}.\] Hence \(\mathcal R_I\) is a polyhedron, possibly empty or lower dimensional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular active set defines a polyhedral parameter region through affine inactive-slack and active-multiplier inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succ0\), and the equality and inequality matrices are independent of \(u\).
The linear objective and constraint right sides depend affinely on \(u\).
The fixed-active-set KKT matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_I\) is the polyhedron defined by inactive primal feasibility and active multiplier nonnegativity.

notation.meaning: Critical region associated with active set \(I\).
Affine fixed-active-set primal and active-multiplier maps.
