Active-Set Transition Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary geometry of adjacent critical regions in an affinely parametrized strictly convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Within a regular critical region \(\mathcal R_I\), both \(x(u)\) and \(z_I(u)\) are affine. A transition from active set \(I\) can therefore occur only on a boundary piece where either an inactive slack vanishes, \[G_jx(u)-h_j-D_ju=0\quad(j\notin I),\] or an active multiplier vanishes, \[z_i(u)=0\quad(i\in I).\] Each such equation defines an affine hyperplane unless it is identically zero or inconsistent. Thus nondegenerate active-set transitions lie on facets of the polyhedral critical-region partition; simultaneous vanishing conditions lie on lower-dimensional intersections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Critical-region facets occur when an inactive constraint becomes tight or an active multiplier reaches zero; simultaneous events form lower-dimensional intersections.
assumptions_latex: The QP data depend affinely on \(u\).
The active KKT system is nonsingular within each incident region.
Transitions are nondegenerate unless stated otherwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial\mathcal R_I\) is contained in the union of zero-slack and zero-multiplier affine sets.

children.title: Solution-Map Nondifferentiability
children.top_down_role: Nonsmooth behavior of solution maps near structural transitions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact differentiability test at a regular interface of continuous affine solution selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x:U\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous and affine on every full-dimensional member \(R_j\) of a finite polyhedral partition of a neighborhood of \(u_0\), with \(x(u)=a_j+M_ju\) on \(R_j\). If \(\mathcal J(u_0)=\{j:u_0\in\overline{R_j}\}\), then \[x\text{ is Fr\'echet differentiable at }u_0\iff M_i=M_j\quad\text{for all }i,j\in\mathcal J(u_0).\] When this holds, the common matrix is \(Dx(u_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous piecewise-affine solution map is differentiable at an interface exactly when all incident affine pieces have the same Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: A finite full-dimensional polyhedral partition covers a neighborhood of \(u_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is differentiable at }u_0\iff M_i=M_j\quad\forall i,j\in\mathcal J(u_0).

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the affine selection on region j
indices of regions incident to the transition point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized Jacobian at a Regular Active-Set Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized first-order representation when a continuous piecewise-affine solution map is not classically differentiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the finite continuous piecewise-affine hypotheses, the Bouligand limiting Jacobians at \(u_0\) are the matrices \(M_j\) from incident full-dimensional regions, and the Clarke generalized Jacobian is \[\partial_Cx(u_0)=\operatorname{conv}\{M_j:j\in\mathcal J(u_0)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The generalized Jacobian is the convex hull of the Jacobians of the affine solution formulas incident to the transition.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is continuous and piecewise affine on a finite polyhedral partition near \(u_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial_Cx(u_0)=\operatorname{conv}\{M_j:j\in\mathcal J(u_0)\}.

Solution-Map Nondifferentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional strictly convex QP showing loss of differentiability at an active-set transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(u\in\mathbb R\), consider \[x(u)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R}\tfrac12(x-u)^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad x\ge0.\] The unique solution is \(x(u)=\max\{u,0\}\). The constraint is active for \(u<0\) and inactive for \(u>0\). Hence \(x\) is globally Lipschitz and piecewise affine, but its one-sided derivatives at \(u=0\) are \(x'_-(0)=0\) and \(x'_+(0)=1\). Therefore uniqueness and strong convexity do not by themselves imply differentiability of the solution map across an active-set transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto the nonnegative half-line is unique and Lipschitz but not differentiable where the constraint changes activity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x(u)=\max\{u,0\}\) is not differentiable at \(u=0\).

children.title: Degenerate Transition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Transition behavior involving nonunique or weakly active structures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic characterization of degeneracy in an active-set sensitivity system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_I\) collect the equality rows and active inequality rows. For \(Q\succeq0\), \[K_I=\begin{bmatrix}Q&C_I^{\mathsf T}\\ C_I&0\end{bmatrix}\] is nonsingular if and only if \(C_I\) has full row rank and \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\ker C_I\). If either condition fails, the fixed-active-set linearized KKT equations fail to have a unique solution for every right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regular active-set sensitivity requires independent active rows and positive curvature on their common nullspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_I\) is nonsingular exactly under full active-row rank and positive reduced curvature.

notation.meaning: Matrix of equality and active-inequality rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Active-Set KKT Singularity Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak Activity Need Not Destroy Smoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affinely parametrized counterexample to treating failure of strict complementarity as automatic primal nonsmoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x \tfrac12x^2-ux\) subject to \(x\le u\), the unique solution is \(x(u)=u\) for every \(u\), and the unique multiplier is \(z(u)=0\). The constraint is active but weakly complementary for every parameter value, while the primal solution map is affine and smooth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero multiplier on an active constraint does not by itself force the primal solution map to be nonsmooth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict complementarity fails, while \(x(u)=u\) remains smooth.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Activity Need Not Destroy Smoothness
Degenerate Transition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of regular active-set sensitivity when LICQ, strict complementarity, or KKT nonsingularity is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Regular active-set differentiation can fail at a parameter \(u_0\) if active gradients are linearly dependent, an active multiplier and its slack both vanish, or the active KKT matrix is singular. For example, minimize \(\tfrac12x^2\) subject to \(x\le u\) and \(-x\le-u\). Feasibility forces \(x(u)=u\). At \(u=0\), both inequalities are active with dependent gradients, and stationarity permits every multiplier pair \((z_1,z_2)=(t,t)\) with \(t\ge0\). Thus the primal solution remains unique, but multipliers and active-set sensitivities are not uniquely determined by the KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At degenerate transitions, the primal optimizer may remain unique while multipliers and differentiated KKT sensitivities become nonunique.
assumptions_latex: Both displayed inequalities are retained as separate constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x(0)=0\) is unique, whereas \(\{(z_1,z_2):z_1=z_2\ge0\}\) is not a singleton.

children.title: Full-KKT Factorizations
children.top_down_role: Direct factorization interfaces retaining the full KKT system.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-KKT Factorizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct full-system factorization for an equality-constrained convex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x\tfrac12x^THx+g^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\), the primal-dual solution satisfies \[K\begin{bmatrix}x\\\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-g\\b\end{bmatrix},\qquad K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}.\] If \(A\) has full row rank and \(H\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\), then \(K\) is nonsingular. A symmetric-indefinite direct method computes a permutation and block-diagonal factorization \(P^TKP=LDL^T\), where \(D\) contains nonsingular \(1\times1\) or \(2\times2\) pivot blocks, and obtains \((x,\lambda)\) by triangular and block-diagonal solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality-QP primal and multipliers can be computed together by a permuted symmetric-indefinite factorization of the nonsingular KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is nonsingular and admits a pivoted factorization \(P^TKP=LDL^T\).

notation.meaning: permutation, triangular factor, and block-diagonal pivot factor

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic and storage cost of retaining and directly factoring the full dense KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=n+m\) be the order of a dense full KKT matrix. A pivoted dense symmetric-indefinite \(LDL^T\) factorization requires \(\Theta(N^3)\) arithmetic and \(\Theta(N^2)\) storage. Once the factors are available, each additional right-hand side requires \(\Theta(N^2)\) arithmetic. For sparse KKT matrices these dense bounds are replaced by costs determined by ordering, fill, and numerical pivoting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense full-KKT factorization is cubic with quadratic storage, while factor reuse makes each additional solve quadratic; sparse cost depends on fill and pivots.
assumptions_latex: The stated primary bounds concern dense direct factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{factor}}=\Theta(N^3),\quad M_{\mathrm{factor}}=\Theta(N^2),\quad T_{\mathrm{solve}}=\Theta(N^2).

notation.meaning: order of the full KKT matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Full-KKT Factorization Cost

children.title: Symmetric-Indefinite Factorization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Factorization families specialized to symmetric-indefinite systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric-Indefinite Factorization Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver interface for applying a pivoted symmetric-indefinite KKT factorization to one or multiple right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a real symmetric KKT matrix \(K\), a right-hand side \(r\), and a pivoting rule admitting \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) pivots. Compute \(P^TKP=LDL^T\). Solve successively \(Lw=P^Tr\), \(Dv=w\), and \(L^Ty=v\), then return \(s=Py\). The output satisfies \(Ks=r\) in exact arithmetic. For multiple right-hand sides or iterative refinement, reuse \((P,L,D)\); terminate refinement when a prescribed scaled residual tolerance \(\|r-Ks\|\le\tau(\|K\|\|s\|+\|r\|)\) is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor the symmetric KKT matrix once, solve through permutation, triangular, and pivot-block stages, and optionally refine to a scaled residual tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Every selected pivot block is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned vector \(s\) solves \(Ks=r\) in exact arithmetic.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convergence condition for refinement using a reused approximate symmetric-indefinite factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) denote the linear correction operator implemented by the computed factors, and refine \(Ks=r\) by \[s_{k+1}=s_k+M(r-Ks_k).\] If, in a consistent norm, \(\rho=\|I-MK\|<1\), then with \(e_k=s-s_k\), \[e_{k+1}=(I-MK)e_k,\qquad \|e_k\|\le\rho^k\|e_0\|.\] Without this contraction condition, reaching a smaller residual is not guaranteed. A small residual controls forward error only after accounting for conditioning of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterative refinement converges geometrically when the reused factor solve is a contraction for the original KKT matrix; otherwise the residual stopping test alone gives no convergence guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is the correction operator supplied by the computed factors.

notation.meaning: approximate inverse action supplied by the factors
forward error at refinement step k

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Convergence of Iterative Refinement

children.title: Pivoting Stability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerical behavior associated with pivot selection plus regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Pivoting Stability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical stability conditions for symmetric-indefinite elimination of full KKT systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An unpivoted \(LDL^T\) elimination of a nonsingular indefinite KKT matrix can encounter a zero or very small pivot even when the full matrix is well conditioned. A symmetric pivoting strategy must therefore select acceptable \(1\times1\) or \(2\times2\) principal pivot blocks and apply the same permutations to rows and columns. When the pivot acceptance test bounds elimination multipliers and rounding errors remain in the standard floating-point model, the computed factors satisfy \[P^T(K+\Delta K)P=\widehat L\widehat D\widehat L^T\] with a small normwise or componentwise backward error controlled by machine precision and factor growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stable indefinite KKT elimination uses symmetric 1-by-1 or 2-by-2 pivoting; backward error depends on machine precision and factor growth.
assumptions_latex: Pivot tests bound the elimination multipliers.
Floating-point operations obey the standard relative-error model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed factors exactly factor a nearby matrix \(K+\Delta K\), with error governed by precision and growth.

notation.meaning: backward perturbation of the KKT matrix

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularization Tradeoff for Small KKT Pivots
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability role and perturbation boundary of primal-dual diagonal regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), a regularized system may use \[K_{\delta}=K+E_{\delta}=\begin{bmatrix}H+\delta_pI&A^T\\A&-\delta_dI\end{bmatrix},\qquad \delta_p,\delta_d>0.\] If \(H+\delta_pI\succ0\), then \(K_{\delta}\) is symmetric quasi-definite and nonsingular, removing structural zero-pivot obstructions. It solves a perturbed system, however. If \(K\) is nonsingular and \(\|K^{-1}E_{\delta}\|<1\), then for \(Ks=r\) and \(K_{\delta}\widehat s=r\), \[\frac{\|\widehat s-s\|}{\|s\|}\le\frac{\|K^{-1}E_{\delta}\|}{1-\|K^{-1}E_{\delta}\|}.\] Acceptance must therefore also test the residual for the original matrix \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal primal-dual regularization can eliminate pivot obstructions but changes the KKT system; its perturbation and the original residual must be controlled.
assumptions_latex: The perturbation bound additionally assumes \(K\) is nonsingular and \(\|K^{-1}E_{\delta}\|<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_{\delta}\text{ is nonsingular, and the displayed perturbation bound controls the solution change}.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularization Tradeoff for Small KKT Pivots

children.title: Range-Space Methods
children.top_down_role: Equality-QP interfaces based on range-space reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Range-Space Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-QP solution by eliminating the primal variable and solving in multiplier space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(H\succ0\), full-row-rank \(A\), and the equality QP \(\min_x\tfrac12x^THx+g^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\), form or apply \(H^{-1}\) through linear solves. Compute \(q=H^{-1}g\) and the range-space matrix \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\). Solve \[S\lambda=-b-Aq,\] then solve \[Hx=-g-A^T\lambda.\] Return \((x,\lambda)\), stopping iterative inner solves when their tolerances ensure the requested primal and stationarity residuals. The matrix \(S\) is symmetric positive definite, so a positive-definite solver may be used for the condensed multiplier system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate the primal variable, solve a positive-definite multiplier system, and recover the primal solution with one further Hessian solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\succ0\), and the returned pair satisfies the equality-QP KKT equations.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit Krylov variant avoiding explicit formation of the Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To apply \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) to \(v\), compute \(w=A^{\mathsf T}v\), solve \(Hy=w\), and return \(Ay\). Consequently, when \(H\succ0\) and \(A\) has full row rank, CG or PCG can solve the multiplier equation using products with \(A,A^{\mathsf T}\), Hessian solves, and, for PCG, an SPD multiplier-space preconditioner; explicit storage of \(S\) is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The range-space Schur complement can be applied matrix-free through one Hessian solve, enabling CG or PCG without forming a dense matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Sv=A(H^{-1}(A^{\mathsf T}v))\).
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Range-Space Iteration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual interpretation for exact and inexact range-space solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\lambda\), let \(x=-H^{-1}(g+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda)\). Then the stationarity residual is zero and \[Ax-b=-\bigl(S\lambda+b+AH^{-1}g\bigr).\] Hence the condensed residual is the negative primal-feasibility residual. If the Hessian back-solve is inexact, its residual \(Hx+g+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda\) must additionally be controlled to certify the full KKT tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact Hessian back-substitution, the Schur residual is exactly the negative equality-feasibility residual; inexact back-solves also require a stationarity check.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax-b=-(S\lambda+b+AH^{-1}g)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Condensed Residual–KKT Residual Correspondence

children.title: Schur-Complement Methods
children.top_down_role: Linear-system interfaces based on Schur-complement formation.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block elimination of a solvable equality-QP KKT system through its primal-block Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and nonsingular, let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and consider the KKT system \[\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-g\\b\end{bmatrix}.\] Assume that the Schur complement \(-AH^{-1}A^T\) is nonsingular. Eliminate \(x\) from \(Hx+A^T\lambda=-g\) and solve \[(-AH^{-1}A^T)\lambda=b+AH^{-1}g.\] Then recover \(x=-H^{-1}(g+A^T\lambda)\) and return \((x,\lambda)\). If \(H\succ0\) and \(A\) has full row rank, then \(AH^{-1}A^T\succ0\), so the nonsingularity assumption holds. Explicit formation is optional: a product with \(AH^{-1}A^T\) can be evaluated by applying \(A^T\), solving with \(H\), and applying \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the primal block and its Schur complement are nonsingular, block elimination produces a uniquely solvable multiplier system and recovers the primal variable by back-substitution. Positive-definite H and full-row-rank A provide a standard sufficient case.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned pair satisfies \(Hx+A^T\lambda=-g\) and \(Ax=b\).

notation.meaning: Schur complement of H in the KKT matrix

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact block factorization of an equality-QP KKT matrix with a nonsingular primal block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), where \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\) is nonsingular, and set \(S=-AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\). Then \[K=\begin{bmatrix}I&0\\AH^{-1}&I\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}H&0\\0&S\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}I&H^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\\0&I\end{bmatrix}.\] Consequently, \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=\operatorname{inertia}(H)+\operatorname{inertia}(S)\), \(\det K=\det(H)\det(S)\), and \(K\) is nonsingular exactly when \(S\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Congruence reduces the KKT matrix to the primal block and its Schur complement, giving exact inertia, determinant, and nonsingularity identities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is congruent to \(\operatorname{diag}(H,S)\), and \(K\) is nonsingular if and only if \(S\) is nonsingular.

notation.meaning: Schur complement of the primal block

knowledge_statements.title: Schur Congruence and Inertia Identity

children.title: Condensed-System Regimes
children.top_down_role: Dimension, density, plus conditioning regimes for condensed systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Condensed-System Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite Hessian regime for condensing the primal block of an equality-QP KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x \tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), with multiplier convention \(Hx+g+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\). Eliminating \(x\) from the KKT equations gives \[AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=-b-AH^{-1}g.\] Because \(H\succ0\) and \(A\) has full row rank, \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\). Thus the unique solution is obtained from \(S\lambda^\star=-b-AH^{-1}g\) and \(x^\star=-H^{-1}(g+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda^\star)\). This condensed regime replaces the indefinite saddle-point system by an \(m\)-dimensional positive-definite system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a positive-definite Hessian and independent equalities, eliminating primal variables yields a positive-definite Schur-complement system for multipliers, followed by primal back-substitution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^m\), and solving the condensed system followed by back-substitution solves the equality-constrained QP.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension, solve-cost, and density conditions favoring multiplier-space condensation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The condensed system has order \(m\), whereas a null-space reduced system has order \(n-m\). Range-space condensation is dimensionally favorable when \(m\ll n-m\), provided solves with \(H\) are efficient and forming or applying \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) does not introduce prohibitive density. If \(m\) is large or \(H^{-1}\) destroys sparsity, the smaller formal dimension alone does not imply a cheaper method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Condensation is most attractive for few constraints and efficient Hessian solves, but Schur-complement density can outweigh its dimension reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim S=m\), with practical cost controlled by Hessian solves and Schur-complement fill.
knowledge_statements.title: Few-Constraint Condensation Regime

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact restrictions of the positive-definite primal-block condensation regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(H\succ0\), \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) is nonsingular iff \(A\) has full row rank. Thus redundant equalities make the classical multiplier system singular even when the primal optimizer is unique. If \(H\) is singular, elimination through \(H^{-1}\) is unavailable; if \(H\) is invertible but indefinite, the Schur complement need not be positive definite. Such cases require generalized elimination or a full KKT treatment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under positive-definite curvature, condensed-system singularity is exactly constraint-rank failure; singular or indefinite Hessians introduce further breakdowns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\succ0\implies AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\iff\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\).
knowledge_statements.title: Classical Condensation Breakdown Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral conditioning bounds for the positive-definite multiplier system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(0<\mu I\preceq H\preceq LI\) and \(A\) has full row rank, then for \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\), \[\frac{\sigma_{\min}(A)^2}{L}I\preceq S\preceq\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A)^2}{\mu}I,\qquad \kappa_2(S)\le\kappa_2(H)\kappa_2(A)^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The condensed system inherits Hessian conditioning and the squared conditioning of the constraint matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T})\le\kappa_2(H)\kappa_2(A)^2\).

notation.meaning: extreme spectral bounds for the Hessian

knowledge_statements.title: Condensed-System Spectral Bounds

children.title: Null-Space Methods
children.top_down_role: Equality-QP reduction through null-space representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct null-space solution of a full-row-rank equality-constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), first compute any \(x_p\) satisfying \(Ax_p=b\) and a basis \(Z\) of \(\ker A\). Solve the reduced system \[Z^{\mathsf T}HZp=-Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_p+g),\] and output \(x^\star=x_p+Zp\). Equality feasibility holds because \(AZ=0\). If multipliers are required, recover the unique \(\lambda^\star\) from \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda^\star=-(Hx^\star+g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameterize every feasible point by a particular solution plus a null-space basis, solve the reduced system, and optionally recover the unique equality multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The null-space reduction produces the unique primal optimizer while maintaining equality feasibility.

notation.meaning: basis matrix for the null space of the constraints

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stopping and optimality test for the null-space method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible \(x\) and a full-column-rank \(Z\) satisfying \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\), \(Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx+g)=0\) is equivalent to the existence of \(\lambda\) satisfying \(Hx+g+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\). If \(H\succeq0\), feasibility and this condition certify global optimality; if \(H\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\), they certify the unique feasible minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is stationary exactly when its gradient has zero null-space component; under convexity this certifies global optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx+g)=0\iff \exists\lambda:\ Hx+g+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Stationarity Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed classification of a singular reduced quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succeq0\) and \(c=Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_p+g)\). The reduced quadratic has a minimizer iff \(c\in\operatorname{range}(G)\); otherwise it is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Range compatibility classifies attainment for a singular positive-semidefinite reduced quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\arg\min\neq\varnothing\iff c\in\operatorname{range}(G)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Reduced-System Outcome Classification

intermediate_metadata.reason: The locally owned inventory is the explicit null-space algorithm, feasibility preservation, primal reconstruction, multiplier recovery, and projected-stationarity certificate. The proposed singular reduced-quadratic classification is deferred as misplaced and supplied under Reduced-Hessian Methods; reduced representation and basis conditioning are also excluded as sibling-owned.

children.title: Reduced-Hessian Methods
children.top_down_role: Linear-algebra interfaces centered on the reduced Hessian.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Hessian Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-Hessian representation induced by an arbitrary full-rank null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every feasible vector has the unique representation \(x=x_p+Zp\). Substitution into \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\) gives \[q(x_p+Zp)=q(x_p)+g_Z^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}H_Zp,\qquad H_Z=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ,\quad g_Z=Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_p+g).\] Hence minimizing the equality-QP is equivalent to minimizing this unconstrained reduced quadratic. Since \(H_Z\succ0\), its unique minimizer satisfies \(H_Zp^\star=-g_Z\), and the corresponding primal optimizer is \(x^\star=x_p+Zp^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting the quadratic to feasible directions produces an equivalent unconstrained quadratic whose Hessian is the reduced matrix formed with a null-space basis.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) has full column rank, \(AZ=0\), and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equality-QP is equivalent to an unconstrained QP with reduced Hessian \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\).

notation.meaning: reduced gradient at the particular point

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-invariant curvature classification of an equality-constrained quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any full-rank basis \(Z\) of \(\ker A\), \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\) iff \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\ker A\), and \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succeq0\) iff \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd\ge0\) for every \(d\in\ker A\). Thus positive definiteness of \(H\) on all of \(\mathbb R^n\) is sufficient but unnecessary; only feasible-direction curvature determines reduced definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-Hessian definiteness is exactly definiteness of the quadratic form on feasible directions.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\iff d^{\mathsf T}Hd>0\ \forall d\in\ker A\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Curvature Classification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment, nonuniqueness, and unboundedness when the reduced Hessian is positive semidefinite but singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succeq0\) and \(c=Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_p+g)\). The reduced quadratic \(\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Gp+c^{\mathsf T}p\) has a minimizer iff \(c\in\operatorname{range}(G)\). When this holds, all minimizers are \(p=-G^\dagger c+v\) with \(v\in\ker G\), and they are unique iff \(G\succ0\). If \(c\notin\operatorname{range}(G)\), the equality-QP is unbounded below along a feasible direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a singular positive-semidefinite reduced Hessian, range compatibility determines attainment; attained solutions are nonunique along the reduced kernel, while incompatibility gives unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\arg\min\neq\varnothing\iff c\in\operatorname{range}(G)\).

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the reduced Hessian

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Reduced-Quadratic Classification

children.title: Null-Space Basis Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Numerical consequences of basis construction plus scaling.

assumptions_latex: \(Z\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Orthonormal null-space bases avoid additional basis-conditioning factors in the reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of null-space basis scaling on reduced-Hessian spectral conditioning.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing \(Z\) by \(\widehat Z=ZR\) changes the reduced Hessian by congruence: \[\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}H\widehat Z=R^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)R.\] Consequently, poor scaling or near-linear dependence in the basis may worsen the reduced system even though the feasible subspace is unchanged. If \(Z^{\mathsf T}Z=I\), then \[\lambda_{\min}(H)\leq\lambda_{\min}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)\leq\lambda_{\max}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)\leq\lambda_{\max}(H),\] so \(\kappa_2(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)\leq\kappa_2(H)\). For a general basis, the bound becomes \(\kappa_2(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)\leq\kappa_2(H)\kappa_2(Z)^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing a null-space basis preserves the feasible subspace but changes the reduced Hessian by congruence; orthonormal bases control the resulting condition number.
knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Basis Conditioning

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arbitrarily Bad Conditioning from Basis Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of coordinate-invariant conditioning for general null-space bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=I_2\), let \(A\) have no rows, and let \(Z_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon)\), where \(0<\varepsilon<1\). Then \(\operatorname{range}(Z_\varepsilon)=\ker A=\mathbb R^2\), but \(Z_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}HZ_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon^2)\) and \(\kappa_2(Z_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}HZ_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^{-2}\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid rescaling of the null-space basis can make the reduced Hessian arbitrarily ill-conditioned even when the full Hessian is perfectly conditioned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(Z_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}HZ_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^{-2}\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrarily Bad Conditioning from Basis Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral invariance between orthonormal bases of the same null space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Z^{\mathsf T}Z=\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}\widehat Z=I\) and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\operatorname{range}(\widehat Z)=\ker A\), then \(\widehat Z=ZQ\) for an orthogonal matrix \(Q\). Consequently, \(\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}H\widehat Z=Q^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)Q\), so the two reduced Hessians have identical eigenvalues, inertia, and, when nonsingular, spectral condition number.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All orthonormal bases of the same null space produce orthogonally similar reduced Hessians with identical spectral conditioning.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) and \(\widehat Z\) have orthonormal columns spanning the same null space
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{spec}(\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}H\widehat Z)=\operatorname{spec}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonal Coordinate Invariance

children.title: Projected Krylov Methods
children.top_down_role: Krylov interfaces incorporating equality-feasible projections.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Krylov Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected conjugate gradients on the null space of equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=I-A^{\mathsf T}(AA^{\mathsf T})^{-1}A\) and define \(K:\ker A\to\ker A\) by \(Kv=PHv\). Initialize \(p_0=0\), \(r_0=-P(Hx_p+g)\), and \(d_0=r_0\). Apply conjugate gradients to \(Kp=-P(Hx_p+g)\): \[\alpha_k=\frac{r_k^{\mathsf T}r_k}{d_k^{\mathsf T}Kd_k},\quad p_{k+1}=p_k+\alpha_kd_k,\quad r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_kKd_k,\] \[\beta_k=\frac{r_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}r_{k+1}}{r_k^{\mathsf T}r_k},\quad d_{k+1}=r_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k.\] Stop when \(\lVert r_{k+1}\rVert\) meets the prescribed tolerance and output \(x_{k+1}=x_p+p_{k+1}\). In exact arithmetic, CG terminates in at most \(n-m\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugate gradients applied to the projected Hessian stays in the feasible null space and solves the equality-QP without explicitly forming a null-space basis.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and \(P=I-A^{\mathsf T}(AA^{\mathsf T})^{-1}A\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conjugate gradients applied with the projected operator generates feasible-space iterates and, in exact arithmetic, obtains the equality-QP solution in at most \(n-m\) iterations.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the constraint null space
projected Hessian operator on the null space

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stopping certificate for feasible projected-CG iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every feasible iterate \(x_k\), define \(r_k=-P(Hx_k+g)\). Then \(r_k=0\) iff \(Hx_k+g\in\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\), equivalently iff there exists \(\lambda_k\) with \(Hx_k+g+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda_k=0\). If \(H\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\), this certifies that \(x_k\) is the unique equality-QP minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected residual vanishes exactly at KKT stationarity and certifies the optimizer for feasible projected-CG iterates.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_k=0\iff x_k=x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Residual Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence rate governed by curvature on the feasible subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=PH|_{\ker A}\succ0\), let \(e_k=x_k-x^\star\), and let \(\kappa=\lambda_{\max}(K)/\lambda_{\min}(K)\). In exact arithmetic, projected CG satisfies \[\|e_k\|_H\le2\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^k\|e_0\|_H.\] It terminates after at most the number of distinct eigenvalues of \(K\), and hence after at most \(\dim\ker A=n-m\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected-CG convergence depends only on the Hessian spectrum restricted to feasible directions, with the standard CG rate and finite termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|e_k\|_H\le2((\sqrt\kappa-1)/(\sqrt\kappa+1))^k\|e_0\|_H\).

notation.meaning: projected Hessian restricted to the null space

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-CG Restricted-Spectrum Bound

children.title: Preconditioned Krylov Methods
children.top_down_role: Krylov interfaces using problem-structured preconditioners.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned Krylov Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetrically preconditioned conjugate gradients for the positive-definite reduced-Hessian system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\) and \(c=-Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_p+g)\). Choose \(p_0\in\mathbb{R}^{n-m}\), set \(r_0=c-Gp_0\), solve \(Mz_0=r_0\), and set \(d_0=z_0\). Iterate \[\alpha_k=\frac{r_k^{\mathsf T}z_k}{d_k^{\mathsf T}Gd_k},\quad p_{k+1}=p_k+\alpha_kd_k,\quad r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_kGd_k,\] then solve \(Mz_{k+1}=r_{k+1}\), set \(\beta_k=(r_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}z_{k+1})/(r_k^{\mathsf T}z_k)\), and set \(d_{k+1}=z_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k\). Stop at the prescribed residual tolerance and output \(x=x_p+Zp_{k+1}\). The standard PCG convergence bounds are governed by \(\kappa_2(M^{-1/2}GM^{-1/2})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioned conjugate gradients solves the positive-definite reduced system, using preconditioner solves to improve the effective spectral condition number.
assumptions_latex: \(x_p\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(Ax_p=b\), and \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) is a full-column-rank basis of \(\ker A\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Preconditioned conjugate gradients solves \(Gp=c\), with standard convergence bounds governed by \(\kappa_2(M^{-1/2}GM^{-1/2})\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral convergence guarantee for reduced-system PCG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p^\star=G^{-1}c\), \(e_k=p_k-p^\star\), and \(\kappa=\kappa_2(M^{-1/2}GM^{-1/2})\). In exact arithmetic, PCG satisfies \[\|e_k\|_G\le 2\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^k\|e_0\|_G.\] It terminates after at most the number of distinct eigenvalues of \(M^{-1/2}GM^{-1/2}\), hence after at most \(n-m\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-system PCG converges geometrically in the energy norm according to the preconditioned condition number and terminates finitely in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|e_k\|_G\le2((\sqrt\kappa-1)/(\sqrt\kappa+1))^k\|e_0\|_G\).

notation.meaning: condition number of the symmetrically preconditioned reduced Hessian

knowledge_statements.title: PCG Energy-Norm Convergence Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for the standard fixed-preconditioner PCG recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The stated standard PCG recurrence is guaranteed when \(G\) and a fixed \(M\) are symmetric positive definite. If \(M\) is singular, indefinite, nonsymmetric, or varies without a flexible-CG recurrence, the positivity or conjugacy properties used by the coefficients and convergence bound may fail. An indefinite reduced operator requires an appropriate indefinite Krylov method rather than standard PCG.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard PCG requires a fixed SPD operator and preconditioner; violating these assumptions removes its usual recurrence and convergence guarantees.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\succ0\) and fixed \(M\succ0\) are the standard validity conditions for the stated PCG recurrence.
knowledge_statements.title: PCG Symmetry and Definiteness Boundary

children.title: Projection–Preconditioner Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility regimes linking projection structure to preconditioner design.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The preconditioned projected operator preserves feasible directions and is self-adjoint and positive definite on \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility criterion for Euclidean orthogonal projection and symmetric positive-definite preconditioning.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A preconditioner is projection-compatible when it preserves the feasible subspace: \[M^{-1}\operatorname{range}(P)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(P),\] equivalently \(PM^{-1}P=M^{-1}P\). Because \(M^{-1}\) is symmetric, this invariance also implies invariance of the orthogonal complement and hence \(PM^{-1}=M^{-1}P\). Therefore \(B=PM^{-1}P\) maps \(\ker A\) into itself, is self-adjoint, and satisfies \(v^{\mathsf T}Bv=v^{\mathsf T}M^{-1}v>0\) for every nonzero \(v\in\ker A\). These properties permit a standard symmetric Krylov recurrence entirely within the feasible subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric preconditioner is compatible when its inverse preserves the feasible null space; then projection and preconditioning commute and retain positive definiteness there.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection–Preconditioner Compatibility

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unprojected Preconditioning Can Leave the Null Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure of feasible-space invariance under an arbitrary SPD preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\) and \(M^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&1/2\\1/2&1\end{bmatrix}\succ0\). For \(v=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}\in\operatorname{range}(P)\), \(M^{-1}v=(1,1/2)^{\mathsf T}\notin\operatorname{range}(P)\), so \(PM^{-1}\ne M^{-1}P\). In contrast, \(PM^{-1}Pv=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}\) remains feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SPD preconditioner need not preserve feasible directions; omitting reprojection can destroy null-space invariance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M^{-1}\operatorname{range}(P)\nsubseteq\operatorname{range}(P)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unprojected Preconditioning Can Leave the Null Space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weaker valid construction when the preconditioner does not preserve the feasible subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(M\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \(B=PM^{-1}P\) maps \(\ker A\) into itself and is self-adjoint positive definite there: for every nonzero \(v\in\ker A\), \(v^{\mathsf T}Bv=v^{\mathsf T}M^{-1}v>0\). Thus commutation is unnecessary when projection is explicitly applied on both sides; it is required to replace \(Bv\) by the unprojected action \(M^{-1}v\) for every feasible \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any SPD preconditioner can be safely sandwiched by the feasible projector; commutation is needed only to omit the additional projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(PM^{-1}P\succ0\text{ on }\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Preconditioner Without Commutation

children.title: Active-Set QP Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Primal, dual, and working-set update families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical feasible working-set method for a strictly convex QP with lower affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_x q(x)=	frac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax\ge b\), let \(x_k\) be feasible and choose linearly independent working rows \(W_k\subseteq\{i:a_i^{\mathsf T}x_k=b_i\}\). Solve \[\min_p\ 
abla q(x_k)^{\mathsf T}p+	frac12p^{\mathsf T}Hp\quad	ext{subject to }A_{W_k}p=0.\] If \(p
e0\), take the largest \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) for which \(A(x_k+\alpha p)\ge b\), update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha p\), and add a blocking constraint when \(\alpha<1\). If \(p=0\), compute \(
abla q(x_k)=A_{W_k}^{\mathsf T}\mu_W\); stop when \(\mu_W\ge0\), and otherwise remove an index with a negative multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible active-set method solves an equality-QP on the current face, adds blocking constraints, and drops constraints whose multipliers violate dual feasibility.
assumptions_latex: Each working-set matrix has linearly independent rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A zero step with \(\mu_W\ge0\) is a KKT certificate; otherwise the rule produces a feasible working-set update.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Primal Active-Set Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of finite-working-set termination arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Finiteness of the family of working sets alone does not imply finite termination. Degenerate zero-length steps, dependent active rows, or tied multiplier choices can permit repeated working sets without strict objective decrease. A finite-termination conclusion therefore requires suitable nondegeneracy or an explicit anti-cycling rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degeneracy can make an active-set method revisit working sets, so finite enumeration alone is not a termination proof.
assumptions_latex: No nondegeneracy or anti-cycling safeguard is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite termination cannot be inferred solely from the finite number of working sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy and Cycling Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual bound-QP representation underlying dual active-set updates for strictly convex primal QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When \(H\succ0\), the QP \(\min\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge b\}\) has the concave dual \[\max_{\lambda\ge0}\ b^{\mathsf T}\lambda-\tfrac12(g-A^{\mathsf T}\lambda)^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}(g-A^{\mathsf T}\lambda),\qquad x=H^{-1}(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda-g).\] A dual active-set method applies bound-active updates to \(\lambda\), maintaining \(\lambda\ge0\), changing the set of zero multipliers, and recovering the associated primal vector from the displayed formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive-definite curvature, dual active-set QP methods are bound-active methods on the nonnegative multiplier dual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual feasibility is \(\lambda\ge0\), and primal variables are uniquely recoverable from each multiplier vector.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Active-Set Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-termination regime for an exact feasible active-set method on a strictly convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the assumptions of the feasible primal active-set interface, suppose additionally that the update rule forbids repetition of a working set without strict objective decrease. Then only finitely many working-set changes occur, and the method terminates at the unique primal minimizer with multipliers satisfying the KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict convexity, exact face solves, independent working rows, and a noncycling update rule give finite termination at the unique KKT solution.
assumptions_latex: All working-set subproblems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method terminates after finitely many working-set changes at the unique primal optimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination under Noncycling Updates

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(\{x:Ax\geq b\}\) is nonempty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The working-set test either produces a feasible objective-reducing step or a verifiable KKT certificate.

notation.meaning: current working set of active constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal feasible active-set interface for convex QPs written with lower inequality bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At feasible \(x_k\), choose \(W_k\subseteq\{i:a_i^{\mathsf T}x_k=b_i\}\) and solve \[\min_p\ 
abla q(x_k)^{\mathsf T}p+	frac12p^{\mathsf T}Hp\quad	ext{subject to}\quad A_{W_k}p=0.\] If \(p
eq0\), take the largest \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) preserving \(A(x_k+\alpha p)\geq b\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha p\), and add a blocking constraint when \(\alpha<1\). If \(p=0\), compute \(
abla q(x_k)=A_{W_k}^{\mathsf T}\mu_W\). Stop if \(\mu_W\geq0\); otherwise remove an index having a negative multiplier and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible active-set method solves equality-QP subproblems, adds blocking constraints after feasible steps, and removes active constraints whose multipliers violate dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set QP Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation is supplied. An exact active-set source is needed to validate the working-set subproblem assumptions, multiplier convention, removal rule, and the claimed step-or-certificate behavior, especially in semidefinite or degenerate cases.

children.title: Interior-Point QP Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual, barrier, and structured Newton-system families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path-following Newton step and positivity-preserving update for a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(s>0\), \(\lambda>0\), define \(r_d=Hx+g-A^{\mathsf T}\lambda\), \(r_p=Ax-b-s\), and \(\mu=s^{\mathsf T}\lambda/m\). For a centering parameter \(\sigma\in[0,1]\), compute \((\Delta x,\Delta s,\Delta\lambda)\) from \[H\Delta x-A^{\mathsf T}\Delta\lambda=-r_d,\quad A\Delta x-\Delta s=-r_p,\quad \Lambda\Delta s+S\Delta\lambda=\sigma\mu\mathbf1-S\lambda.\] Choose a fraction-to-boundary step preserving strict positivity, update all variables, and stop when primal, dual, and complementarity residuals satisfy the prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual interior-point iteration solves the structured Newton equations and takes a positivity-preserving step.
assumptions_latex: The current slack and multiplier vectors are strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update preserves strict positivity and targets feasibility, stationarity, and perturbed complementarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Newton Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical Newton-iteration bound for the logarithmic barrier with m affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume strict primal-dual feasibility, existence of an optimum, initialization in a fixed central neighborhood, and sufficiently accurate short-step Newton solves. For the logarithmic barrier with \(m\) inequality slacks, a short-step path-following method reduces the complementarity gap to at most \(\varepsilon\) in \[O\!\left(\sqrt m\log\frac{m\mu_0}{\varepsilon}\right)\] Newton iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical short-step path following requires order square-root-of-m times a logarithmic accuracy factor in Newton iterations.
assumptions_latex: Initialization lies in a prescribed central neighborhood.
Newton directions are computed to the accuracy required by the short-step analysis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The complementarity gap is at most \(\varepsilon\) after \(O(\sqrt m\log(m\mu_0/\varepsilon))\) Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.title: Short-Step Path-Following Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbed primal-dual KKT system for lower affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax-b=s\ge0\), the primal-dual central path consists of \((x(\mu),s(\mu),\lambda(\mu))\), \(\mu>0\), satisfying \[Hx+g-A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0,\quad Ax-b-s=0,\quad S\lambda=\mu\mathbf1,\quad s>0,\ \lambda>0.\] If a sequence of such points is bounded as \(\mu\downarrow0\), every accumulation point satisfies the QP KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The central path consists of strictly positive primal-dual points satisfying feasibility, stationarity, and uniform perturbed complementarity.
assumptions_latex: Central-path points exist for the considered positive parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bounded accumulation points as \(\mu\downarrow0\) are KKT points.
knowledge_statements.title: QP Central Path

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulation dependence of standard feasible-start path-following assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The nonempty system \(x\ge0\), \(-x\ge0\) defines \(\{0\}\) but has no point satisfying both displayed inequalities strictly. Thus nonemptiness alone does not provide positive slacks for a given representation; infeasible-start methods, removal of implicit equalities, or relative-interior/facial reformulation may be required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Opposing or redundant inequalities can destroy literal strict feasibility even when the feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nonempty displayed inequality system need not admit a strictly positive slack vector.
knowledge_statements.title: Literal Strict-Feasibility Boundary

assumptions_latex: The feasible region \(\{x:Ax\geq b\}\) has a strictly feasible point
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration computes a primal-dual Newton direction and preserves strict positivity by a fraction-to-boundary step.

notation.meaning: diagonal matrices of slacks and multipliers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual path-following interface for convex QPs with lower inequality bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax-b=s\geq0\), form \(r_d=Hx+g-A^{\mathsf T}\lambda\), \(r_p=Ax-b-s\), and \(\mu=s^{\mathsf T}\lambda/m\). Compute \((\Delta x,\Delta s,\Delta\lambda)\) from \[H\Delta x-A^{\mathsf T}\Delta\lambda=-r_d,\quad A\Delta x-\Delta s=-r_p,\quad \Lambda\Delta s+S\Delta\lambda=\sigma\mu\mathbf1-S\lambda.\] Choose a fraction-to-boundary step maintaining \(s+\alpha\Delta s>0\) and \(\lambda+\alpha\Delta\lambda>0\), update all variables, and stop when primal, dual, and complementarity residuals meet tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual interior-point iteration solves the structured Newton equations for feasibility, stationarity, and perturbed complementarity, then takes a positivity-preserving step.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point QP Interfaces

The displayed primal-dual Newton system is plausible and sign-consistent for lower-bound inequalities, but an exact source is required for this path-following variant, centering equation, fraction-to-boundary rule, and stopping interface.

children.title: Bound-QP Projection Method Family
children.top_down_role: Projection, Cauchy-point, and subspace-minimization families.

children.title: Gradient-Projection Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Projected-gradient families for inequality-constrained QPs.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projected-gradient fixed points are exactly the minimizers of the convex bound-constrained QP.

notation.meaning: componentwise projection onto the bound box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected-gradient iteration and stopping interface for a convex box-constrained QP.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.1 Convergence Analysis of Gradient Methods p. 20
source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\in[l,u]\), select \(\alpha_k>0\) by a prescribed constant-step or descent line-search rule and update \[x_{k+1}=\Pi_{[l,u]}\bigl(x_k-\alpha_k(Hx_k+g)\bigr).\] Stop when \(\lVert r_{\bar\alpha}(x_k)\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) for a fixed \(\bar\alpha>0\), and output \(x_k\). For every \(\alpha>0\), the exact condition \(r_\alpha(x)=0\) is equivalent to \(0\in Hx+g+N_{[l,u]}(x)\), which is necessary and sufficient for global optimality because the objective and feasible box are convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take a gradient step, project it onto the bound box, and stop when the projected-gradient residual is small; zero residual exactly characterizes optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Projection Interfaces

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3.1 Convergence Analysis of Gradient Methods p. 20
source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp scalar failure boundary for constant-step projected gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the unconstrained one-dimensional quadratic \(q(x)=\tfrac12Lx^2\), \(L>0\), projected gradient reduces to \(x_{k+1}=(1-\alpha L)x_k\). Thus \(0<\alpha<2/L\) gives convergence, \(\alpha=2/L\) produces a two-cycle unless \(x_0=0\), and \(\alpha>2/L\) makes nonzero iterates diverge in magnitude. Consequently, positivity of a constant step alone is not a convergence condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed projected-gradient step can cycle or diverge when it reaches or exceeds the classical two-over-Lipschitz threshold.
assumptions_latex: No active bounds alter the scalar iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Constant-step convergence cannot be claimed for arbitrary \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Step Stability Boundary

children.title: Bound-Constrained QP Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Specialized interfaces for lower-bound plus upper-bound constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order certificate for a convex QP over finite, one-sided, absent, or fixed component bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\), \(H\succeq0\), and \(B=[l,u]\). For feasible \(x\), set \(d=Hx+g\). Then \(x\) is globally optimal if and only if \(0\in d+N_B(x)\), equivalently \[x=\Pi_B(x-\alpha d)\quad\text{for every, or for some, }\alpha>0.\] Componentwise, \(d_i=0\) for \(l_i<x_i<u_i\), \(d_i\ge0\) for \(x_i=l_i<u_i\), and \(d_i\le0\) for \(x_i=u_i>l_i\); a fixed coordinate \(l_i=u_i=x_i\) imposes no sign condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible box-QP point is optimal exactly when free gradient components vanish and active-bound components have the correct inward sign, equivalently when it is a projected-gradient fixed point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normal-cone inclusion, coordinate signs, and projection fixed-point equation are equivalent global-optimality certificates.
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Bound-QP Optimality Interfaces

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form projection interface for component bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(B=[l,u]\) with \(l_i\le u_i\), the Euclidean projection is separable: \[(\Pi_B(v))_i=\min\{u_i,\max\{l_i,v_i\}\},\] using the natural conventions for infinite endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a bound box is coordinatewise clipping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The box projector is evaluated independently in every coordinate.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the bound box

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Box Projector

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coordinate sign conditions, normal-cone inclusion, and projected fixed-point equation are equivalent optimality interfaces.

notation.meaning: quadratic gradient at the candidate point
normal cone to the bound box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order certificate interface for convex QPs with finite or infinite component bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible \(x\) minimizes \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\) over \([l,u]\) if and only if \(0\in d+N_{[l,u]}(x)\). Componentwise, this means \(d_i=0\) when \(l_i<x_i<u_i\), \(d_i\geq0\) when \(x_i=l_i<u_i\), and \(d_i\leq0\) when \(x_i=u_i>l_i\); fixed coordinates require no sign test. Equivalently, for any \(\alpha>0\), \[x=\Pi_{[l,u]}(x-\alpha d).\] Feasibility and these finitely checkable sign conditions therefore certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible bound-QP point is optimal exactly when each free gradient component vanishes and each active-bound component has the correct inward sign.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Constrained QP Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normal-cone, coordinate-sign, and projection fixed-point certificates are mathematically standard and mutually consistent, but the record supplies no source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Cauchy-Point Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cauchy-point roles within projected QP architectures.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonattainment on an Unbounded Projected Ray
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment failure with an infinite bound and a recession descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In one dimension, let \(q(x)=-x\), \(x_0=0\), and \([l,u]=[0,+\infty)\). Then \(g_0=-1\), \(x(t)=\Pi_{[0,+\infty)}(t)=t\), and \(q(x(t))=-t\to-\infty\). Hence the projected-path problem has no generalized Cauchy point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infinite bound can let the projected ray follow an unbounded descent direction, so its minimum need not be attained.
assumptions_latex: An infinite box endpoint is allowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{t\ge0}q(x(t))=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonattainment on an Unbounded Projected Ray

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized Cauchy Point on a Projected Gradient Path
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cauchy-point definition for a convex quadratic along a box-projected negative-gradient ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\), \(H\succeq0\), \(x_0\in[l,u]\), and \(g_0=Hx_0+g\). Define \(x(t)=\Pi_{[l,u]}(x_0-tg_0)\) for \(t\ge0\). Between consecutive positive bound-hitting times, \(x(t)\) is affine and \(q(x(t))\) is a univariate convex quadratic. When the path objective attains its infimum, the generalized Cauchy point is \(x_C=x(t_C)\), where \(t_C\) is the smallest minimizer. It is found by scanning breakpoints and any stationary point lying in the current segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The generalized Cauchy point is the first minimizer of the quadratic along its piecewise-affine projected negative-gradient path.
assumptions_latex: The path objective attains its infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_C\) minimizes \(q\) along the projected ray and is located at a segment stationary point or breakpoint.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Cauchy Point on a Projected Gradient Path

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment regime for generalized Cauchy-point search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every endpoint \(l_i,u_i\) is finite, then each nonconstant coordinate of \(x(t)=\Pi_{[l,u]}(x_0-tg_0)\) reaches its terminal bound after a finite time. Thus there is \(T<\infty\) such that \(x(t)=x(T)\) for all \(t\ge T\), and every continuous objective, including \(q\), attains its minimum along the path on \([0,T]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite box the projected ray eventually becomes constant, so a generalized Cauchy point always exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{t\ge0}q(x(t))\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Box Attainment

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generalized Cauchy point minimizes the quadratic along the piecewise-affine projected-gradient path and determines an initial active set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized Cauchy point for a convex quadratic along a box-projected negative-gradient path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the projected-gradient path by \[x(t)=\Pi_{[l,u]}(x_0-tg_0),\qquad t\geq0.\] Its breakpoints are the positive times at which a previously free component first reaches a finite bound. Between consecutive breakpoints, \(x(t)\) is affine and \(q(x(t))\) is a univariate convex quadratic. A generalized Cauchy point is \(x_C=x(t_C)\), where \(t_C\) is the smallest global minimizer of \(q(x(t))\) over \(t\geq0\). The zero-breakpoint regime gives \(x_C=x_0\); otherwise \(t_C\) lies either at a breakpoint or at the stationary point of one quadratic segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The generalized Cauchy point is the first minimizer of the quadratic along the projected negative-gradient path, whose regimes are separated by bound-hitting breakpoints.
knowledge_statements.title: Cauchy-Point Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and the assumptions do not guarantee that the projected path objective attains a global minimum when infinite bounds are allowed. The assertion that a zero-breakpoint regime yields \(x_C=x_0\) is also not valid without a more precise regime definition.

children.title: Subspace-Minimization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Reduced subproblem interfaces following projected identification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduced solve after fixing selected variables at their current bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the free-coordinate set and \(A\) its complement, with \(x_A\) fixed at feasible bounds. If \(H_{FF}\succ0\), the unique unconstrained minimizer on this affine face satisfies \[H_{FF}x_F^*=-(g_F+H_{FA}x_A).\] If \(l_F\le x_F^*\le u_F\), the lifted point is the unique minimizer on the selected face. Otherwise the step must be truncated or the reduced bound-QP solved; accepting it directly would violate feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With active coordinates fixed and positive-definite free curvature, one reduced solve gives the exact face minimizer when it remains within the free bounds.
assumptions_latex: Coordinates in \(A\) are fixed at feasible bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A bound-feasible solution of the reduced system is the unique minimizer on the selected face.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Free-Variable Face Solve

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness boundary for an unconstrained reduced quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\phi(p)=\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Rp+c^{\mathsf T}p\) with \(R\succeq0\), an unconstrained minimizer exists exactly when \(c\in\operatorname{Range}(R)\). In that case the minimizer set is \(-R^{\dagger}c+\operatorname{Null}(R)\); it is unique exactly when \(R\succ0\). If \(c\notin\operatorname{Range}(R)\), the unconstrained reduced problem is unbounded below, although reduced bounds may truncate the offending direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular reduced Hessian admits a minimizer only when the reduced gradient lies in its range, and uniqueness requires positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existence is equivalent to \(c\in\operatorname{Range}(R)\), and uniqueness to \(R\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Reduced-Hessian Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-space representation of a convex bound-QP on a selected trial subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\), \(H\succeq0\), let \(x_0\in[l,u]\), and let \(Z\) have full column rank. Restricting \(x=x_0+Zp\) gives \[\min_p\ \tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)p+(Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_0+g))^{\mathsf T}p\quad\text{subject to }l\le x_0+Zp\le u.\] Any reduced minimizer lifts to the minimizer of the original quadratic over the selected bound-compatible subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a bound-constrained convex QP to a chosen subspace yields a smaller convex QP whose minimizer lifts back to that subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reduced optimizer \(p^*\) yields the subspace optimizer \(x_0+Zp^*\).

notation.meaning: basis or selector for the trial subspace

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Compatible Subspace Reduction
Subspace-Minimization Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-space representation for a convex bound-constrained quadratic program on a selected free-variable subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(H\succeq0\), and let \(x_0\) satisfy \(\ell\le x_0\le u\). For a full-column-rank matrix \(Z\), restrict trial points to \(x=x_0+Zp\). Subspace minimization is then the reduced convex quadratic program
\[\min_p\;\tfrac12 p^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)p+(Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_0+g))^{\mathsf T}p\quad\text{subject to}\quad \ell\le x_0+Zp\le u.\]
If the columns of \(Z\) select variables not fixed at bounds, its solution supplies the free-variable correction while preserving all bound constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a bound-constrained convex QP to a chosen subspace yields a smaller convex QP whose solution gives a feasible free-variable correction.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and positive semidefinite.
\(x_0\in[\ell,u]\), and \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) has full column rank.
The reduced feasible set \(\{p:\ell\le x_0+Zp\le u\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*\) solves the reduced QP and \(x^*=x_0+Zp^*\) is feasible for the original bounds.

notation.meaning: Basis or selector for the minimization subspace.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and content kind fit the leaf, and the reduced-QP algebra is correct. However, the cited trust-region subspace-minimization section does not specifically support the asserted bound-constrained free-variable interface. A source with a precise locator for reduced-space or subspace minimization in bound-constrained QP is required.

children.title: Operator-Splitting QP Interfaces
children.top_down_role: ADMM, proximal splitting, and certificate-producing variants.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled ADMM for a convex quadratic separated from a closed convex constraint set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\), \(P\succeq0\), and let \(C\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Applied to \(\min f(x)+\delta_C(z)\) subject to \(x-z=0\), scaled ADMM with \(\rho>0\) is \[x^{k+1}=\arg\min_x\{f(x)+\tfrac\rho2\|x-z^k+u^k\|^2\},\quad z^{k+1}=\Pi_C(x^{k+1}+u^k),\quad u^{k+1}=u^k+x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}.\] Its standard residuals are \(r^{k+1}=x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\) and \(s^{k+1}=\rho(z^{k+1}-z^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-copy ADMM alternates a regularized quadratic solve, projection, and scaled-dual update, monitored by primal and dual residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration is a two-block operator-splitting interface with explicit primal and dual residuals.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Block Variable-Copy ADMM Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate of primal unboundedness commonly reported as dual infeasibility by splitting solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x:l\le Ax\le u\}\), \(P\succeq0\), suppose the feasible set is nonempty and there is \(d\ne0\) such that \[Pd=0,\qquad q^{\mathsf T}d<0,\qquad Ad\in\operatorname{rec}([l,u]).\] Then every feasible \(x\) generates the feasible ray \(x+td\), and the objective tends to \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible zero-curvature recession direction with negative linear slope certifies unboundedness below.
assumptions_latex: The row-bounded feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal optimal value is \(-\infty\), so no finite dual optimum exists.

notation.meaning: recession cone of the row-bound box

knowledge_statements.title: QP Recession Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificate validated by certificate-producing splitting solvers for row-bounded QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(l\le Ax\le u\), define \(y_+=\max(y,0)\) and \(y_-=\min(y,0)\). If \[A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad u^{\mathsf T}y_+ + l^{\mathsf T}y_-<0,\] with every multiplier component paired with an infinite support value required to be zero, then the row-bounded constraint system is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nullspace vector with negative signed support over the row-bound box certifies primal infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Components paired with infinite support values are zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No \(x\) satisfies \(l\le Ax\le u\).

notation.meaning: positive and negative parts of the certificate vector

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Form Primal-Infeasibility Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scope of the Two-Block Convergence Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the standard ADMM convergence interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The two-block convergence conclusion does not follow from the displayed iteration alone when a saddle point is absent, subproblems are solved with uncontrolled errors, or a naive cyclic extension uses three or more blocks. Such variants require separate regularity, error-control, or algorithm-specific convergence results.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard two-block ADMM convergence does not automatically extend to missing saddle points, uncontrolled inexact solves, or naive multi-block updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Those variants lie outside the stated two-block convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.title: Scope of the Two-Block Convergence Guarantee

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence guarantee for exact convex two-block splitting with identity coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For proper closed convex \(f\) and \(g\), suppose \(\min_{x,z}f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(x-z=0\) has a saddle point. With fixed \(\rho>0\) and exact subproblem solves, two-block ADMM satisfies \(x^k-z^k\to0\), \(\rho(z^k-z^{k-1})\to0\), and the objective values converge to the optimum. Every primal cluster point is optimal; if the primal optimizer is unique, the primal iterates converge to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact two-block ADMM converges in residual and objective value when a saddle point exists; uniqueness gives convergence to the unique primal optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal and dual residuals vanish and objective values converge to the optimal value.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Block ADMM Convergence Interface
Operator-Splitting QP Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block ADMM interface for a convex QP separated into a quadratic term and a closed convex constraint set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(P\succeq0\), a nonempty closed convex set \(C\), penalty \(\rho>0\), and initial \(z^0,u^0\), apply ADMM to \(\min_x \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x+\delta_C(z)\) subject to \(x-z=0\):
\[x^{k+1}=\arg\min_x\left\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x+\tfrac\rho2\lVert x-z^k+u^k\rVert_2^2\right\},\]
\[z^{k+1}=\Pi_C(x^{k+1}+u^k),\qquad u^{k+1}=u^k+x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}.\]
Stop when the primal residual \(x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\) and dual residual \(\rho(z^{k+1}-z^k)\) meet prescribed tolerances; output \(z^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ADMM alternates a regularized quadratic solve, projection onto the constraint set, and a scaled-dual update, stopping when primal and dual residuals are small.
assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive semidefinite.
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration defines an operator-splitting interface whose fixed points satisfy the QP optimality conditions.

notation.meaning: Indicator function of the constraint set.
Euclidean projection onto the constraint set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the operator-splitting container, and the displayed scaled-form ADMM iteration is mathematically coherent. No citation is supplied for the iteration, residual definitions, or fixed-point optimality claim; an authoritative ADMM source with a section or theorem locator is required.

children.title: Sparse-Direct Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Direct linear-algebra interfaces exploiting general sparsity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaled Residual Certificate for a Sparse-Direct Solve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori verification independent of the internal factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a computed solution \(\widehat s\) to \(Ks=r\), define \[\eta=\frac{\|r-K\widehat s\|}{\|K\|\,\|\widehat s\|+\|r\|},\] taking \(\eta=0\) when numerator and denominator both vanish. A small \(\eta\) is a normwise backward-error certificate under the corresponding joint perturbation convention. It does not by itself certify small forward error when \(K\) is ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized residual certifies backward accuracy, while forward accuracy additionally depends on conditioning.
assumptions_latex: A consistent subordinate matrix and vector norm is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta\le\tau\Longrightarrow\text{a normwise joint backward error no larger than }\tau\text{ under the stated scaling.}
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Residual Certificate for a Sparse-Direct Solve

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of a nonsingular sparse factor-and-solve contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K\) is singular, an interface assuming nonsingularity cannot promise a unique solution. The system \(Ks=r\) is consistent exactly when \(r\in\operatorname{range}(K)\). If consistent, its solutions are \(s_0+\ker K\); if inconsistent, no exact solution exists.
