Rank-revealing factorization, regularization, or a least-squares or minimum-norm contract is then required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singularity changes a unique sparse solve into rank detection, regularization, or generalized solution selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A unique direct solution is unavailable without an additional selection or regularization rule.}
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-System Boundary for Sparse-Direct Interfaces
Sparse-Direct Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic-numeric sparse direct solution interface for symmetric QP linear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a sparse symmetric nonsingular QP linear-system matrix \(K\) and right-hand side \(r\), choose a fill-reducing permutation \(\Pi\). Perform symbolic analysis of \(\Pi K\Pi^{\mathsf T}\), then compute a stable sparse factorization
\[\Pi K\Pi^{\mathsf T}=LDL^{\mathsf T},\]
where symmetric pivoting may replace scalar pivots by blocks. Solve successively \(Ly=\Pi r\), \(Dz=y\), and \(L^{\mathsf T}w=z\), and return \(s=\Pi^{\mathsf T}w\). For repeated QP solves with unchanged sparsity, reuse the symbolic analysis and update only numerical factors and triangular solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse-direct interface permutes and factors the QP system, then uses triangular solves; unchanged sparsity permits reuse of symbolic analysis.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is sparse, symmetric, and nonsingular.
The pivoting strategy produces a numerically admissible block-diagonal factor \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned vector \(s\) satisfies \(Ks=r\) up to numerical factorization and solve errors.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the sparse-direct interface leaf, and the symbolic/numeric factorization workflow is plausible. The sparse LDL factorization, block-pivoting qualification, symbolic reuse claim, and numerical-error conclusion require an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Block-Banded Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Direct interfaces exploiting block-banded QP structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical direct recursion for block half-bandwidth one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric block-tridiagonal matrix with diagonal blocks \(D_i\) and subdiagonal blocks \(E_i=K_{i,i-1}\), set \(S_0=D_0\) and, for \(i=1,\ldots,N\), \[L_i=E_iS_{i-1}^{-1},\qquad S_i=D_i-E_iS_{i-1}^{-1}E_i^{\mathsf T}.\] If every \(S_i\) is nonsingular, these blocks define a block \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization. A right-hand side is solved by forward substitution, solves with the \(S_i\), and backward substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-tridiagonal system is factored through recursive block Schur complements and solved by forward-backward substitution.
assumptions_latex: The matrix is symmetric and block tridiagonal.
Every recursive Schur complement \(S_i\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The recursion produces an exact block }LDL^{\mathsf T}\text{ factorization.}
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Tridiagonal LDL Recursion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualification on band preservation for indefinite or numerically unstable systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an indefinite block-banded matrix, stable symmetric pivoting can interchange blocks or select pivots not compatible with the declared stage order. The resulting factors need not remain within the original block band. Band preservation is therefore guaranteed by the SPD unpivoted regime, not by block bandwidth alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block bandwidth alone does not guarantee band-preserving factors when stability requires pivoting.
assumptions_latex: The matrix is not assumed positive definite.
The factorization may use stability-driven symmetric pivoting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Declared block bandwidth does not by itself imply equal factor bandwidth.}
knowledge_statements.title: Pivoting and Band-Preservation Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bandwidth Preservation under Positive-Definite Block Cholesky
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural closure of an SPD block-banded interface under elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\succ0\) be symmetrically block partitioned with \(K_{ij}=0\) for \(|i-j|>w\). In the declared block order, its unpivoted block Cholesky factorization \(K=LL^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies \(L_{ij}=0\) whenever \(i-j>w\). Thus no factor block occurs outside the original lower-band envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unpivoted Cholesky preserves the block bandwidth of an SPD system.
assumptions_latex: The declared block ordering is used without pivoting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_{ij}=0\quad\text{whenever }i-j>w.
knowledge_statements.title: Bandwidth Preservation under Positive-Definite Block Cholesky
Block-Banded Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structured linear-system representation induced by stagewise QP variables and local couplings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition a QP linear system into stage blocks \(s=(s_0,\ldots,s_N)\). It has block half-bandwidth \(w\) when its coefficient matrix \(K=[K_{ij}]_{i,j=0}^N\) satisfies
\[K_{ij}=0\quad\text{whenever}\quad |i-j|>w.\]
The solver interface exposes the ordered block dimensions, the nonzero blocks \(K_{ij}\) with \(|i-j|\le w\), and compatible right-hand-side blocks. A block-banded elimination may operate only on this envelope, provided pivoting or regularization does not introduce couplings outside the declared band.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagewise local coupling produces a block-banded QP system, represented by ordered blocks and a fixed block half-bandwidth for structured elimination.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is partitioned conformably with the ordered stage variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The QP linear solve can be presented through the block data \(\{K_{ij}:|i-j|\le w\}\) and the declared ordering.

notation.meaning: Coefficient block coupling stages i and j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the block-banded interface leaf. The bandwidth definition is precise, but the band-preserving elimination qualification and solver-interface claim have no inspectable citation. A block-banded factorization source with a specific section or page is required.

children.title: Fill-In Complexity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Ordering-dependent storage plus factorization growth.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar symbolic complexity for a fixed elimination order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_j\) be the number of later neighbors of vertex \(j\) in the filled graph. A conventional scalar symmetric factorization has storage \[O\!\left(n+\sum_{j=1}^n d_j\right)\] and arithmetic \[O\!\left(n+\sum_{j=1}^n d_j^2\right).\] For \(N\) uniform blocks of size at most \(b\) and block half-bandwidth \(w\), band-preserving dense-block factorization uses \(O(Nw^2b^3)\) arithmetic and \(O(Nwb^2)\) scalar storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct-factor complexity is governed by filled later-neighbor counts; fixed block size and bandwidth give linear scaling in the number of blocks.
assumptions_latex: A fixed elimination order is used.
The scalar bounds use conventional factorization kernels.
The block-banded factorization does not use bandwidth-expanding pivoting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Fixed }w,b\text{ imply linear work and storage in }N;\text{ growing filled degrees can make both superlinear.}

notation.meaning: Filled later-neighbor count at elimination step j.
Block half-bandwidth and maximum block size.

knowledge_statements.title: Filled-Degree Arithmetic and Storage Bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparse Input with Dense Ordering-Induced Fill
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering counterexample showing that input nonzero count does not determine factor complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the sparsity graph be a star on vertices \(\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}\), with center \(0\). It has \(n-1\) edges. Eliminating the center first makes its \(n-1\) later neighbors a clique and creates \(\binom{n-1}{2}\) fill edges. Eliminating all leaves before the center creates no fill.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same sparse star pattern produces quadratic fill or no fill solely through the elimination order.
assumptions_latex: The numerical factorization follows the selected symbolic ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |E|=O(n),\qquad |E_{\mathrm{filled}}|=\Theta(n^2)\text{ under the center-first order.}
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Input with Dense Ordering-Induced Fill

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic-elimination representation of direct-factor storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric sparsity graph and fixed elimination order, eliminating a vertex connects all of its currently uneliminated neighbors into a clique. Repetition produces the filled graph. Ignoring accidental numerical cancellation, an off-diagonal position in symbolic Cholesky or structurally symmetric \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) is present exactly when the corresponding ordered pair is an edge of the filled graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor sparsity is determined by the graph obtained by making every eliminated vertex's later neighbors a clique.
assumptions_latex: A fixed symmetric ordering is used.
Numerical pivoting does not change the symbolic order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{pattern}(L)\text{ is determined by the filled elimination graph.}
knowledge_statements.title: Filled-Graph Characterization of Factor Sparsity
Fill-In Complexity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic and storage regimes for direct factorization under bounded block bandwidth or general sparse elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a symmetric positive-definite block-banded matrix with \(N\) block rows, uniform block size \(b\), and block half-bandwidth \(w\), band-preserving Cholesky factorization requires
\[O(Nw^2b^3)\quad\text{arithmetic operations},\qquad O(Nwb^2)\quad\text{stored scalars}.\]
For a general sparse symmetric matrix, an elimination ordering defines a filled graph; if \(d_j\) is the number of later neighbors of eliminated vertex \(j\), scalar factorization uses \(O(\sum_j d_j^2)\) arithmetic and \(O(\sum_j d_j)\) factor storage. Thus complexity is governed by ordering-induced fill, not solely by the original number of nonzeros.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Banded factorization is linear in block rows for fixed bandwidth and block size; general sparse cost depends on the filled elimination graph.
assumptions_latex: The banded matrix is symmetric positive definite and factored without bandwidth-expanding pivoting.
Block dimensions are uniformly bounded by \(b\).
For the graph bound, \(d_j\) counts later neighbors after fill under the chosen ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixed \(w\) and \(b\) give linear scaling in \(N\), whereas growing filled degrees can cause superlinear storage and arithmetic.

notation.meaning: Maximum block size and block half-bandwidth.
Filled later-neighbor count at elimination step j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind is correct for this terminal container, and the stated banded and filled-graph regimes are plausible. Exact arithmetic and storage bounds require a source that fixes the counting conventions, block model, and filled-degree definition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality and uniqueness certificate for the finite-horizon unconstrained linear-quadratic interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_t,K_t\) satisfy the finite-horizon Riccati equations and let \(G_t=R_t+B_t^{\mathsf T}P_{t+1}B_t\succ0\). Every trajectory satisfying \(x_{t+1}=A_tx_t+B_tu_t\) obeys \[J(x,u)=\tfrac12x_0^{\mathsf T}P_0x_0+\tfrac12\sum_{t=0}^{N-1}(u_t+K_tx_t)^{\mathsf T}G_t(u_t+K_tx_t).\] Hence equality with the lower bound holds exactly when \(u_t=-K_tx_t\) at every stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Riccati matrices express the cost as the optimal value plus positive control-residual squares, certifying the unique optimal control sequence.
assumptions_latex: The objective and dynamics are those of the homogeneous finite-horizon linear-quadratic problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J\ge\tfrac12x_0^{\mathsf T}P_0x_0,\qquad J=\tfrac12x_0^{\mathsf T}P_0x_0\iff u_t=-K_tx_t\ \forall t.
knowledge_statements.title: Completion-of-Squares Riccati Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Horizon Scaling of Dense Riccati Sweeps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense arithmetic and retained-factor storage for fixed stage dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For horizon \(N\), state dimension \(n_x\), and control dimension \(n_u\), conventional dense Riccati recursion uses \[O\!\left(N(n_x^3+n_x^2n_u+n_xn_u^2+n_u^3)\right)\] arithmetic. Retaining all \(P_t\) and \(K_t\) uses \(O(N(n_x^2+n_xn_u))\) scalars. Thus work and retained-factor storage are linear in \(N\) when \(n_x,n_u\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed state and control dimensions, a dense Riccati sweep has linear work and retained-factor storage in the horizon.
assumptions_latex: Conventional dense matrix arithmetic is used.
All value matrices and feedback gains are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T=O(N),\qquad M=O(N)\quad\text{for fixed }n_x,n_u.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Horizon Scaling of Dense Riccati Sweeps

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the plain global-quadratic backward-forward interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With nonredundant stage inequalities such as \(C_tx_t+D_tu_t\le d_t\), the unconstrained law \(u_t=-K_tx_t\) can be infeasible, and the constrained value function is generally piecewise quadratic rather than one global quadratic. The plain Riccati sweep therefore does not solve the constrained QP in general and must be embedded in a constrained-QP procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stage inequalities generally invalidate the plain global-linear-feedback Riccati solution.
assumptions_latex: At least one stage inequality can bind.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Unconstrained Riccati optimality alone implies neither constrained feasibility nor constrained optimality.}
knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Constrained Riccati Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Riccati Recursion as Stagewise Block Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-algebra interpretation of the equality-constrained finite-horizon optimal-control interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With variables ordered by stage, the KKT system for a stage-additive linear-quadratic control problem is block banded. Eliminating stages backward forms the value-function Schur complements \(P_N,\ldots,P_0\). When every required pivot block \(G_t\) is nonsingular, this elimination is algebraically equivalent to the backward Riccati recursion; substitution recovers the controls, states, and dynamics multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Riccati recursion is specialized block elimination of the stage-ordered optimal-control KKT system.
assumptions_latex: The objective is stage-additive and quadratic.
Every control pivot \(G_t\) used by the elimination is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Riccati elimination and stagewise KKT elimination produce the same solution.}

notation.meaning: Value-function Hessian or stage Schur complement.

knowledge_statements.title: Riccati Recursion as Stagewise Block Elimination
Riccati-Based Optimal-Control Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward-forward Riccati interface for finite-horizon equality-constrained linear-quadratic control QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For dynamics \(x_{t+1}=A_tx_t+B_tu_t\) and cost \(\tfrac12x_N^{\mathsf T}Q_Nx_N+\sum_{t=0}^{N-1}\tfrac12(x_t^{\mathsf T}Q_tx_t+u_t^{\mathsf T}R_tu_t)\), set \(P_N=Q_N\). For \(t=N-1,\ldots,0\), compute
\[G_t=R_t+B_t^{\mathsf T}P_{t+1}B_t,\quad K_t=G_t^{-1}B_t^{\mathsf T}P_{t+1}A_t,\]
\[P_t=Q_t+A_t^{\mathsf T}P_{t+1}A_t-A_t^{\mathsf T}P_{t+1}B_tK_t.\]
Starting from the prescribed \(x_0\), sweep forward with \(u_t=-K_tx_t\) and the dynamics. Affine terms are handled by an accompanying backward affine recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Riccati interface solves a finite-horizon linear-quadratic control QP by a backward matrix recursion followed by forward state-control recovery.
assumptions_latex: Only linear dynamics and equality constraints are included in this basic interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The backward-forward recursion returns the unique optimal control sequence and its induced state trajectory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Riccati interface leaf, and the recursion is the standard finite-horizon LQR recursion under the stated definiteness assumptions. No authoritative source with a precise recursion locator is supplied, so the optimality and uniqueness conclusion remains unsupported.

children.title: Low-Rank Update Interfaces
children.top_down_role: QP interfaces exploiting low-rank changes across related systems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact small-dimensional test for a symmetric positive-definite rank-one downdate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\succ0\) and \(\widetilde K=K-uu^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(\widetilde K\succ0\) if and only if \(u^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}u<1\); it is singular when this scalar equals one and indefinite when it exceeds one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-one downdate preserves positive definiteness exactly when its leverage is below one.
assumptions_latex: K\text{ is real symmetric positive definite}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K-uu^{\mathsf T}\succ0\iff u^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}u<1.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Downdate Definiteness Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact small-core criterion for preserving positive definiteness under a symmetric low-rank downdate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\succ0\), \(D\succeq0\), and \(\widetilde K=K-UDU^{\mathsf T}\). Then \[\widetilde K\succ0\iff I-D^{1/2}U^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}UD^{1/2}\succ0.\] Equality of the largest eigenvalue of \(D^{1/2}U^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}UD^{1/2}\) to one gives singularity, while a value exceeding one gives indefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-r downdate preserves positive definiteness exactly when the largest eigenvalue of its small leverage matrix is below one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K-UDU^{\mathsf T}\succ0\iff\lambda_{\max}(D^{1/2}U^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}UD^{1/2})<1.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-r Downdate Definiteness Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional arithmetic and storage cost for a supplied rank-r inverse correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a valid updated inverse action has the form z=K^{-1}b-WS^{-1}V^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}b, where W=K^{-1}U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r} and the nonsingular r\times r core S has been factored. Each right-hand side then requires one application of K^{-1}, O(nr) factor-vector work, and O(r^2) work with the factored core. Storing W,V, and the core factor requires O(nr+r^2) additional words.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After preprocessing, each low-rank-corrected solve costs one base solve plus linear-in-n factor work and a small dense solve.
assumptions_latex: The stated inverse-correction representation is valid.
W\text{ and a factorization of }S\text{ are reusable}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{updated}}=T_{K^{-1}}+O(nr+r^2),\qquad M_{\mathrm{extra}}=O(nr+r^2).

notation.meaning: Precomputed base inverse applied to update columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Reusable Low-Rank Correction Cost
Low-Rank Update Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-action update for QP systems modified by a low-rank symmetric term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be nonsingular and let a modified QP system be \(\widetilde K=K+UCV^{\mathsf T}\), where \(C\) is nonsingular and the update rank is \(r\). If \(C^{-1}+V^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}U\) is nonsingular, then
\[\widetilde K^{-1}=K^{-1}-K^{-1}U\bigl(C^{-1}+V^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}U\bigr)^{-1}V^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}.\]
Hence an interface need only provide applications of \(K^{-1}\), the update factors, and an \(r\)-dimensional dense solve. A symmetric update uses \(V=U\) and symmetric \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-r modification can be solved using the old inverse action plus a dense r-dimensional correction, avoiding refactorization of the full QP system.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(C\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\) are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed identity gives the exact inverse action for \(\widetilde K=K+UCV^{\mathsf T}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the low-rank update interface leaf, and the displayed Woodbury identity is internally consistent under the stated nonsingularity assumptions. A precise authoritative locator for the identity and inverse-action interpretation is required.

children.title: Matrix-Free Operator Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Operator-based interfaces avoiding explicit matrix assembly.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of a purported transpose oracle to define a symmetric KKT action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the forward constraint action be \(Av=v\) on \(\mathbb R\), but let the supplied purported transpose action be \(B y=2y\). Then \(y^{\mathsf T}Av=yv
e2yv=v^{\mathsf T}By\) whenever \(yv
e0\). Hence \(B
e A^{\mathsf T}\), and the block action \((Hv+By,Av)\) is not the symmetric KKT operator associated with \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward identity oracle paired with a doubled transpose oracle violates the adjoint identity and cannot represent a symmetric KKT system.
assumptions_latex: The primal and constraint spaces are one-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \langle y,Av\rangle\ne\langle By,v\rangle.

notation.meaning: supplied but inconsistent purported transpose action

knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint-Inconsistency Failure Example

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact objective, gradient, and directional-curvature information supplied by a Hessian action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x+c\) with symmetric \(H\), an oracle returning \(Hv\) determines \[q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}(Hx)+g^{\mathsf T}x+c,\qquad \nabla q(x)=Hx+g,\qquad \frac{d^2}{dt^2}q(x+tv)=v^{\mathsf T}(Hv).\] Each quantity is obtained without storing entries of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Hessian-vector oracle suffices to evaluate a quadratic objective, its gradient, and curvature along any direction.
assumptions_latex: H\text{ is a symmetric linear operator}.
The oracle returns exact products with compatible dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v\mapsto Hv\text{ determines }q(x),\ \nabla q(x),\text{ and }v^{\mathsf T}Hv\text{ without explicit assembly}.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Quadratic Evaluation Identities

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic conditions for Hessian, constraint, and adjoint-action oracles to represent declared convex-QP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H:X\to X\), \(\mathcal A:X\to Y\), and \(\mathcal A^*:Y\to X\) be dimensionally compatible oracles on finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces. They represent a symmetric convex equality-QP operator only if they are linear and, for all compatible \(v,w,y\), \[\langle w,\mathcal Hv\rangle=\langle\mathcal Hw,v\rangle,\qquad \langle v,\mathcal Hv\rangle\ge0,\qquad \langle y,\mathcal Av\rangle=\langle\mathcal A^*y,v\rangle.\] Conversely, these universal identities establish that \(\mathcal H\) is self-adjoint positive semidefinite and that the supplied \(\mathcal A^*\) is the adjoint of \(\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearity, Hessian symmetry and positivity, and forward-adjoint consistency are the exact algebraic conditions for declared matrix-free convex-QP operators.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ and }Y\text{ are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces}.
\mathcal H,\mathcal A,\mathcal A^*\text{ have dimensionally compatible outputs}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal H=\mathcal H^*\succeq0\quad\text{and}\quad\mathcal A^*\text{ is the adjoint of }\mathcal A.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Operator Consistency Conditions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Krylov protocol for an exact self-adjoint equality-QP KKT operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal K be self-adjoint and nonsingular, and let M\succ0 be a fixed preconditioner with available inverse action. Preconditioned MINRES uses applications of \mathcal K and M^{-1}, inner products, and vector updates, stopping when \|b-\mathcal Kz^k\|_{M^{-1}}/\|b\|_{M^{-1}}\le\tau. In exact arithmetic it terminates in at most the degree of the minimal polynomial of M^{-1}\mathcal K, hence no more than the operator dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact self-adjoint KKT and fixed SPD preconditioner actions support matrix-free MINRES with a preconditioned-residual test.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is fixed, self-adjoint, and positive definite}.
Operator and preconditioner actions are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{\|b-\mathcal Kz^k\|_{M^{-1}}}{\|b\|_{M^{-1}}}\le\tau\text{ is computable, and exact-arithmetic termination occurs in at most the operator dimension}.
knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned Matrix-Free MINRES Interface
Matrix-Free Operator Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle representation of QP linear algebra without explicit storage of system matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A matrix-free convex-QP interface represents \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\) and linear constraints \(Ax=b\) through routines computing \(v\mapsto Hv\), \(v\mapsto Av\), and \(y\mapsto A^{\mathsf T}y\), together with vectors \(g,b\). Consequently, the KKT operator is applied as
\[\mathcal K(v,y)=\bigl(Hv+A^{\mathsf T}y,\;Av\bigr).\]
Krylov or proximal iterations may use this operator and a preconditioner without assembling \(H\), \(A\), or the KKT matrix. The transpose routine must be adjoint-consistent with the forward constraint routine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free QP exposes Hessian, constraint, transpose, and preconditioner actions, allowing iterative solution without explicitly assembling the KKT matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a symmetric positive-semidefinite linear operator.
The supplied actions of \(A\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}\) are mutually adjoint.
All operator outputs have dimensions compatible with the primal and constraint spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle routines determine every product with the saddle-point operator \(\mathcal K\) needed by a matrix-free iterative solver.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the matrix-free operator interface leaf, and the KKT operator application is correct for equality constraints. The oracle requirements, adjoint-consistency condition, and iterative-solver usage have no inspectable source locator.

children.title: Approximation-Quality Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Accuracy limits associated with low-rank or implicit representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform objective control without a domain-radius bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=\mathbb R\), \(q(x)=0\), and \(\widetilde q(x)=\tfrac12\varepsilon x^2\), the Hessian error is \(\varepsilon\), but \(|\widetilde q(x)-q(x)|=\varepsilon x^2/2\) is unbounded on \(X\). Thus operator-norm error alone does not give uniform objective approximation on an unbounded domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even arbitrarily small Hessian error produces unbounded objective discrepancy when the domain allows arbitrarily large vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{x\in X}|\widetilde q(x)-q(x)|=+\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Domain Objective-Error Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value accuracy under spectral-norm Hessian approximation on a bounded feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x+c\) and \(\widetilde q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x+c\). If nonempty \(X\) satisfies \(\|x\|_2\le R\) and \(\|\widetilde H-H\|_2\le\varepsilon\), then \(\sup_{x\in X}|\widetilde q(x)-q(x)|\le\varepsilon R^2/2\). If both minima are attained, any minimizer \(\widetilde x\) of \(\widetilde q\) satisfies \(q(\widetilde x)-q(x^*)\le\varepsilon R^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a radius-R feasible set, Hessian error epsilon causes at most epsilon R squared objective suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: X\ne\varnothing\text{ and }\|x\|_2\le R\text{ for all }x\in X.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(\widetilde x)-q(x^*)\le\varepsilon R^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Domain Objective Approximation Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform solution-location control without a fixed positive curvature margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\delta,\varepsilon>0\), let \(q_\delta(x)=\tfrac12\delta x^2-x\) and \(\widetilde q_{\delta,\varepsilon}(x)=\tfrac12(\delta+\varepsilon)x^2-x\). Then \(\|\widetilde H-H\|_2=\varepsilon\), while \[x^*=\delta^{-1},\qquad \widetilde x^*=(\delta+\varepsilon)^{-1},\qquad |x^*-\widetilde x^*|=\frac{\varepsilon}{\delta(\delta+\varepsilon)}.\] For every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), the displacement diverges as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrarily small Hessian error can move the minimizer arbitrarily far when no uniform positive curvature margin is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{\delta>0}|x^*-\widetilde x^*|=+\infty\quad\text{for every fixed }\varepsilon>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Curvature Minimizer-Instability Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity guarantee supplied by a Hessian approximation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If H\succeq\mu I and \|\widetilde H-H\|_2\le\varepsilon, then \widetilde H\succeq(\mu-\varepsilon)I. Thus \varepsilon<\mu preserves strong convexity, \varepsilon=\mu guarantees only positive semidefiniteness, and \varepsilon>\mu gives no convexity guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral error below the curvature margin preserves strong convexity; beyond the margin convexity is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_{\min}(\widetilde H)\ge\mu-\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Curvature-Preservation Boundary
Approximation-Quality Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution-error boundary for approximate strongly convex QP Hessians and its failure without curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(H\succeq\mu I\) for \(\mu>0\), and let \(\widetilde q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(\lVert\widetilde H-H\rVert_2\le\varepsilon<\mu\). Their unconstrained minimizers satisfy
\[\lVert\widetilde x^*-x^*\rVert_2\le\frac{\varepsilon}{\mu-\varepsilon}\lVert x^*\rVert_2.\]
The denominator marks the quality boundary: if the approximation error reaches the curvature scale, \(\widetilde H\) need not remain positive definite. When \(\mu=0\), no uniform minimizer-distance bound follows from an operator-norm Hessian error alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hessian approximation below the strong-convexity margin controls minimizer error; at or beyond that margin, convexity and uniform solution stability can fail.
assumptions_latex: Both models share the same linear term \(g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\widetilde x^*-x^*\rVert_2\le\varepsilon\lVert x^*\rVert_2/(\mu-\varepsilon)\), while no analogous uniform bound is guaranteed at \(\mu=0\).

notation.meaning: Strong-convexity modulus of the exact Hessian.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the stated minimizer perturbation bound is consistent with the unconstrained strongly convex setting. The exact bound and the claimed failure boundary at zero curvature require an authoritative perturbation-analysis source with a specific locator.

children.title: Decomposable QP Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces exposing separable objective or constraint structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility certificate for a primal decomposable-QP interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the copy-and-consistency interface, a tuple \((z,x_1,\ldots,x_m)\) represents a feasible global point exactly when \(x_i\in X_i\) and \(x_i-E_i z=0\) for every component. Omitting a consistency equation generally enlarges the represented feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local feasibility plus zero consistency residuals exactly certifies global feasibility of the copy formulation.
assumptions_latex: The copy formulation is the exact representation declared by the interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (z,(x_i))\text{ feasible}\iff x_i\in X_i\text{ and }x_i-E_i z=0\quad\forall i.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Feasibility and Consistency Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal decomposition through local copies of shared coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let component \(i\) use coordinates \(E_i z\), local Hessian \(H_i\succeq0\), linear term \(g_i\), and polyhedron \(X_i\). Introducing \(x_i=E_i z\) gives the equivalent QP \[\min_{z,(x_i)}\sum_i\left(\tfrac12x_i^{\mathsf T}H_ix_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x_i\right)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad x_i\in X_i,\;x_i=E_i z\quad\forall i.\] Exact equivalence requires every copied occurrence of a shared coordinate to be linked to the same global coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shared coordinates can be copied into local QPs and tied to one global variable by consistency equations, yielding an exact decomposable interface.
assumptions_latex: Each X_i is a nonempty closed convex polyhedron.
Every duplicated coordinate is covered by a consistency equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{z:E_i z\in X_i\ \forall i\}\text{ and the copy formulation have identical feasible }z\text{ and objective values}.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Copy-and-Consistency Interface
Decomposable QP Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable convex QP representation with local variables and a low-dimensional linear coupling constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A decomposable convex QP has blocks \(x_i\in X_i\) and the form
\[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}\;\sum_{i=1}^m\left(\tfrac12x_i^{\mathsf T}H_ix_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x_i\right)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{i=1}^m A_ix_i=b,\]
where \(H_i\succeq0\) and each \(X_i\) is a nonempty closed convex polyhedron. For a multiplier \(y\), the Lagrangian separates as
\[L(x,y)=-b^{\mathsf T}y+\sum_{i=1}^m\left(\tfrac12x_i^{\mathsf T}H_ix_i+(g_i+A_i^{\mathsf T}y)^{\mathsf T}x_i+\delta_{X_i}(x_i)\right).\]
Thus local minimizations communicate only through the shared multiplier and coupling residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable block QP with one linear coupling constraint decomposes into independent local quadratic subproblems for each fixed shared multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(H_i\) is symmetric positive semidefinite for every block \(i\).
Each \(X_i\) is a nonempty closed convex polyhedron.
The coupled feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed \(y\), minimizing \(L(x,y)\) separates into \(m\) independent local QP minimizations.

notation.meaning: Local contribution to the coupling constraint.
Multiplier for the shared coupling equality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the decomposable-QP interface leaf, and the Lagrangian separation formula matches the stated coupling equality. No source is supplied for the decomposition interface or fixed-multiplier separability claim.

children.title: Distributed QP Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Execution interfaces spanning multiple computational agents.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface-level certificate independent of a particular distributed algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a connected communication graph, agent-local points represent one feasible global point when all local constraints hold and every edge residual \(x_i-x_j\) is zero. Nonzero edge residuals measure failure of consensus but do not by themselves measure optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local feasibility and zero edge residuals certify a common feasible point on a connected graph; optimality requires additional stationarity information.
assumptions_latex: Local constraint sets collectively encode the declared global model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i\in X_i\ \forall i\text{ and }x_i-x_j=0\ \forall\{i,j\}\in E\Longrightarrow\text{one globally consistent feasible point}.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Consensus-Feasibility Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity condition for consensus imposed only through communication edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_c=(V,E)\) be an undirected communication graph and let each agent have \(x_i\in\mathbb R^n\). Edge equalities \(x_i=x_j\) for all \(\{i,j\}\in E\) enforce one global consensus for every assignment satisfying them if and only if \(G_c\) is connected. If it is disconnected, different connected components may take different values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise agreement along communication edges enforces one global value exactly when the communication graph is connected.
assumptions_latex: All local copies have the same dimension.
The edge equalities are imposed exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:x_i=x_j\ \forall\{i,j\}\in E\}=\{x:x_1=\cdots=x_{|V|}\}\iff G_c\text{ is connected}.
knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Graph Consensus Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm-independent optimality certificate for a consensus-form convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let connected graph \(G=(V,E)\) have node-edge incidence matrix \(B\), and consider \(\min_x f(x)=\sum_{i\in V}f_i(x_i)\) subject to \((B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I)x=0\). If the relative-interior constraint qualification \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\ker(B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I)\ne\varnothing\) holds, then a feasible \(x\) is globally optimal if and only if there is an edge multiplier \(\lambda\) satisfying \[0\in\partial f(x)+(B\otimes I)\lambda,\qquad (B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I)x=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a standard constraint qualification, consensus plus stationarity balanced by edge multipliers is necessary and sufficient for global optimality.
assumptions_latex: f_i\text{ is closed, proper, and convex for every }i.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is optimal}\iff\exists\lambda:\ 0\in\partial f(x)+(B\otimes I)\lambda\ \land\ (B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I)x=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Edge-Multiplier Distributed KKT Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributed protocol for a strongly convex separable QP with one affine coupling block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \min_{x_i\in X_i}\sum_i(\tfrac12x_i^{\mathsf T}H_ix_i+c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i) subject to \sum_iA_ix_i=b, workers compute x_i^k=\arg\min_{x_i\in X_i}\{\tfrac12x_i^{\mathsf T}H_ix_i+c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i+(y^k)^{\mathsf T}A_ix_i\}. They transmit A_ix_i^k; a coordinator forms r^k=\sum_iA_ix_i^k-b and broadcasts y^{k+1}=y^k+\alpha_kr^k unless the declared residual tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers solve local strongly convex QPs and a coordinator updates the coupling multiplier from the aggregate feasibility residual.
assumptions_latex: X_i\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex for every }i.
The coupled problem has a primal-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r^k=0\text{ together with the local minimization conditions is a KKT certificate for the coupled QP}.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinator–Worker Dual-Gradient Protocol

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rate and communication cost for unconstrained strongly convex local blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If X_i=\mathbb R^{n_i}, define L=\lambda_{\max}(\sum_iA_iH_i^{-1}A_i^{\mathsf T})>0. For constant 0<\alpha\le1/L, dual-gradient ascent satisfies d(y^*)-d(y^k)\le\|y^0-y^*\|_2^2/(2\alpha k). Each iteration performs one local solve per worker, transmits one coupling vector per worker, and uses one aggregate reduction and one multiplier broadcast.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-step dual ascent has an O(1/k) dual-value bound and one reduction-and-broadcast round per iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d(y^*)-d(y^k)=O(k^{-1})\text{ with one reduction-and-broadcast communication round per iteration}.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Gradient Communication and Convergence Bound
Distributed QP Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus ADMM interface for distributed solution of separable convex quadratic programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_z\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(z)\), where each \(f_i\) is a closed proper convex quadratic possibly including a local polyhedral indicator, introduce copies \(x_i=z\). Given \(\rho>0\), initialize \(z^0,u_i^0\), and iterate in parallel:
\[x_i^{k+1}=\arg\min_{x_i}\left\{f_i(x_i)+\tfrac\rho2\lVert x_i-z^k+u_i^k\rVert_2^2\right\},\]
\[z^{k+1}=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m(x_i^{k+1}+u_i^k),\qquad u_i^{k+1}=u_i^k+x_i^{k+1}-z^{k+1}.\]
Stop when consensus and dual residuals meet prescribed tolerances; output \(z^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus ADMM solves local regularized QPs in parallel, averages their shifted solutions, and updates local dual variables until agreement is reached.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is closed, proper, and convex.
The consensus problem has a primal-dual solution.
Communication permits computation of the global average at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any converged fixed point satisfies \(x_i^*=z^*\) and the first-order optimality condition for \(\min_z\sum_i f_i(z)\).

notation.meaning: Agent-local copy of the consensus variable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the distributed-QP interface leaf, and the consensus ADMM updates are coherent for the stated consensus formulation. An authoritative source with a precise locator is required for the updates, residual stopping rule, and fixed-point optimality claim.

children.title: Coupling-Structure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem-coupling patterns governing decomposition viability.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Syntactic block-coupling representation for cross-block objective terms and multi-block constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed partition \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), form a hypergraph on vertices \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Each displayed constraint row contributes the hyperedge \(e_r=\{i:a_{r,i}\ne0\}\), and each nonzero off-diagonal Hessian block \(H_{ij}\) contributes the edge \(\{i,j\}\). A vertex partition has no displayed cross-part coupling exactly when every such edge and hyperedge lies within one part.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coupling hypergraph records every block jointly touched by a constraint row or Hessian cross-term; absence of crossing edges exactly certifies syntactic block separation.
assumptions_latex: The block partition and displayed formulation are fixed.
Structural coupling is judged before redundancy elimination or algebraic reformulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No displayed cross-part coupling}\iff\text{every coupling edge or hyperedge lies in one part}.

notation.meaning: blocks touched by displayed constraint row r

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Coupling Hypergraph

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of a small decomposition interface when every balanced separation requires a large separator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sequence of block-coupling hypergraphs, if every separator producing two nontrivial component sets contains a number of separator coordinates comparable to the total problem dimension, then separator-based decomposition has no lower-dimensional primal interface. This is a structural boundary, not a claim that every distributed algorithm becomes ineffective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When all useful separations require nearly full-dimensional separators, separator-based decomposition loses its small-interface advantage.
assumptions_latex: Interface size is measured by separator-coordinate dimension.
Only nontrivial component separations are considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \dim(x_S)=\Theta(n)\Longrightarrow\text{no asymptotically lower-dimensional separator interface}.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense-Coupling Regime Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional separation induced by a coupling-hypergraph separator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the variable blocks be partitioned into \(V_1,S,V_2\) so that no objective edge or constraint hyperedge meets both \(V_1\) and \(V_2\) after the separator blocks \(S\) are removed. For any fixed value of the separator variables, the displayed QP terms and constraints involving \(V_1\) and \(V_2\) separate into two independent subproblems. The separator-coordinate dimension therefore upper-bounds the primal interface dimension of this decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Removing a separator and fixing its variables separates the remaining displayed QP into independent component subproblems.
assumptions_latex: All cross-component coupling is represented by the declared hypergraph.
The separator variables are fixed consistently across adjacent components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_S\text{ fixed}\Longrightarrow\text{independent subproblems on }V_1\text{ and }V_2.
knowledge_statements.title: Separator-Conditioned Decomposition Regime
Coupling-Structure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural regimes determined by the graph of cross-block Hessian and constraint couplings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition QP variables into blocks \(x_1,ldots,x_m\). Define the coupling graph \(G=(V,E)\), with \(V=\{1,ldots,m\}\), by placing \(\{i,j\}\in E\) whenever a Hessian block \(H_{ij}\neq0\) or some constraint row contains nonzero coefficients in both blocks. If \(G\) is disconnected, the QP separates by connected components after independently assigning uncoupled constraint rows. If \(G\) is connected but has small separators, elimination or message passing can localize most computation to components joined through separator variables. Dense coupling corresponds to large separators and removes this structural advantage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disconnected coupling graphs yield independent QPs; small graph separators support localized computation, while dense coupling limits decomposition benefits.
assumptions_latex: The QP variables and coefficient matrices have a fixed conformal block partition.
Each constraint row is assigned to the blocks on which it has nonzero coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Connected components characterize exact separability, while separator size characterizes the interface dimension required between coupled subproblems.

notation.meaning: Graph of cross-block objective or constraint coupling.
Hessian block coupling variable blocks i and j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind is plausible for this structural-regime leaf, but the opening variable list contains the malformed text `x_1,ldots,x_m` rather than a valid ellipsis. More importantly, the separator/interface-dimension assertions and treatment of multi-block constraint rows require a precise graph or hypergraph decomposition source before a reliable mathematical replacement can be approved.

children.title: Convexity Recognition
children.top_down_role: Recognition of quadratic structures acceptable to convex-QP pipelines.

assumptions_latex: \(n,p,s\in\mathbb N\), \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(r\in\mathbb R\).
\(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{s\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{the quadratic program is convex}\iff Q_s\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: symmetric part of the quadratic coefficient matrix
the symmetric matrix M is positive semidefinite

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition criterion for a finite-dimensional quadratic program with affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\) for \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\). Define \(Q_s=(Q+Q^{\mathsf T})/2\). Because \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx=x^{\mathsf T}Q_sx\), the quadratic program is convex precisely when \(Q_s\succeq0\). Equivalently, convexity is recognized by \(d^{\mathsf T}Q_sd\ge0\) for every \(d\in\mathbb R^n\); the affine constraints define a convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional quadratic program with affine constraints is convex exactly when the symmetric part of its objective matrix is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity Recognition

children.title: Quadratic Canonicalization
children.top_down_role: Transformation into solver-facing convex QP representations.

assumptions_latex: \(n,p,s\in\mathbb N\), \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(r\in\mathbb R\).
\(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{s\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^s\).
Variables and constraint rows have fixed finite orderings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{\mathsf T}Hx+a^{\mathsf T}x+r=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}(H+H^{\mathsf T})x+a^{\mathsf T}x+r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical matrix representation of an affine-constrained convex quadratic program.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(Q=H+H^{\mathsf T}\) and \(c=a\). Then the scalar quadratic objective \(x^{\mathsf T}Hx+a^{\mathsf T}x+r\) is represented without changing its values as \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\). With fixed variable and row orderings, the canonical solver data are \((Q,c,r,A,b,G,h)\) for the model \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\ Gx\le h.\] The canonical matrix \(Q\) is symmetric, and the represented objective is convex exactly when \(Q\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetrize and scale the quadratic coefficient, order variables and constraint rows consistently, and export the objective and affine constraints as canonical matrix data.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Canonicalization

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

children.title: Recognition-to-Canonicalization Handoff
children.top_down_role: Transfer of curvature, sign, plus domain metadata into canonicalization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical invariants required when a recognized quadratic model is transferred into canonical convex-QP data; status vocabulary and serialization format remain implementation-defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given ordered variables, a quadratic objective \(x^{\mathsf T}Hx+a^{\mathsf T}x+r\), and affine constraints, form \(Q=H+H^{\mathsf T}\). Accept the model for an ambient convex-QP pipeline only if \(Q\succeq0\), then export \((Q,a,r,A,b,G,h)\) and bijective variable and row maps. A handoff is valid exactly when dimensions agree and decoding through the maps reconstructs the original objective and every affine constraint. Failure of the PSD test must not be reported as primal infeasibility or unboundedness; it means only that this convex-QP handoff does not apply.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer recognized models by exporting equivalent canonical matrices and reversible index maps; validate dimensions and exact reconstruction, and keep model-class rejection distinct from optimization status.
assumptions_latex: All constraints are affine and have fixed finite orderings.
Coefficient extraction and index maps are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\succeq0\ \land\ \operatorname{decode}(Q,a,r,A,b,G,h)=\operatorname{input}\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{a valid equivalent convex-QP handoff}.

notation.meaning: reconstruction using the exported variable and row maps

knowledge_statements.title: Schema-Neutral Recognition-to-Canonicalization Contract
Recognition-to-Canonicalization Handoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic handoff from recognized convexity to canonical QP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a quadratic model with ordered variables, objective coefficients \((H,a,r)\), and affine constraints. Form \(Q=H+H^{\mathsf T}\) and test \(Q\succeq0\). If the test fails, return status \(\mathrm{not\_convex\_QP}\). Otherwise assemble equalities as \(Ax=b\), inequalities as \(Gx\le h\), retain the variable and row index maps, and output \((Q,a,r,A,b,G,h)\) together with status \(\mathrm{convex\_QP}\). The output is accepted only when all dimensions agree and reconstructing the objective and constraints through the index maps reproduces the input model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetrize and test the Hessian, reject nonconvex models, then export dimensionally consistent canonical matrices plus index maps for accepted convex QPs.
assumptions_latex: The input has a quadratic objective and affine constraints.
Coefficient extraction and variable ordering are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\succeq0\Rightarrow (Q,a,r,A,b,G,h)\text{ is canonical convex-QP data equivalent to the input}.\)

notation.meaning: input quadratic coefficient matrix before canonical symmetrization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the handoff leaf and is internally plausible, but no source supports the proposed statuses, index-map requirements, acceptance test, or exact handoff schema. An authoritative modeling-system or solver-interface specification is required.

children.title: Sparsity-Preserving Handoffs
children.top_down_role: Transfer of sparse matrix representations into solver interfaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact validation of sparse serialization using declared structural indices rather than numerical support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a canonical sparse matrix by dimensions \((m,n)\), a declared structural index set \(S\), indexed values \(M_S\), and row and column maps. A handoff passes an exact round-trip certificate when decoding and re-encoding reproduce all these data. Equality of numerical supports \(\{(i,j):M_{ij}\ne0\}\) alone is insufficient because an indexed value may be zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse handoff is certified by round-tripping dimensions, declared indices, indexed values, and index maps; numerical nonzeros alone do not determine structural sparsity.
assumptions_latex: The sparse format has deterministic encoding and decoding rules.
The declared pattern and index maps are transmitted data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{encode}(\operatorname{decode}(m,n,S,M_S))=(m,n,S,M_S)\text{ with the original index maps}.

notation.meaning: values indexed by the declared structural pattern

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Handoff Round-Trip Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lossless sparse transmission of a symmetric QP Hessian through one stored triangle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric \(Q\), an interface may transmit one triangle with dimensions, triangle convention, structural indices, indexed values, and variable map. Decoding sets \(\widehat Q_{ji}=\widehat Q_{ij}\) off the diagonal. The representation is lossless exactly when this reconstruction reproduces every entry and declared symmetric structural pair of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric Hessian may be handed off through one triangle if the triangle convention and mappings reconstruct all values and structural pairs exactly.
assumptions_latex: The stored triangle and diagonal convention are unambiguous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat Q=Q\text{ and the decoded symmetric structural pattern equals the declared pattern of }Q.

notation.meaning: Hessian reconstructed by the receiving interface

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Triangular Sparse Handoff
Sparsity-Preserving Handoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation of structural zeros when exporting canonical QP matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q,A,G\) be canonical QP matrices, and define \(\operatorname{supp}(M)=\{(i,j):M_{ij}\ne0\}\). A modeling-to-solver handoff is sparsity-preserving when it transmits each matrix in a sparse format with explicit dimensions and index maps, and its decoded matrices \(\widehat Q,\widehat A,\widehat G\) satisfy \(\widehat Q=Q\), \(\widehat A=A\), \(\widehat G=G\), and \(\operatorname{supp}(\widehat M)=\operatorname{supp}(M)\) for \(M\in\{Q,A,G\}\). Symmetric triangular storage is permitted if decoding restores both the values and support of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A handoff preserves sparsity when decoding exactly restores every canonical matrix and its structural nonzero pattern, allowing documented triangular storage for symmetric matrices.
assumptions_latex: Canonical matrices have fixed row and column orderings.
Stored entries and dimensions are transmitted without numerical dropping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{supp}(\widehat M)=\operatorname{supp}(M)\) for every transmitted canonical matrix \(M\).

notation.meaning: index set of nonzero entries of M
matrix decoded by the solver interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf, but the cited sparsity section does not yet establish this modeling-to-solver interface definition. Moreover, the record defines support by numerical nonzeros while describing it as a structural nonzero pattern; those notions can differ when explicitly stored zeros are allowed. A source defining the intended sparse handoff semantics is needed before choosing the reliable formulation.

children.title: Block-Structure-Preserving Handoffs
children.top_down_role: Transfer of block, stage, or band metadata into solver interfaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation of declared variable, equality-row, and inequality-row block structure under solver-facing permutations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal I=(I_1,\ldots,I_k)\), \(\mathcal J^=(J^=_1,\ldots,J^=_u)\), and \(\mathcal J^{\le}=(J^{\le}_1,\ldots,J^{\le}_v)\) be partitions of variable, equality-row, and inequality-row indices. A handoff preserves block structure when it exports these partitions together with bijective maps \(P_x,P_=,P_{\le}\) such that decoding the solver matrices \((\widehat Q,\widehat A,\widehat G)\) gives \(Q=P_x^{\mathsf T}\widehat QP_x\), \(A=P_=^{\mathsf T}\widehat AP_x\), and \(G=P_{\le}^{\mathsf T}\widehat GP_x\). Consequently every declared zero, diagonal, block-diagonal, or coupling submatrix is recoverable exactly. Storage sparsity alone does not preserve semantic block identity unless these partitions and maps are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block handoff is structure-preserving exactly when separate variable, equality-row, and inequality-row partitions can be recovered through exported bijective maps and reproduce all matrix blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal I\), \(\mathcal J^=\), and \(\mathcal J^{\le}\) are explicit disjoint exhaustive partitions.
\(P_x\), \(P_=\), and \(P_{\le}\) are permutation matrices or equivalent bijective index maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q=P_x^{\mathsf T}\widehat QP_x,\quad A=P_=^{\mathsf T}\widehat AP_x,\quad G=P_{\le}^{\mathsf T}\widehat GP_x.

notation.meaning: export-to-original index maps represented as permutations

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Recoverable Block Handoff
Block-Structure-Preserving Handoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation of declared variable and constraint partitions in canonical QP export.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal I=(I_1,\ldots,I_p)\) partition variable indices and \(\mathcal J=(J_1,\ldots,J_q)\) partition constraint rows. A canonical QP handoff preserves block structure when it exports these partitions and index maps such that decoded blocks obey \(\widehat Q_{I_iI_k}=Q_{I_iI_k}\) and \(\widehat A_{J_jI_i}=A_{J_jI_i}\) for all applicable indices, with the analogous identity for \(G\). Consequently, a block declared zero, diagonal, or uncoupled before export has the same property after decoding; permutations are allowed only when the exported maps recover the original partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block structure is preserved when exported partitions and index maps let the solver recover every matrix block and every declared coupling pattern exactly.
assumptions_latex: Variable blocks and constraint-row blocks form explicit partitions.
The handoff exports bijective index maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat Q_{I_iI_k}=Q_{I_iI_k}\) and \(\widehat A_{J_jI_i}=A_{J_jI_i}\) for every declared block.

notation.meaning: submatrix of M indexed by rows U and columns V

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the leaf, but the cited general sparsity section does not yet support the stated interface contract. The row partition is applied explicitly to A while the analogous partition for G is left unspecified, so the exact block-preservation predicate also requires clarification from an authoritative source.

children.title: Structure-Loss Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Canonicalization or export paths that obscure exploitable structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Loss Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operations that preserve model equivalence but can destroy exploitable matrix structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Structural preservation is not implied by algebraic equivalence. For example, let \(Q=I_n\) and apply an invertible change of variables \(x=Ty\). The transformed Hessian is \(T^{\mathsf T}QT=T^{\mathsf T}T\), which is generally dense when \(T\) is dense, although the two quadratic objectives are equivalent under the substitution. Likewise, eliminating variables by a Schur complement can create fill-in. Thus a handoff crosses a structure-loss boundary whenever its substitutions, eliminations, permutations without recoverable maps, or explicit zero dropping fail to preserve the declared sparsity or block invariants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent reformulations can lose exploitable structure: dense coordinate changes or eliminations may create fill-in even though they preserve the optimization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is invertible and dense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T^{\mathsf T}QT=T^{\mathsf T}T\) may be dense despite \(Q\) being diagonal.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Audit certificate for preservation of declared computational structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given declared invariants consisting of dimensions, sparsity patterns, variable and constraint permutations, block partitions, and provenance maps, an export is structure-auditable when decoding followed by the supplied inverse maps reproduces every declared invariant. Failure of any equality certifies structure loss even if the decoded optimization problem is algebraically equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An export preserves declared structure only when its decoded data and inverse maps reproduce every declared sparsity, ordering, partition, and provenance invariant.
assumptions_latex: The invariants to be preserved are declared before export.
Every permitted transformation has a supplied reconstruction map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal I(\operatorname{reconstruct}(\operatorname{decode}(E)))=\mathcal I(\text{canonical model})
knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Invariant Export Audit

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of row provenance despite preservation of the represented model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let original constraint rows be indexed by \(R\), and suppose an export supplies aggregated data \((\bar A,\bar b)=(WA,Wb)\). Even when the aggregation preserves the feasible set of the particular model, the original row identities and block ownership are not recoverable in general unless the handoff also supplies \(W\) and sufficient reconstruction metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint aggregation may preserve a feasible set while erasing row identities and block ownership unless reconstruction metadata is retained.
assumptions_latex: Structural meaning is attached to original row identities or blocks.
No reconstruction-equivalent provenance metadata is transmitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\bar A,\bar b)\not\Rightarrow(A,b,\text{original row partition})\quad\text{in general}.
knowledge_statements.title: Irrecoverable Provenance Loss Under Aggregation

children.title: Solver-Status Handoffs
children.top_down_role: Transfer of termination categories plus solver outcome metadata.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Portable transfer of backend termination information without prescribing universal status names.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A solver-status handoff consists of a normalized outcome class, the original backend status, termination-cause metadata, and a documented mapping. The mapping may assert a mathematical outcome—optimality to a declared tolerance, primal infeasibility, or unboundedness—only when the associated point or certificate predicate is satisfied. Operational outcomes such as interruption, resource limit, iteration limit, and numerical failure must preserve their uncertainty and must not be mapped to a mathematical outcome without supporting evidence. Distinct backend statuses may share a normalized class only if no mathematical information required by downstream consumers is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map backend statuses through documented semantics, preserve operational uncertainty and termination causes, and attach mathematical outcomes only when supporting result fields validate them.
assumptions_latex: The result refers to the same canonical QP submitted to the backend.
The backend status meanings and mapping table are documented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{normalized\ mathematical\ outcome}\ \Longrightarrow\ \operatorname{supporting\ predicate\ verified}.
knowledge_statements.title: Semantics-Preserving Solver-Status Mapping
Solver-Status Handoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic conditions for transferring terminal convex-QP solver statuses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex QP result, a status handoff is semantically valid only when its status belongs to a documented finite set and its accompanying fields satisfy the status predicate. An \(\mathrm{optimal}\) status requires a returned primal-dual point meeting the stated optimality tolerances; \(\mathrm{primal\_infeasible}\) requires a verifiable infeasibility certificate; \(\mathrm{dual\_infeasible}\) or \(\mathrm{unbounded}\) requires a documented recession certificate; and \(\mathrm{unknown}\) makes no mathematical claim. Implementation-specific statuses must be mapped explicitly rather than silently identified with these mathematical outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transferred solver status is valid only when documented semantics and the accompanying solution or certificate fields support the claimed outcome.
assumptions_latex: The handed-off model is the same canonical QP solved by the backend.
Status meanings and tolerances are documented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{status}\text{ is accepted}\Rightarrow\mathrm{associated\ status\ predicate\ holds}.\)

notation.meaning: normalized terminal outcome reported by the solver interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the status-handoff leaf, but the normalized vocabulary and the predicates attached to dual infeasibility, unboundedness, and unknown are interface-dependent and uncited. A specific authoritative result-schema or solver-status specification is required.

children.title: Accuracy Handoffs
children.top_down_role: Transfer of residual, tolerance, plus solution-quality metadata.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Portable transmission of approximate convex-QP accuracy without imposing a solver-specific norm or scaling convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{s\times n}\), and a reported tuple \((x,y,z)\) with \(z\ge0\), define \(e_{\rm eq}=Ax-b\), \(e_{\rm ineq}=(Gx-h)_+\), \(e_{\rm stat}=Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z\), and either componentwise complementarity \(e_{{\rm comp},i}=z_i(h_i-(Gx)_i)\) or its aggregate. An accuracy handoff is interpretable only when it transmits the chosen norms, absolute or relative scaling denominators, aggregation rule, and tolerances. Each reported accuracy claim is valid only if recomputation from the canonical data under those transmitted conventions satisfies its stated bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accuracy metadata must declare its residual formulas, norms, scaling, aggregation, and tolerances, and every claimed bound must be reproducible from the canonical model and returned vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(G\in\mathbb R^{s\times n}\).
The inequality convention is \(Gx\le h\) with \(z\ge0\).
Every relative scaling denominator is positive or has a documented zero-scale fallback.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{reported\ accuracy}=\operatorname{recomputed\ accuracy}\quad\text{under the transmitted convention}.

notation.meaning: componentwise or declared aggregate complementarity residual

knowledge_statements.title: Declared Accuracy-Measure Handoff
Accuracy Handoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware residual fields for approximate convex-QP solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), an accuracy handoff for primal-dual data \((x,y,z)\) must state its norms, scaling, and tolerances. With \(z\ge0\), define \(r_p=(Ax-b,(Gx-h)_+)\), \(r_d=Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z\), and \(r_c=z^{\mathsf T}(h-Gx)\). A claim of tolerance \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_c)\) is consistent only if \(\lVert r_p\rVert\le\varepsilon_p\), \(\lVert r_d\rVert\le\varepsilon_d\), and \(|r_c|\le\varepsilon_c\), under the transmitted convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accuracy fields must identify norms, scaling, and tolerances and must agree with recomputed primal, dual, and complementarity residuals.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier convention is \(z\ge0\) for \(Gx\le h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert r_p\rVert\le\varepsilon_p,\ \lVert r_d\rVert\le\varepsilon_d,\ |r_c|\le\varepsilon_c\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the accuracy-handoff leaf, and the displayed sign convention is internally coherent. However, norms, scaling, aggregation of equality and inequality residuals, and complementarity accuracy are precisely the convention-dependent parts of the claim and have no cited source. Matrix and vector domains are also omitted.

children.title: Certificate Handoffs
children.top_down_role: Transfer of optimality or failure certificate artifacts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transport contract for optimality, primal-infeasibility, and unboundedness artifacts; the underlying certificate theorems remain in their canonical mathematical topics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For canonical data \((Q,c,A,b,G,h)\) with \(Q\succeq0\), a certificate handoff must identify its type, sign convention, index maps, exact or approximate interpretation, and verification tolerances. An optimality artifact carries \((x,y,z)\) with \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), \(z\ge0\), \(Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0\), and \(z_i(Gx-h)_i=0\). A primal-infeasibility artifact carries \((y,z)\) with \(z\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}y+h^{\mathsf T}z<0\). An unboundedness artifact carries a feasible base point \(x_0\) and direction \(d\) with \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), \(Qd=0\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\). Acceptance requires successful verification against the same canonical model after decoding all maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transmit a typed, convention-complete artifact and accept it only after verifying the appropriate KKT, Farkas, or recession-ray predicates against the handed-off model.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(G\in\mathbb R^{s\times n}\).
Inequalities use \(Gx\le h\) and nonnegative multipliers.
For the unboundedness artifact, \(x_0\) satisfies \(Ax_0=b\) and \(Gx_0\le h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{verify}(\operatorname{type},\operatorname{artifact},Q,c,A,b,G,h)=\mathrm{true}\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{the artifact supports its declared mathematical outcome}.

notation.meaning: feasible base point for a recession ray

knowledge_statements.title: Typed Convex-QP Certificate Handoff
Certificate Handoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Self-contained optimality certificate transferred with a convex-QP result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex QP \(\min \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), a handed-off tuple \((x,y,z)\) with \(z\ge0\) is an exact optimality certificate when \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), \(Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0\), and \(z_i(Gx-h)_i=0\) for every inequality index \(i\). Under convexity, these primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity relations certify that \(x\) is globally optimal. An approximate certificate must additionally transmit its norm and tolerance conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual tuple certifies global optimality when it satisfies convex-QP feasibility, stationarity, nonnegative multipliers, and complementarity under a consistent sign convention.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is nonempty and the displayed multipliers exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y,z)\text{ satisfies the displayed KKT relations}\Rightarrow x\text{ is globally optimal}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the leaf, and the displayed KKT relations are sufficient for global optimality of a convex QP under the stated sign convention. Constraint qualification is not needed for this sufficiency direction, but an authoritative KKT source and explicit data domains are still required.

children.title: Cross-Field Consistency Checks
children.top_down_role: Consistency checks across status, accuracy, plus certificate fields.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite validation of relationships among status, primal-dual vectors, objective values, accuracy metadata, certificates, and index maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Decode every result field into the canonical model ordering and first verify its dimensions. Recompute any reported objective value as \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\), recompute every claimed residual under its transmitted convention, and verify every certificate according to its declared type. A mathematical-outcome status is accepted only when its required point or certificate is present and valid. Mutually contradictory mathematical claims—such as a verified finite optimum together with verified unboundedness for the same model—must be rejected. Interruption, iteration-limit, and numerical-failure outcomes make no unsupported optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness claim. Optional diagnostic fields may be retained but cannot override failed mathematical predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decode and dimension-check all fields, recompute values and residuals, verify typed certificates, and reject unsupported or contradictory status-field combinations.
assumptions_latex: All fields identify the same canonical model instance.
Index maps and all approximate-comparison conventions are available.
The status handoff documents which mathematical predicate, if any, it claims.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{accept}(R)\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{all populated mathematical fields of result }R\text{ are dimensionally and logically compatible}.

notation.meaning: constant term of the canonical objective

knowledge_statements.title: Schema-Neutral Cross-Field Validation
Cross-Field Consistency Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical and numerical validation across status, accuracy, solution, and certificate fields.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex-QP result record is cross-field consistent when every populated field is dimensionally valid and all claimed implications can be recomputed from the canonical data. In particular, \(\mathrm{optimal}\) requires a primal vector and residuals within the reported tolerances; an infeasibility or unboundedness status requires its corresponding certificate and must not simultaneously claim a finite optimal point; reported objective value \(v\) must satisfy \(v=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+r\) within its stated tolerance; and all primal-dual vectors must conform to the variable and constraint index maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate dimensions, recompute objective and residuals, and reject contradictory combinations of statuses, solutions, tolerances, and certificates.
assumptions_latex: Canonical model data and index maps accompany the result.
Every approximate comparison has a declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{accepted\ result}\Rightarrow\mathrm{status,\ value,\ residual,\ dimension,\ and\ certificate\ predicates\ are jointly satisfied}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the cross-field-check leaf, but the accepted status implications, certificate requirements, exclusivity rules, and tolerance semantics depend on a result schema that is not cited. A specific authoritative interface specification is required.

children.top_down_role: Complexity distinctions and boundaries at which a nominal convex QP becomes invalid, ambiguous, unstable, or computationally misleading.
