children.title: Polynomial-Time Convex QP Solvability
children.top_down_role: Ellipsoid and interior-point complexity routes under finite-dimensional data encodings.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unambiguous bit-complexity statement for a nonempty bounded rational feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let rational binary-encoded data define \[\min\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\},\qquad Q\succeq0,\] and suppose the feasible polyhedron is nonempty and bounded. In the Turing model, an ellipsoid-based convex-optimization algorithm can return a feasible \(x_\varepsilon\) satisfying \(f(x_\varepsilon)\le f^*+\varepsilon\) using bit complexity polynomial in the dimensions, total input length \(L\), and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\). Feasibility of the rational affine system is separately decidable by polynomial-time linear programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A promised-feasible bounded rational convex QP can be solved to additive objective accuracy in polynomial bit complexity; affine feasibility is a separate polynomial-time problem.
assumptions_latex: All data are rational and binary encoded.
The feasible polyhedron is nonempty and bounded.
\(\varepsilon>0\) is the requested additive objective accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T=\operatorname{poly}(n,m,L,\log(1/\varepsilon)).
knowledge_statements.title: Promised-Feasible Rational Convex-QP Approximation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary of ordinary bit-complexity tractability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A running-time bound polynomial in binary input length \(L\) and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) is a Turing bit-complexity guarantee. It does not establish strong polynomiality, which additionally requires an arithmetic-operation count polynomial in the dimensions independently of coefficient magnitudes and polynomially bounded intermediate encoding lengths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bit-polynomial convex-QP solvability does not by itself imply a strongly polynomial algorithm.
assumptions_latex: Complexity is measured for binary-encoded rational data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{poly}(n,m,L,\log(1/\varepsilon))\not\Rightarrow\text{strong polynomiality}.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak versus Strong Polynomiality Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ellipsoid-compatible representation of rational convex-QP optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succeq0\), introduce \(t\) and \[E=\{(x,t):Ax=b,\ Gx\le h,\ f(x)\le t\}.\] Violated affine constraints separate directly. If \(f(\bar x)>\bar t\), then \[f(\bar x)+\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\le t\] is valid for \(E\) and violated by \((\bar x,\bar t)\). Together with polynomially encoded search bounds, this supplies the separation route used by ellipsoid optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex quadratic epigraph has an explicit separation oracle, giving the standard ellipsoid route to polynomial approximation.
assumptions_latex: Coefficients and query points are rationally represented.
Polynomially encoded bounds on the relevant search region are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Convex-QP approximation reduces to polynomially many polynomial-time separation calls.}
knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Separation Route
Polynomial-Time Convex QP Solvability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-complexity statement for rational convex QPs under standard finite encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a convex quadratic program with rational data \((Q,c,A,b,G,h)\), where \(Q\succeq0\), encoded in binary with total length \(L\). Under the standard Turing bit model and a bounded rational polyhedral feasible region, an ellipsoid or polynomial-time interior-point method can compute an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal feasible solution, or decide the applicable feasibility alternative, using a number of bit operations polynomial in the dimensions, \(L\), and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\). Here \(\varepsilon\)-optimal means that the returned feasible objective value is at most \(\varepsilon\) above the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational convex QP with bounded polyhedral feasible region can be solved to additive accuracy in time polynomial in encoding size, dimensions, and log inverse accuracy.
assumptions_latex: All problem data are rational and binary encoded with length \(L\).
\(Q\succeq0\) and the feasible polyhedron is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T=\operatorname{poly}(n,m,L,\log(1/\varepsilon))\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind matches the exact leaf, but the bit-complexity claim needs an authoritative theorem with an exact locator. The phrase 'applicable feasibility alternative' is not defined, and the treatment of infeasibility, weak feasibility, encoding growth, and the selected ellipsoid or interior-point route cannot be validated without that source.

children.title: Special Structured QP Complexity Classes
children.top_down_role: Separable, bounded-variable, network, and other structure-restricted subclasses.

assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(q_1,\ldots,q_n)\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and \(q_i\ge0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
The unit-cost real-arithmetic model is used for the operation count.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{the problem is solvable using }O(n)\text{ scalar arithmetic and comparison operations}.\)

notation.meaning: an optimal value of coordinate i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic complexity of separable box-constrained convex quadratic programs.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(q_1,\ldots,q_n)\) and independent bounds \(\ell_i\le x_i\le u_i\), the problem decomposes as \[\min_{\ell\le x\le u}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x=\sum_{i=1}^n\min_{\ell_i\le t\le u_i}\left(\tfrac12q_it^2+c_it\right).\] If \(q_i>0\), then \(x_i^*=\min\{u_i,\max\{\ell_i,-c_i/q_i\}\}\). If \(q_i=0\), choose \(x_i^*=\ell_i\) when \(c_i>0\), choose \(x_i^*=u_i\) when \(c_i<0\), and choose any \(x_i^*\in[\ell_i,u_i]\) when \(c_i=0\). Hence an optimizer is computed with \(O(n)\) scalar arithmetic and comparison operations in the unit-cost real-arithmetic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagonal convex quadratic objective with only variable bounds decomposes into independent scalar problems, yielding an optimizer in linear arithmetic time by clipping each unconstrained minimizer or selecting an endpoint.
knowledge_statements.title: Special Structured QP Complexity Classes

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 General Problem Statement and Special Model Forms p. 3

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictly convex separable box QP with one coupling equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{\ell\le x\le u}\sum_{i=1}^n\left(\tfrac12q_ix_i^2+c_ix_i\right)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad\sum_{i=1}^n a_ix_i=b,\qquad q_i>0.\] For multiplier \(\lambda\), define \[x_i(\lambda)=\Pi_{[\ell_i,u_i]}\!\left(-\frac{c_i+\lambda a_i}{q_i}\right),\qquad \phi(\lambda)=\sum_i a_ix_i(\lambda).\] The function \(\phi\) is continuous and nonincreasing. If the equality is feasible, any root \(\phi(\lambda)=b\) yields the unique optimizer. Given a root bracket, bisection localizes a root interval to width \(\delta\) in \(O(n\log((\lambda_U-\lambda_L)/\delta))\) arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly convex diagonal box QP with one resource equality reduces to a scalar monotone multiplier equation.
assumptions_latex: The box and resource equality have a common feasible point.
\([\lambda_L,\lambda_U]\) brackets a root for the stated bisection bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi(\lambda^*)=b\Longrightarrow x(\lambda^*)\text{ is the unique optimizer.}

notation.meaning: Aggregate resource use at a multiplier.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Quadratic Resource-Allocation Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity reduction for a Cartesian product of independent QP blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(Q_1,\ldots,Q_p)\), \(c=(c_1,\ldots,c_p)\), and the feasible set is \(X_1\times\cdots\times X_p\), then the QP decomposes into \(p\) independent block minimizations. If block \(i\) requires work \(T_i\), serial work is \(\sum_iT_i\), while ideal unlimited-resource parallel depth is \(\max_iT_i\). A cross-block Hessian term or constraint destroys this independent decomposition in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Cartesian block-separable QP has additive serial work and ideal parallel depth determined by its hardest block.
assumptions_latex: There are no cross-block objective terms or constraints.
The parallel-depth statement ignores communication and scheduling overhead.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{serial}}=\sum_iT_i,\qquad T_{\mathrm{parallel}}=\max_iT_i\text{ under ideal concurrency.}
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Block Complexity Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Network-structured equality-constrained quadratic subclass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be a node-arc incidence matrix and \(D\succ0\) diagonal. For \[\min_x\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Dx+c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{s.t.}\quad Bx=d,\] KKT elimination gives \[(BD^{-1}B^{\mathsf T})y=-(d+BD^{-1}c),\qquad x=-D^{-1}(c+B^{\mathsf T}y).\] The coefficient is a weighted graph Laplacian. Removing one redundant conservation equation or fixing one dual gauge per connected component makes the relevant dual system nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable quadratic network-flow equality model reduces to a weighted graph-Laplacian solve.
assumptions_latex: One dual gauge per connected component is fixed when necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The network QP is solved by a weighted Laplacian system followed by diagonal recovery.}
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Network-Flow Laplacian Reduction

children.title: Practical QP Complexity Drivers
children.top_down_role: Dimension, sparsity, fill, conditioning, accuracy, and active-set combinatorics.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dimensions Alone Do Not Determine Practical Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary against treating nominal QP dimensions as a runtime predictor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two convex QPs with identical numbers of variables and constraints can induce different factor fill, conditioning, active-set sequences, and attainable accuracy. Therefore no solver-independent practical runtime or memory prediction follows from \((n,m_e,m_i)\) alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal QP dimensions do not imply equal practical runtime, memory use, or numerical difficulty.
assumptions_latex: Solver implementation, sparsity pattern, numerical values, and stopping requirements are allowed to differ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (n,m_e,m_i)\text{ alone is not a complete practical-complexity descriptor.}
knowledge_statements.title: Dimensions Alone Do Not Determine Practical Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Practical decomposition of total solver work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a QP algorithm performs \(k\) major iterations with linear-algebra work \(C_j\) and auxiliary or update work \(U_j\), then \[T=\sum_{j=1}^k(C_j+U_j).\] Dimensions, sparsity, ordering, and fill principally influence \(C_j\); scaling, conditioning, requested tolerance, globalization, degeneracy, and working-set changes can influence \(k\) and \(U_j\). Neither iteration count nor one factorization cost alone is a complete practical complexity measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Practical runtime combines per-iteration linear algebra with the number and type of iterations.
assumptions_latex: Work is measured for a specified implementation, numerical environment, and stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A practical assessment must account for both iteration behavior and per-iteration cost.}

notation.meaning: Linear-algebra and auxiliary work at iteration j.

knowledge_statements.title: Per-Iteration Cost versus Iteration-Count Separation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditioning Converts Residual Error into Solution Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative explanation of conditioning as a practical linear-solve driver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular KKT or reduced system \(Kz=r\) and approximation \(\widehat z\), set \(e=\widehat z-z\) and \(\rho=r-K\widehat z\). Then \[e=-K^{-1}\rho,\qquad \frac{\|e\|}{\|z\|}\le\kappa(K)\frac{\|\rho\|}{\|r\|}\] when \(r,z\ne0\), where \(\kappa(K)=\|K\|\|K^{-1}\|\). Hence the same relative residual can correspond to very different forward errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The condition number amplifies residual error into error in a computed QP step.
assumptions_latex: A consistent subordinate norm is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Relative forward error is bounded by }\kappa(K)\text{ times relative residual.}

notation.meaning: Normwise condition number of the solved system.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Converts Residual Error into Solution Error

assumptions_latex: A numerical method targets primal-dual residual tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Practical time and memory depend on KKT-system dimensions, sparsity and fill, numerical conditioning, requested accuracy, and active-set changes.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct linear algebra identifies KKT dimensions, sparsity, fill, and conditioning as numerical cost drivers
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Practical drivers for sparse direct interior-point and active-set implementations, not a universal worst-case bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex QP \(\min_x \tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\). In a direct primal-dual implementation, each major iteration factors or updates a KKT matrix whose order is governed by \(n\), \(m_e\), and the currently represented inequalities. Its arithmetic and storage costs depend on the nonzero pattern and elimination fill, while attainable accuracy and iteration behavior depend on scaling, conditioning, and \(\varepsilon\). For active-set methods, the number and sequence of working-set changes add a combinatorial driver not determined by dimensions alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: QP runtime and memory are driven by dimensions, sparse-factorization fill, conditioning, requested accuracy, and, for active-set methods, the sequence of working-set changes.
knowledge_statements.title: Practical QP Complexity Drivers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and scope fit the terminal container, and the statement is appropriately implementation-specific rather than a worst-case bound. Its claims about factorization cost, fill, conditioning, iteration behavior, and active-set changes require an inspectable numerical-QP source.

knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite Quadratic-Objective Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes ambient nonconvexity from convexity after restriction to the feasible affine hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x\), where \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), and let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron. A negative eigenvalue of \(Q\) makes \(f\) nonconvex on \(\mathbb R^n\), so minimizing it over a polyhedron is not in general a convex QP. Let \(L=\operatorname{span}(F-F)\), the direction space of \(\operatorname{aff}(F)\). The restriction of \(f\) to \(F\) is convex if and only if \(d^\top Qd\ge0\) for every \(d\in L\). Thus ambient indefiniteness crosses the convex-QP boundary unless the feasible affine geometry excludes every negative-curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indefinite Hessian makes the objective nonconvex in the ambient space, but the restricted problem is convex exactly when the Hessian is positive semidefinite on the direction space of the feasible affine hull.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) has at least one negative eigenvalue
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ambient indefiniteness lies outside the convex-QP model class unless \(d^\top Qd\ge0\) for every direction \(d\in\operatorname{span}(F-F)\).

notation.meaning: Direction space of the feasible affine hull

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Large Scale Indefinite Quadratic Problems p. 247

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative Curvature Need Not Imply Unboundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates departure from convex-QP objective curvature from unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The problem \[\min_{-1\le x\le1}-\tfrac12x^2\] has negative objective curvature and is nonconvex as a minimization problem, yet its compact feasible interval gives the finite attained optimum \(-1/2\) at \(x=\pm1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Crossing the convex-QP boundary through negative curvature does not imply unboundedness when the feasible polyhedron is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{|x|\le1}-x^2/2=-1/2\quad\text{despite }Q=-1<0.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative Curvature Need Not Imply Unboundedness

assumptions_latex: Each quadratic constraint has symmetric Hessian \(P_i\in\mathbb S^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding a genuine quadratic constraint produces a QCQP; positive-semidefinite constraint Hessians preserve convexity but not the QP model class.

notation.meaning: Hessian of the ith quadratic constraint

review_flags: locator supports convex-set background; QCQP-specific source desirable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-class boundary between affine-constrained QPs and quadratically constrained quadratic programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint \(g_i(x)=\tfrac12x^\top P_i x+a_i^\top x-r_i\le0\) is genuinely quadratic when \(P_i\ne0\). Adding such a constraint to a quadratic-objective model yields a QCQP rather than an affine-constrained QP. If \(P_i\succeq0\) for every inequality, each set \(\{x:g_i(x)\le0\}\) is convex, so the resulting model can be a convex QCQP. If some relevant \(P_i\) is indefinite, its sublevel set can be nonconvex; convex-QP tractability then cannot be inferred from the objective Hessian alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A genuine quadratic constraint changes a QP into a QCQP. Positive-semidefinite constraint Hessians preserve convexity; indefinite ones can destroy it.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Constraint Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical relaxation relation at the discrete-decision boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_I\) be the feasible set of a minimization MIQP and let \(F_R\supseteq F_I\) result from dropping integrality while retaining all other constraints and the objective \(f\). Then \[v_R:=\inf_{x\in F_R}f(x)\le v_I:=\inf_{x\in F_I}f(x).\] If an attained relaxation optimizer \(x^R\) satisfies the original integrality restrictions, then \(x^R\in F_I\) and \(f(x^R)=v_R=v_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The continuous relaxation gives a lower bound, and an integral relaxation optimizer certifies exactness and global MIQP optimality.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
The relaxation optimum is attained for the exactness conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^R\in F_I\Longrightarrow f(x^R)=v_R=v_I.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Relaxation Bound and Exactness Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity boundary for the unrestricted convex-MIQP class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The class of mixed-integer QPs with \(Q\succeq0\) contains binary linear optimization: set \(Q=0\), impose affine constraints, and require \(x_j\in\{0,1\}\) for the binary variables. Therefore a polynomial-time algorithm for all such MIQPs would solve every binary linear optimization instance in polynomial time. The continuous convex-QP polynomial-time guarantee consequently does not extend to the unrestricted mixed-integer class unless \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex MIQP contains binary linear optimization, so unrestricted discrete decisions destroy the general continuous-QP tractability guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The number of integer variables is part of the input.
Standard binary encoding and the usual \(\mathrm{P}\ne\mathrm{NP}\) complexity distinction are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Unrestricted convex MIQP is NP-hard.}
knowledge_statements.title: Binary Linear Optimization Embedding

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Integrality Gap with Positive Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example showing that convex curvature does not make the continuous relaxation exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\min\{(x-\tfrac12)^2:x\in\{0,1\}\},\] the integer optimum is \(v_I=\tfrac14\). Dropping integrality gives \(0\le x\le1\), whose unique optimizer is \(x=\tfrac12\) with \(v_R=0\). The objective is strictly convex, yet the continuous relaxation has gap \(v_I-v_R=\tfrac14\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a one-variable strictly convex quadratic can have a strict integrality gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_R=0<\tfrac14=v_I.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Integrality Gap with Positive Curvature

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precise geometric boundary between continuous convex QPs and mixed-integer quadratic models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A model with affine constraints, \(Q\succeq0\), and genuine integer restrictions is an MIQP rather than a continuous convex QP. Whenever two feasible integer assignments have a strict convex combination that violates integrality, its feasible set is nonconvex. Thus “convex MIQP” describes objective curvature and its continuous relaxations, not convexity of the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-semidefinite objective curvature does not make a genuinely discrete feasible set convex.
assumptions_latex: At least one integrality restriction is genuine rather than redundant.
For the geometric nonconvexity conclusion, two feasible points have a strict convex combination that violates integrality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The original discrete model is outside continuous convex optimization even when }Q\succeq0.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Feasible-Set Boundary

assumptions_latex: At least one component of \(x\) is required to lie in \(\mathbb Z\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Integrality changes a convex continuous QP into an MIQP and removes the general continuous convex-QP tractability guarantee.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: setting Q=0 and imposing binary domains embeds binary linear optimization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates continuous convex QPs from mixed-integer quadratic optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x \tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x\) subject to affine constraints and \(x_j\in\mathbb Z\) for \(j\in I\ne\varnothing\). Even when \(Q\succeq0\), the feasible set is discrete in the indexed coordinates, so the model is a mixed-integer quadratic program rather than a convex QP. The subclass obtained by taking \(Q=0\), bounding integer variables by \(0\le x_j\le1\), and requiring integrality contains binary linear optimization. Consequently, polynomial-time guarantees for continuous convex QPs do not extend to this model class in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requiring any variable to be integer creates an MIQP; even with a convex objective, the class contains binary linear optimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Decision Boundary

children.title: Robust-QP Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundary between nominal convex QPs plus robust counterparts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary where a robust affine row becomes second-order conic rather than an ordinary affine QP row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal U=\{u:\|u\|_2\le1\}\), the robust constraint \[(a_0+Pu)^{\mathsf T}x\le b\quad\forall u\in\mathcal U\] is equivalent to \[a_0^{\mathsf T}x+\|P^{\mathsf T}x\|_2\le b.\] Unless the norm term reduces to an affine function on the declared domain, this is a second-order-cone constraint rather than an affine constraint of an ordinary QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Euclidean-ball uncertainty in an affine row generally produces an exact SOC robust counterpart, leaving the ordinary-QP class while preserving convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{\|u\|_2\le1}(a_0+Pu)^{\mathsf T}x=a_0^{\mathsf T}x+\|P^{\mathsf T}x\|_2.
knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoidal Affine-Uncertainty Conic Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex-QP-preserving robust counterpart for affine constraints over a finitely generated polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U=\operatorname{conv}\{u^1,\ldots,u^N\}\), \(a(u)=a_0+Au\), and \(b(u)=b_0+d^{\mathsf T}u\). Then \[a(u)^{\mathsf T}x\le b(u)\quad\forall u\in\mathcal U\] is equivalent to \[a(u^j)^{\mathsf T}x\le b(u^j),\qquad j=1,\ldots,N.\] Hence a fixed positive-semidefinite quadratic objective and finitely many such robust rows have an exact finite convex-QP counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine uncertainty over a polytope given by finitely many vertices reduces exactly to constraints at those vertices and preserves the finite convex-QP class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall u\in\mathcal U:\ a(u)^{\mathsf T}x\le b(u)\iff a(u^j)^{\mathsf T}x\le b(u^j)\ \forall j.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Vertex Robust Affine Counterpart

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite affine robust counterpart obtained by LP duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal U=\{u:Fu\le g\} be nonempty and bounded. The robust row (a_0+Pu)^{\mathsf T}x\le b for every u\in\mathcal U is equivalent to the existence of \eta\ge0 satisfying F^{\mathsf T}\eta=P^{\mathsf T}x and a_0^{\mathsf T}x+g^{\mathsf T}\eta\le b. Thus finitely many such rows with a fixed PSD quadratic objective form a finite convex QP in the extended variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LP duality converts bounded polyhedral affine uncertainty into auxiliary multipliers and finitely many affine constraints.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal U=\{u:Fu\le g\}\text{ is nonempty and bounded}.
The uncertain row is affine in u.
The objective Hessian is fixed and positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{u:Fu\le g}u^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}x=\min_{\eta\ge0}\{g^{\mathsf T}\eta:F^{\mathsf T}\eta=P^{\mathsf T}x\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral-Uncertainty Support-Function Dual

assumptions_latex: Uncertainty ranges over a specified set \(\mathcal U\)
Constraints must hold for every \(u\in\mathcal U\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A robust QP is generally a quantified optimization problem, and it is a finite convex QP only when its robust counterpart admits an affine finite reformulation.

notation.meaning: Constraint data at uncertainty realization u

review_flags: source treats uncertainty broadly; robust-counterpart source required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary induced by universal uncertainty quantification and robust-counterpart reformulation.

source_refs.locator: 3.5 Decision Making under Uncertainty: Stochastic Model Forms p. 191

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The robust model \(\min_x \sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\{\tfrac12x^\top Q(u)x+q(u)^\top x	ext{ when applicable}\}\) with constraints \(G(u)x\le h(u)\) for all \(u\in\mathcal U\) is not merely a QP with fixed coefficients. It belongs to the finite convex-QP class only if the universal constraints and objective reduce exactly to finitely many affine constraints and a positive-semidefinite quadratic objective in the chosen variables. Otherwise its robust counterpart may be conic, nonsmooth, semi-infinite, or nonconvex, depending on \(\mathcal U\) and the data dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Universal protection against uncertainty is a robust optimization model, becoming a finite convex QP only under an exact affine-quadratic reformulation.

assumptions_latex: At least one coefficient depends on an unresolved parameter \(u\in\mathcal U\)
No realization, probability law, scenario rule, or robust quantifier has been selected

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D(u)=(Q(u),q(u),A(u),b(u),G(u),h(u))\) denote QP data indexed by \(u\in\mathcal U\). Before specifying whether \(u\) is observed, sampled, probabilistically distributed, adversarially selected, or universally quantified, \(D(u)\) defines a family of optimization problems rather than a single deterministic QP. A deterministic model is obtained only after choosing semantics and eliminating or instantiating \(u\). That operation may preserve a convex quadratic objective with affine constraints, but it may instead introduce expectations, maxima, additional constraints, or nonconvex dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficients depending on an unresolved uncertain parameter define a family of QPs until a realization, scenario, stochastic, or robust interpretation is chosen.

children.title: Scenario-Based Reformulation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Transition to finite-scenario representations of uncertain QP data.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Based Reformulation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario deterministic equivalent with one shared continuous decision vector and affine scenario constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be finite and let the shared decision be \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). For each \(s\in S\), let \(p_s\ge0\), \(Q_s\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(q_s\in\mathbb R^n\), \(G_s\in\mathbb R^{m_s\times n}\), and \(h_s\in\mathbb R^{m_s}\), with \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\). The objective \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s(\tfrac12x^\top Q_sx+q_s^\top x)\), together with \(G_sx\le h_s\) for every \(s\in S\), is the deterministic QP having \(\bar Q=\sum_{s\in S}p_sQ_s\), \(\bar q=\sum_{s\in S}p_sq_s\), and vertically stacked inequalities \(\bar Gx\le\bar h\). Because \(\bar Q\succeq0\), this QP is convex. Scenario constructions involving integer decisions, genuinely quadratic constraints, nonlinear recourse, or infinitely many scenarios do not in general admit this ordinary finite-QP representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite weighted convex-quadratic scenarios with a shared continuous decision and affine scenario constraints aggregate and stack into one deterministic convex QP; richer or infinite scenario constructions generally require another model class.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) is shared by all scenarios

children.title: Infeasible QP Models

assumptions_latex: The QP has constraints \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The QP is infeasible exactly when its affine constraint system has a Farkas certificate.

notation.meaning: Farkas multipliers for equalities and inequalities

review_flags: locator is broader than the stated affine Farkas alternative
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infeasibility of an affine-constrained QP is independent of its objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\). The QP is infeasible precisely when \(F=\varnothing\), irrespective of its quadratic objective. For this affine system, infeasibility is equivalent to the existence of \(y\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\) and \(z\in\mathbb R_+^{m_i}\) satisfying \(A^\top y+G^\top z=0\) and \(b^\top y+h^\top z<0\). Such \((y,z)\) is a directly checkable Farkas certificate that no point can satisfy all equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A QP is infeasible when its affine feasible set is empty; Farkas multipliers provide a finite certificate independent of the objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible QP Models

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Phase-I Feasibility Test for Affine QP Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-independent auxiliary linear program deciding feasibility of the affine QP constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\), solve
\[\rho^*=\min_{x,s^+,s^-,r}\ \mathbf 1^\top(s^++s^-)+\mathbf 1^\top r\quad\text{s.t.}\quad Ax-b=s^+-s^-,\quad Gx-h\le r,\quad s^+,s^-,r\ge0.\]
This linear program is feasible and attains its finite optimum. Moreover, \(\rho^*=0\) if and only if \(F\ne\varnothing\), while \(\rho^*>0\) if and only if the QP is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing aggregate affine-constraint violation gives value zero exactly for feasible QP constraints and a positive value exactly for infeasible constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F=\varnothing\iff\rho^*>0,\qquad F\ne\varnothing\iff\rho^*=0.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative positive and negative equality violations.

children.title: Unbounded QP Models

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status definition for a feasible convex QP whose objective is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\ne\varnothing\) and \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x\), where \(Q\succeq0\). The QP is unbounded below precisely when
\[\inf_{x\in F}f(x)=-\infty.\]
This status requires feasibility; an empty feasible set is classified as infeasible rather than unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex QP is unbounded below when it has feasible points but its objective values have no finite lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\in F}f(x)=-\infty.

children.title: Infeasibility–Unboundedness Diagnostic Boundary

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility–Unboundedness Diagnostic Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates infeasibility from unboundedness below using their mutually different diagnostic certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\) and \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x\), where \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\). Infeasibility means \(F=\varnothing\); it is certified when \(y\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\) and \(z\in\mathbb R_+^{m_i}\) satisfy \(A^\top y+G^\top z=0\) and \(b^\top y+h^\top z<0\). Unboundedness below instead presupposes \(F\ne\varnothing\). It is certified by \(x_0\in F\) and a nonzero direction \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), \(Qd=0\), and \(q^\top d<0\). Therefore an infeasible QP is not classified as unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infeasibility means that no feasible point exists, whereas unboundedness below requires a feasible point and a recession direction along which the objective tends to minus infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m_e\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{m_i\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^{m_i}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Infeasibility is the condition \(F=\varnothing\), while unboundedness below requires \(F\ne\varnothing\) and a recession direction \(d\ne0\) with \(Qd=0\) and \(q^\top d<0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x\), and fix an optimum \(x^\star\in F\). For any \(y\in F\), set \(d=y-x^\star\). Then \(y\) is also optimal if and only if \(d^\top Qd=0\) and \((Qx^\star+q)^\top d=0\). Because \(Q\succeq0\), the first equality is equivalent to \(Qd=0\). Hence primal solutions are nonunique exactly when a nonzero feasible displacement from an optimum has both zero quadratic curvature and zero first-order objective change; the entire feasible segment between the two optima is optimal.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simultaneous Primal and Multiplier Multiplicity Example

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \min_{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^2}\tfrac12x_1^2 subject to x_1=0 and x_1=0. Its primal optimal set is \{(0,t):t\in\mathbb R\}. Coupled Primal-Dual Multiplicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicity of both projections of the KKT solution set for a convex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the convex quadratic program 
\[\min_x\ \tfrac12 x^\top Qx+c^\top x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\;Gx\le h,\]
with KKT solution set \(\mathcal K\) consisting of triples \((x,y,z)\) satisfying primal feasibility, \(z\ge0\), stationarity \(Qx+c+A^\top y+G^\top z=0\), and complementarity \(z_i(Gx-h)_i=0\) for every \(i\). Coupled primal-dual multiplicity occurs when
\[|\pi_x(\mathcal K)|>1\quad\text{and}\quad |\pi_{y,z}(\mathcal K)|>1.\]
Thus at least two primal optimizers and at least two dual-multiplier pairs occur among KKT solutions; the definition does not require every primal optimizer to be paired with every dual optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupled multiplicity means that the KKT solution set has more than one primal projection and more than one dual-multiplier projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\pi_x(\mathcal K)|>1\) and \(|\pi_{y,z}(\mathcal K)|>1\).

children.title: Dependent Constraints
children.top_down_role: Linear dependence within equality systems or candidate active sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp separation between local active-gradient dependence and global feasible-set redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In one dimension, consider \(x\le0\) and \(-x\le0\). Their common feasible set is \(\{0\}\), and both inequalities are active at \(x=0\). Their active gradients \(1\) and \(-1\) are linearly dependent. Nevertheless neither constraint is redundant: deleting the first yields \([0,\infty)\), while deleting the second yields \(( -\infty,0]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two opposite inequalities are dependent at their common active point, yet neither is globally redundant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}\begin{bmatrix}1\\-1\end{bmatrix}=1<2,\qquad F_{-1}\ne F,\qquad F_{-2}\ne F.
knowledge_statements.title: Dependence Does Not Imply Redundancy
Dependent Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear dependence among equality and active-inequality gradients at a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the constraint system \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), let \(I(x)=\{i:(Gx-h)_i=0\}\) at a feasible point \(x\), and form the active-constraint Jacobian
\[J(x)=\begin{bmatrix}A\\G_{I(x)}\end{bmatrix}.\]
The constraints active at \(x\) are dependent when \(J(x)\) does not have full row rank. Equivalently, there exist coefficients \(u\) and \(v\), not both zero, such that
\[A^\top u+G_{I(x)}^\top v=0.\]
This is a local property of the active representation; it need not imply that any represented constraint is globally redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active constraints are dependent when their gradients are linearly dependent, equivalently when the active-constraint Jacobian lacks full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}J(x)<\operatorname{rows}(J(x))\).

notation.meaning: index set of active inequalities at x
Jacobian containing equality and active-inequality rows

children.title: Redundant Constraints
children.top_down_role: Duplicated or implied restrictions that add no distinct feasible-set boundary.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Programming Redundancy Tests for Affine Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deletion tests for one affine inequality or equality in a QP constraint representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Bx\le d,\ Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\) denote the remaining constraints. An inequality \(g^{\mathsf T}x\le h\) is redundant exactly when \(\sup_{x\in P}g^{\mathsf T}x\le h\). An equality \(g^{\mathsf T}x=h\) is redundant exactly when both \(\sup_{x\in P}g^{\mathsf T}x\le h\) and \(\inf_{x\in P}g^{\mathsf T}x\ge h\). A feasible point violating the candidate constraint certifies nonredundancy; an unbounded relevant extremum also implies nonredundancy for finite \(h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize the candidate affine expression over the remaining constraints; one upper-bound test handles an inequality and matching upper and lower tests handle an equality.
assumptions_latex: The remaining set \(P\) is nonempty and is represented by affine equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g^{\mathsf T}x\le h\text{ redundant}\iff\sup_{x\in P}g^{\mathsf T}x\le h;\qquad g^{\mathsf T}x=h\text{ redundant}\iff\sup_{x\in P}g^{\mathsf T}x\le h\le\inf_{x\in P}g^{\mathsf T}x.

notation.meaning: polyhedron defined by the remaining constraints

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Programming Redundancy Tests for Affine Constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact multiplier certificates for redundancy relative to a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x:Bx\le d,\ Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\). The inequality \(g^{\mathsf T}x\le h\) is valid on \(P\), hence redundant when added to its description, if and only if there exist \(y\ge0\) and unrestricted \(z\) such that \[B^{\mathsf T}y+A^{\mathsf T}z=g,\qquad d^{\mathsf T}y+b^{\mathsf T}z\le h.\] An equality \(g^{\mathsf T}x=h\) is redundant exactly when certificates of this form exist for both \(g^{\mathsf T}x\le h\) and \(-g^{\mathsf T}x\le-h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A redundant affine inequality has a Farkas multiplier certificate; a redundant equality has certificates for both inequality orientations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g^{\mathsf T}x\le h\ \forall x\in P\iff\exists y\ge0,z:\ B^{\mathsf T}y+A^{\mathsf T}z=g,\ d^{\mathsf T}y+b^{\mathsf T}z\le h.

notation.meaning: polyhedron defined by the remaining constraints

This does not assert the same complexity for every global minimum-description problem.

A polynomial-time linear-programming method is used.

Redundant Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global redundancy defined by invariance of the QP feasible set after deleting a constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{x:Ax=b,\;Gx\le h\}\), and let \(F_{-j}\) be the feasible set obtained by deleting constraint \(j\) while retaining every other constraint. Constraint \(j\) is redundant precisely when
\[F_{-j}=F.\]
For an inequality \(g_j^\top x\le h_j\), this is equivalent to every point satisfying the remaining constraints also satisfying \(g_j^\top x\le h_j\). For an equality, deletion must likewise leave the feasible set unchanged. Redundancy concerns the represented feasible region and is independent of the quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is redundant when deleting it leaves the feasible set unchanged; this is stronger than mere dependence at one active point.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(F_{-j}\) are formed from the same constraint system except for constraint \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(j\) is redundant if and only if \(F_{-j}=F\).

children.title: Constraint Rank-Loss Consequences
children.top_down_role: Effects of deficient constraint rank on multipliers, factorization, or active-set identification.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier Affine Family under Rank Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier nonuniqueness caused directly by a null direction of the active Jacobian transpose.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x,\lambda)\) satisfy the equality or unrestricted fixed-working-set stationarity equation \(Qx+c+J^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\). If \(v\ne0\) lies in \(\ker(J^{\mathsf T})\), then \((x,\lambda+t v)\) satisfies the same stationarity equation for every \(t\in\mathbb R\). For inequality KKT multipliers, only values of \(t\) preserving nonnegativity are admissible, so rank loss alone need not produce two feasible inequality-multiplier vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A left-null vector of the active Jacobian generates an affine family of unrestricted multipliers; inequality signs can truncate that family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Qx+c+J^{\mathsf T}(\lambda+t v)=0\quad\forall t\in\mathbb R.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Affine Family under Rank Loss
Constraint Rank-Loss Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact singularity consequence of rank loss in an active-set KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\) be an active-constraint Jacobian and let
\[K=\begin{bmatrix}Q&J^\top\\J&0\end{bmatrix}.\]
If \(J\) lacks full row rank, then some \(v\ne0\) satisfies \(J^\top v=0\). Consequently,
\[K\begin{bmatrix}0\\v\end{bmatrix}=0,\]
so \(K\) is singular for every symmetric \(Q\). Thus the usual nonsingular-KKT conclusions, including locally unique multiplier recovery from this linear system, are unavailable. Rank loss alone does not prove primal nonuniqueness, because uniqueness may still follow from curvature on feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-deficient active Jacobian makes the corresponding saddle-point KKT matrix singular and prevents multiplier uniqueness from being inferred from linear-system nonsingularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is singular because \((0,v)\in\ker K\) for some \(v\ne0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct standard saddle-point matrix consequence of row-rank loss
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated singularity consequence follows from row-rank loss, is properly limited with respect to primal uniqueness, and fits a failure-boundary leaf, but it lacks a source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility consequence of rank loss in a linear equality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\), rank deficiency of \(A\) does not by itself determine feasibility. The system is feasible if and only if \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\), equivalently if and only if \(y^{\mathsf T}b=0\) for every \(y\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-deficient equality system is feasible exactly when its right-hand side satisfies every dependence relation among the rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ax=b\text{ is feasible}\iff b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\iff y^{\mathsf T}b=0\ \forall y\in\ker(A^{\mathsf T}).

children.title: Weakly Active Constraints
children.top_down_role: Active constraints with marginal multiplier support or limited numerical separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Active Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak activity relative to a specified KKT solution and inequality multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an inequality-constrained convex QP with inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), let \((x^*,y^*,z^*)\) be a KKT solution. Inequality \(i\) is weakly active at that solution when
\[g_i(x^*)=0\quad\text{and}\quad z_i^*=0.\]
It is strongly active when \(g_i(x^*)=0\) and \(z_i^*>0\). Because multipliers can be nonunique, weak activity is defined relative to the selected KKT multiplier unless \(z_i^*=0\) for every multiplier associated with \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is weakly active at a KKT solution when it is tight but its associated nonnegative multiplier equals zero.

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier of the ith inequality
